fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach IGCSE subjects to a named syllabus code at both tiers, and they plan in weeks rather than in topics. The first question any of them will ask is which series your child is entered for, because that single fact decides how much of the specification a plan can afford to revisit.

intro.heading: Where your child is now, where the grade needs to be, and the weeks in between
paragraphs: Parents searching for an IGCSE home tutor in Fujairah rarely want a discussion of pedagogy. They want to know whether there is still time. A mock came back two grades below target, or a subject that was fine in Year 10 has quietly stopped working, and the real question is arithmetic: how many teaching weeks remain before the papers, how much of the gap those weeks can close, and what it costs per week to find out. Almost nothing written about tutoring in this market answers that, because answering it honestly sometimes means telling a family to buy less.

The arithmetic on the east coast has an extra term in it. Fujairah is on the far side of the Hajar mountains, roughly an hour and a half of driving from Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah and often closer to two from Dubai. A visiting tutor taking a two-hour lesson in Fujairah city from a base in Sharjah is away from that base for around five hours. That time is real and somebody pays for it, which is why visiting rates in the UAE sit in a higher band than online rates and why visiting availability on this coast is usually weekends, a two-hour minimum, or both. The first table on this page sets that out properly rather than leaving it as a vague note about convenience.

IB Gram's answer to it is to remove the drive. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time so a session sits in a Fujairah evening after the bus and a meal. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; a tutor arriving at the door is a service we run only in India. That is a limitation and it is stated here rather than implied. What it buys is a subject match chosen from everyone who teaches the specification rather than from whoever is prepared to cross the mountains on a Tuesday.

The rest of the page is the timeline. There is a diagnostic stage, which should take one session and produce a document. There is the block of roughly twelve weeks in which a single subject genuinely moves, and the evidence for that movement is marked work rather than anybody's impression. There is the Year 11 year counted from October to results day, window by window, with what should exist at the end of each. There are the last six weeks, which are a different kind of work entirely and are mostly wasted on new content. And there is the conversation about Ramadan, term dates and what happens when the plan slips, which it usually does once.

One honest caveat before any of it. A grade is not a purchase. Nothing on this page promises a number, a jump or a result, because no tutor can deliver one and anyone offering it is selling something other than teaching. What a good plan offers is that the mark your child is capable of actually appears on the paper, which is a smaller claim and a far more achievable one. Most lost marks on IGCSE papers are not lost to ignorance. They are lost to unwritten working, misread command terms and time spent in the wrong order, and those are the things a term of structured weekly work reliably repairs.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: A home-tutoring question is really a question about which stage your child is standing in, because each stage has a different number of weeks attached and a different kind of work available inside them. The four below cover almost every enquiry that arrives from the east coast.

programmes.name: Year 10: the cheap year to fix things
programmes.description: The first year of the two-year course, examined by nobody, which makes it the least expensive year in which to repair a foundation. Work done here compounds: algebraic fluency secured in Year 10 pays into every science paper in Year 11, while the same work bought in March of Year 11 competes with revision for the same hours. A block of eight to twelve weekly sessions in Year 10 typically achieves more than twice that number bought later.
programmes.countryNote: East-coast families often wait, understandably, because nothing is being examined and the school report looks survivable. The practical argument for not waiting is the local subject list: if a Year 10 diagnostic shows that Extended tier is at risk in mathematics, there is still time to decide whether a tier change or a tuition block is the answer, and both of those decisions get harder once entries for the series are in.

programmes.name: Year 11: the run to the series
programmes.description: Around thirty-four teaching weeks, interrupted by mocks, holidays and Ramadan, ending in a series of written papers. The year divides naturally into content completion, mock analysis, whole-paper practice and final rehearsal, and the mistake families make most often is using the later windows for the earlier kind of work. Revising topics in April when the problem is timing produces a student who knows more and scores the same.
programmes.countryNote: Mock timing varies between schools in Fujairah, and the mock is the single most useful document a tutor can be given, because it shows where marks went rather than how the student seemed. Ask the school when mocks fall for your child's cohort in September, then plan the first tuition block to land immediately afterwards rather than before, when there is nothing to diagnose from.

programmes.name: The November series and resits
programmes.description: Both major boards run an autumn series as well as a summer one, which means a disappointing grade is not a lost year. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE examinations in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and Cambridge runs June and November series. A resit plan is short, narrow and built entirely around the papers that went wrong.
programmes.countryNote: For a Fujairah student the resit question is partly logistical, because the entry may need to go through a centre in another emirate if the school does not enter the autumn series. Settle where the paper will be sat at the same time as deciding to resit, and confirm which administrative zone that centre sits in before reading any timetable.

programmes.name: The summer bridge into sixth form
programmes.description: The six to eight weeks between the last paper and the start of Year 12, which almost nobody uses and which repays use more than any equivalent period in the school year. A short block here covers the content the A Level or Diploma course assumes rather than teaches: calculus notation, moles beyond the IGCSE treatment, and the reading load that sixth form drops on a student in week one without warning.
programmes.countryNote: The bridge matters more on the east coast because some students change school or emirate for sixth form, which means arriving in a new cohort with a different scheme of work and no shared history with the teacher. A student who has already met the first three weeks of content starts that term as a participant rather than as somebody catching up.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: The note against each subject below is about time: how long a block of weekly one-to-one work usually needs before the change shows in marked work. These are patterns from teaching the specifications, not promises, and a diagnostic replaces them with something specific to your child.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The fastest subject to move and the one where the first five weeks matter most, because almost every later topic rests on algebraic manipulation. A student whose arithmetic is fine and whose algebra is not will often show a measurable change within a month. A student missing number work from Year 9 needs a term, and saying so early saves a family from buying the wrong plan.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Moves in two stages. Numerical confidence arrives first, usually inside four or five weeks, because the calculations follow patterns. Circuit and field reasoning takes longer, because it has to be rebuilt rather than practised. A plan that treats physics as one subject with one timeline consistently underestimates the electricity topics and overestimates everything else.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: The most measurable subject on this list. Moles calculations either work or they do not, and the same is true of balanced equations and organic pathways, which makes progress visible in marked work faster than in biology. Six to eight weeks of weekly work usually converts a student who understands chemistry into one who scores it.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The slowest of the three sciences to shift, because the problem is almost never comprehension. It is volume and recall under time. Progress comes from repeated retrieval and from marking long answers against the published criteria, which means the useful work happens between sessions and the session exists to set it up and audit it.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Responds quickly in directed writing and slowly in reading response. Teaching a student the shape of a strong directed-writing answer can change marks within three or four weeks. Teaching close textual analysis is a term's work, because it depends on reading habits that do not form in a fortnight. Honest sequencing matters more here than in any other subject.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: The speaking and listening components are the ones that move fastest, and they are the hardest for a student to rehearse alone, which makes them unusually good value in a weekly slot. Reading and writing improve steadily rather than suddenly. A term of weekly conversation practice with targeted correction is the standard shape of a plan here.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455, Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram discipline is a three-week job and it carries a surprising share of the available marks. Data-response technique takes longer because it is really a reading skill. A plan that starts with diagrams gets an early visible improvement, which also buys the student the confidence to do the slower work.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450, Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: The evaluative command terms are the whole ceiling, and they are teachable in about a month of weekly work on past questions. Content knowledge is rarely the limiting factor by Year 11. This is a subject where four well-used sessions can do more than a term of general revision, which is worth knowing before buying a longer block.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Two independent timelines in one subject. Theory recall responds to the same retrieval work as biology. The algorithms and pseudocode paper responds to writing code by hand against the board's own conventions, which a confident Python student may never have done. Diagnose which half is weak before committing to a number of weeks.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Not a subject to start late. It assumes fluency the main mathematics course is still building, so a block bought in the final two terms usually turns into remedial work on 0580 content under a different name. Started in Year 10 alongside the main course, it is the best preparation available for sixth-form mathematics.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Fujairah changes the weekly rhythm a plan has to fit inside: when the bus arrives, when a quiet room is free, and which evenings are already gone. The notes below are about that rhythm, because a slot nobody can keep is worse than no slot at all.

regions.name: Fujairah city
regions.note: Shortest journeys home and the widest choice of school, which usually means the earliest workable weekday slot in the emirate. Families here are also the most likely to have an activity already booked on two weekday evenings, so the useful question is not when a lesson could start but which evening is genuinely free for a whole term.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: The bus run rather than the distance sets the clock here. A realistic first slot sits after arrival and a meal, which in most households means an hour later than parents expect when they first pick a time. Picking a slot thirty minutes later than seems necessary is the single best way to stop a plan from quietly collapsing in week four.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Households here are frequently running more than one school timetable, with siblings finishing at different times. Where two children both need a weekly slot, putting them in consecutive hours on the same evening protects the rest of the week and means one quiet room is prepared once rather than twice.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Close enough to the city that an evening out is plausible, which in practice means the calendar fills. The families here who keep a plan going for a full term are the ones who treat the weekly session as fixed rather than movable, and who agree at the outset which two weeks of the year it will be skipped.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: Quieter and further from the city's activity schedule, which tends to make the weekly slot easier to protect and the plan easier to sustain across a whole term. The constraint here is usually one shared study space, so a paired sibling booking in consecutive hours works better than two separate evenings.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: The longest journey to anything in-person and the smallest local subject list, which means a plan here is normally built for the whole year rather than bought in short blocks. Families in Dibba also need term dates confirmed from the specific school rather than assumed, because the wider area is served by more than one administration.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Highway villages where the school journey is already long, so an evening slot competes directly with the student's remaining energy. A mid-evening session of fifty minutes with a marked set to follow usually works better here than a longer sitting, and the plan should say so rather than defaulting to a full hour.

regions.name: Masafi
regions.note: At the mountain pass, with some students attending school in another emirate entirely. That matters for a timeline because term dates, mock weeks and holiday patterns can differ from their neighbours', so the Year 11 calendar below has to be rebuilt against the actual school rather than against the emirate.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of booking, each defined by how many weeks it has to work in. The honest version of this choice starts with the calendar rather than with a preference, because a format that suits a year does not suit a fortnight.

modes.title: The twelve-week block
modes.description: The standard shape when a term is available. One weekly hour, the same tutor, the same slot, working through the specification in sequence with a marked question set between sessions. A review falls at week five, when a recurring error should have stopped appearing, and again at week eleven, when the decision is whether to extend, change subject or stop.

modes.title: The six-week pre-series run
modes.description: Bought for the weeks immediately before the papers and built entirely around whole papers and the published mark schemes. No new content unless a diagnostic finds a gap that is genuinely cheap to close. The work is timing, command terms, the order answers are attempted, and the five errors that keep recurring in that student's own scripts.

modes.title: Paired sibling or paired subject slots
modes.description: Two consecutive fifty-minute sessions on one evening, either two subjects for one student or one subject each for two children in the same house. It protects the rest of the week, uses one prepared quiet room, and keeps both plans visible to the same parent in the same written record.

sections.heading: What a visiting IGCSE tutor on the east coast actually costs per teaching hour
paragraphs: Visiting tuition is priced per hour, which is the least informative way to price it. The number a Fujairah family should be comparing is cost per teaching hour, and on this coast those two figures diverge sharply because of the mountains. A tutor based in Sharjah who teaches a two-hour lesson in Fujairah city is committed for roughly five hours door to door. Whoever absorbs that time pays for it: either the rate sits at the top of its band, or there is a travel surcharge, or there is a two-hour minimum booking, or the availability is weekends only.

Published market bands in the UAE put visiting one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate table sits at the lower end of the visiting range, at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reported up to AED 500. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits, and those two numbers only become comparable once both are divided down to a per-hour figure.

None of this makes visiting tuition the wrong choice. For a younger student who genuinely needs an adult sitting beside them, or for a family that wants a person in the house, it can be worth every dirham. What it does mean is that the honest comparison is not AED 250 against AED 250. It is a narrower subject list, a narrower availability window and a higher real rate against a wider tutor pool and a fixed weekday slot. The table below sets out the drive-time arithmetic from the five bases a Fujairah family is most likely to be quoted from.

A note on what IB Gram does and does not do here, stated plainly rather than buried. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; tutors arriving at the door is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The reason this page costs out visiting tuition anyway is that a parent comparing options deserves the real numbers for both, including the option we do not sell.

sections.heading: Finding out where your child actually is, in one session
paragraphs: A timeline needs a starting point, and a report comment is not one. Reports describe how a student seemed across a term. A marked paper shows where the marks went, which is a completely different document and the only one from which a plan can be written. The single most useful thing a Fujairah parent can do before any tuition is bought is to photograph two or three pages of the most recent marked mock and send them with the enquiry.

The diagnostic session itself should take forty-five minutes and should produce something written. In that time a specialist can watch a student attempt a timed question, see what they do when they are stuck, check two or three foundational skills the specification assumes, and read one marked script. What comes out is a statement of which topics are secure, which are not, whether the losses are content, technique or timing, and a realistic number of weeks. It should name the syllabus code and the tier it is planning against.

The distinction between content, technique and timing is the one that decides everything afterwards, and it is the one most plans never make. A student who does not know the topic needs teaching, which takes weeks. A student who knows it and writes it badly needs mark-scheme work, which takes sessions. A student who knows it, writes it well and runs out of time needs whole-paper rehearsal, which takes practice rather than instruction. Buying twelve weeks of teaching for a timing problem is the most common way families waste money in this market.

If the diagnostic concludes that tuition is not the right purchase, that is a legitimate outcome and it gets written down. Sometimes the honest answer is that the student needs to use the school's own clinic properly for a term, or that the problem is sleep and screen hours rather than chemistry, or that one subject is being carried at the expense of three others and the choice is a timetable decision for the school. A diagnostic that can only ever conclude in favour of buying lessons is a sales call with a worksheet attached.

sections.heading: What twelve weeks of weekly one-to-one work actually changes
paragraphs: Twelve weeks is the shortest block in which a subject reliably moves and the longest a family should commit to before a review. The shape is consistent across subjects. The first two sessions are foundation repair, which feels like going backwards and is the part students resist. Sessions three to five introduce the specification content in order with a marked question set between each. Around week five, a recurring error either stops appearing in the marked sets or it does not, and that binary is the first honest review point.

From week six the work changes character. Content coverage continues, but whole questions replace individual skills and the marking starts naming mark-scheme points rather than right and wrong. By week nine most students can attempt a full past question in the subject under time, and the sessions become about reading their own scripts critically. Week eleven is the second review: extend, switch to a different subject, or stop because the subject is now self-sustaining. All three are real outcomes and the third is not a failure.

The part of this that families underestimate is what happens outside the hour. A weekly session with no work between sessions is a conversation, and it moves marks very little. Twenty targeted questions on the one error that keeps recurring will do more for a grade than an extra hour of teaching, which is why every session here ends with a set and the next one starts by marking it. Parents do not need to teach anything; they need to know whether the set was done, and the written record tells them.

Measured honestly, a twelve-week block in a single subject usually produces a student who writes the marks they already deserved, plus some of the content they were missing. Whether that is one grade or two depends entirely on how much of the original gap was technique rather than knowledge, which is why the diagnostic comes first. Anybody quoting a grade improvement before seeing a marked paper is guessing, and anybody quoting one afterwards is still guessing with better information.

sections.heading: The Year 11 year, counted window by window from October
paragraphs: Roughly thirty-four teaching weeks separate the start of Year 11 from the summer papers, and they are not interchangeable. Each window supports a different kind of work, and the commonest planning error is using a late window for early work: revising topics in April when the problem is paper timing produces a student who knows more and scores exactly the same. The table below assigns each window its job and says what should exist at the end of it.

The first window, September to late November, is the one that carries the tier decision. Cambridge publishes a final entry date for each series months ahead of the papers, and once entries are submitted the tier is fixed on the statement of entry. For the March 2027 series, as a worked example of the gap, final entries fall on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Whatever series your child sits, ask the exam officer for the final entry date in September and treat it as the deadline for every tier conversation.

The middle windows belong to the mock. A mock paper is the most valuable document of the year because it converts a vague worry into a list, and the list is short: most students lose marks in three or four identifiable places, repeatedly. December to mid-February is for closing those. Mid-February to the end of March is for whole papers under time, which is a different skill and needs practising rather than learning. April onwards is rehearsal, logistics and sleep.

Two practical items that belong in the same calendar. Pearson publishes its International GCSE timetables for each series and also issues provisional timetables in advance, so any date should be checked against the live page rather than a restatement. And Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, stating that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Confirm your centre's zone before printing anything.

sections.heading: The last six weeks, and what they can honestly fix
paragraphs: The six weeks before a series are the most commonly misused period in the whole timeline. Families buy teaching and students want reassurance, when what the weeks can actually deliver is a higher mark for knowledge the student already has. Almost every script in this window loses marks to the same small set of causes: working not shown, command terms misread, time spent in the wrong order, and one or two genuinely weak topics that keep appearing. Those are repairable in six weeks. A missing year of content is not, and saying so in week six is kinder than discovering it in week two of the papers.

The method is unglamorous. Week six is a diagnostic on the two weakest papers, sat to time, marked properly, and reduced to a written list of the errors that recur by frequency rather than by how annoying they are. Weeks five and four take the top two errors and rebuild them with targeted question sets. Week three moves to mark-scheme language, because a student who can name the criterion they are meeting writes differently from one who is hoping. Weeks two and one are whole papers, timing plans and logistics.

What the student does alone matters more in this window than at any other time, and it is where a plan either works or quietly fails. Twenty questions on one recurring error beats an extra hour of teaching, every time. A full paper attempted to time and then marked by the student against the published criteria, with the tutor auditing the marking rather than redoing it, teaches more about the examiner's expectations than a term of explanation. Parents do not need to understand the chemistry; they need to know the paper was attempted and marked.

The last item on the list is not academic. Confirm the statement of entry, the correct zone timetable, the centre and the room in the final week, not on the morning. Cambridge is explicit that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after using the wrong zone version of the timetable, and that is an avoidable way to lose a grade that no amount of tuition can repair afterwards.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holiday weeks and the weeks a plan has to survive
paragraphs: A thirty-four week plan written in September will meet at least three interruptions, and the ones that break plans are the predictable ones. The UAE academic year carries a shortened school day during Ramadan, a set of public holidays that move with the lunar calendar, and a mid-year break whose dates differ between schools and sometimes between emirates. A plan that pretends otherwise collapses in its sixth week and takes the family's confidence with it.

The practical approach is to decide the skip weeks before the block starts rather than negotiating them one at a time. Two agreed weeks in a twelve-week block is realistic and keeps the rest of the schedule intact. During Ramadan the usual answer is not to pause but to move: a shortened school day frees the afternoon, and a session after Iftar works well for older students who are revising late anyway. Either way, the time changes once for the month rather than drifting weekly, because a slot that moves every week is a slot that gets missed.

Holidays themselves are worth using rather than avoiding, particularly the winter break in a Year 11 year. Three sessions in a week with nothing else competing for the hours can do what six weekly sessions do during term, which makes a holiday block the cheapest acceleration available in the calendar. The limit is the student, not the subject: a child who has just finished a term of mocks may need the first week of a break to be a break.

For Masafi and Dibba families there is an extra step, because a student attending school in another emirate may be working to different term dates and mock weeks from their neighbours. Build the plan against the school's published calendar rather than against the emirate's general pattern, and confirm the mock weeks in September when the school sets them, since those weeks are the anchor for everything the plan does afterwards.
bullets: Agree two skip weeks at the start of a block rather than negotiating weekly
During Ramadan, move the slot once for the month instead of rescheduling each week
A three-session week inside a holiday break accelerates more than the equivalent term weeks
Build against the specific school's calendar, not the emirate's general pattern

sections.heading: What a parent does between the sessions
paragraphs: Parents repeatedly ask what they should be doing, and the honest answer is less than they fear and more than nothing. Nobody needs to learn the chemistry. What a plan needs from a parent is three things: that the weekly slot is protected, that the question set between sessions is attempted, and that the written record is read rather than filed. Those three are the difference between a plan that works and an identical plan that does not.

Protecting the slot sounds trivial and is the hardest of the three. A session that moves twice becomes a session that is missed, and a missed session in a twelve-week block is eight per cent of the plan. The practical trick is to choose a slot thirty minutes later than seems necessary, so the bus, the meal and the inevitable delay all fit inside the margin rather than eating into the lesson. Families who do this keep plans going for whole terms; families who optimise for the earliest possible start tend not to.

Reading the record matters because it is the only window a parent has into a lesson they were not in. A useful record says what was covered, which question set was issued, and which mark-scheme points the previous set lost. Over five weeks a pattern becomes visible without any technical knowledge at all: either the same loss keeps appearing or it stops. If it keeps appearing for five weeks and nothing in the plan changes, that is the moment to ask the question rather than to wait politely for the next review.

One thing a parent should not do is become the enforcer of the between-session work in a way that turns the subject into a battleground. If the set is not getting done, the useful conversation is with the tutor about whether it is the wrong length, the wrong difficulty or the wrong time of day. A set that takes forty minutes and is attempted is worth more than one that takes two hours and is not.

sections.heading: When the weeks are not enough, and what to buy instead
paragraphs: Sometimes a family arrives eight weeks before a series asking for two subjects rebuilt and a tier change, and the honest answer is that the hours do not exist. Saying so loses the booking. It also saves several thousand dirhams from being spent on a plan that was never going to land, and it keeps the family's trust for the resit or for the sibling behind them. No tutoring provider in this market publishes that limit, which is one of the stranger silences in the whole set of pages competing for this search.

When the weeks are short, the right purchase changes rather than disappearing. Narrowing to one subject rather than three concentrates the hours where they can still move a grade. Narrowing further to the two papers with the most recoverable marks concentrates them again. In some cases the best advice is to protect the subjects that are already working, because a student spending every evening rescuing chemistry can lose two grades elsewhere without noticing, and a timetable triage conversation is worth more than any number of lessons.

The autumn series is the other honest option, and it is routinely forgotten. Both major boards run a November or autumn series as well as a summer one, so a grade that goes wrong in June is a delay rather than a year. A resit plan is narrow, cheap relative to a full year, and built entirely around the specific papers that went wrong. For a Fujairah student the logistics need settling early, because the entry may need to go through a centre in another emirate and the administrative zone must be confirmed with that centre.

All of this gets said in the trial lesson, before money changes hands. One free 45-minute session per family, no card details required, ending in a written statement of what the subject needs and how many weeks that is. If the statement says the weeks are not there, it says so in writing, with a recommendation for what to do instead. That is the only version of this conversation worth having, and it is better had in October than in May.

process.title: Say which series your child is entered for
process.description: The series fixes the number of teaching weeks available, and the number of weeks decides what kind of plan is honest. Send the subject, the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series in the first message. All five sit on the option booklet or the statement of entry, and with them a plan can be written in one conversation instead of three.

process.title: Send the marked mock, not the report
process.description: Photographs of two or three marked pages tell a specialist where the marks went, which a report comment cannot. If no mock exists yet, say when the school has scheduled them, because the most useful first tuition block usually starts the week after a mock rather than the week before it.

process.title: Take the 45-minute diagnostic
process.description: One free trial session per family, no card details required. Your child attempts a timed question while the tutor watches what happens when they get stuck, and the session ends in a written statement: topics secure, topics not, whether the losses are content, technique or timing, and a realistic number of weeks. If tuition is the wrong purchase, the statement says so.

process.title: Fix a slot with margin and two skip weeks
process.description: Choose a weekday slot thirty minutes later than seems necessary, so the bus, the meal and the usual delay fit inside the margin. Agree the two weeks in the block that will be skipped before the block starts. Both of these sound administrative and both are the reason plans survive a full term.

process.title: Review at week five and week eleven, against marked work
process.description: At week five a recurring error has either stopped appearing in the marked sets or it has not, and that is the review. At week eleven the decision is to extend, switch subject or stop because the subject is now self-sustaining. Stopping is a legitimate outcome, and a review that consists of asking whether everyone is happy is not a review.

whyPoints.title: Plans with an end date
whyPoints.description: Every block is a stated number of sessions with a review point and a finish, not a rolling monthly charge. Families know at the outset what they are buying and when the decision to continue falls. Open-ended bookings are how a term becomes a year without anybody producing an account of what changed.

whyPoints.title: Marked work as the only evidence
whyPoints.description: Progress is read from question sets marked against the board's published criteria, with the mark-scheme point named against each loss. A parent who was not in the lesson can still see whether a specific error has stopped appearing. Nothing here is reported as a general sense that things are going well.

whyPoints.title: Travel priced honestly, including the option we do not sell
whyPoints.description: This page costs out visiting tuition from five bases with the drive counted, because a parent comparing options needs the real figure for both. IB Gram delivers online only in the UAE, with no home visits anywhere in the country, and says so rather than letting a parent assume otherwise.

whyPoints.title: A slot built around the school bus
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time with deliberate margin after the bus and a meal, because a slot that is thirty minutes too early is a slot that gets missed. The tutor pool is wide enough to make an east-coast evening slot a normal request rather than a favour.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, at any point
whyPoints.description: Nothing on this page promises a number, a jump or a result. What a plan can honestly offer is that the mark your child is already capable of appears on the paper, which is where most lost IGCSE marks actually are. Any provider promising a specific number in advance is selling something that is not teaching.

whyPoints.title: The limits said first
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE, no group classes, no tutor for a syllabus code nobody teaches, and a written no when the weeks remaining are too few. Those statements cost bookings and they are the reason what is described on this page is what arrives in the lesson.

faqs.question: How much does a visiting IGCSE tutor charge to drive out to Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Published market bands for visiting one-to-one tuition in the UAE run roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Bestimate's Dubai rate table sits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reported up to AED 500. For the east coast the number matters less than the structure: a tutor coming from Sharjah is committed for about five hours to teach for two, so expect a two-hour minimum, a surcharge, weekend-only availability, or a rate at the top of the band.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor in Fujairah cost per actual contact hour?
faqs.answer: Divide everything down before comparing. A monthly package of four two-hour home visits quoted at AED 1,599 to 1,799 works out around AED 200 to 225 per teaching hour, while eight online sessions quoted around AED 799 works out near AED 100. Neither figure includes what the family absorbs in rearranged evenings or in a narrower subject list. The comparison that matters is cost per teaching hour against subject match, because a cheaper hour teaching the wrong specification is not cheap at all.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to homes anywhere in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and tutors arriving at a family's door is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time so the slot sits in a Fujairah evening after the school bus and a meal. This page prices visiting tuition anyway, because a parent weighing the options deserves real figures for the option we do not sell as well as the one we do.

faqs.question: How many weeks of tuition does my son need before the June series?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the losses are content, technique or timing, and that cannot be answered from a report. Broadly: a timing problem responds to four to six weeks of whole-paper work, a technique problem to six to eight weeks of mark-scheme work, and a genuine content gap to a term or more. A diagnostic session that watches your son attempt a timed question and reads one marked script will give a specific number, in writing, along with what happens if that number is not available.

faqs.question: We are starting in January with papers in May. What can realistically change?
faqs.answer: A great deal, provided the plan accepts what January means. There is time to close the three or four errors a mock exposed, time to build whole-paper timing, and time to rehearse command terms properly. There is not time to rebuild a missing year of content in three subjects at once. The realistic January plan narrows to one or two subjects, works from marked scripts rather than from the textbook, and spends March and April on whole papers rather than on topic revision.

faqs.question: My daughter is at a grade 4 and needs a grade 6. Is that jump realistic?
faqs.answer: Nobody can promise it and anybody who does is selling something other than teaching. What can be assessed is how much of the current gap is technique rather than knowledge, because that fraction is what moves fastest. A student sitting at a 4 who understands the content and writes it badly has a very different ceiling from one who is missing half the specification. The diagnostic exists to tell you which of those is true before you commit a term of evenings and several thousand dirhams to finding out.

faqs.question: How do I know the plan is working after the first month?
faqs.answer: Read the marked sets rather than asking how things are going. By about week five a specific recurring error has either stopped appearing in your child's own written work or it has not, and that is a binary you can check without knowing the subject. A useful record names the mark-scheme point lost against each question, so the pattern is visible across four or five weeks. If the same loss is still there at week five and nothing in the plan has changed, ask then rather than waiting for a review.

faqs.question: What should my child be doing between the weekly sessions?
faqs.answer: One targeted set, finished. Twenty questions on the single error that keeps recurring does more for a grade than an extra hour of teaching, because the hour explains and the set embeds. Later in a plan the set becomes a full paper attempted to time and marked by the student against the published criteria, with the tutor auditing that marking rather than redoing it. If the set is not getting done, the fix is usually its length or its timing rather than more pressure.

faqs.question: Do lessons continue through Ramadan, and at what time of day?
faqs.answer: They continue, with the time moved once for the month rather than renegotiated weekly. The shortened school day frees the afternoon, which suits younger students, while older students revising late often do better in a slot after Iftar. The important part is making a single change for the month: a slot that drifts every week is a slot that gets missed, and a missed week in a twelve-week block is a meaningful fraction of the plan. Agree the Ramadan timing when the block is first set up.

faqs.question: Can we pause tuition over the school holidays and pick it up again?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families pausing is sensible. The alternative worth considering in a Year 11 year is using part of a break as a short intensive block instead: three sessions in a week with nothing else competing for the hours achieves roughly what six weekly term-time sessions achieve, which makes it the cheapest acceleration in the calendar. The limit is the student rather than the subject. A child who has just finished mock weeks may need the first week of a break to actually be a break.

faqs.question: What happens in the last fortnight before the first paper?
faqs.answer: Almost no new content. Week two is whole papers under strict timing, a plan for the order answers will be attempted, and a decision about how the first ten minutes of each paper will be spent. The final week is short retrieval bursts, early nights and logistics. That last item is not trivial: confirm the statement of entry, the centre, the room and the correct zone version of the timetable, because Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting in Year 10 rather than waiting until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the cheapest year in which to fix anything, because nothing is being examined and the work compounds. Algebraic fluency secured in Year 10 pays into every science paper the following year, while the same work bought in March of Year 11 competes directly with revision for the same evenings. A block of eight to twelve sessions in Year 10 typically achieves more than twice that number bought in the final two terms, which is an argument about timing rather than about effort.

faqs.question: What happens when a visiting tutor cancels during exam term?
faqs.answer: This is the structural risk of a long drive and it is worth asking about before booking rather than after. A tutor crossing the Hajar mountains has weather, traffic and their own commitments between them and your child, and a cancellation in the final six weeks is a week of the plan gone with no easy replacement nearby. Online sessions carry the same risk of illness and none of the travel risk, and a wider tutor pool means a cover session is a realistic option rather than a theoretical one.

faqs.question: Who writes the revision timetable, the family or the tutor?
faqs.answer: The tutor should draft it, the student should own it, and the parent should be able to read it. A plan written by a tutor who has seen marked scripts will prioritise by where the marks actually are, which almost never matches what the student feels worst about. A plan the student has not agreed to will not survive February. The practical version is one page: which papers, in which order, which errors are being tracked, and what happens in each of the remaining weeks.

faqs.question: Can we change tutors part way through a block if the match is wrong?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should be raised early rather than endured politely. A mismatch usually shows up in the first three sessions as a student who is working but not being stretched, or who is being taught above the level the diagnostic found. Because the written record travels with the plan, a new tutor starts from the marked sets rather than from scratch. Changing tutor at week two costs a session of continuity; changing at week ten costs most of the block.

faqs.question: How late in Year 11 is it still worth paying for tuition?
faqs.answer: Up to about six weeks before the first paper, with the plan narrowed and the goal changed. In that window tuition cannot repair a missing year of content, but it can reliably recover marks lost to unwritten working, misread command terms and poor time allocation, and those account for a surprising share of the gap on most scripts. Inside six weeks the honest answer is sometimes no, and it should come in writing from a diagnostic rather than after the first invoice.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the number of weeks you have left
fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: Everything on this page follows from one figure: the teaching weeks between today and your child's series. With a term available, a twelve-week block in one subject with marked work between sessions is the shape that reliably moves a grade. With six weeks, the plan narrows to the papers where marks are most recoverable. With fewer than that, the honest answer may be the autumn series and a short, specific plan instead. One free 45-minute diagnostic, no card details, gives you that number in writing, along with what it can and cannot buy, before anyone asks you for money.

fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE subjects live over video, to a named syllabus code and tier. Each works from a shared page the student can scroll back through afterwards, which is the part of online teaching that has no equivalent in a room with a whiteboard that gets wiped.

intro.heading: Four things sold as online tuition, and why only one of them reads your child's work
paragraphs: The phrase online tutoring covers at least four products that behave nothing alike. A recorded video course is a library: well made, inexpensive, available at two in the morning, and completely indifferent to whether your child understood lesson four. A large live group class is a lecture with a chat box. A small group class is a class. A marketplace hour bought one at a time is a conversation with a stranger who has not seen last week's work. Scheduled one-to-one with a matched specialist is the only format in which somebody reads your child's own written answers and tells them which mark-scheme point they missed.

That difference is the whole argument, and it is worth stating in terms of cost rather than quality. A recorded course at a low monthly price is excellent value for a self-starting student who is already on track. For a student who is stuck, it is the most expensive thing on the list, because nothing in it diagnoses anything and six months can pass with the same gap still in place. Parents in Fujairah who have already tried a subscription and seen no change usually arrive at this page having learnt that the hard way.

The east coast makes the comparison sharper than it would be in Dubai. Fujairah sits on the Gulf of Oman behind the Hajar mountains, and the private-school set is small, so a student taking a less common subject at Extended tier may have no local specialist within an hour and a half of driving. Online delivery is not a compromise in that situation. It is the only arrangement in which the tutor is chosen because they teach Cambridge 0625 rather than because they live in the right emirate, and it is why IB Gram delivers to UAE families this way.

Being clear about what that means: every UAE lesson here is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time so it falls in a Fujairah evening. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; a tutor arriving at the door is a service we run only in India. That is a limitation, and it is stated at the top rather than discovered later. What this page does instead of apologising for it is explain exactly how the teaching works, because the mechanics are where parents' real doubts live and almost nobody writes them down.

So: the comparison table, then the anatomy of an hour, then how mathematics and chemical equations get written on a screen, then the practical science question, which is the one every science parent asks and which has a precise answer depending on which paper the school entered. After that, the setup a Fujairah household actually needs, what happens when a connection drops, how a timed paper is supervised on video, the attention arithmetic against a class of thirty, and what happens to recordings and a minor's data. None of it is difficult. It is just unwritten everywhere else.

fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Online delivery does not change which qualification a student is sitting, and the qualification is what a tutor plans against. Four families of specification cover almost every enquiry from the east coast, and the first job in any match is identifying which one is on the statement of entry.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge International's international GCSE, taught as a two-year course and examined by written papers, with many syllabuses split into a Core and an Extended tier. The sciences are the ones where online delivery needs a specific answer, because Cambridge offers a practical test and an alternative-to-practical paper and schools choose between them. Cambridge runs its examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah schools entering Cambridge are generally entering smaller cohorts than Dubai schools, which affects which tier is offered and sometimes whether a subject is offered at all. For an online tutor the practical consequence is that the syllabus code and the practical paper route both need confirming from the school rather than assumed from the subject name.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international GCSE, graded 9 to 1, with Foundation and Higher tiers in some subjects and a different approach to assessing practical science from Cambridge's. Pearson runs International GCSE examinations in May/June and November each year, publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and released its November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.
programmes.countryNote: It is common for one east-coast school to enter Pearson for mathematics and Cambridge for the sciences, which means a family can be managing two boards inside one child's timetable. An online tutor working across both needs to say so explicitly, because model answers from the wrong board actively mislead a student in English and in the sciences.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course, ending in Checkpoint tests that Cambridge runs in March, May and October. Nothing here counts towards a final grade, which makes it the cheapest stage at which to repair algebraic fluency, written science structure and reading speed. Online delivery suits this stage particularly well, because sessions can be short and frequent rather than long and weekly.
programmes.countryNote: On the east coast this stage is also when a family finds out whether the school can actually staff the subject combination a student wants at IGCSE. A Year 9 diagnostic that flags a problem leaves time for the school conversation, which is a different and often more useful outcome than a tuition booking.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The sixth-form route most east-coast British-curriculum students take next, in three or four subjects, with a sharp rise in mathematical demand across the sciences and in the length of reasoning the papers reward. Online one-to-one is heavily used at this stage, because the subject combinations get narrow enough that a local specialist frequently does not exist in a small emirate.
programmes.countryNote: Some Fujairah students sit sixth form in another emirate or as private candidates, which changes exam logistics as well as teaching. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so a student sitting at a centre outside their school's emirate needs the zone confirmed by that centre.

fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: The note against each subject below is about the screen: what a video lesson does better than a room, and what it has to work around. These are practical observations about teaching the specifications remotely rather than claims about outcomes.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject online delivery suits best, provided the tutor writes by hand on a graphics tablet rather than typing. Working appears line by line in the student's view and stays on the shared page afterwards, so a method can be reread three days later. The thing to watch is the student writing on paper off-camera; the paper needs to be visible or photographed into the page at the end.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Circuit diagrams and ray diagrams work well drawn live, and simulations handle what a Fujairah classroom often cannot set up quickly anyway. The genuine constraint is apparatus handling, which matters only if the school has entered the practical test rather than the alternative paper, so that question gets settled before the first lesson.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Equations, mole calculations and organic pathways are all writing, which the screen handles cleanly. Observation language is the part that needs deliberate work remotely: a student who has done the experiment in school still has to learn to describe a colour change in the words the mark scheme accepts, and video lessons can drill that against photographs and recorded demonstrations.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Mostly a retrieval and long-answer subject, which means most of the useful work happens between sessions and the lesson exists to set it up and audit it. That structure suits online delivery, because the question sets and the marking live in a shared document the student keeps rather than in a book that gets left at school.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Annotating a passage together on screen is better than doing it on paper, because both people see the same marks and the annotated text is saved. Directed writing is drafted live in the shared page and edited in front of the student, which is the fastest way to show how a response gains a mark rather than being told that it would.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: The speaking component is the strongest case for live video in the whole subject list: a scheduled conversation with targeted correction is almost impossible to arrange otherwise and impossible to replicate with a recording. Listening practice also works well, since audio is delivered cleanly and can be replayed at the exact point of confusion.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455, Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagrams are the marks, and drawing them live while the student narrates the mechanism is more effective than either reading them or copying them. Data-response work uses the shared page well, with the stimulus and the answer side by side so the tutor can point at the line of data a claim should have come from.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450, Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward planning, and planning is visible on a shared page in a way it never is in a notebook. The evaluative command terms get taught by rewriting the student's own six-line answers in front of them, which is the single most useful thing a screen does in this subject.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: The one subject where the medium is an outright advantage: code is written, run and broken in a shared editor, and the pseudocode conventions the written paper expects can be practised side by side with working Python so the student sees exactly where the two differ.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654, 0653)
subjects.description: The route many east-coast students take when three separate sciences will not fit the timetable. Remotely, the useful work is teaching the student to notice which discipline a question has moved into, because most lost marks here come from answering a chemistry question in physics register rather than from not knowing the content.

fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Online delivery makes distance irrelevant and makes two other things matter instead: a connection that holds for an hour and a room where nobody interrupts. The notes below are about those two, community by community, because they are the practical variables a Fujairah household controls.

regions.name: Fujairah city
regions.note: Fixed-line broadband is widely available and rarely the limiting factor here. The real constraint is household noise in the early evening, so the useful question is which room has a door and whether the session can be held there consistently rather than wherever is free that night.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Residential and well served for connectivity, with the practical issue being shared bandwidth: a lesson competing with streaming in two other rooms degrades audio before it degrades video, and audio is the part that matters. Agreeing that the hour is a low-traffic hour costs nothing and fixes most complaints.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Households here often run more than one school timetable, which means two children may need the same quiet room on the same evening. Consecutive slots work better than parallel ones on separate devices, since parallel sessions in one house compete for both bandwidth and quiet.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Coastal and well connected, with a mobile fallback that is usually strong enough to finish a lesson if the fixed line drops. Worth testing the tether before it is needed rather than during a session, because the two minutes spent working it out mid-lesson always come out of the teaching.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: Quieter households and fewer competing evening commitments, which tends to make the weekly slot easier to protect. Where the home has a single shared study area, a headset with a microphone is the cheapest improvement available: it fixes echo, cuts background noise and makes an hour markedly less tiring.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: The community where online delivery changes the subject list rather than just the convenience, because the nearest in-person specialist is a long drive in any direction. Connectivity is generally adequate for one-to-one video; the sensible precaution is a tested mobile fallback given the distance to any alternative.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Highway villages where the school journey is already long, so energy rather than bandwidth is the binding constraint. A fifty-minute session with a marked set to follow usually works better here than a full hour, and the plan should be written that way rather than defaulting to the longer slot.

regions.name: Masafi
regions.note: Inland at the mountain pass, with some students attending school in another emirate and therefore working to different term dates. For a video lesson the terrain matters less than it feels like it should; what matters is confirming that the household's upload speed holds, since upload is what carries the student's camera and handwriting.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah city and the east coast

fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways the live format gets used, distinguished by what the hour is for rather than by price. The format should follow the diagnosis: a student who cannot do the topic and a student who cannot write the answer need different hours.

modes.title: Weekly teaching slot
modes.description: A scheduled hour with the same tutor, working through the specification in order on a shared page the student keeps. Handwritten working appears live, the question set for the week is issued in the same document, and last week's set is marked at the start of the next session so nothing is ever reviewed from memory.

modes.title: Supervised paper sittings
modes.description: A full past paper attempted to time with the camera on and the tutor present but silent, then marked against the published criteria. It is the closest thing to exam conditions a household can arrange, and it produces the only data that reliably shows whether a timing problem is real or imagined.

modes.title: Short targeted sessions
modes.description: Twenty-five to thirty minutes on a single skill, used where a weekly hour is too long for the student or the problem is narrow. It suits younger students, late-evening slots after a long school journey, and the final weeks before a series when the work is error-specific rather than topic-based.

sections.heading: The four products sold as online IGCSE tuition
paragraphs: Before comparing prices it is worth separating the products, because they are not variants of one thing. A recorded video course is a library of explanations with quizzes attached. A large live group class is a scheduled lecture, usually with a chat box and a presenter who cannot see thirty faces. A small group class is a class, with the pace set by the median student. A marketplace hour is one-to-one teaching bought singly, often from a different person each time. A matched one-to-one arrangement is the same specialist weekly, holding a written record of what your child specifically keeps getting wrong.

Each is the right answer for somebody. For a disciplined student revising subjects they already understand, a recorded course is unbeatable on cost and is available at hours when no tutor is. For a student who wants structure and company and is broadly on track, a small group class delivers both and spreads the hourly cost. For a one-off problem in a single topic, a marketplace hour is efficient and cheap. The format that costs the most and delivers the least is a recorded subscription bought for a student who is stuck, because nothing in it notices that they are.

The dividing line across all four is diagnosis. Only a format in which somebody reads your child's own written answers week after week can tell you that the marks are going to unshown working in question six, or that command terms are being misread, or that the content is fine and the timing is not. That information is the thing a parent is actually buying, and the table below is organised around which formats can produce it rather than around the headline rate.

One figure for context. Published market bands put a qualified online subject tutor in the UAE at roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour, with budget and university-student online rates from around AED 45 and specialists above AED 200. Recorded courses and large group classes sit well below all of that per hour of content, which is exactly why the comparison has to be about what each format does rather than what it costs.

sections.heading: What a live one-to-one hour actually contains
paragraphs: Parents who have never watched an online lesson imagine a video call with a person talking, which is a reasonable fear because plenty of online tutoring is exactly that. A lesson built properly has a shape, and the shape is visible in the shared document afterwards, which is the easiest way for a parent to check what they bought. The first ten minutes are the previous week's marked set: not a chat about how it went, but the specific questions that lost marks, with the mark-scheme point named against each.

The middle thirty minutes are teaching, and the teaching is written rather than spoken. A tutor working on a graphics tablet produces handwritten working that appears line by line in the student's view, so a method is built in front of them at the speed they can follow rather than revealed complete. The student writes too, in the same document or on paper held to the camera, because a tutor who never sees the student's own handwriting is guessing about where the method breaks.

The final fifteen minutes are the student working while the tutor watches and says as little as possible. This is the segment most online lessons skip and the one that carries the most information, because what a student does when stuck is diagnostic in a way that a correct answer never is. Do they reread the question, check units, write anything at all, or freeze? The set for the following week comes out of what happens in those fifteen minutes.

Then the record. Within a day the session produces written notes, the set that was issued, and the marks from the previous set with each loss attributed. Over five weeks that record becomes the only honest answer to whether the plan is working, because a specific error has either stopped appearing in the student's own written work or it has not. A parent can read that pattern without knowing any chemistry.

sections.heading: Writing mathematics and chemistry on a screen
paragraphs: The commonest objection to online tuition in these subjects is that you cannot write on a screen. You can, and the quality of the writing is the single biggest difference between a good online tutor and a poor one. A tutor using a graphics tablet writes as naturally as on paper, in colour, with the previous three lines still visible, and the page persists after the lesson instead of being wiped. For a method with eight steps, that persistence is a genuine advantage over a physical whiteboard.

What does not work is a tutor typing mathematics into a chat window, or talking through a method while the student takes it on trust. Nor does a tutor sharing a slide deck they prepared for somebody else. The test a parent can apply without understanding the subject is simple: open the shared document after the lesson and look for handwriting. If the page is empty, or it is a document the tutor brought in finished form, nothing was built with your child in it.

The student's side matters just as much. IGCSE mathematics and science papers are marked on written working, and method marks are thrown away by students who do arithmetic in their heads. A tutor who cannot see the student's page cannot catch that habit. The practical arrangements that work are the student writing directly into the shared document, or writing on paper with a second camera angle, or photographing the page into the document at the end of each segment so the tutor marks what was actually written.

For chemistry specifically there is a second benefit. Reaction pathways, mole calculations and balanced equations all reward being written out repeatedly in the same place with corrections visible, and a shared page accumulates that history across a term. A student revising in April can scroll to the week in November when the mole triangle finally made sense, which is not something a notebook does reliably and not something a recorded course offers at all.

sections.heading: Practical science when nobody is in the laboratory
paragraphs: This is the question every science parent asks, and it has a precise answer that depends on which paper the school entered. Cambridge offers two routes for assessing practical skills in its IGCSE sciences: a practical test, sat with apparatus, and an alternative-to-practical written paper that tests the same skills on paper. Schools choose which to enter, and the choice is not always visible to parents until the statement of entry arrives. A tutor who does not ask which one is being sat is planning in the dark.

Where the school has entered the alternative-to-practical route, the entire assessment is written, and online delivery is not a compromise at all. The skills examined are reading a scale, tabulating results, plotting and interpreting a graph, identifying a variable that should have been controlled, spotting the anomalous reading, and describing an improvement to a method. Every one of those is taught better on a shared page with a real data set in front of both people than it is in a room with a whiteboard.

Where the school has entered a practical test, the apparatus work happens in school and the tutor's job changes rather than disappears. Remote teaching covers method design, the language of observation, measurement precision and the write-up conventions the mark scheme rewards, while the school's laboratory covers the handling. That division is honest and it is what most tutoring, remote or not, has always done, since no tutor is running a titration in a family's kitchen either.

Pearson's international GCSE sciences take a different approach again, assessing practical skills through the written papers rather than through a separate practical test, so the specification should be checked rather than assumed from habit. In all cases confirm the route with the school and verify the current arrangements on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com, which publish the live documents and supersede any restatement elsewhere, including this one.

sections.heading: Sitting a timed past paper under video supervision
paragraphs: Most students have never sat a past paper under genuine exam conditions before the real thing, which is why timing problems appear for the first time in the room that matters. A supervised sitting over video solves it cheaply. The paper is opened at an agreed moment, the camera stays on, the tutor is present and says nothing, and the clock runs to the real duration. No questions are answered during the attempt, which is the part students dislike and the part that makes the data worth having.

Afterwards the student marks their own script against the published criteria first, and the tutor audits that marking rather than redoing it. This order matters more than it sounds. A student who has marked their own paper against the criteria has read the examiner's expectations in their own handwriting, which teaches more about how marks are awarded than any amount of being told. The tutor's audit then catches the places where the student was generous to themselves, which is itself diagnostic.

The output is marks per section rather than a total. A total tells a family a grade they already feared; marks per section tell them that the first four questions were fine, question seven lost six marks to unshown working, and the last two questions were never attempted because twelve minutes were spent on a diagram. Those are three different problems with three different fixes, and only one of them is about knowing the subject.

Scheduling matters too. Supervised sittings belong between mock weeks rather than on top of them, and two per subject across the final two months is usually enough to settle the timing question. A student who has sat the paper to time twice and read their own marking knows what the first ten minutes of the real paper will be spent on, which is the most useful thing anybody can carry into an examination hall.

sections.heading: The connection, the equipment and the room
paragraphs: The technical requirements for one-to-one video tuition are modest and the failures are nearly always the same four things: no headset, so the room echoes and both people tire; a phone instead of a laptop, so the shared page is unreadable; a shared space, so the hour is interrupted; and untested upload bandwidth, because upload carries the student's camera and handwriting while everyone only ever tests download. None of those needs money to fix, and all of them are better fixed before the first lesson than during it.

Across Fujairah, fixed-line broadband is generally adequate for a one-to-one video lesson, and a mobile tether is a reasonable fallback worth testing in advance rather than discovering mid-session. The practical variable in most households is not the line but what else is using it. A lesson competing with two streams elsewhere in the house loses audio quality before it loses video, and audio is the part that carries the teaching. Agreeing that the lesson hour is a low-traffic hour costs nothing.

The room is the underrated one. An hour in a kitchen with people moving through it produces a student who is present and not working, which looks identical to a student who is struggling with the subject. A door, a table at the right height, a light source that is not behind the screen, and a phone left in another room are worth more to the quality of the hour than any upgrade to the equipment. Families who set this up once rarely revisit it; families who improvise each week complain about online tuition in general.

When something does fail, the protocol should be agreed rather than improvised. If a connection drops for under five minutes the lesson resumes and overruns; beyond that the session is rescheduled rather than salvaged, because fifteen minutes of a broken link teaches nothing and costs the student their concentration. The shared page means nothing is lost either way: the work up to the drop is still on it, and the next session picks up from the visible line.

sections.heading: Attention arithmetic against a class and a group
paragraphs: A school class is a good place to learn and a poor place to be diagnosed. In a class of twenty-five, a teacher who gave every student equal individual attention would manage a little over two minutes each per hour, and no competent teacher distributes it that way: the time goes where the need is loudest, which is not always where it is greatest. A quiet student with a specific gap can go a term without anybody reading their working closely. That is not a criticism of schools; it is arithmetic.

A small online group of six changes the number without changing the kind. The pace is set by the median student, the questions asked are the ones somebody was confident enough to ask, and the written work marked is usually marked collectively. For a student who is on track it is good value and genuinely useful. For a student who is stuck, the same structural problem applies as in a class, just with fewer people in it.

One-to-one is bought for the fifteen minutes in every hour where somebody watches your child work and says nothing. That is where the diagnosis lives, and it cannot be delivered to two students at once because it requires undivided attention on one person's process. Everything else in a one-to-one lesson, including the teaching, is available more cheaply elsewhere. The honest pitch for the format is narrow and it is that.

Which means the sensible purchase for most families is not one format but a sequence. A recorded course or a group class for breadth and structure, one-to-one for the specific thing that is not moving, and a supervised paper sitting to check the timing. Any tutoring page that tells a parent one-to-one is the answer to every question is selling rather than advising, and a family that has already tried a cheaper format and seen it work does not need persuading otherwise.
