fujairah/igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: A near-me search rarely specifies the tier, and the tier is what decides whether a local tutor can help at all. The four structures below cover almost every IGCSE enquiry from the east coast, and each one has a different local availability picture attached.

programmes.name: IGCSE Core tier and Pearson Foundation
programmes.description: The lower of the two tiers, covering less of the specification and reaching a restricted grade range. It is the right entry for a student who needs a secure pass and the confidence that comes with it, and the wrong entry for one aiming at a sixth-form prerequisite. Tutoring at this tier is mostly foundation work: number, algebraic basics and the structure of a written answer, done patiently and repeatedly.
programmes.countryNote: Core-tier help is the easiest thing to find locally on the east coast, because the content sits within the range of a competent generalist. If your child is entered at Core and needs confidence rather than specialism, a nearby tutor or the school's own clinic is often the better and cheaper answer, and this page would rather say so than sell past it.

programmes.name: IGCSE Extended tier and Pearson Higher
programmes.description: The full specification and the full grade range, with papers that reward multi-step reasoning and penalise unshown working. This is where the local pool thins sharply, because teaching Extended content well requires somebody who knows the papers rather than somebody who knows the subject. The gap between those two is invisible in a first conversation and obvious by the third mock.
programmes.countryNote: Extended tier is the commonest reason a Fujairah family ends up looking beyond the emirate. A parent can usually tell within two sessions: a tutor who knows the tier talks about which paper a topic appears on and how many marks it carries, while a tutor who does not talks about the topic in general terms and sets textbook exercises.

programmes.name: Co-ordinated and Double Award Sciences
programmes.description: The route taken when three separate sciences will not fit a timetable, with content trimmed from biology, chemistry and physics and examined across shared papers. It sounds easier than three sciences and frequently is not, because one paper moves between three sets of conventions and students lose marks switching register rather than through ignorance.
programmes.countryNote: This is the science route many east-coast students sit, and it is also the one local tutors are least likely to have taught, since most specialists teach one discipline. A chemistry specialist tutoring a double-award student needs to know which chemistry the award actually includes, and that is a syllabus question rather than a subject one.

programmes.name: Single-subject and private candidate entry
programmes.description: Entering one subject through an approved exam centre without being taught it in school, used for a subject the school cannot staff, for a resit, or for a first language the school does not examine. The centre manages the entry and the family manages the teaching, which makes the tutor the only person who sees the whole subject rather than one class of it.
programmes.countryNote: Relatively common on this coast precisely because the local subject list is short. The practical trap is exam-day logistics: the nearest centre accepting that syllabus may be in Sharjah or Dubai, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Confirm the centre and the zone before paying for any teaching.

fujairah/igcse-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: The note against each subject is about local supply: whether a small east-coast school and the market around it can usually cover it, and what happens when they cannot. This is the part a near-me search cannot tell you and the part that decides whether distance matters for your child.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The one subject where local supply is usually adequate at Core tier and often adequate at Extended. If your child needs mathematics help and nothing else, start with what is nearby and with the school's own clinic. The exception is a student targeting a high grade, where paper-level knowledge matters more than general competence.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taught to small cohorts where it is taught at all, and rarely covered by the local market. Calculus, vectors and matrices a year early put it outside the range of a generalist tutor. This is the clearest case on the whole list where a specialist on video beats anybody within driving distance.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Local supply is patchy and skewed towards mechanics, because that is what most generalists are comfortable with. Electricity and electromagnetism, which carry a disproportionate share of lost marks, are the topics where a non-specialist tends to explain the textbook back rather than rebuild the reasoning.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Reasonably well covered for Core content, thinner at Extended where moles calculations and organic pathways separate grades. Worth asking any local tutor directly which practical route the school entered, because a tutor who has not thought about that question has not planned for the paper your child will sit.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The most widely available of the three sciences locally, and the one where availability matters least, because the work is retrieval and long-answer discipline done mostly between sessions. A competent nearby tutor who sets and marks properly will do as well here as a distant specialist.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Widely available in form and rarely available in substance, because teaching it well means marking against the published criteria rather than correcting grammar. Ask to see a piece of written feedback before booking: the difference between the two approaches is visible in one page.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Good local availability for reading and writing, much thinner for the speaking component, which needs a scheduled conversation partner who corrects specific things and records what was corrected. That component is the one most commonly underprepared and the one video handles best.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 and 0450)
subjects.description: Frequently taught by one teacher at a small school and rarely represented in the local tutoring market at all. Both subjects are decided by a narrow set of techniques, diagram discipline in economics and evaluative command terms in business, which makes a few well-targeted sessions unusually effective wherever they come from.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Almost never covered by the local market, and the subject where a confident programmer can still lose heavily on the written paper because the pseudocode conventions are unfamiliar. A specialist working in a shared editor over video is the standard arrangement for this subject on the east coast.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508) and Arabic Foreign Language (Cambridge 0544)
subjects.description: Arabic teaching is well supplied locally in general terms, but the two Cambridge routes are not interchangeable and the reading demand differs sharply between them. Confirm which syllabus your child is entered for before booking anybody, nearby or otherwise, because a strong Arabic teacher is not automatically a 0508 teacher.

fujairah/igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: What a near-me search can actually offer differs community by community, and the difference is supply rather than connectivity. The notes below describe what is realistically within reach of each place and where families there tend to end up looking.

regions.name: Fujairah city
regions.note: The only community in the emirate where a near-me search returns a usable list, since the schools and the market around them are concentrated here. Families in the city should genuinely try local first for mainstream subjects at Core tier before looking further, because the cost and the convenience both favour it.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Close enough to the city that local options are reachable without a major journey, which makes the real question timing rather than distance. A session in the city means leaving home again after the bus and a meal, and the families who sustain that for a whole term are fewer than the ones who plan to.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Within reach of the city but typically running two school timetables in one household, which doubles the logistics of any in-person arrangement. Where two children both need help, the journey arithmetic changes faster than the hourly rate does, and a near-me result that works for one child rarely works for both.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: On the coastal strip with good access to the city and to the Sharjah road, which means local options exist and out-of-emirate freelancers will quote. Those quotes carry travel inside them, usually as a two-hour minimum or weekend-only availability, so compare on cost per teaching hour rather than on the headline rate.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: A quieter pocket where the nearest tuition option is a deliberate trip rather than a detour. The pattern here is two subjects compressed into one evening journey, which suits revision and suits a foundation rebuild poorly, since the second subject gets whatever energy the first one left.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: The thinnest near-me result in the emirate: roughly three quarters of an hour to Fujairah city and considerably more to anything in Sharjah. Families here are the ones for whom video delivery changes the subject list available rather than merely the convenience of getting to it.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Highway villages with no local cluster of their own, served by the road to the city in one direction and to Dibba in the other. Any in-person arrangement here means a journey on both sides of the lesson, which is the clearest case for an evening slot at home on video.

regions.name: Masafi
regions.note: At the mountain pass and closer to the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah road network than to Fujairah city, so a near-me search here returns results in a different emirate. Students from Masafi sometimes attend school in another emirate too, which means term dates and mock weeks need confirming from the school itself.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah city and the east coast
schoolClusters.note: The private schools inside the emirate, and the reason the local tutoring market is the size it is. Small cohorts mean short subject lists, and short subject lists are what a near-me search is really measuring. Students we support attend schools in this group; none is a partner, client or sponsor of IB Gram.
schools: Our Own English High School, Fujairah

schoolClusters.note: Roughly ninety minutes from Fujairah city and considerably more from Dibba, which is the distance a near-me search is quietly asking families to drive. Some Masafi and Dibba students attend school in this group, under a different regulator and sometimes on different term dates.
schools: Scholars Indian School, Ras Al Khaimah

fujairah/igcse-tutor-near-me.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as context for local supply and distance on the east coast. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement arrangement with any of them.
fujairah/igcse-tutor-near-me.modesIntro: Three ways of arranging help once distance stops being the organising question. Each is defined by when it happens rather than by where, because the clock is the constraint a Fujairah household genuinely cannot negotiate.

modes.title: Late-afternoon weekday slot
modes.description: The standard arrangement, set after the school bus and a meal with deliberate margin so that a normal delay does not eat into the hour. The slot is fixed for the whole block rather than negotiated weekly, because a time that moves twice is a time that gets missed, and a missed session is a meaningful fraction of a twelve-week plan.
bullets: Start time chosen thirty minutes later than seems necessary
Same weekday every week on Gulf Standard Time
Prayer-time collisions checked once at the start of the block, not weekly
Agreed in advance which two weeks of the block will be skipped

modes.title: Weekend block for longer journeys
modes.description: Two consecutive sessions on a Saturday morning, which suits households in Qidfa, Mirbah and Dibba where the weekday evening is already spent on travel and school work. It trades frequency for length, so it works better for revision and whole-paper practice than for rebuilding a foundation from the beginning.
bullets: Two sessions back to back rather than one long sitting
Suits revision and paper practice more than foundation repair
Leaves the weekday evenings for the set issued at the end of the block
Reviewed after a month against the marked sets, as any plan is

modes.title: Paired sibling slots
modes.description: Consecutive hours for two children in one household, which removes the duplicated logistics that make in-person arrangements expensive for Merashid and Al Gurfa families. One quiet room is prepared once, one evening is committed, and both written records are reviewed by the same parent at the same points.
bullets: Consecutive slots on one evening, one prepared room
Separate tutors where the subjects or stages differ
Separate written records, reviewed together
Checked after a month to confirm neither plan is being starved

sections.heading: The distance arithmetic, community by community
paragraphs: A near-me result is only as useful as the journey behind it, and on the east coast those journeys vary from ten minutes to the best part of two hours. The table below gives approximate one-way driving times from eight Fujairah communities to the three in-person options a family is likely to be offered: something in Fujairah city, something in Kalba or Khor Fakkan, and something in Sharjah. Times are approximate and depend on the road and the hour, so treat them as planning figures rather than promises.

Read the last column rather than the first three. A lesson has a journey on both sides of it, and on a school night that round trip competes with homework, a meal and sleep. For a family in the city centre the round trip is fifteen minutes and barely registers. For a family in Dibba it is an hour and a half of driving around a one-hour lesson, which is not a sustainable weekly commitment for anybody and is the reason those households either go without or go online.

The same arithmetic applies in reverse to a tutor coming to you, which is what most near-me searches are actually hoping for. A tutor based in Sharjah teaching a two-hour lesson in Fujairah city is committed for roughly five hours door to door. That time appears in the rate, in a two-hour minimum, in weekend-only availability, or in a cancellation when something goes wrong on the road. Published market bands put visiting one-to-one tuition in the UAE at roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online.

None of which makes the near option wrong. For a Fujairah city family needing mainstream mathematics at Core tier, the nearest competent tutor is probably the best purchase available and this page would rather say so than argue past it. The arithmetic matters for the other cases: the Extended-tier student, the subject nobody local teaches, and the household where the journey makes a weekly commitment impossible to keep for a full term.

sections.heading: Seven things parents want, scored against distance
paragraphs: Near-me searches bundle several different wishes into one word, and separating them is what makes the decision tractable. A parent typing that phrase usually wants some combination of: the right subject at the right tier, somebody who knows the exact syllabus the school entered, a weekly slot that actually happens, an adult physically present with a younger child, written feedback on their own child's work, cover when the tutor is unwell, and a sensible cost per teaching hour. Proximity delivers one of those outright and is neutral or unhelpful on the rest.

The one it delivers is physical presence, and it is not a small thing. A twelve-year-old who drifts every four minutes needs somebody in the room, and no amount of shared-screen technology substitutes for an adult closing a book and pointing at a page. Families with a younger child who genuinely cannot hold attention for fifty minutes should weight that heavily, pay the visiting rate, and treat this page's conclusion as not applying to them.

Where proximity is actively unhelpful is subject match. The pool within thirty minutes of Al Gurfa consists of whoever lives within thirty minutes of Al Gurfa, and for Additional Mathematics 0606 or Cambridge 0478 Computer Science that pool is frequently empty. A family that insists on local for those subjects is choosing between a generalist teaching above their range and nothing, which is a worse choice than the one video offers. Reliability runs the same way: a tutor crossing the mountains has weather, traffic and fuel between them and your child.

Cost per teaching hour is the quietest of the seven and often the largest. Visiting rates absorb travel, which is why the published bands sit higher than online bands, and a two-hour minimum turns a one-hour need into a two-hour invoice. A family comparing AED 250 locally with AED 250 online is not comparing like with like, because one of those numbers has an hour and a half of driving folded into it and the other does not.

sections.heading: The weekday clock: bus, meal, prayer times and the earliest viable start
paragraphs: The constraint that breaks more tuition plans on the east coast than money or distance is the clock. Parents pick a start time based on when school finishes, then discover that school finishing and a child being ready to work are separated by a bus route, a journey, a meal and a change of clothes. A slot set thirty minutes too early does not fail immediately. It fails in week four, when the accumulated lateness has turned a fifty-minute lesson into a thirty-five-minute one and nobody has said anything.

The arithmetic is worth doing once, properly, before the block starts. Take the school's actual finish time, add the bus route rather than the direct drive, add twenty minutes for a meal and a pause, and set the slot after that. For most Fujairah communities this lands the first genuinely viable weekday start later in the afternoon than parents expect. The cost of getting this right is nothing; the cost of getting it wrong is a plan that quietly degrades.

Prayer times are the second variable and they move through the year, which is the part that catches families out. A slot that sits comfortably before Maghrib in December collides with it in June, and a collision handled by shortening the lesson every week is a plan losing ten minutes a session. The practical approach is to check the collision once at the start of a block, choose a slot that holds across the whole period, and make one deliberate change for Ramadan rather than a weekly negotiation.

Older students are a different case and the honest advice differs. A Year 11 student revising until late is often better served by a session after Iftar during Ramadan, or by a later evening slot year-round, than by a mid-afternoon hour when they are still recovering from the school day. The table below gives planning figures by community; the real numbers come from your own school's finish time and your own bus route, and they are worth writing down before any slot is agreed.

sections.heading: Small cohorts and the subjects nobody local teaches
paragraphs: The real reason a near-me search disappoints on the east coast is not that tutors are scarce in general. It is that the subjects Fujairah families most often need help with are the ones the local market never developed, because the schools themselves teach them to a handful of students. A cohort of three in Additional Mathematics does not generate a local tutoring market in Additional Mathematics. Neither does a single class of Computer Science, or an Economics set taught by the one teacher who also carries Business Studies.

This has a second effect that families notice before they can name it. When a subject is taught to very few students, a child who drifts has fewer routes back inside school hours: no second set to join, no departmental colleague running a parallel clinic, and a teacher whose free periods are already committed. The school is not failing; it is staffed in proportion to its size. But it does mean that the support a Dubai family would find within the school has to come from outside it here.

Where a specialist exists but not within driving distance, the honest arrangement is the one this page is about: one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time so the hour sits in a Fujairah evening. Where no specialist exists on the platform at all for a given syllabus code and tier, a family should be told that rather than matched to the nearest adjacent subject. A chemistry specialist is not a computer science tutor, and discovering that in week six costs a term.

There is a planning conclusion in this for Year 9 families. If a subject choice depends on a subject the school teaches to very few students, find out in Year 9 how it will be supported rather than in Year 11 when the mock arrives. Sometimes the answer changes the choice, and that is a better outcome than two years of quiet struggle followed by an expensive rescue.
bullets: Small cohorts mean no local market in the subjects that need one most
Fewer routes back inside school when a student drifts in a single-set subject
A specialist on video is matched to the code, not to the drive
Ask in Year 9 how a thinly staffed subject will be supported

sections.heading: Verifying a tutor you found nearby
paragraphs: A near-me result is a name and a phone number, which is less information than a parent needs before letting somebody teach their child. The verification questions are the same whether the tutor is ten minutes away or on a screen, and a legitimate tutor answers all of them without hesitation. The first is the permit: private tutoring in the UAE runs on a private tuition work permit administered through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Ask whether they hold it.

The second question is about the specification. Which syllabus codes have they taught, for how long, and which tier? A tutor who answers with a subject name rather than a code has probably not planned against a paper, and the difference shows up by the third session. The third question is for a sample of written feedback from another student with the name removed. One page tells you whether marking means correcting mistakes or naming the criterion that was missed, and those are different jobs.

The fourth is awkward and worth asking anyway: is the tutor currently teaching at your child's own school? Press reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules describes school staff being barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a comparable restriction. Anybody offering your child's own class teacher privately is offering an arrangement that needs examining rather than a shortcut.

Two things nobody can honestly offer you, near or far. No tutor or platform is approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and a claim of that kind on any page is a reason to look elsewhere rather than a reassurance. And no tutor can promise a grade. What a good one can promise is that the mark your child is already capable of appears on the paper, which is a smaller claim and a far more useful one.
bullets: Ask about the MoHRE private tuition work permit; it is free and valid two years
Ask for syllabus codes and tiers taught, not subject names
Ask for one page of anonymised written feedback before booking
Treat any claim of regulator approval as a warning rather than a credential

sections.heading: Why Gulf Standard Time matters more than a postcode
paragraphs: Once teaching happens over video, the only geographical fact left that affects a lesson is the clock. Gulf Standard Time is UTC+4, and a tutor teaching into it has to be awake, prepared and unhurried at a time that suits a Fujairah evening rather than their own convenience. That is a scheduling commitment, and it is the question a parent should ask instead of asking where the tutor lives.

It matters because the alternative is familiar to anyone who has tried a marketplace. A slot offered at a time that works for the tutor's time zone drifts, gets rescheduled, or quietly becomes the last appointment of somebody's long day. A slot that is scheduled deliberately into the UAE evening and held there for a whole block behaves completely differently, and the difference shows up as sessions that happen rather than sessions that are moved.

Several providers competing for these searches route UAE parents to non-UAE telephone numbers without stating where the teaching happens or in which time zone it is scheduled, and one shows a Dubai footer address on a page about a different emirate. Both are reasonable grounds for suspicion. The questions are simple and a straight answer is quick: which time zone is my child's lesson scheduled in, and is there a UAE office? IB Gram's answers are UTC+4 and no.

The practical consequence for a Fujairah family is that the useful filter is not distance but availability inside a specific window. A specialist who can teach at five in the afternoon Gulf Standard Time every Tuesday for twelve weeks is more valuable than a nearer generalist who can offer alternating Saturdays, because consistency is what makes a plan work. That is the trade this page is really describing, and it is a better trade than the map suggests.

sections.heading: What a trial lesson has to produce
paragraphs: A trial lesson is the only part of this decision that generates real evidence, and most of them are wasted because they are run as demonstrations rather than diagnostics. A demonstration shows a tutor being impressive for forty-five minutes. A diagnostic puts the student in front of a timed question, watches what happens when they get stuck, checks two or three skills the specification assumes, and reads a marked script. The difference is what comes out at the end.

What should come out is a written statement, and a parent should expect it rather than hope for it. It names the syllabus code and tier it is planning against. It says which topics are secure and which are not. It says whether the losses are content, technique or timing, because those three need different numbers of weeks and buying the wrong one is the commonest waste of money in this market. And it gives a realistic number of weeks, with what happens if that number is not available.

The condition on the trial should also be stated clearly, since the word free is used loosely across this market. Here it is one trial lesson per family, 45 minutes, with no card details required and no obligation afterwards. If a provider offers a free trial and then asks for payment details before it, or counts it against a package you have not yet agreed to, that is a condition that belongs on the same screen as the offer rather than in a later conversation.

The last thing a trial should be able to do is conclude against itself. Sometimes the honest outcome is that the school's own clinic used properly for a term is the right answer, or that a nearby tutor at Core tier is better value than anything on this page, or that the problem is a timetable decision for the school rather than an academic one. A diagnostic that can only ever recommend buying lessons is a sales call with a worksheet attached, and it is worth recognising one before it costs you a term.
bullets: Expect a written statement, not an impression, at the end of the session
Content, technique and timing need different numbers of weeks
One trial per family, 45 minutes, no card details, no obligation
A diagnostic that cannot recommend against tuition is not a diagnostic

process.title: Do the clock arithmetic first
process.description: Take the school's actual finish time, add the bus route rather than the direct drive, add twenty minutes for a meal, and write down the earliest time your child can genuinely start working. Check once whether that time collides with prayer times across the whole block. This single calculation protects more plans than any other decision in the process.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, the tier and the series
process.description: Three facts that a near-me search cannot supply and that decide whether local help is even possible. They sit on the option booklet or the statement of entry. With them a match takes one conversation, and for a subject the local market never developed they are the only filter that changes the answer.

process.title: Try local first where local is enough
process.description: For mainstream mathematics or biology at Core tier, the school's own clinic and the nearest competent tutor are usually the better purchase on cost and convenience, and this page recommends starting there. Come back to a specialist if the marks do not move after a term, or if the subject is one nobody nearby teaches.

process.title: Take the 45-minute diagnostic
process.description: One trial lesson per family, no card details required. Your child attempts a timed question while the tutor watches the process, and the session ends in a written statement naming the code, the tier, which topics are secure and whether the losses are content, technique or timing. If a nearby option would serve better, it says so.

process.title: Fix one slot and hold it for the block
process.description: Same weekday, same time on Gulf Standard Time, with margin built in and two skip weeks agreed before the block starts. Consistency does more for a plan than any individual lesson, and the families whose plans survive a whole term are the ones who treat the slot as fixed rather than movable.

whyPoints.title: Matched by code, not by distance
whyPoints.description: The filter applied is the syllabus code and tier your child is entered for, with no geographical constraint, which is the only way a Dibba family gets an Additional Mathematics 0606 specialist. For subjects the local market never developed, this is the difference between a specialist and a generalist working above their range.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled into the Fujairah evening
whyPoints.description: Lessons are set on Gulf Standard Time, UTC+4, after the bus and a meal, with margin so a normal delay does not eat the hour. The slot is held for the whole block rather than renegotiated weekly, because consistency is what makes a twelve-week plan actually deliver twelve sessions.

whyPoints.title: The local option recommended where it is better
whyPoints.description: This page says plainly that for mainstream subjects at Core tier a nearby tutor or the school's own clinic is usually the better purchase. A tutoring page that recommends itself for every situation is less useful than one that marks out where it does not apply, and families can tell the difference.

whyPoints.title: Real distance figures, not vague convenience claims
whyPoints.description: Approximate drive times from eight communities to three destinations, with the round trip around a one-hour lesson stated. Visiting rates are given as published market bands with the travel noted. A parent can check every one of those numbers against their own route, which is the point of publishing them.

whyPoints.title: Verification questions you can use anywhere
whyPoints.description: The permit, the syllabus codes, a page of anonymised written feedback, and whether the tutor teaches at your child's own school. Those four questions work on a local tutor and on us equally, and a provider that would rather you did not ask them is telling you something.

whyPoints.title: No claims nobody can support
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no accreditation, no UAE office, no grade promises, and no home visits anywhere in the UAE. Each of those is something a competing page in this market asserts, and declining to assert them is the only honest position available to anybody in this business.

faqs.question: Why does searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in Fujairah return so little?
faqs.answer: Because a proximity search ranks what exists nearby, and the tutoring market around a small private-school set is correspondingly small. Fujairah sits behind the Hajar mountains with far fewer private schools than Dubai, and the subjects east-coast families most need help with are the ones local schools teach to a handful of students, so no local market in them ever developed. The result is a short list rather than a broken search. The practical response is to work out which parts of what you want actually depend on distance.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tuition centre in Fujairah city at all?
faqs.answer: Fujairah city is where the emirate's private schools and the market around them are concentrated, so it is the one community where a proximity search returns a usable list, and group options for mainstream subjects are the likeliest thing to find. What a centre generally cannot carry is a niche subject or Extended-tier teaching in a subject it has only staffed at Core, because that depends on who it can employ locally. Ask any centre which syllabus codes and tiers it teaches rather than which subjects it offers.

faqs.question: How far is the nearest tuition option from Dibba Al-Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Roughly three quarters of an hour by road to Fujairah city, and two hours or more to anything in Sharjah. Around a one-hour lesson that is about an hour and a half of driving on a school night, which almost no family sustains for a full term, and which is why Dibba households are the clearest case where video delivery changes the subject list available rather than just the convenience. Treat these as planning figures and check them against your own route.

faqs.question: What does living close to a tutor actually buy my child?
faqs.answer: One thing outright: an adult physically present in the room, which genuinely matters for a younger student who needs redirecting every few minutes and for whom no shared screen substitutes. It does not buy a better subject match, because the pool near you is whoever lives near you. It does not buy reliability, since a tutor crossing the mountains has weather and traffic in the way. And it usually costs more per teaching hour, because visiting rates have travel folded into them.

faqs.question: What time can a weekday session realistically start in Sakamkam?
faqs.answer: Later than most parents first assume. Take the school's actual finish time, add the bus route rather than the direct drive, which is typically twenty to thirty-five minutes, then add about twenty minutes for a meal and a pause. That usually puts the first genuinely workable start in the late afternoon. A slot set thirty minutes too early does not fail immediately; it fails in week four, when accumulated lateness has turned a fifty-minute lesson into thirty-five and nobody has mentioned it.

faqs.question: Do prayer times affect when tuition can be scheduled on the east coast?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the part that catches families out is that they move through the year. A slot sitting comfortably before Maghrib in December can collide with it in June, and handling that collision by trimming ten minutes off every lesson is a plan quietly losing a session a month. Check the collision once at the start of a block, pick a time that holds across the whole period, and make a single deliberate change for Ramadan rather than renegotiating week by week.

faqs.question: My child's school bus gets home at five. Is that too late for a lesson?
faqs.answer: Not at all, but it does mean the lesson starts later than five. Allow twenty minutes for a meal and a change of clothes, and set the slot with margin so a delayed bus does not eat into the hour. For an older student revising anyway, an early evening slot often works better than an earlier one, because the alternative is an hour spent recovering from the school day. For a younger child, a shorter session at that time usually beats a full hour.

faqs.question: Should I choose a nearby generalist or a specialist who is far away?
faqs.answer: It depends on the tier and the subject. For mainstream mathematics or biology at Core tier, the nearby option is usually the better purchase on cost and convenience, and the school's own clinic is better still. For Extended tier, for Additional Mathematics 0606, for Computer Science 0478 or for anything the local school teaches to very few students, a specialist matched to the syllabus code wins clearly, because the alternative is a generalist working above their range.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is who they say they are before lesson one?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Do they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years. Which syllabus codes and tiers have they taught, and for how long. Can they show one page of anonymised written feedback they gave another student. And are they currently teaching at your child's own school, which carries conduct restrictions worth examining. A legitimate tutor answers all four without hesitation, and the third tells you more than any certificate will.

faqs.question: Are there IGCSE tutors in Khor Fakkan or Kalba?
faqs.answer: Both are within about twenty-five to thirty-five minutes of Fujairah city and have their own schools, so some local provision exists, though the same constraint applies: supply follows the size of the school set. A family in Fujairah city weighing a trip to Kalba should compare the round trip against what the trip actually gains, which is usually availability rather than specialism. Ask specifically about the tier and the syllabus code before committing to a weekly journey in either direction.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to know my child's school to be useful?
faqs.answer: Knowing the school's scheme of work is genuinely useful, because it sets the order your child is meeting the content in and a sensible tutor keeps close to it. Knowing the school socially is not useful at all, and in one respect it is a complication: conduct rules restrict a teacher from privately tutoring students enrolled at their own school. What matters is the syllabus code, the tier and the scheme of work, and all three can be shared in a single message.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same house share one weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Sharing one slot rarely works, because two students at different stages need different hours and one of them ends up watching. Consecutive slots on the same evening work very well: one quiet room prepared once, one evening committed, two separate written records reviewed by the same parent at the same points. Where the subjects or the stages differ, the two hours should be with different tutors, matched separately to each child's syllabus code and tier.

faqs.question: Which time zone do the tutors teach in?
faqs.answer: Lessons are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, UTC+4, so the slot falls in a Fujairah evening rather than at whatever hour suits the tutor's own day. This is worth asking any provider directly, because several competing for these searches route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without saying where the teaching happens, and one shows a Dubai address on a page about a different emirate. A straight answer takes one sentence, and IB Gram holds no UAE office or centre.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a student in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: For a mainstream subject at a common tier, usually within a few days, because the match is to a syllabus code rather than to a location and the pool is not limited by who will drive over the mountains. For a niche subject or an uncommon tier it can take longer, and if nobody teaches that code you should be told so rather than matched to the nearest adjacent subject. A chemistry specialist is not a computer science tutor, and finding that out in week six costs a term.

faqs.question: Is weekend tuition better than a weekday evening on the east coast?
faqs.answer: For households in Dibba, Qidfa and Mirbah, often yes, because the weekday evening is already spent on a long school journey and homework. Two consecutive sessions on a Saturday morning suit revision and whole-paper practice well. They suit rebuilding a foundation less well, because that work needs frequency rather than length. The compromise many families settle on is one weekday slot and one weekend block in the final two months, with the weekend block used for supervised timed papers.

faqs.question: What exactly should I be looking for during a trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Evidence rather than charm. Your child should spend part of the session attempting a timed question unaided while the tutor watches what happens when they get stuck. At the end you should receive something written: the syllabus code and tier being planned against, which topics are secure, whether the losses are content, technique or timing, and a realistic number of weeks. A session that produces only a cheerful verdict that your child will be fine was a demonstration, and you still do not know what you are buying.

fujairah/igcse-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Do the arithmetic, then decide what distance is worth
fujairah/igcse-tutor-near-me.closingBody: The honest conclusion of a near-me search on this coast is split. For mainstream subjects at Core tier, start with the school's own clinic and the nearest competent tutor, because that is cheaper and simpler and this page would rather you knew it. For Extended tier, for the subjects your school teaches to a handful of students, and for households where the round trip makes a weekly commitment impossible to keep, a specialist matched to the syllabus code and scheduled into a Fujairah evening is the better arrangement. One free 45-minute diagnostic, no card details, will tell you in writing which of those two describes your child.

fujairah/merashid.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work on the parts of a course that are assessed but not taught: coursework criteria, independent revision structure, exam technique and the self-managed Diploma core. Each takes one student at a time and works to the school's own internal deadlines.

intro.heading: The taught syllabus is only half of what a Merashid student is assessed on
paragraphs: Merashid sits at the northern edge of Fujairah City, the first district a family reaches coming down the coast road. Children here mostly attend the city's private schools, the run is short by this emirate's standards, and class teaching is generally fine. That is why so many enquiries from this part of town start with a puzzled sentence: the lessons are good, the teacher is good, the homework gets done, and the grade is not where it should be.

The explanation is usually structural rather than academic. A school timetable covers the taught syllabus. It does not, and cannot, cover the parts of an IB Diploma or an IGCSE programme that are assessed but self-managed. The Extended Essay is worked on largely alone, with a supervisor who meets the student a handful of times. The internal assessment is produced outside lessons. Theory of Knowledge has a fraction of the timetable its two assessed components deserve. Independent revision is assumed rather than taught. Exam technique is practised in mocks and rarely analysed.

Added up, that unsupervised portion carries a large share of the final result, and it is where a conscientious student most often loses a grade. They are not failing to learn chemistry. They are managing an Extended Essay with no method for narrowing a research question, revising by rereading notes because nobody showed them anything better, and writing internal assessment evaluations that describe limitations without connecting them to the result. All of those are teachable and almost none of them are taught.

A small-emirate school makes the gap wider. Fujairah's cohorts are small, so a single teacher may carry a subject across several year groups and a Diploma supervisor may be supervising essays in subjects outside their specialism. Nobody is at fault; the arithmetic simply leaves less supervision per student than a large Dubai school can provide. The compensating resource has to come from outside.

There is one more reason this half of the course is neglected: it is invisible until it is late. A content gap shows up in a test within weeks. A badly chosen Extended Essay research question shows up fourteen months later, when the essay is written and the word limit will not accommodate the argument. A weak revision method shows up on results day. Each of those is cheap to fix early and almost impossible to fix at the point the family finds out, which is why the useful conversation about support happens in September rather than in the spring term.

IB Gram works on that half. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one to one, over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India. For a Merashid family the point is not convenience; it is that the specialist supporting an Extended Essay in economics should be an economist, and in this emirate that person is unlikely to live down the road. The sections below set out what is taught, what is not, and what to do about the difference.

fujairah/merashid.programmesIntro: The size of the unsupervised load differs sharply between programmes. The Diploma hands a student the most to manage alone, IGCSE hands over less but gives no training for it, and the Middle Years Programme is where the habits either form or do not.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus a core of three components that are assessed and largely self-directed: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. The IB recommends around forty hours of student work on the Extended Essay, with a small number of recorded reflection sessions with a supervisor. The rest of that time is the student's to organise, and organising it is the skill nobody examines directly.
programmes.countryNote: In a Fujairah school with small Diploma cohorts, Extended Essay supervisors are sometimes allocated across subject boundaries because there are not enough specialists to go round. A Merashid student writing on an economics question may be supervised by a teacher from another department, who can manage the process well and still cannot interrogate the subject content. That is the specific gap external support should fill.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal examinations across eight to ten subjects, with the self-managed load concentrated in revision rather than coursework. Students are given a revision timetable template and almost never taught a revision method, so most default to rereading notes and highlighting, which research has long shown to be among the least effective uses of study time available.
programmes.countryNote: An IGCSE student in Fujairah is typically carrying Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the international options, which means the independent study load is larger than the subject count suggests. A revision plan that allocates equal time to every subject ignores that and collapses in the first fortnight of study leave.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, culminating for many students in the Personal Project, which is the first substantial piece of independent work in the programme. It is also the first honest test of whether a student can plan, sustain and reflect on a long task without being chased, which is exactly what the Diploma core will demand.
programmes.countryNote: The Personal Project is the cheapest place to learn project management, because the stakes are lower than the Extended Essay and the skills transfer directly. A Merashid student who learns to keep a process journal properly here arrives in Year 12 with the habit already formed, which is worth more than any subject content learned in the same period.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four externally examined subjects with no central core, so the unsupervised load is almost entirely revision and exam technique. The jump from IGCSE is largest in the expectation of independent reading, and students who wait to be told what to study outside lessons tend to discover the problem after the first set of internal exams.
programmes.countryNote: Small A Level classes in this emirate mean fewer worked examples seen and fewer marked scripts to compare against. Working complete past papers under timed conditions and then marking them against the published scheme is the substitute for a large class's accumulated experience, and it is a habit rather than a resource.

fujairah/merashid.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones where the self-managed component carries the most weight, with a note on what the student has to manage alone in each. That is where sessions are aimed rather than at the taught content.

subjects.name: Extended Essay, any subject
subjects.description: A four thousand word independent research essay with a supervisor the student meets a small number of times. The dominant failure is a research question too broad to answer in the limit, chosen in week one and never revisited. Narrowing it properly before any drafting begins is the highest-value hour of the whole process.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Two assessed components: an exhibition built around three objects with a commentary, and an essay of up to 1,600 words on a prescribed title. Students lose marks by discussing the topic generally instead of addressing the exact title, and by choosing exhibition objects that illustrate nothing arguable.

subjects.name: Sciences internal assessment
subjects.description: An individual investigation assessed across four criteria worth twenty-four marks in total, produced outside lesson time. Evaluation is marked separately from conclusion, which is why a single closing paragraph attempting both scores badly on each. Linking each limitation to the direction of the error is the specific fix.

subjects.name: Mathematics exploration
subjects.description: A self-chosen piece assessed across five criteria worth twenty marks, including personal engagement and reflection as separate criteria. Topic choice therefore matters as much as execution, and a topic lifted from a suggestion list usually caps the engagement and reflection marks before a line is written.

subjects.name: History investigation
subjects.description: A 2,200 word investigation assessed across three criteria worth twenty-five marks, with source evaluation assessed in its own right. Students who treat the source section as an introduction rather than an assessed component lose the easiest marks on the task, and the reflection criterion is routinely written in the last hour.

subjects.name: Business Management and Economics coursework
subjects.description: Written commentary or research work built on real organisations or published articles, with application to the chosen case assessed rather than general theory. The usual loss is a well-explained concept that never engages with the specific case, which reads as competent and scores in the lower bands.

subjects.name: Independent revision method
subjects.description: Not a subject, but the single largest unsupervised determinant of an exam grade. Retrieval practice, spaced review and timed past-paper work under exam conditions outperform rereading and highlighting substantially, and almost no student is taught the difference before study leave begins.

subjects.name: Exam technique and paper management
subjects.description: Pacing, question selection, marks-per-minute discipline and knowing when to abandon a part and return to it. Mocks reveal these problems and are rarely analysed for them, so the same pacing failure repeats in the live paper with higher stakes attached.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE 0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject where independent practice has the clearest return, because fluency responds to volume. Students who do thirty mixed multi-stage questions a week improve measurably; students who reread worked examples do not, however much time they spend at the desk.

subjects.name: Sciences (IGCSE 0620, 0625 and 0610)
subjects.description: Practical-skills questions on apparatus, anomalous results and improvements are examined on the written papers and almost never revised deliberately, because they do not look like content. They are among the most reliably recoverable marks available to an independent reviser.

subjects.name: English A and English as a Second Language
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0500 and 0510
subjects.description: Essay planning is the self-managed skill that matters, and it is improved by planning many essays rather than writing a few. A student who plans five essays in an hour learns more about argument structure than one who writes a single essay in the same time.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Examined subjects with their own homework and reports, taught under rules that prohibit substituting the prescribed content. Independent study here is vocabulary retention and structured written answers, both of which respond to short frequent practice rather than long weekly blocks.

sections.heading: What the timetable covers and what it hands to the student
paragraphs: The useful audit for a Merashid family takes one sheet of paper. On the left, list everything the school timetables and teaches. On the right, list everything the student is assessed on. The second list is longer, and the difference between the two is the part of the course nobody is scheduled to teach. That is where a conscientious student loses marks while doing everything they are asked.

For a Diploma student the right-hand column is substantial. The Extended Essay, which the IB recommends around forty hours of student work on. The internal assessment in every subject, produced outside lessons. Theory of Knowledge, which carries two assessed components against a thin timetable allocation. Creativity, Activity, Service, which runs for eighteen months and requires seven learning outcomes to be evidenced. Independent revision. Exam technique. None of those is optional and most are self-scheduled.

For an IGCSE student the column is shorter but not empty, and the training for it is non-existent. Students are handed a revision timetable template in Year 11 and left to fill it, with no instruction in what to put in the boxes. Most default to rereading notes and highlighting, which feels productive and reliably underperforms timed retrieval practice on the same content in the same number of hours.

sections.heading: The internal deadline calendar nobody prints
paragraphs: Families plan around exam dates because those are published. The deadlines that actually determine a Diploma grade are internal, set by the school, and often communicated once in an assembly. By the time a parent hears about the first Extended Essay draft deadline it has usually passed, and the student has produced something written in a weekend rather than researched over a term.

Ask the coordinator for the whole internal calendar in writing at the start of Year 12, and put it somewhere the household can see. It will typically include an Extended Essay subject and supervisor decision, a research question deadline, reflection session dates, a first full draft, a final submission to the school, internal assessment draft deadlines for each subject, Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay milestones, and the school's own cut-off for uploading work. Each of those sits months before anything the boards publish.

The sequence matters more than any single date. An internal assessment draft deadline two weeks after a mock exam block is a known pressure point, and a student carrying three Higher Levels will meet three of those within a fortnight. Seeing that collision in September allows the work to be moved forward. Seeing it in January means choosing which piece to do badly.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge and CAS: the two components nobody revises
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service occupy an odd position. Both are compulsory, both are assessed or must be completed satisfactorily, and neither feels like a subject, so both get the time left over. For a student under pressure in three Higher Levels, that means they get almost none until a deadline is visible, at which point they consume a week that was needed elsewhere.

Theory of Knowledge has two assessed pieces: an exhibition built around three objects with a commentary of up to 950 words, and an essay of up to 1,600 words written on one of the prescribed titles. The marks are lost in predictable places. Students write about the topic of the title rather than addressing the title itself. They choose exhibition objects that are personally meaningful but illustrate nothing arguable. They assert claims without the counter-claim the rubric expects.

CAS is not graded but must be completed, and it runs for eighteen months with seven learning outcomes to evidence and a project of at least a month. Reconstructing eighteen months of reflections in the final term is both miserable and visible to a coordinator. Fifteen minutes of honest recording after each activity removes the problem entirely, and it is the easiest habit in the whole Diploma to build.

For a Merashid student in a small cohort these components are also the ones where peer support is thinnest. There may be no classmate who has thought hard about the same prescribed title, which makes an external reader more useful here than in a subject where the textbook does some of the work. Confirm current word limits and requirements with your school's coordinator, since the published requirements are revised between cycles.
bullets: Answer the prescribed title, not the topic the title mentions
Choose exhibition objects that make an argument, not ones that are meaningful
Record CAS reflections within a day of the activity, not at the end
Confirm current word limits and requirements with your school's coordinator

sections.heading: Independent revision that works, and the kind that feels like working
paragraphs: The gap between the best and worst use of a revision hour is enormous, and almost no student is told about it. Rereading notes and highlighting are the default because they are comfortable, produce a visible result and require no decisions. Timed retrieval, where the student writes down what they can recall before checking, is uncomfortable, produces evidence of ignorance, and works substantially better per hour spent.

A workable independent plan has four features. It is built on specific past-paper questions rather than topics. It spaces each topic so it returns after a gap rather than being finished in one block. It includes self-marking against the published scheme, which is where the student discovers what the scheme rewards. And it allocates unequal time, because the subject with the mandatory-subject homework attached and the subject sitting two grades below target do not need the same hours.

The handover matters as much as the plan. A revision method taught in the abstract is forgotten; a method run with supervision for a fortnight on the student's actual subjects, then deliberately handed over, usually survives. That is why a study-skills block is worth more in October than in April, when there is no time left to form a habit before it has to carry the exams.

sections.heading: The academic-honesty line on work nobody supervises
paragraphs: Self-managed work is exactly where the honesty question gets difficult, because nobody is watching. A student alone with an Extended Essay at midnight and a market full of operators selling finished coursework is in a genuinely tempting position, and some of those operators advertise openly in this region at fixed prices. Under IB rules that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student: a withdrawn grade or a withdrawn diploma.

The honest boundary is easy to state and worth stating out loud at the start of any coursework block. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria and their mark allocations. They may question a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. They may challenge a method before data collection. They may read a draft the student has produced and name where the evaluation is thin, which claim is unsupported, and which criterion is capping the mark. All of that is teaching.

What a tutor must not do is supply text, restructure an argument into their own words, or hand back something the student could not have made. The practical test is whether the feedback points at the student's work or replaces it. Schools require an authenticity declaration, and supervisors are expected to have seen the work develop across drafts, which is also why a sudden jump in quality between drafts is a problem rather than a success.

Generative text tools have made this sharper rather than vaguer. Schools and boards expect work to be the student's own and expect any permitted use of tools to be declared. The safe rule in a Merashid household is that anything that produces sentences the student did not think of should not go near an assessed piece, and that the school's own policy is the one that governs.

sections.heading: Private candidate and retake routes from Fujairah
paragraphs: Some Merashid families end up needing a route outside their school: a student who moved mid-course, one who needs a single retake to meet a university condition, or one taking an additional subject the school does not timetable. These routes exist and they are administrative rather than mysterious, but they have to be arranged through a centre and they have deadlines that sit well before the exam.

The board position is the starting point. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with final entries due months ahead; for the March 2027 series, entries were due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

The practical steps are to find a centre willing to accept external candidates, confirm which components it can administer, and check the entry deadline against the calendar before committing to a plan. Practical and speaking components are the usual constraint, because not every centre can offer every component for an external candidate. Ask that question first rather than last.

A tutor's role on a retake is narrower and more useful than on a full course: identify from the previous script exactly where the marks went, work on those, and sit timed papers. A retake plan that revises the whole syllabus again generally reproduces the original result, because the original result was not caused by the whole syllabus.

sections.heading: Building a weekly plan that survives the Merashid school run
paragraphs: A study plan drawn without the actual week in it is a wish. The exercise that works starts from fixed commitments and allocates what remains, rather than starting from subjects and hoping the hours exist. For a Merashid family the school run is short, which is a real advantage, so the limiting factors are activities, mandatory-subject homework and fatigue rather than travel.

Protect one evening entirely. Not for tutoring and not for revision, but as slack, because a week with no spare evening fails the first time anything goes wrong and then stays failed. Then allocate the independent study blocks to the days when the student is least tired, which is usually earlier in the week, and put the longest coursework session on a weekend morning when sustained attention is actually available.

Allocate unequal time deliberately. The subject two grades below target and the subject with a coursework deadline in three weeks both need more than the subject sitting comfortably at target, and an equal-time plan is a plan to leave the weakest subject weakest. Reviewing this allocation every half term against marked work keeps it honest, because the priorities move during the year.

In Ramadan, rebuild rather than persist. Afternoon study is the least productive part of a fasting student's day, so the independent blocks move to after Iftar and shorten, and the hardest new content moves out of the period entirely. The plan should be rewritten for that month rather than carried through it with the same boxes unfilled.
bullets: Start from fixed commitments and allocate what is left, not the reverse
Keep one evening entirely free as slack, every week

sections.heading: Where an external tutor adds value to work the student must own
paragraphs: There is a reasonable objection to all of this: if the work must be the student's own, what is a tutor for? The answer is that teaching someone to produce better work and producing it for them are completely different services, and only one of them is useful anyway. A student who is taught the criteria learns something that transfers to the next piece; a student handed finished text learns nothing and carries a malpractice risk.

The value sits in four places. First, subject interrogation: a specialist can push on whether an economics argument actually holds, which a supervisor from another department cannot. Second, criteria literacy: the published criteria are specific and most students have never read them against their own draft. Third, process discipline: external deadlines a fortnight before the school's own change behaviour more than good intentions do. Fourth, a second reader, which in a small cohort may not otherwise exist.

What a Merashid family should expect from a coursework block is therefore a written boundary at the start, feedback that names criteria rather than rewriting sentences, and a visible trail of the student's own drafts improving. If a provider's output is a better document rather than a better student, the service being sold is not tutoring and the risk sits with the child.

The same logic applies to revision and exam technique. A tutor who runs a student's revision for them has created a dependency that ends the day study leave starts. A tutor who builds a method, supervises it for a fortnight and hands it over has done the job properly, and the handover should be in the plan from the first session rather than negotiated later.
bullets: Subject interrogation a cross-specialism supervisor cannot provide
Criteria read against the student's own draft, not in the abstract
External deadlines set ahead of the school's own
A method built, supervised briefly, then deliberately handed over

sections.heading: What to ask your school before booking anything
paragraphs: Half the value of this page is obtainable for free from the school office, and it is worth collecting before spending money on support. The requests are short, reasonable and rarely refused, and the answers determine what kind of help is actually needed rather than what sounds useful.

Ask for the full internal deadline calendar for the year in writing, including Extended Essay, internal assessment, Theory of Knowledge and CAS milestones. Ask which subject each Extended Essay supervisor specialises in, and whether your child's supervisor teaches that subject. Ask for the syllabus codes and tiers your child is entered for in every examined subject. Ask for the criterion-level breakdown rather than the summary grade on the next report.

Then ask two harder questions. What support does the school provide for independent revision method, as opposed to a timetable template? And how many lesson hours are allocated to Theory of Knowledge this year? Neither question is a complaint; both tell you precisely which part of the self-managed load is genuinely unsupported in your child's case, which is the only part worth paying for.

With those answers in hand the brief for any tutor becomes specific. Rather than asking for general Diploma support, a Merashid parent can ask for six sessions on an economics Extended Essay research question with a supervisor from another department, or a revision-method block in October aimed at three subjects sitting below target. Specific briefs are cheaper and they work.
