sections.heading: What coaching for a 7 costs in the UAE, and who charges what
paragraphs: IB maths tutoring rates in AED span roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour in this market, and the spread is not explained by quality alone. It is explained by who is teaching, whether travel is included, and whether the hour is one-to-one. Most competitor pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all; two publish prices in US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in. The table below collects the published figures, with each attributed to the provider or rate card that published it.

Read the bands as a market, not as our price list. IB Gram is a matching platform, so what a family pays depends on the coach, the level and the session length agreed after the free trial lesson. The useful exercise with this table is not finding the lowest number. It is working out the cost per mark. Twenty-four hours at AED 200 is AED 4,800; if those hours are aimed at a diagnosed Paper 1 fluency gap and a capped Criterion E, they are buying identifiable marks. The same AED 4,800 spread over two years of general homework supervision is buying attendance.

Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session land at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Context helps here: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, so a tutoring budget set last year has not been squeezed by fees this year.

Two cost traps are worth naming. The first is paying a premium rate for work that is not premium work: marking past papers and drilling algebra are the same tasks at AED 200 and at AED 650. The second is paying by the month for sessions that are not needed in that month, which is common in the quiet middle of DP1. Buy hours against a diagnosed gap and a deadline, and ask any provider to show the arithmetic that connects the two.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one versus an in-home maths tutor in the UAE
paragraphs: Parents searching for a maths tutor in the UAE usually start by looking for someone who will come to the house, and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In-home tutoring is real, widely available in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and priced at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel folded in. What you buy with the premium is a tutor sitting beside the student and a parent who can see the session happening. What you pay for it is a smaller pool, a commute that eats into the hour, and a specialist shortage the further you get from the two big cities.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address. Home visits are a service we offer only in India, and every UAE lesson runs one-to-one over live video with a shared whiteboard and the student's own working held up to the camera. We are explicit about this because the alternative, implying a doorstep service and then delivering a video call, is a trust failure several providers in this market commit by routing UAE parents to an overseas phone number.

The case for online here is not that it is cheaper, although it usually is once travel is priced. It is that the selection pool stops being geographic. A family in Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah has almost no chance of finding a resident Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3 specialist at any price, and a family in Dubai Marina choosing from tutors willing to drive to Dubai Marina at 17:30 is choosing from a list shaped by traffic rather than by subject depth. Over video, the constraint is the coach's calendar.

Screen-sharing also changes what the hour contains. Past papers are marked live on screen, the error log is a shared document rather than a parent's memory, and recorded explanation of a worked question can be replayed before the next session. sections.heading: How many hours a 7 takes, counted backwards from the session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, and the November session functions mainly as a retake route. Working backwards from the session is the only way to turn a grade target into a number of hours and therefore into a price. The variables are the starting grade, whether the exploration is already internally marked, and whether the student is at SL or HL, because HL carries Paper 3 and Paper 3 needs its own block of timed practice.

The honest ranges are wide and worth stating plainly. A student holding a 6 with a completed exploration and 20 or more weeks in hand typically needs one session a week. A student at a 5 with an unfinished exploration draft needs the exploration block first, then topic repair, and usually moves to two sessions a week in the final stretch. A student at a 4 in HL at the DP1 report is looking at a two-year rebuild, because the algebra and calculus underneath Paper 3 cannot be compressed into a term. Any provider quoting the same package to all three has not read the papers.

Deadlines that are not the exam also shape the plan. The exploration deadline is internal and set by your child's school, which is why two students in different Dubai schools can be on completely different timelines for the same session. Cambridge's published March 2027 series offers a useful parallel for how far ahead entries sit: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026, so the administrative deadline lands more than two months before the first paper. Confirm every IB date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org rather than from a tutoring page, including ours.

Ramadan is the other fixed point in a UAE plan. School days shorten, family routines change, and the practical answer is to move sessions to post-Iftar timing, typically 21:00 to 22:30 Gulf Standard Time, rather than to pause for a month that sits immediately before the session. sections.heading: The regulator, the permit, and what a parent should verify
paragraphs: Private schooling in the UAE is regulated emirate by emirate, and knowing which authority governs your child's school is more useful than it sounds, because the inspection report is a free diagnostic. Dubai's KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi's ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately and federally. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an amount is quoting something unverified. MoHRE's own service is listed as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', with no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app and e-services.

Two things follow for a parent hiring maths help. Ask an individual tutor directly whether they hold the permit, because it costs them nothing to obtain and nothing to show. And do not ask for your child's own classroom teacher: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. A tutoring operation running premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal category again, needing a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute.

IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board accreditation and claims none. We are an independent tutor-matching platform with no UAE office, centre or branch, and nothing on this page should be read as an endorsement by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Where this page cites a regulator, it is to explain what that body does and to link you to its own page.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and what maths has to show
paragraphs: A maths grade is not only a university currency. For families planning to stay in the UAE, the Ministry of Education equivalency route for a secondary certificate also has subject and grade requirements, and the British-track rules are published clearly enough to repeat. Students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That five-subject rule is worth knowing precisely, because at least one provider ranking for UAE tutoring queries publishes a six-subject requirement. On the American track, English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. Those are the figures in the published guidance.

For the IB, no points threshold can responsibly be printed here. The guidance we can source does not state one, so any page quoting an IB score for equivalency is quoting something unverified. The correct step is to read the requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate, in the year you need it. IB Gram does not perform, submit or influence equivalency or attestation, and tutoring is not a requirement for any part of that process.

What this does mean for maths coaching is practical. If your child's plan includes a UAE university, the maths evidence the Ministry looks at may be an IGCSE grade and an SAT Math score rather than the DP grade you have been budgeting coaching hours against. A family in that position is often better served by a short block on SAT Math technique alongside the DP work than by more hours on the same DP syllabus.

sections.heading: The timetable your maths hours are competing with
paragraphs: A coaching plan that ignores the rest of a UAE school week fails on scheduling rather than on teaching. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, which is the rule every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement sits on.

The detail matters for timing. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time in 40-minute lesson units, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language.

What a parent feels is a full week. An IB student carrying six DP subjects, the exploration, the Extended Essay, TOK and a mandatory-subject block has very little unallocated weekday time before 18:00. The practical answer is to place maths sessions after the mandatory block, usually from 18:00 onwards, and to move the heavier exploration work to a weekend morning when the student is not already five hours into a school day. Two 45-minute sessions often outperform one 90-minute session for exactly this reason.

Ramadan compresses this further. School hours shorten, the family rhythm shifts, and the month frequently sits close to the May session. Pausing for four weeks at that point is expensive in a way that is easy to underestimate. Moving to post-Iftar slots around 21:00 to 22:30 Gulf Standard Time keeps the error log alive, and an online session is far easier to reschedule that way than a visit that depends on somebody driving across the city.

sections.heading: Getting started, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Send the most recent marked maths paper and the school's assessment calendar, take a free trial lesson with no card details asked for, and read the written plan that follows it. The plan names the component to be worked on first, the number of sessions, the session length and the coach. If the plan does not connect a diagnosed gap to a number of hours, it is not a plan and you should ask for one before paying for anything.

Coverage is the part most providers leave out. Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3 and the exploration at HL are the two narrowest specialisms in IB maths, and there are weeks in the UAE academic year, particularly the six before the May session, when no UAE-based coach with that specialism has a free evening slot. We say so rather than filling the slot with a generalist. The alternative we offer is a coach from our India-based IB team working to Gulf Standard Time, which is a 90-minute offset at most and often none.

Payment is per agreed block rather than open-ended, and a block can stop. A plan that is working should show up in marked work within three or four sessions: fewer accuracy marks lost on the same question type, a Criterion B issue closed, a Paper 3 question completed in time. If that is not visible, the right response is to change the coach or stop, not to add hours. Lead details are collected only to arrange matching and sessions, and you can ask for them to be deleted at any time.

One last honest note on expectations. A 7 in IB Mathematics is earned by a student who does the practice between sessions, and the strongest predictor we see is not the number of hours bought but whether the ten-minute daily manipulation work actually happens. Coaching makes that work targeted and checkable. It does not replace it, and no provider who tells you otherwise is describing something real.

process.description: Email or upload the most recent marked mock or class assessment, plus the school's assessment calendar and the exploration deadline. One marked paper tells a coach more than a half-hour conversation about how a student is finding the course, because the lost marks are visible on the page.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A 45 to 60-minute diagnostic over live video, with no card details asked for. The coach works through the paper with the student, separates method errors from accuracy slips, and checks whether the technology dependence pattern is present on Analysis and Approaches Paper 1.

process.description: A short document naming the first component to be worked on, the sessions needed, the session length and the coach's rate. The hours and the gap are connected explicitly, so you can see what you are buying and compare it to the market bands published on this page.

process.title: Run weekly one-to-one sessions
process.description: Same slot each week on Gulf Standard Time, over live video with a shared whiteboard. Written notes follow each session covering what was taught, what was set and what the error log now shows, so progress is visible without a parent sitting in the lesson.

process.title: Re-diagnose at each mock, then stop
process.description: Each school mock resets the plan: the error log is compared against the new paper and hours are moved to whatever is still costing marks. When the diagnosed gaps are closed, the block ends. Open-ended weekly tutoring across two years is how families overspend without noticing.

whyPoints.title: Hours priced against marks, not postcodes
whyPoints.description: A plan names the component, the gap and the number of sessions before a price is agreed. That makes cost per mark something you can actually compare between providers, which is the one comparison the published pages in this market avoid making possible.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published and attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page carries the provider or rate card that published it and the year. Three of the six strongest competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family pays in.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line written down
whyPoints.description: Exploration, Extended Essay and TOK support is teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own draft. No coach here produces assessed text, and we decline the request when it is made. One provider ranking for these queries sells completed Internal Assessments; that risks the student's whole diploma.

whyPoints.title: Subject depth instead of proximity
whyPoints.description: Because UAE lessons run over live video, an Applications and Interpretation HL statistics specialist or an Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 coach is reachable from Umm Al Quwain as easily as from Jumeirah. The selection pool is a calendar rather than a driving radius.

whyPoints.description: In the weeks before the May session the narrowest HL specialisms genuinely run out of evening slots. We say so and offer a Gulf Standard Time alternative from our India-based IB team rather than quietly substituting a generalist at specialist rates.

faqs.question: How hard is it to get a 7 in IB Maths AA HL?
faqs.answer: Hard, and specifically hard in ways that are identifiable. Analysis and Approaches HL asks for proof, algebraic fluency and chained calculus, with Paper 1 sat without technology and Paper 3 worth 20% of the grade. Most students who miss a 7 are not short of understanding; they lose accuracy marks inside correct method, or abandon a Paper 3 build-up partway through. Both are trainable. The students who get there practise manipulation in short daily blocks rather than long weekend sessions, and they treat the exploration as 20 marks to be earned rather than a task to be submitted.

faqs.question: What does IB 7 in maths coaching cost per hour in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The UAE market runs from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for a budget online tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel folded in, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB specialist. Those come from published rate cards: EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table. IB Gram is a matching platform, so the rate depends on the coach and level agreed after the free trial lesson. The number worth comparing is the rate multiplied by the hours a diagnosed gap actually needs.

faqs.question: How many coaching hours does a move from a 5 to a 7 in maths usually take?
faqs.answer: With 24 to 30 weeks in hand, one session a week rising to two in the final stretch is the common shape, which lands somewhere between 30 and 48 hours. At a mid-market AED 250 an hour that is roughly AED 7,500 to AED 12,000 across the run. The spread is driven by the exploration: a student whose draft is unfinished spends the first block on criteria work, which is cheaper per mark than anything else on the course. A student who also needs algebraic rebuilding at HL should expect a longer plan, and any provider quoting one package for every starting point has not read the papers.

faqs.question: Is Maths AA HL or AI HL the better route to a 7?
faqs.answer: Neither is easier; they reward different things. Analysis and Approaches rewards proof, algebra and calculus, with a technology-free Paper 1. Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, statistics and written interpretation, with a calculator allowed throughout. Choose on university fit first, because engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics degrees commonly list Analysis and Approaches while business, design, psychology and social sciences commonly accept either. Check each programme's own entry page in your application year and keep a screenshot, because requirements change between cycles and no tutoring page, this one included, is a reliable source for an admissions rule.

faqs.question: Can a coach help with the mathematical exploration without breaking IB honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is clear. A coach may teach the mathematics a topic needs on a parallel example, question a topic choice until the student can defend it, explain what each criterion rewards, and give feedback on a draft the student has produced, quoted against the criterion wording. A coach may not produce any part of the assessed text, edit it to completion or supply one. Everything submitted stays the student's own work. This matters because an IB malpractice finding is an expulsion risk for the student, and at least one provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB mathematical exploration worth and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: Twenty marks, carrying 20% of the final grade in all four IB maths courses. It is marked by the school against five criteria and then moderated by the IB. Criterion A covers presentation, worth 4 marks. Criterion B covers mathematical communication, also 4. Criterion C covers personal engagement, worth 3. Criterion D covers reflection, worth 3. Criterion E covers use of mathematics, worth 6, and is the one capped by a topic whose mathematics sits below course level. Most lost marks across the UAE students we see are in A, B and D rather than in the mathematics itself.

faqs.question: My child's Paper 1 is far weaker than Paper 2. What does that tell you?
faqs.answer: In Analysis and Approaches it usually means technology dependence. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, so a student who has learned the calculator route to every answer has no fallback when the device is taken away. The pattern shows up as correct setups with arithmetic or manipulation failures, and it takes four to eight weeks of timed non-calculator sets to close rather than a few sessions. In Applications and Interpretation the same gap reads differently, because a calculator is permitted throughout, so a weak Paper 1 there points at method choice instead.

faqs.question: We have eleven weeks until the May session. Is a 7 in maths still realistic?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on where the student is now and whether the exploration is already marked. From a solid 6 with the exploration behind them, eleven weeks of two sessions a week spent on timed papers and error triage is a realistic plan, costing roughly AED 5,500 to 7,000 at a mid-market rate. From a 4 at HL it is not, and a coach who says otherwise is selling hours. The useful question at this range is which component returns marks fastest, and the answer is usually timed full papers with real marking rather than more content teaching.

faqs.question: Does my child need a maths coach sitting in the room for this to work?
faqs.answer: No, and in the UAE the trade-off usually runs the other way. Lessons here are delivered one-to-one over live video with a shared whiteboard and the student's own working held to the camera. Past papers are marked live on screen, and the error log is a shared document rather than something a parent has to remember. What you give up is physical presence. What you gain is that the coach is selected for Paper 3 or exploration depth rather than for willingness to drive across Dubai at 17:30, and a 19:00 session starts at 19:00.

faqs.question: Do private maths tutors in the UAE need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any page quoting an amount with caution. Ask a tutor directly; it costs them nothing to show.

faqs.question: Can maths sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families that is better than pausing. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the month often falls close to the May session, so four weeks off is expensive at exactly the wrong time. Sessions typically move to roughly 21:00 to 22:30 Gulf Standard Time, which keeps the error log current and the timed-paper rhythm intact. Rescheduling an online session around a changed family routine is straightforward in a way that a visit depending on someone driving across the city is not. Tell the coach the preferred window before the month starts so the slot is held.

faqs.question: Will five IGCSE passes including maths satisfy UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. At least one competing site states six subjects, which does not match the published guidance. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority in the year you apply. IB Gram does not perform or influence equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: Is small-group maths coaching cheaper than one-to-one for a 7?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, yes: tuition centres in Dubai and Sharjah typically charge a third to a half of the one-to-one rate per student for groups of two to four. Cheaper per mark, usually not. A 7 turns on one student's specific lost marks, and a group runs at the group's pace on the group's weaknesses. Groups work well for a syllabus pass, for keeping pace during DP1, or for shared timed-paper practice where everyone is marked individually afterwards. For the final push on a diagnosed gap, one-to-one hours bought against that gap return more for the money.

faqs.question: What happens if no UAE-based specialist is free for AA HL Paper 3?
faqs.answer: We tell you. Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3 is one of the narrowest specialisms in IB maths, and in the six weeks before the May session the UAE-based coaches who cover it genuinely run out of evening slots. Rather than filling the slot with a generalist at specialist rates, we offer a coach from our India-based IB team working to Gulf Standard Time, which is a 90-minute offset at most and frequently none. If neither is available for the window you need, we say that too, and point you at the school's own maths department in the meantime.

faqs.question: Which Dubai and Abu Dhabi schools do your IB maths students come from?
faqs.answer: Students we support attend established IB World Schools across both cities, including Dubai International Academy - Emirates Hills, GEMS World Academy - Dubai, Uptown International School, Deira International School, Raha International School and the American Community School of Abu Dhabi. Those schools are named as context for the UAE IB system, not as partners or clients: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any school or school group. What matters more for a coaching plan than the school's name is its internal exploration deadline, which varies by several weeks between them.

faqs.question: Do maths coaching rates rise closer to the exam session?
faqs.answer: Published hourly rates in this market do not generally change by season, but availability does, and that has the same effect on what a family pays. In the weeks before the May session the specialists with Paper 3 and exploration experience fill first, so late bookers choose from a narrower pool and more often end up in the higher band. Booking the final-stretch block in advance holds both the slot and the rate. The other seasonal cost is less visible: a plan started eight weeks out can only buy timed-paper technique, while the same budget spent twenty weeks out can buy the content repair underneath it.

ib-7-in-maths-coaching.closingHeading: Start with one marked paper and a free trial lesson
ib-7-in-maths-coaching.closingBody: If a 7 in IB Mathematics is the target, the first useful step costs nothing: send the most recent marked paper and the school's assessment calendar, and take a free trial lesson over live video with no card details asked for. You will get back a named component to work on first, the number of sessions it needs, and a rate you can compare against the AED bands published on this page. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, anywhere in the seven emirates. If the remaining weeks are too few for the gap in front of us, we will tell you that instead of selling you hours.

ib-biology-ia-help.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are Biology specialists who have taken investigations from a half-formed question to a submitted report. Each has taught the current Biology guide, marked against the four criteria, and worked with UAE school deadlines that sit weeks ahead of the IB's own submission window.

intro.heading: What Biology IA help costs in the UAE, and what sets the number
paragraphs: A Biology Internal Assessment is the one piece of Diploma work a parent can watch going wrong in real time. The data is collected, the school deadline is six weeks out, and the document on the screen describes a graph instead of arguing from it. That is the point at which families in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah start asking what help costs. The honest answer is that it depends on which of the four criteria has broken and how much usable work already exists. This page prices both, rather than quoting an hourly figure and leaving you to guess the total.

The investigation is marked out of 24 and is worth 20% of the final Biology grade, at Standard Level and Higher Level alike. Those 24 marks split evenly across four criteria: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, six marks each. A student who drops four marks on Data analysis has given away more of the final grade than a student who drops four marks spread across a whole written paper, because the IA denominator is small. That asymmetry is the entire financial argument for buying hours here rather than buying generic revision.

Rates across the UAE for IB science support run from roughly AED 150 an hour for a qualified generalist to AED 450 and above for a genuine subject specialist, with premium named tutors quoted higher still. Those are bands published by UAE providers and by Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table, not an IB Gram price list. What moves a family's total is rarely the hourly figure. It is the hour count, and the hour count is set by which criterion is failing and how late the question arrives.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. For investigation work that is not a compromise. The session that earns its fee is the one where a spreadsheet is open, the tutor's cursor sits on the cell where a standard deviation belongs, and the student types the formula. A shared screen does that better than two people angling one laptop between them, and it means a family in Fujairah draws on the same Higher Level Biology specialist as a family in Jumeirah, at the same rate, without anyone paying for a drive.

There is a line worth stating before any price. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback against the published criteria. The report is authored by the student, every sentence of it. Providers in this market sell finished investigations outright; the IB treats that as malpractice, and the consequence lands on the candidate rather than the seller. Every hour costed below is teaching time. None of it is text, editing to completion, or a document that arrives ready to upload.

ib-biology-ia-help.programmesIntro: An investigation does not appear from nowhere in Year 12. The habits that earn Criterion A and Criterion D marks are built in the Middle Years Programme, and the same experimental writing feeds an Extended Essay in Biology. Here is where each programme sits, and what each one costs a UAE family in time.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Biology
programmes.description: Standard Level runs to 150 taught hours and Higher Level to 240, built around four themes studied at four levels of organisation: molecules, cells, organisms and ecosystems. Assessment is Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the internal investigation at 20%. Paper 1 splits into multiple-choice questions and a data-based section, which is why data-handling practice earned during the IA pays twice. The scientific investigation is a single independent piece, 24 marks, reported inside 3,000 words.
programmes.countryNote: Most UAE schools set an internal IA deadline weeks ahead of the IB's own upload window, so the real date a family works to is the school's, not the IB's. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain schools to ADEK, Sharjah schools to SPEA; the inspection body does not set the IA calendar, the subject teacher does. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal deadline in writing before buying any hours.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed against four criteria of its own: Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science. Criteria B and C are the direct ancestors of Diploma Criterion A and Criterion B. A student who has written a controlled method and processed data with uncertainties in MYP 5 arrives in Year 12 needing teaching, not rescue. One term of MYP science-skills work is the cheapest IA insurance a family can buy.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools that run MYP alongside a national curriculum stream often compress the sciences into fewer lab hours, and the gap shows later in Criterion B. Families moving from a CBSE or American stream into MYP 4 or 5 commonly arrive without having recorded an instrument uncertainty in their lives. That is a teachable gap, and it costs two or three hours in Year 10 against eight or nine in Year 13.

programmes.name: Extended Essay in Biology
programmes.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay, supervised in school, with its own criteria and a reflection process recorded with the supervisor. A Biology Extended Essay that involves primary data runs into exactly the same statistics and uncertainty questions as the investigation, usually at larger scale and with a longer write-up. Students who have already fought through error bars and a significance test for their IA find the essay's data chapter far less expensive in hours than classmates starting cold.
programmes.countryNote: Fieldwork options in the UAE are genuinely good and genuinely underused: mangrove transects at Jubail and Al Zorah, intertidal quadrats along the Khor Fakkan coast, soil salinity gradients on the fringes of Al Ain's farms. Supervisors rarely have time to scope those, and a tutor can help a student assess feasibility, permissions and seasonal timing before a question is committed to.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study and its own core, including a reflective project. Where Biology is one of the chosen Diploma courses, the student sits the same papers and completes the same 24-mark investigation as a full Diploma candidate. The reflective project is separate work with separate criteria, and the two are often confused in the same household, which wastes hours.
programmes.countryNote: A handful of UAE schools offer the Career-related Programme alongside the Diploma, usually with health-science or business pathways. Parents comparing quotes should check which piece of work a tutor is being asked to support, because an hour of reflective-project coaching and an hour of Biology investigation coaching are not interchangeable even though both get called coursework at home.

ib-biology-ia-help.subjectsIntro: Biology rarely arrives alone. The subjects below are the ones UAE families book alongside an investigation, either because the same statistics appear in them or because a second science is sitting on the same deadline week.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: 240 taught hours, with extension content inside the same four themes rather than bolted on at the end. Paper 2 runs two and a half hours and rewards extended explanation. HL students write the same 24-mark investigation as SL students on the same 3,000-word ceiling, which surprises families who expect a longer piece for the heavier course.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: 150 taught hours, the same four themes at shallower depth, and an identical internal assessment. SL candidates are the ones most often caught by Criterion B, because fewer lab hours means fewer chances to practise recording uncertainties before the investigation that counts.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The science most often paired with Biology in a UAE Diploma timetable, and the one whose investigation deadline usually collides with it. Chemistry IA work leans harder on uncertainty propagation, so a student doing both can learn error analysis once and spend it twice.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course sitting across Groups 3 and 4, with fieldwork-heavy investigation options that suit UAE coastal and desert sites. Students here need sampling design and descriptive statistics more than they need laboratory technique, and the teaching hours split differently as a result.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Human-participant investigations dominate, which puts informed consent and the IB's ethical guidelines at the centre of Criterion A rather than at the margins. A student measuring recovery heart rate on classmates needs the ethics paragraph written properly or marks go before any data is collected.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The Psychology internal assessment is an experimental study with its own criteria and a required inferential test, so families who have already met a t-test through Biology find the statistical section far quicker. The write-up conventions differ, and mixing them up costs marks in both subjects.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The course that formally teaches the chi-squared test, correlation and regression that Biology Criterion B quietly expects. Students taking Biology with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches instead often meet these tools for the first time inside their own investigation, under deadline.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most UAE engineering and medicine applicants are pushed towards, and the one that spends least time on applied statistics. An AA student writing a Biology investigation usually needs an hour on what a p value means before an hour on how to compute one.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Where controlled methods, variable tables and data processing are first assessed. Two terms of deliberate Criterion B and C practice here is the lowest-cost intervention available to a UAE family thinking three years ahead rather than three weeks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK sits beside the investigation in the same months and competes for the same evenings. It is worth knowing which deadline is immovable before hours are bought: the TOK essay and exhibition run on the school's own schedule, and families frequently buy Biology hours in a week that TOK had already claimed.

ib-biology-ia-help.regionsTitle: Biology IA support across the seven emirates
ib-biology-ia-help.regionsIntro: Delivery is online, so the tutor pool does not shrink as you move away from Dubai. What does change is the school calendar, the number of IB World Schools nearby, and how far a family has had to travel for help until now. Here is the position emirate by emirate.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest Diploma market in the country, regulated by KHDA, with the largest number of IB World Schools and therefore the largest number of competing internal IA deadlines in the same fortnight. Rate quotes here are the ones competitors publish, and they are the highest in the UAE.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, whose professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Families offered evening lessons by a child's own Biology teacher should know that position before accepting, and it is a common offer in the capital.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. Fewer Diploma schools means fewer Higher Level Biology specialists within driving distance, which is precisely where online delivery changes the maths for a family.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Under ADEK alongside Abu Dhabi city, with a smaller Diploma cohort and a genuine shortage of science specialists willing to drive out. Fieldwork options around the farms and the Jebel Hafeet slopes are unusually good for an ecology investigation and almost nobody uses them.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level regulator. A handful of IB World Schools serve the emirate, and families here have historically driven into Sharjah or Dubai for subject-specialist help, paying for the journey in both directions.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education is regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge. The Diploma cohort is small enough that a Higher Level Biology student may be one of a dozen in the emirate, which makes a local in-home specialist close to unobtainable and an online one ordinary.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory on the east coast, with the longest distances to a Diploma science specialist of anywhere in the country. The Khor Fakkan and Dibba coastline is also the best intertidal fieldwork in the UAE for an ecology investigation.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the UAE, also supervised by the Ministry of Education. Al Sinniyah Island and the Khor Al Beidah mudflats sit on the doorstep and offer sampling-design investigations that no examiner has read a hundred times.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of private enrolment. Seven new schools open for 2026-27, three of them IB, adding 16,846 places. More IB seats means more investigations due in the same weeks.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and the Diploma cohort is concentrated on the island and in Khalifa City. Al Ain's smaller cohort is the clearest case for online delivery anywhere in the country, because a Higher Level Biology specialist within driving distance may simply not exist.

SPEA regulates Sharjah's private schools and approves their fees and curricula; Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, while Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education. Diploma provision thins quickly moving north, and so does specialist availability on the ground.

ib-biology-ia-help.modesIntro: Three ways families buy investigation hours, with different totals. The right one depends on how far the work has got and how many weeks remain, not on how much help a student is thought to need in general.

modes.description: A standing session from the question-setting stage to the final upload, usually sixty or ninety minutes a week across eight to twelve weeks. The tutor sees the work accumulate, which means Criterion D can be written from a real record of what went wrong at the bench rather than reconstructed from memory at the end. This is the lowest-stress and highest total-hours option.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for Biology investigation support
paragraphs: A qualified subject tutor working online in the UAE is quoted between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour, and a genuine IB specialist between AED 200 and AED 450 or above. Those are the published bands, not an estimate. Three of the six best-ranking pages in this search publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in.

The bands matter less than the structure behind them. A generalist at AED 150 can teach Biology content competently and still not know that Criterion B will not award marks for a mean without a measure of spread. A specialist at AED 300 who has marked against the current criteria will diagnose that in ten minutes. The cheaper hour is only cheaper if it moves a mark, and on investigation work it frequently does not.

Travel is the other hidden multiplier. In-home one-to-one across the UAE is quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour, and the upper half of that range is paying for a car on Sheikh Zayed Road at six in the evening. Online delivery removes that line item entirely, which is why the same specialist hour costs a family in Ras Al Khaimah what it costs a family in Jumeirah.

sections.heading: The four criteria and where the 24 marks actually sit
paragraphs: Nobody else in this search names a single criterion. That is the strangest gap in the whole cluster, because the criteria are published, they are four, and they are worth six marks each. A parent who knows which criterion is weak can buy three hours instead of twelve.

Criterion A, Research design, is where investigations are lost before any data exists. The question has to be narrow enough that the data collected can answer it, the independent and dependent variables have to be named and measurable, and the method has to be repeatable by a stranger. Ethics and safety belong here too, and on human-participant work they are not optional paragraphs.

Criterion B, Data analysis, is where UAE students lose the most marks in practice. Raw data needs units and instrument uncertainties as recorded at the bench, processing has to be shown rather than asserted, an appropriate statistical test has to be chosen and justified, and graphs need error bars. A table of means with no spread is the single commonest form of this failure, and it is cheap to fix if the raw data survives.

Criteria C and D, Conclusion and Evaluation, are the ones students rush in the final week. A conclusion has to answer the stated question using the processed data and set the result against accepted biology, with a citation. An evaluation has to rank sources of error by how much they actually mattered and propose extensions a person could run, which is a different task from listing human error and asking for more repeats.

sections.heading: Where Biology investigation marks are lost in UAE classrooms
paragraphs: Three patterns account for most of the lost marks in the investigations UAE students bring to a first session, and all three are diagnosable in a fifteen-minute read. Knowing which one applies is what turns an open-ended tutoring spend into a quotable number of hours.

The first is a question that cannot be answered by the data. A student measures the effect of temperature on catalase activity at three temperatures, one trial each, and then asks whether temperature affects enzyme rate. The data cannot carry the claim, and Criterion A and Criterion C both suffer. This is a Criterion A failure that only becomes visible at the conclusion stage, which is the expensive way to find it.

The second is processing that stops at a mean. Five levels of the independent variable, three repeats each, a tidy table of averages, and nothing about spread. No standard deviation, no error bars, no test. Criterion B is six marks and this costs three or four of them. It is also the cheapest repair on the list, provided the raw readings were written down rather than averaged on the spot, which is why the first question in any session is whether the raw data still exists.

The third is an evaluation written as an apology. Students in a hurry list every imperfection they can remember, weight them all equally, and propose more repeats. What the criterion rewards is a ranked account: which error plausibly moved the result and in which direction, which did not matter, and what a better-designed follow-up would change. That reordering is a one-hour conversation and it is worth more than another week of reading.
bullets: A question narrower than the dataset is cheap to fix; a dataset narrower than the question is not
Raw readings kept at the bench are worth more later than a tidy average recorded in the moment
Error bars are the single most visible signal that Criterion B has been taken seriously
An unranked evaluation reads as a confession; a ranked one reads as analysis
A citation in the conclusion costs ten minutes and separates a 4 from a 6 on Criterion C

sections.heading: What you pay for at each stage, counted back from the school deadline
paragraphs: Hours are not evenly spread across an investigation. Two stages absorb most of them, and neither is the stage families worry about first. Setting the question and processing the data together account for roughly two-thirds of the one-to-one time a typical investigation needs.

The table below is built on a mid-band market rate of AED 250 an hour, taken from the published ranges above rather than from an IB Gram price list. Use it to sanity-check any quote, including ours: a provider proposing twenty hours for an investigation that has already collected clean data is selling a package rather than diagnosing a problem.

The costs assume the raw data survives and the school's feedback round is still open. Both of those collapse the budget when they fail. A student who averaged at the bench and discarded the readings has to collect again, which may not be possible once the lab timetable has moved on. A student whose teacher has already given the one permitted round of written feedback cannot submit a revised draft for another round, however many hours are bought.

The right question for a parent is not what the hourly rate is. It is which row of this table the work is sitting in, and whether the stage before it was completed properly. Hours bought into a broken Criterion A are the most expensive hours in Diploma tutoring, because the analysis they fund answers a question the data was never able to address. Ask any provider to name the stage first and the price second, and compare the two answers against the rows below before committing to a number of weeks.

sections.heading: The statistics hours nobody budgets for
paragraphs: Ask a UAE parent what Biology investigation support is for and they will say the write-up. Ask a Biology teacher and they will say the statistics. Criterion B is six of 24 marks and it is the criterion most often answered with a test chosen because a classmate used it.

Choosing the test is the teachable part. The data's shape decides it: two groups of continuous measurements point one way, counts in categories point another, and a continuous independent variable with several levels points to correlation and regression. A student who can say why a chi-squared test does not apply to their enzyme rates has already earned Criterion B marks that a student who ran one anyway has lost.

Interpreting the output is where the second hour goes. A p value is not a verdict and r squared is not a percentage of correctness. The criterion wants a statement of what the test shows about the stated question, at a named significance level, with the limits of the inference acknowledged. That is a short paragraph and it takes most students two attempts.

None of this needs software a UAE family has to buy. A spreadsheet handles standard deviation, a t-test, chi-squared and a regression line, and it handles error bars. A session spent inside the student's own spreadsheet, with the tutor's cursor on the cell and the student typing, is worth three spent on a worked example about somebody else's bean plants.

sections.heading: Online investigation help versus an in-home Biology tutor in the UAE
paragraphs: Plenty of UAE families start by looking for someone to sit at the kitchen table, and the search phrase reflects that. It is a fair question and it deserves a straight answer rather than a dismissal: a visiting tutor is quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour in this market, the upper half of that covers the journey, and the pool a family can reach is whoever happens to live within a twenty-to-thirty-minute drive.

IB Gram delivers to UAE families as one-to-one online tuition over live video. That is the whole of the offer, stated here and on every country page on this site, and it is not a fallback. For investigation work specifically it is the better format, because the object being worked on is a spreadsheet and a document rather than a page of practice questions.
The comparison below is about this task, not tutoring in general. Where an in-home arrangement genuinely wins, the table says so. Where it costs a family money for no mark, it says that too.

The scarcity argument is the one that decides it in most of the country. A Higher Level Biology specialist who has marked against the current criteria is not a common professional in Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain, and in Al Ain the pool is thin enough that a family may have no realistic local option at all. Online delivery means the shortlist is national rather than local, at one rate, with nobody billing for the drive and nobody declining a Tuesday slot because of the distance involved.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the part of this the money cannot buy
paragraphs: One provider ranking in this search sells completed investigations at AED 3,750. That is not a competing service with a different price; it is a different transaction, and the risk sits entirely with the student. The IB's academic-honesty procedures treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the candidate is the one who faces the consequence. No refund policy reaches that outcome.

What a tutor may do is substantial and worth paying for. A tutor may teach the biology, explain a criterion in the examiner's own wording, ask why a method controls a variable, show how a statistical test works on the student's own numbers, point at a paragraph and say that it describes rather than explains, and hand back a prioritised list of what is weak. All of that is teaching, and all of it moves marks.

What a tutor may not do is supply any of the report. Not a sentence, not a reworded paragraph, not a conclusion the student copies in their own words afterwards. The student's teacher also operates under a limit here: IB regulations allow one round of formal written feedback on a draft, which is why the pre-submission timing in the stage table matters so much. A family paying for a second opinion after that round has closed is paying for information nobody can now act on through the school.

Ask any provider in this market a direct question before paying: what exactly will be returned to my child, and in whose words will it be? A provider who will not answer that in writing has told you the answer.

sections.heading: The investigation inside the whole Biology grade
paragraphs: Twenty per cent is an awkward share. Large enough that four lost marks move a grade, small enough that families postpone it in favour of papers. Seeing the components side by side usually settles the argument about where the next ten hours should go.

Paper 1 carries 36% and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. The data-based section is the one to notice here: it tests exactly the skills Criterion B rewards. A student who has learnt to read error bars, spot an unsupported trend claim and interpret a significance statement for their own investigation has been revising Paper 1B at the same time, which is the strongest argument for doing investigation work properly rather than quickly.

Paper 2 carries 44% and rewards extended explanation, with Higher Level candidates sitting two and a half hours against Standard Level's hour and a half. Command terms decide marks here more than content does. Students who answer outline with an explanation and explain with an outline lose marks they have the knowledge to earn, and the same instinct shows up in a conclusion written as a description.

Check the current component weightings and durations against your child's subject guide or Diploma coordinator before building a revision plan on them, and treat any IB exam or results date you read online as unconfirmed until the coordinator or ibo.org states it. The practical consequence of the table below is simple arithmetic: four marks recovered on the investigation shift the final grade by more than four marks recovered on Paper 2, because the investigation is marked out of 24 while the papers are marked out of far more. That is the number to hold on to when deciding where the next block of hours goes.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from your school's own deadline
paragraphs: The date that governs an investigation is the school's internal deadline, not the IB's submission window. UAE Diploma coordinators typically set theirs weeks earlier so marking and moderation can be completed in order, and families who plan around a date found online are routinely a month out.

Get the internal deadline in writing from the coordinator before buying any hours. Then count backwards through the milestones below. Most of them are set by people inside the school, which is also why most of them can be negotiated earlier but almost never later.

No IB exam or results date appears on this page deliberately. The IB publishes those, secondary sites paraphrase them inaccurately, and a wrong date in a revision plan is worse than no date. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the picture is clearer and worth noting by contrast: Cambridge's March 2027 series, for instance, closes final entries on 27 November 2026 for an exam period starting 3 February 2027, which is a two-month gap between paperwork and papers. Internal deadlines work the same way, for the same administrative reasons.

Ramadan shifts roughly eleven days earlier each year and currently falls inside the Diploma teaching year, with shortened school days and evenings reorganised around Iftar. Sessions move to post-Iftar slots for the month without a rescheduling charge; what families should not do is assume the fortnight after Eid can absorb work that was due before it. Count the weeks backwards with the fasting month and the Eid break struck out, and the picture that emerges is usually three or four fewer usable weeks than the calendar suggests. Data collection, which depends on a school laboratory being open and staffed, is the stage that suffers most from that arithmetic.

sections.heading: What the regulators control about what you pay, and what they do not
paragraphs: School fees and tutoring fees sit in different regulatory worlds, and UAE parents are often surprised by which one is governed. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Nothing equivalent applies to private tutoring. The hourly figure a tutor quotes is not set, capped or reviewed by any authority in the country.

What is regulated is who may teach. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, applied for through MoHRE and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the ministry has not published a fine schedule, so any specific figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. Because the permit itself costs nothing, no tutor can reasonably price it into an hourly rate.

Abu Dhabi adds a condition families meet in person. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. When a child's own Biology teacher offers evening lessons, that is the rule in play, and the offer is worth declining for the student's sake rather than the teacher's.

Beyond fee approval, the emirate regulators shape the calendar a family is paying into. SPEA in Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods; KHDA oversees quality in Dubai; ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain; the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. None of them sets an internal assessment deadline. That remains the subject teacher's call, which is why the first question in this process is a question for the school.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency, UAE universities, and what the investigation mark is worth later
paragraphs: Families weighing the cost of investigation support often ask whether the mark follows the student anywhere beyond the grade. It does, in two ways, and neither is the one parents expect.

The first is the subject grade itself, which is what universities read. Ministry of Education equivalency for a UAE secondary certificate is curriculum-specific, and the published rules are clearer for some tracks than others. For the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency is demonstrated by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with at least 450 in SAT Math. One competing page in this market publishes a six-subject requirement for IGCSE candidates, which is wrong, and inheriting a wrong number from a ranking page is how families make plans that fail.

For the International Baccalaureate, no points threshold is published here. The equivalency article that sources the British and American requirements does not state one, and an unsourced figure on a page like this would be worse than silence. Verify the IB position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority directly. Equivalency is a process the family and the school complete with the Ministry; it is not something a tutoring platform performs, arranges or guarantees, and no amount of tutoring is required for it.

The second way the investigation mark travels is less obvious. Degree programmes in the Gulf and beyond that interview for laboratory science ask applicants to talk about an independent investigation, and a student who designed their own question, chose their own statistical test and can explain what the error bars showed has something concrete to say. That is a return on the same hours, and it is the part no mark scheme records.

process.title: Send the question, the criterion and the deadline
process.description: Three things get a useful answer: the investigation question as currently written, which criterion the teacher has flagged, and the school's internal deadline. A draft or a spreadsheet helps more than a description of one. Within that message a realistic hour count can be given rather than a package.

process.title: A free first lesson on the actual work
process.description: One 45-minute lesson at no charge, one per student, with no card details taken and nothing to cancel afterwards. It runs on the student's own investigation, not a sample task, because the only useful diagnosis is of the document that will be submitted. You will hear which criterion is weakest and roughly what fixing it costs.

process.title: Agree the hours against named criteria
process.description: Hours are scoped to criteria, in writing, before anything is booked. Four hours on Data analysis is a different commitment from twelve weeks of general Biology support, and conflating the two is how tutoring budgets in this market quietly double. If the work needed is two hours, the quote is two hours.

process.title: Work the criteria in order, on the student's screen
process.description: Sessions run with the student's own spreadsheet and document open and the student at the keyboard. Each one ends with written criterion-referenced notes. Nothing is typed into the report by anyone but the student, and the feedback trail is kept because Criterion D is written from it weeks later.

process.title: Hand back and step away before submission
process.description: Support stops while the school's own feedback round is still open, so the student has time to act on it independently and their teacher sees work the student can account for. If no Higher Level specialist is free at your Gulf Standard Time slot, you will be told that rather than offered a generalist at the same rate.

This one publishes the market's bands in AED, names the provider and the date each figure came from, and separates them from what IB Gram does. A worked example about someone else's data teaches a procedure; the student's own data teaches a judgement.

faqs.question: How much does IB Biology IA help cost in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Market rates for IB science support in the UAE run from about AED 150 an hour for a qualified generalist online to AED 200-450 for a subject specialist, with premium named tutors quoted from AED 500. Those bands come from UAE providers' own rate pages and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table, dated October 2026. The total depends far more on hour count than on rate. A broken Criterion B with the raw data intact is typically three or four hours; an investigation whose question cannot be answered by the data collected costs considerably more, because earlier stages have to be redone.

faqs.question: How many one-to-one hours does a Biology investigation actually need?
faqs.answer: Eight to twelve hours spread across the whole investigation is typical when support starts at the question-setting stage, and four to six when it is scoped to a single weak criterion. The distribution is uneven: narrowing the question and processing the data absorb around two-thirds of the time, while the conclusion and evaluation are usually one or two hours each. A provider quoting twenty hours for an investigation that already has clean collected data is selling a package rather than diagnosing a problem. Ask which criteria the hours are attached to before agreeing to any number.

faqs.question: Which of the four Biology IA criteria is worth paying for first?
faqs.answer: Criterion B, Data analysis, in most cases. It carries six of the 24 marks and it is where UAE students lose the most in practice, usually by presenting means with no measure of spread, no error bars and no statistical test. It is also the cheapest criterion to repair, provided the raw readings were recorded rather than averaged at the bench. Criterion A is more important but less fixable late: if the question cannot be answered by the data collected, no amount of analysis rescues it, which is why a single hour before data collection is worth several afterwards.

faqs.question: My daughter's data is collected but her graphs have no error bars. Is that an expensive fix?
faqs.answer: No, provided the raw readings still exist rather than only the averages. Standard deviation and error bars take about thirty minutes to teach in a spreadsheet, and the student does the work. The longer part is deciding whether a statistical test is also needed and which one fits, which is another hour or two. At a mid-band market rate of AED 250 an hour, that is a two-to-three-hour job. If the repeats were averaged on the spot and the individual readings discarded, the spread cannot be recovered and the lab timetable may not allow recollection.

faqs.question: Is a t-test or a chi-squared test right for enzyme rate results?
faqs.answer: Enzyme rates are continuous measurements, so a chi-squared test does not apply; chi-squared handles counts falling into categories. If two conditions are being compared, an unpaired t-test fits. If the independent variable was measured at five or more levels, a correlation coefficient with regression and r squared says more about the relationship. A student who can explain why chi-squared was ruled out has already earned Criterion B credit that a student who ran one anyway has lost. Choosing and justifying the test is the teachable hour; computing it in a spreadsheet takes minutes.

faqs.question: A tutor offered to tidy up the wording of my son's report. Where is the line?
faqs.answer: Changing a student's sentences is editing, and on assessed work it is not permitted. A tutor may point at a paragraph and say it describes where it should explain, ask what mechanism the student thinks is operating, or note that the conclusion does not answer the stated question. The student then rewrites it themselves. The practical test is whose words end up in the submitted report. If any of them are not the student's, the work is no longer the student's, and under IB academic-honesty procedures the consequence falls on the candidate rather than the provider.

faqs.question: Does the 3,000-word ceiling include data tables and the bibliography?
faqs.answer: The limit applies to the body of the report rather than to tables of raw and processed data, graph labels, or the reference list, but the detail matters and the current subject guide is the authority. Ask the Diploma coordinator to confirm what the school counts, in writing, because interpretations vary between teachers and the consequence of a late discovery is severe. Students who overrun almost always solve it by cutting the evaluation, which hands away Criterion D marks. Planning the word budget across the four criteria before drafting is a half-hour conversation that protects two or three marks.

faqs.question: The school already gives feedback. Why pay for more?
faqs.answer: Because the school's feedback is limited to one formal written round on a draft under IB regulations, it arrives on a timetable set for thirty students at once, and it is not always specific enough for a student to act on alone. Paid support is useful before that round, so the draft the teacher sees is the student's best work rather than their first attempt. It is far less useful afterwards, when no revised draft can be resubmitted through the school. Timing decides the value here more than quality does.

faqs.question: Three weeks to the deadline and nothing is processed. What can money still fix?
faqs.answer: Quite a lot, in a specific order. Processing and statistics first, because Criterion B is six marks and is achievable in three or four hours if the raw data exists. Then the conclusion, which needs to answer the stated question using the processed data with one citation to published biology. Then the evaluation, ranked rather than listed. What cannot be fixed in three weeks is a question the data cannot answer or a collection window that has closed. Establish which of those applies before booking anything, because it changes the whole plan.

faqs.question: Why is this quoted per hour instead of as a fixed package?
faqs.answer: Because the work needed varies by a factor of four depending on what already exists. A student with clean data and a weak evaluation needs two hours. A student whose question cannot be answered by the data collected needs the method stage again. A fixed package prices the average, which means families with small problems subsidise families with large ones. Hours scoped to named criteria are also auditable: at the end of four hours on Criterion B, either the processing and the statistics are right or they are not, and that is a conversation a parent can have.

faqs.question: Does the mark my child's Biology teacher awards stay as it is?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The teacher marks against the four criteria and the IB moderates a sample of the school's marks, which can move a cohort's marks down as well as up. That is one reason a report should be written so a stranger could follow it: the moderator has never met your child, never saw the laboratory, and reads only what is on the page. Methods described as repeatable by someone else, and raw data presented with its units and uncertainties, survive moderation better than work that relies on the teacher's memory of the project.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to after Iftar during Ramadan without a rescheduling fee?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sessions shift to post-Iftar slots for the month at no extra charge, and the regular slot is held. School days shorten during Ramadan across the UAE, which changes when a student is actually able to concentrate rather than merely available. The planning point is different: Ramadan and Eid together remove usable teaching weeks from the calendar, so an investigation deadline that falls shortly afterwards needs its data collection finished before the month starts, not during it. Count the weeks backwards with the fasting period removed.

faqs.question: We live in Ras Al Khaimah rather than Dubai. Does that change the price or the tutor?
faqs.answer: Neither, which is the main practical argument for online delivery. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so the rate carries no travel component and the shortlist of Biology specialists is national rather than whoever lives within a half-hour drive. Ras Al Khaimah's private schools are regulated by the emirate's own Department of Knowledge, and the Diploma cohort is small enough that a Higher Level Biology student may be one of very few in the emirate. Locally, a subject specialist for that student is close to unobtainable; online, they are ordinary.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in the UAE need a permit, and is that cost passed to us?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it costs nothing, so there is nothing to pass on. Private tutoring runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, applied for through MoHRE and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The ministry has not published a fine schedule, so treat any specific amount you read online as unverified.

faqs.question: Will a strong investigation mark help with UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is assessed on certificates and grades rather than on individual coursework components, so the investigation helps only through the subject grade it contributes to. The published British-track rule requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. No International Baccalaureate points threshold is published on this page because the sourced article does not state one; verify that on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority. Equivalency is completed by the family and the school, not by a tutoring platform.

faqs.question: What happens to our booking if no Biology HL specialist is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: You are told, before any payment, rather than matched with a generalist at a specialist rate. Higher Level Biology investigation work in a specific Gulf Standard Time window is a narrow requirement, and in peak deadline weeks it occasionally cannot be filled immediately. The options are a different time slot, a short wait, or a referral elsewhere. No competitor page researched for this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is why families usually discover one after paying a deposit rather than during the first conversation.

ib-biology-ia-help.closingHeading: Start with the criterion, not the hourly rate
ib-biology-ia-help.closingBody: Send the investigation question as it currently reads, the criterion the teacher has flagged, and the school's internal deadline. The first 45-minute lesson is free, one per student, with no card details taken, and it runs on your child's own work rather than a sample task. At the end of it you will know which of the four criteria is costing marks, roughly how many hours fixing it takes, and what that comes to against the published UAE market bands on this page. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, anywhere in the seven emirates. Every sentence of the report stays your child's own.
