intro.heading: CAS is the only part of the Diploma a student can fail without sitting a paper
paragraphs: Creativity, Activity, Service is the part of the IB Diploma Programme that UAE parents hear least about and worry about last. It carries no marks, contributes nothing to the 45 points, and appears on no results slip. It is also one of three core requirements, alongside Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, that a candidate must complete for the Diploma to be awarded. A student can sit every paper in the May session, do well, and still leave without the Diploma because a coordinator could not sign off CAS. That is the whole reason this page exists.

The problem is almost never laziness. It is timing. CAS is designed to run across roughly eighteen months, which means it begins in the first weeks of DP1, long before exam pressure makes anything feel urgent. UAE families are unusually exposed to the gap this creates. The school year here is cut across by long summer travel, a stretch of months when outdoor activity moves indoors or stops, Ramadan shifting the shape of the whole day, and a resident population that relocates mid-programme. A CAS plan written in September that assumes twelve uninterrupted months is already wrong by December.

The second problem is counting hours. The IB's current CAS guide sets no hours total. The old 150-hour expectation was removed from the programme requirements, although many UAE schools keep an internal number in their CAS handbook because a running total is easier to monitor than evidence is to read. Hours are not what a coordinator signs against. Evidence against each of the seven CAS learning outcomes is, together with reflection showing that something actually changed. A student with 210 logged hours and nothing against outcome six is further from completion than one with seventy hours and a complete portfolio.

So IB CAS guidance in the UAE does unglamorous work. It puts the three documented interviews on a calendar before anyone needs them. It makes the CAS project, minimum one month and run with other students through five stages, start early enough that the demonstration stage is not improvised in the last fortnight of DP2. It audits the CAS portfolio reflections against the seven outcomes rather than against a total. And it teaches reflection as a skill, because "it was a great experience and I learned a lot" is the most common sentence in a CAS portfolio that is about to be sent back.

Everything described here is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. For CAS that is not a compromise, it is the right shape. CAS mentoring is conversation, planning and reading: a mentor reads a reflection, asks the question the student has not asked themselves, and returns it. None of that improves by driving across Sheikh Zayed Road at five in the afternoon. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE, and home visits are part of the service only in India. The comparison table below sets out what each format costs a Gulf family in money and in time.

The sections that follow are ordered as a clock. The seven outcomes first, because they define what evidence must exist. Then the eighteen-month sequence read from its end, the sign-off, back to the first interview. Then the CAS project stages, the reflection problem, the exclusions written into the IB's own guide that catch UAE students most often, what the market charges, the service calendar in this region, and the honesty boundary a mentor must not cross.
bullets: CAS is a completion requirement, not a graded component: no points, no grade, no exam
Seven learning outcomes, each needing evidence at least once across the programme
Three documented interviews: start of DP1, end of DP1, final term of DP2
A CAS project lasting at least one month, planned and run with other students
No hours total in the current IB guide; the number in your school's handbook is its own
Sessions online on Gulf Standard Time, with home visits offered only in India

ib-cas-guidance.programmesIntro: CAS belongs to the Diploma Programme, but the habits it tests begin earlier. A Year 9 student in the MYP is already doing Service as Action and will run a Personal Project. A Career-related Programme student has Service Learning instead of CAS. The four entries below describe where each one sits inside a UAE school's structure and what it means for the CAS clock.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: CAS lives here, next to Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. It is monitored, not marked. The school appoints a CAS coordinator and usually a CAS adviser per student, holds three documented interviews, and keeps a portfolio of evidence and reflection. The Diploma is not awarded until CAS is signed as complete, which makes it the only core element with a pass-fail character and no appeal route through a remark.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools the DP cohort is often small, which cuts both ways. A coordinator with thirty candidates knows each portfolio, so gaps surface early and loudly. The same coordinator is frequently also a subject teacher with a full timetable, so the reading of reflections happens in bursts around reporting weeks. Families who wait for the school to chase them usually get chased late.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP has its own core, and Service Learning sits where CAS sits in the Diploma, alongside personal and professional skills, a reflective project and a language development element. The vocabulary differs, the discipline does not: identify a real need, plan with the people affected, act, reflect in writing, and show what was learned. Mentoring treats it as the same muscle trained on a different frame.
programmes.countryNote: A handful of UAE schools run the CP next to the DP, often with hospitality, business or engineering pathways tied to local employers. Students moving between the two programmes in DP1 can usually carry evidence across, but the reflective project and the CAS project are different artefacts with different rules, and the transfer has to be agreed with the coordinator rather than assumed.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Service as Action runs through all five MYP years and the Personal Project closes the programme in Year 11. Both rehearse the CAS habits: choosing something, planning it, keeping a record, and writing about it honestly afterwards. A student who has written real reflections in the MYP arrives in DP1 able to produce a usable CAS entry in twenty minutes rather than a paragraph a coordinator will reject.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run the full continuum, so a Year 11 Personal Project supervisor and a DP1 CAS adviser may be the same person in the same corridor. Where a family has moved in from a Cambridge or CBSE school, the student reaches DP1 with no reflection practice at all. That gap is the single most common reason a first CAS interview goes badly here.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP ends with an exhibition in the final year: a collaborative inquiry into a real issue, presented to the school community. It is CAS in miniature, and the structure is recognisably the same, from investigation through to a public demonstration. Mentioning it here matters because parents of younger children in UAE IB schools often meet this language years before anyone says the word CAS to them.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai alone offers seventeen different curricula across its private schools, with the International Baccalaureate taking roughly seven per cent of the emirate's private-school enrolment according to Dubai Media Office figures for 2024-25. Families choosing a PYP school now are choosing the continuum that ends in CAS, and the exhibition in Year 6 is the first visible sign of how a school handles reflection.

ib-cas-guidance.subjectsIntro: CAS is not a subject, so the mentoring streams below are built around what a portfolio actually needs. Most families use two or three of them rather than all. The first session identifies which, by reading the existing portfolio against the outcome list and the time left on the clock before the final interview.

subjects.name: CAS portfolio and evidence audit
subjects.description: A line-by-line read of what is in the portfolio against the seven outcomes, producing a gap list rather than encouragement. Photographs, supervisor confirmations, dates and the reflection attached to each experience are checked for the things coordinators reject: no date, no named responsible adult, no evidence the student initiated anything.

subjects.name: Reflection writing as a skill
subjects.description: Practice at the four moves the IB describes: describing what happened, naming the feeling, generating an idea, and asking a question. Worked on the student's own entries, never rewritten for them. Most students need three or four supervised attempts before the fifth one stops reading like a thank-you note.

subjects.name: The CAS project, stage by stage
subjects.description: Investigation, preparation, action, reflection and demonstration, with a real calendar against each. The collaboration requirement and the one-month minimum are planning constraints, not paperwork, and treating them as paperwork is why projects collapse at the action stage.

subjects.name: Service learning design
subjects.description: Choosing between direct, indirect, advocacy and research service, and then identifying a need with the community rather than for it. This is where outcome six and outcome seven are usually won or lost, and where a mentor's main job is to refuse the first idea politely.

subjects.name: Creativity strand planning
subjects.description: Turning an existing interest, an instrument, a film habit, a sketchbook, into something with a recorded arc. Passive consumption does not count. The work is converting "my son plays piano" into a documented progression with a challenge, a plateau and a reflection on both.

subjects.name: Activity strand planning
subjects.description: Physical commitment that is sustained and recorded, with attention to the stretch of the UAE year when outdoor training moves indoors. Club sport counts, but only if the student can show development and reflection rather than attendance across a season.

subjects.name: Coordinator interview preparation
subjects.description: Each of the three documented interviews has a different job: plan, mid-point audit, completion. Preparation means arriving able to say which outcomes are evidenced, which are not, and what the plan is for the gap, in the student's own words and without reading from a sheet.

subjects.name: Global significance and ethics
subjects.description: The two outcomes students most often leave empty. Engagement with an issue of global significance means a local action connected to a wider pattern and understood as such. Ethics means being able to say which choice was difficult and why, including the choices made badly.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge alongside CAS
subjects.description: TOK and CAS share a submission window and compete for the same evenings. Running both with one mentor keeps the exhibition and the essay from colliding with the project's demonstration stage, and the knowledge questions a student meets in service work are often the best TOK material they have.

subjects.name: Extended Essay process coaching
subjects.description: Research question, supervisor meetings and the reflection form, handled as process rather than content. Feedback on the student's own drafts only. Families usually book this alongside CAS because the two sit in the same months and are both easy to postpone until they cannot be.

subjects.name: Subject tutoring that protects CAS time
subjects.description: When a Higher Level subject is eating every evening, CAS stops. Targeted subject work, most often Mathematics, Chemistry or Physics at HL, is sometimes the fastest route to a CAS plan that survives DP2, because it returns the hours the panic was consuming.

ib-cas-guidance.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in the UAE changes what is realistic for CAS, mostly through distance, heat and who is on the other end of a service commitment. The notes below are about CAS opportunity and session timing rather than school catchments, and they are the detail a generic activity list leaves out.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Dense with IB schools, so CAS project collaborators are easy to find inside one cohort. The trap is that everyone chooses the same two school-run service clubs, and a coordinator reading thirty identical portfolios will push back on initiative under outcome three.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai, Business Bay and Jumeirah
regions.note: Apartment living limits the Activity strand to facilities with bookable slots, which makes a recorded progression easier, not harder. Evening traffic through the Al Khail and Sheikh Zayed corridors is why online sessions here are usually set at 7pm or later.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JLT and Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: A highly transient resident population, so service partners change hands often and a commitment started in DP1 may lose its supervising adult by DP2. Keeping the named responsible adult and their confirmation in the portfolio as you go matters more here than anywhere.

regions.name: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Villa communities with real distances between them, so a CAS project built around weekly in-person meetings costs an hour of driving each way. Projects designed to meet online and act in person once a fortnight survive Abu Dhabi geography far better.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: A smaller IB cohort means fewer ready-made collaborators and a longer search for a service partner, balanced by genuine, identifiable local need and supervisors who stay in post for years. Continuity of evidence is usually stronger here than in the coastal cities.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Curricula, programmes and assessment methods are approved by the emirate's own authority, so school CAS handbooks here are often more prescriptive about what counts. Checking the handbook against the IB's own outcome list early prevents work done to the wrong standard.

regions.name: Ajman and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Private schools in both emirates are supervised federally rather than by an emirate regulator. IB cohorts are small, so a CAS project often has to recruit collaborators from another school entirely, which is permitted and usually strengthens the collaboration evidence.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah
regions.note: The two emirates almost no tutoring page mentions. Distance from the main IB clusters makes online CAS mentoring the only practical option for most families, and local environmental and heritage service work here produces outcome six evidence that is genuinely the student's own.

schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of Diploma candidates in the country, and the place where CAS handbooks diverge most. Some schools run a tight adviser system with timetabled CAS slots; others leave the portfolio entirely to the student between interviews. Knowing which kind your school is changes the mentoring plan completely.

Cohorts are smaller and advisers tend to know every portfolio by name, so a gap against an outcome is usually flagged at the second interview rather than discovered in DP2. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for school staff also shape who may tutor a student privately.

A thinner IB map, with candidates sometimes travelling between emirates for school. CAS projects built here often cross school boundaries out of necessity, and the collaboration evidence that results is stronger than the single-cohort version produced in a large Dubai school.

ib-cas-guidance.modesIntro: CAS work comes in bursts rather than a steady weekly rhythm, so the formats below are shaped around the clock rather than around a timetable slot. Most families start with the audit, then take a fortnightly rhythm, then a short sprint block around the project's action and demonstration stages.

modes.title: Fortnightly CAS portfolio mentoring
modes.description: A forty-five or sixty-minute session every two weeks across DP1 and DP2, which matches the pace at which a portfolio genuinely changes. The student brings what they have written since last time, the mentor reads it live, and the session ends with one named outcome to evidence and one entry to rewrite. Short, frequent and boring is what works here.
bullets: One outcome targeted per session, named before the session ends
Reflections read on screen and questioned, never edited by the mentor
A running gap list the family can see at any point
Pauses around mocks and exam weeks without losing the thread

modes.title: CAS project sprint block
modes.description: A concentrated block of four to six sessions covering investigation and preparation, then a check at the action stage and a final one before demonstration. The one-month minimum means the project cannot be compressed, but the planning around it can be done properly in a fortnight. The sprint exists so the demonstration stage is designed rather than improvised.
bullets: A dated plan across all five stages before the action starts
Collaboration roles agreed and recorded, not assumed
A named responsible adult identified at the preparation stage
Demonstration format chosen early: assembly, exhibition, report or presentation

modes.title: Interview preparation sessions
modes.description: One session before each of the three documented interviews. The student rehearses saying out loud which outcomes are evidenced, which are not, and what the plan is for the gap. Coordinators are not trying to catch anyone out, but a student who cannot describe their own portfolio reads as one who did not build it.
bullets: A one-page outcome status the student has written themselves
Practice answering the question behind the question
Honest framing of a commitment that fell through
Agreed next actions to bring back to the adviser

modes.title: Diploma core bundle
modes.description: CAS, Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay process coaching held by one mentor across DP1 term three and DP2 term one, the months in which all three compete. One person holding all three deadlines is the difference between a sequenced plan and three separate people each asking for the same Thursday evening.
bullets: One calendar covering CAS, TOK and Extended Essay internal deadlines
Service work mined for TOK knowledge questions where it fits honestly
Feedback on the student's own drafts only, at every stage
Scheduling that treats the project's demonstration stage as fixed

sections.heading: The seven CAS learning outcomes, and what each one actually asks for
paragraphs: CAS is signed off against seven learning outcomes, each of which must be evidenced at least once somewhere across the eighteen months. That is the entire standard. There is no mark, no band and no weighting, which is precisely why it confuses families used to a syllabus. A coordinator is not asking whether your child did enough. They are asking whether, for each of seven statements, there is something in the portfolio that shows it.

The outcomes are not evenly difficult. Undertaking a new challenge and showing perseverance tend to look after themselves, because they fall out of any sustained commitment. Initiating and planning an experience is harder, because joining a school club initiated by a teacher does not evidence it. Engagement with issues of global significance and the ethics of choices are the two that are routinely left blank until someone reads the portfolio properly, and they are the two that cannot be retrofitted in a fortnight.

The practical consequence is that a CAS plan should be written against the outcome list, not against a list of activities. Three well-chosen commitments can cover all seven. Nine scattered ones can cover four. The first job of any audit is therefore to map what already exists onto the list and see which statements have nothing sitting under them, because a student who has been busy for a year will usually assume the answer is none of them and be wrong. The table below sets each outcome next to the kind of evidence that satisfies it and the specific way UAE students tend to come up short, which is usually a function of how well-organised their schools are rather than how willing the student is.

Three strong commitments usually cover more outcomes than nine weak ones
Outcomes 6 and 7 are the ones that cannot be added late

sections.heading: The eighteen-month CAS clock, read from the sign-off backwards
paragraphs: Read CAS forwards and it looks like two years of opportunity. Read it from the end and it looks like a short sequence of fixed points with very little slack. The final point is the coordinator's sign-off, which happens before the Diploma is awarded and after everything else has been recorded. Nothing can be added after it. A portfolio that is incomplete when the third interview comes round is not a portfolio that needs another month; it is one that needs a conversation about what is still possible.

Working backwards, the third documented interview sits in the last term of DP2, by which point the CAS project must already have reached its demonstration stage. Demonstration is a public act of some kind, which means it has to be scheduled with other people and therefore planned a term ahead. Push back further and the project's action stage has to run for at least a month, inside the second half of DP1 or the start of DP2, which puts investigation and preparation in DP1's second term. The first interview, with its self-review and plan, belongs in the first six weeks of DP1.

That chain is why CAS deadlines before the May session are a DP1 problem rather than a DP2 one. Every point in the table below is set by the school rather than by the IB, so the exact weeks differ between a Dubai school and one in Sharjah. The sequence does not differ, and neither does the consequence of a slip: each delay compresses the stage after it, and the stage with no give in it is the one-month action period.

sections.heading: The CAS project: one month minimum, five stages, and the collaboration rule
paragraphs: Every Diploma student must complete at least one CAS project. It has to last a minimum of one month, it has to be collaborative, and it must move through the five CAS stages: investigation, preparation, action, reflection and demonstration. It can sit in any single strand or combine them. Those are the only hard constraints, and all three are routinely broken by projects that look impressive and get sent back.

The one-month rule is a duration rule, not an effort rule. A single ambitious weekend is not a CAS project however much work it contains. Collaboration means working with others in a way the student can describe, including the part that was difficult; a project where one student did everything and three signed their names fails the fifth outcome even if the project itself succeeded. Demonstration is the stage most often skipped, because it requires an audience and therefore a date in someone else's diary.

A CAS project in Dubai has one structural advantage and one structural problem. The advantage is density: within a single large IB cohort it is easy to find three collaborators with compatible timetables. The problem is that the obvious projects are already running, so investigation has to find a need nobody in the cohort has already adopted. In Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah the balance inverts, and the harder part is assembling the group. The table sets each stage against what it has to produce and the failure that follows when it is skipped.

sections.heading: Why "I learned a lot" fails, and what a usable reflection contains
paragraphs: Most CAS portfolios that get returned are not short of experiences. They are short of reflection, or they contain something that looks like reflection and is actually gratitude. The sentence that signals it is always close to the same: the experience was great, the people were lovely, and the student learned a lot about themselves. Nothing in that is checkable, and nothing in it evidences an outcome. A coordinator cannot sign against it because there is nothing to sign against.

The IB describes reflection as having four elements, and they are a usable checklist rather than a theory. Describe what happened, plainly and specifically. Say what you felt, including the uncomfortable parts. Generate an idea, meaning something you would now do differently. Ask a question, meaning something the experience left unresolved. A reflection with all four is usually three or four sentences long. A reflection with none of them can run to a page and still be empty.

The other half of the problem is timing. Reflection written months later becomes narrative, because the detail has gone and only the summary remains. CAS portfolio reflections work when they are written close to the event and revisited later, which is why fortnightly mentoring beats a single rescue block. The mentor's job here is narrow and specific: read the entry, ask the question the student avoided, and hand it back. A mentor who rewrites a reflection has removed the only thing the reflection was evidence of.
bullets: Describe, feel, generate an idea, ask a question: four moves, three or four sentences
Written within days of the experience, then revisited at the next interview
A difficulty named honestly evidences more than a success described warmly
The student's own words throughout, including the clumsy ones

sections.heading: What the IB's CAS guide excludes, and the UAE version of each mistake
paragraphs: The CAS guide carries a list of things that do not count. It exists because students reasonably assume that anything generous, time-consuming or difficult must qualify, and much of it does not. Reading the exclusions early saves a term of misdirected effort. Reading them in DP2 is how a portfolio that looked full turns out to be half empty.

Several exclusions bite particularly hard in the UAE. Work for which the student is personally rewarded is out, which catches paid coaching at a sports academy and paid tutoring of younger pupils, both common here. All forms of duty within the family are out, which catches the student who looks after younger siblings every afternoon. Anything that forms part of the student's own Diploma course requirements is out, so a Biology Internal Assessment cannot also be CAS. Religious devotion, and anything that reads as proselytising, is out.

Two more are worth naming because they look like strengths. Fundraising with no defined end is excluded, which is awkward in a region where the charity gala is a social institution: a total raised is not a need identified. And an experience with no responsible adult on site to confirm what the student did is excluded, which is why an unsupervised beach clean-up with friends produces warm reflections and no usable evidence. None of these exclusions means the experience was worthless; it means the experience cannot be the thing a coordinator signs against, and a student who understands the difference stops arguing and starts building a second strand. Each row below pairs the rule with how it tends to appear in a UAE portfolio, and with the version of the same intention that does count.

sections.heading: What CAS and Diploma core support costs across the UAE market
paragraphs: Nobody in this part of the market publishes rates for core support, which is why parents comparing three quotes for CAS mentoring usually find three different billing models and no basis for comparison. The figures below are market bands observed across UAE provider rate cards in October 2026, grouped by provider model rather than by brand. They are not IB Gram's prices, and no page should be read as a quotation. Our own number comes after a trial session, when the amount of work left on the clock is actually known.

The useful thing to understand is that CAS is billed differently from subject tutoring. Subject work is sold by the hour across a term. Core support is usually sold either as a small retainer that assumes fortnightly contact, or as a project block tied to the CAS project stages, or as a single audit followed by a short series. The hourly figure matters less than how many hours the model assumes, and a cheap hourly rate attached to a twenty-session assumption is not cheap.

The second thing to watch is what the fee covers between sessions. CAS mentoring generates reading: reflections arrive, get read, and come back annotated with questions. A rate that covers only the live hour and bills reading separately will quote lower and cost more. The final column of the table gives the source and date for each band, because an AED figure without a date and a method is not information a parent can act on.

sections.heading: Online CAS mentoring against the in-home and school-only alternatives
paragraphs: The honest comparison for CAS is not online against in-home. It is online against doing nothing, because the default for most families is to rely entirely on the school and discover at the second interview that the portfolio is thin. School support is free, it is run by people who know the standard, and it is spread across a cohort by a coordinator who also teaches a full timetable. It is usually enough for an organised student and rarely enough for a disorganised one.

Where an in-home mentor is the alternative, the arithmetic in the UAE is unkind. A sixty-minute session plus a round trip across Dubai at five in the afternoon costs two and a half hours of somebody's evening, and the travel is priced into the market rate. A Marina family choosing an in-home mentor is choosing from whoever is free within a twenty-minute drive; the same family choosing online CAS mentoring is choosing from mentors who have supervised Diploma cores, wherever they happen to live.

For CAS specifically, the online format loses nothing, because the work is reading and conversation rather than demonstration at a whiteboard. Reflections are shared on screen, annotated live and handed straight back. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE, and home visits are part of the service only in India, so the table below compares what each format actually delivers rather than pretending a choice exists that does not.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the heat window and the UAE service calendar
paragraphs: A CAS plan is a calendar, and the UAE calendar is not the one the guide was written against. Three features of the year here reshape it. The long summer break empties service partners of their volunteers and takes many families out of the country for weeks. A long stretch of the year makes sustained outdoor activity impractical, which pushes the Activity strand indoors or into early mornings. And Ramadan moves the usable part of the day, with community and charitable work at its most abundant precisely when school energy is lowest.

Handled deliberately, each of these is an opportunity rather than an obstacle. Ramadan is the richest month of the year for genuine service in this region, and a project whose action stage lands inside it has no shortage of real, identified need to work against. The practical adjustment is timing: sessions shift to post-Iftar slots, and the action stage is planned around evening availability rather than afternoons. CAS during Ramadan does not stop, it relocates.

The summer gap is the one that actually breaks plans, because it arrives at the end of DP1 and lasts long enough to end a commitment. A supervising adult who leaves over the summer takes the confirmation of three months of work with them unless it was recorded at the time. The rule for UAE families is simple: get the named responsible adult, the dates and their confirmation into the portfolio while the experience is still happening, not when the interview is announced.
bullets: Sessions move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan rather than pausing
Record the named responsible adult and their confirmation as you go, not later
Plan the Activity strand around the months when outdoor training is impractical
Treat the long summer break as a stop in the commitment, and plan the restart

sections.heading: Academic honesty and CAS: the line a mentor does not cross
paragraphs: CAS is not marked, which leads some families to assume the honesty rules are looser here. They are not. The CAS portfolio is a record of the student's own experiences and the student's own thinking, and a reflection written by somebody else is a false record in a document the school relies on to award a Diploma. There are providers in this market that will produce assessed work to order. That is a malpractice exposure for the student, and it is not something IB Gram does at any price.

The boundary is workable and clear. A mentor may explain the outcomes, question a plan, point out that an activity will not satisfy outcome three, read a reflection and say which of the four elements is missing, rehearse an interview, and help a student build a calendar they then keep. A mentor may not write or rewrite a reflection, invent evidence, supply a project idea and call it the student's initiative, or draft any part of a portfolio entry. The same line applies to the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge: feedback on the student's own work, never production of it.

There is a related UAE rule worth knowing before any private arrangement is made. Individuals providing private tuition in the country need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years and carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. A family should never be arranging lessons with their child's own classroom teacher.
bullets: A mentor questions and returns a reflection; the student writes every word of it
No portfolio entry, project idea or reflection is ever produced for the student
Private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE permit, free of charge for two years
Abu Dhabi ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of their own students

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why CAS sign-off still sits with the IB
paragraphs: Parents often expect a regulator to adjudicate a CAS dispute. None of them will. The emirate authorities license schools, inspect them, and in several emirates approve curricula and fees; the Diploma itself, and the completion of CAS within it, is the IB's framework administered by the school's own coordinator. Knowing which body does what saves a family from writing to the wrong address when a portfolio is rejected in DP2.

Dubai's private schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah's authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge both regulate private education in their emirates and approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. All of this comes from the UAE government's own private-schools guidance.

One more thing sits alongside CAS in a UAE student's final year and is worth separating from it. Ministry of Education equivalency, which matters for admission to universities inside the country, is a documents process run by the ministry and the emirate attestation authority, not by a school or a tutor. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. No IB points threshold should be taken from any tutoring page, this one included: check it on the ministry's own site, because CAS completion and equivalency are two separate gates and failing either one is sufficient on its own.

process.title: Send the portfolio as it stands
process.description: Not a tidied version. A screenshot of the CAS management system, the entries written so far, and the dates of the interviews already held. A half-built portfolio tells a mentor more in five minutes than a conversation does in an hour, because the gaps are visible rather than reported.

process.title: Free trial session: the outcome audit
process.description: One session spent reading the portfolio against the seven outcomes and the time left on the clock. It ends with a written gap list naming which outcomes are evidenced, which are not, and which of them can still realistically be evidenced before the third interview. No payment is taken before this session happens.

process.title: Agree the clock, not the activities
process.description: The gap list becomes a dated plan working backwards from the school's own final sign-off, with the CAS project's one-month action stage placed first because it has no give in it. Everything else is arranged around that month. The plan is the student's to keep, in their own handwriting if they prefer.

process.title: Mentor matched to the core, not to a subject
process.description: Matching looks for someone who has supervised Diploma cores and read portfolios, and whose availability fits Gulf Standard Time after the school run. If nobody suitable is free in the week you need to start, we say so and give a date rather than putting a subject tutor on core work.

process.title: Fortnightly pressure until the sign-off
process.description: Sessions every two weeks, each targeting one named outcome and one entry to rewrite, with the gap list updated so the family can see the portfolio closing. The rhythm tightens into a sprint block around the project's action and demonstration stages, then loosens again for exam term.

whyPoints.title: The clock is the product
whyPoints.description: Most CAS help sells activity ideas. The scarce thing is a dated sequence working backwards from the sign-off, with the one-month action stage placed where it still fits. A family that knows which month the demonstration stage has to happen in rarely needs rescuing in DP2.

whyPoints.title: Audited against outcomes, not hours
whyPoints.description: The first session produces a gap list against the seven CAS learning outcomes, which is the standard the coordinator actually applies. Hour totals are a school's internal monitoring tool. A portfolio can be long on hours and still be unsignable, and that is the failure we look for first.

whyPoints.title: The student writes every word
whyPoints.description: A mentor reads a reflection, names which of the four reflective elements is missing, asks the question that was avoided, and returns it. Nothing is drafted, rewritten or supplied. That boundary is the reason the portfolio remains evidence of anything at all.

whyPoints.title: Built for the UAE year
whyPoints.description: Sessions on Gulf Standard Time, post-Iftar slots through Ramadan, and planning that assumes the long summer break will interrupt a commitment rather than hoping it will not. Evidence and supervisor confirmations are recorded while an experience is live, because supervising adults leave over the summer.

whyPoints.title: Independent, and honest about limits
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any school, group, regulator or examination board. Where a mentor with the right core experience is not available for the week you need, we give you a date instead of a substitute, and we publish market rate bands rather than implying ours are the market.

whyPoints.title: One mentor across the whole core
whyPoints.description: CAS, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay compete for the same months and the same evenings. One person holding all three internal deadlines produces a sequence. Three people each asking for Thursday produces a collision, usually in the term when Higher Level coursework also peaks.

faqs.question: Does CAS count towards my child's IB points?
faqs.answer: No. CAS carries no marks and contributes nothing to the 45 points. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together can add up to three points; CAS adds none. What CAS does is gate the award itself. It is one of three core requirements a candidate must complete for the Diploma to be issued, so a student can perform well in every examined subject and still not receive the Diploma if the coordinator cannot sign CAS as complete. Treat it as a pass-fail condition attached to the whole qualification rather than as a subject that might cost a point or two.

faqs.question: How many CAS hours does the IB actually require?
faqs.answer: None. The current CAS guide sets no hours total, and the widely quoted 150-hour figure was removed from the programme requirements. What the IB asks for is sustained engagement across roughly eighteen months, a reasonable balance between Creativity, Activity and Service, and evidence against each of the seven learning outcomes. Many UAE schools still publish an hours expectation in their own CAS handbook, because a running total is easier to monitor than a portfolio is to read. Follow your school's number if it has one, but understand that the coordinator signs against evidence and reflection, not against the total.

faqs.question: What happens if CAS is not finished before the May session?
faqs.answer: The examinations proceed as normal, because CAS and the papers are separate processes. The Diploma does not. If the coordinator cannot record CAS as complete, the candidate receives certificates for individual subjects rather than the Diploma, regardless of the points earned. In practice schools chase hard through DP2 precisely to avoid this, and most incomplete cases are resolved before the final interview. The ones that are not tend to involve a missing CAS project rather than a thin portfolio, because the one-month action stage cannot be compressed into the weeks before sign-off.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma student in the UAE start CAS?
faqs.answer: In the first six weeks of DP1, with the first documented interview. That interview produces the self-review and the plan, and everything downstream is dated from it. Working forwards, at least one experience per strand should be logged in DP1 term one, project investigation and preparation in term two, and the project's one-month action stage in the second half of DP1 or the opening of DP2. A student who starts in DP2 is not short of enthusiasm; they are short of the eighteen months the programme assumes, and the stage that suffers is always the project.

faqs.question: What exactly is the CAS project, and must it last a month?
faqs.answer: Every Diploma student completes at least one CAS project, and yes, one month is the minimum duration. It must be collaborative, must pass through all five CAS stages, and may sit in any strand or combination of strands. The month is about duration rather than effort, so an intensive weekend does not qualify however much work it contains. The stages that get skipped are reflection during the action, and demonstration, which needs an audience and therefore a date in somebody else's diary. Plan the demonstration before the action starts, not afterwards.

faqs.question: Can a mentor write my child's CAS reflections?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider offering to is offering something that puts your child at risk. The portfolio is a record of the student's own experiences and thinking, and the school relies on it to award a Diploma. A mentor's work is to explain what each outcome asks for, read what the student has written, name which of the four reflective elements is missing, ask the question the student avoided, and hand it back. The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge: feedback on the student's own work, never production of it.

faqs.question: Our son plays club football in Dubai. Does that satisfy the Activity strand?
faqs.answer: It can, but attendance alone will not. The strand needs sustained commitment with development the student can show and reflect on, which means a dated record of where the skill started, where it plateaued and what changed. If he is paid for junior coaching alongside it, that part is excluded, because activity for which the student is personally rewarded does not count unless the benefit goes to a cause. The usable version is the training arc plus the reflections, with a named responsible adult at the club able to confirm his role and attendance.

faqs.question: Can a paid internship or work in the family business count for CAS?
faqs.answer: Generally no, on two separate grounds. Activity for which the student is personally rewarded financially is excluded unless the benefit is passed to a worthy cause, which rules out most paid placements. All forms of duty within the family are also excluded, which rules out the family business and the common case of looking after younger siblings every afternoon. Work experience that benefits only the student is excluded as well. The way through is to take the same skill outside the household and the payroll, to a need somebody else has identified, with a supervising adult who will confirm what was done.

faqs.question: How do we find real service opportunities in Abu Dhabi over the summer?
faqs.answer: Start before the summer, because partners lose volunteers and supervising staff for the same weeks your family is travelling. Registered organisations are the practical route, since they can confirm attendance and a role, and that confirmation is what the portfolio needs. Where a commitment will break for six weeks, record the named responsible adult, the dates and their confirmation before the break rather than afterwards, and plan the restart as part of the plan. Indirect and research service also travel well; a student out of the country can still work on material a partner has asked for.

faqs.question: What happens in the three CAS interviews, and what is recorded?
faqs.answer: The first, in the first weeks of DP1, covers the self-review, the chosen strands and the initial plan. The second, around the end of DP1, audits progress: which outcomes are evidenced, which are not, and whether the project is under way. The third, in the final term of DP2, is completion, where the student accounts for all seven outcomes. All three are documented by the coordinator or adviser. Nobody is trying to catch a student out, but one who cannot describe their own portfolio in their own words reads as one who did not build it.

faqs.question: Can one piece of work be used for both CAS and an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: No. CAS experiences must be distinct from the student's Diploma course requirements, so fieldwork done for a Biology Internal Assessment cannot also be logged as Service, and a Visual Arts piece submitted for assessment cannot also be the Creativity strand. The honest route is to run a separate strand on a related theme and reflect on it separately, which often produces better material anyway because the reflection is not constrained by an assessment criterion. Where a student has already double-logged, raise it with the adviser early rather than hoping the overlap goes unnoticed.

faqs.question: What does engagement with issues of global significance actually mean?
faqs.answer: It means a local action the student can connect, with evidence, to a wider pattern, and can describe the limits of. A beach clean-up becomes outcome six when the student has found out what the local waste data says, who it affects and what the action does and does not change. It is not outcome six because the issue sounds global. The common failure here is a fundraising total with no identified need behind it. Identify the need first, with the people affected, and the outcome follows from the reflection rather than from the scale of the activity.

faqs.question: Does CAS stop during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It relocates rather than stops. Ramadan is the richest month of the year for genuine service in this region, so a project whose action stage lands inside it rarely struggles to find real, identified need to work against. Mentoring sessions move to post-Iftar slots, and the action stage is planned around evening availability instead of afternoons. Religious devotion itself is excluded from CAS, so the logged work is the organised community activity around it, not the observance. Plan the shift in advance, because booking a supervising adult's evening during Ramadan is harder at short notice.

faqs.question: What does CAS mentoring cost in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: Market bands surveyed in October 2026 run from AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online platforms, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel priced in, and AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB specialist. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650. Those are market figures, not ours. Core work is usually billed as a fortnightly retainer or a staged project block rather than by the hour, so ask how many hours a quote assumes before comparing two of them.

faqs.question: Are these CAS sessions online, or does a mentor travel to us?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are part of the service only in India. For CAS the format costs nothing, because the work is reading and conversation: reflections are shared on screen, annotated live and handed straight back. It also widens the choice of mentor from whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive to anyone who has supervised Diploma cores, which matters more for core work than for a weekly subject lesson.

faqs.question: Does CAS affect a UAE university application or Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, and only through the Diploma. Equivalency is a documents process run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority, and no tutor performs or guarantees it. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels. No IB points threshold should be taken from a tutoring page, this one included; check it on the ministry's own site. CAS matters because without it the Diploma is not awarded at all.

faqs.question: Our child relocated mid-Diploma and the service commitment broke. What now?
faqs.answer: This is common in the UAE and it is recoverable, provided the evidence from the first placement was recorded while it was live. Bring the dates, the named responsible adult and any confirmation to the adviser, treat the broken commitment as material for a reflection on perseverance rather than a gap to hide, and rebuild around a new partner. Where the CAS project was the casualty, the one-month action stage has to be replanned rather than resumed. Starting that conversation at the next scheduled interview, not later, is what keeps the sign-off on the original clock.

ib-cas-guidance.closingHeading: Start with the gap list, not the activity list
ib-cas-guidance.closingBody: If your child is in DP1, the useful next step is small: send the portfolio as it stands, with the dates of any interviews already held. One free trial session is enough to produce a written gap list against the seven CAS learning outcomes and a dated plan working backwards from the school's own sign-off, with the project's one-month action stage placed first. If your child is already in DP2 and the portfolio is thin, the same session will tell you honestly what is still reachable and what is not. Sessions run online on Gulf Standard Time, and the reflections stay your child's own work throughout.

A school draft deadline has appeared on the calendar, the Scientific Investigation is worth a fifth of the Chemistry grade, and nobody at home can tell whether the write-up in front of them is close or nowhere near. This page counts the whole thing backwards from submission week, names the assessment criteria and the marks attached to each, and explains what a tutor working over live video can legitimately do at every stage.

ib-chemistry-ia-help.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach DP Chemistry at Standard and Higher Level and work on the Scientific Investigation as a piece of science, not a piece of writing. Expect questions about your control variables and your uncertainty columns long before anyone discusses paragraphs or formatting.

intro.heading: The investigation has a date on it, so start from the date
paragraphs: Almost every family that goes looking for IB Chemistry IA help in the UAE arrives at the same moment in the same week. The school has issued an internal deadline for a first full draft. The student has some readings in a notebook, a title that sounds like a question, and a growing suspicion that the numbers do not show what the title promised. The deadline is in eleven days. Nobody in the house knows whether that is a crisis or a normal Tuesday in DP1.

It is usually neither. The Scientific Investigation is a single piece of work carrying twenty-four marks and a fifth of the Chemistry grade, and it is the one component where a student can still change their own outcome by weeks of ordinary effort rather than by luck on the day. What makes it feel like a crisis is that the work has no visible structure from outside. A past paper has a mark scheme a parent can see. An investigation looks like a document that is either finished or not, and the gap between a mark in the low teens and a mark in the low twenties is invisible until somebody who marks these things reads it.

So this page is organised as a countdown rather than as a list of services. The milestone table below counts weeks backwards from a school draft deadline and says what should physically exist by each point: a question narrow enough to generate a trend, a method with a measured range rather than an intended one, a results table with uncertainties already in the column headings, a processed graph, and only then prose. Families who work in that order spend far less money on tutoring than families who write first and then try to rescue the chemistry afterwards.

Three things are specific to doing this in the UAE, and no competitor page in this market mentions any of them. School laboratory access here is tightly timetabled, so a method that needs four afternoons of bench time may simply be unavailable, and the student needs to know that in week one rather than week six. The Ramadan and Eid dates move each year against a school calendar that already compresses the second term, which routinely eats the fortnight a student assumed they had. And the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons that KHDA requires in every Dubai private school, whatever the licensed curriculum, sit in the same week as the Chemistry deadline and are not optional.

What follows names the assessment criteria by letter and by mark, shows where UAE students lose marks in each, sets out plainly what a tutor may and may not touch under IB academic-honesty rules, and publishes what this kind of support actually costs across the UAE market with the rates attributed to the providers who published them. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. Nobody is sent to a UAE address, and for coursework weeks that turns out to be the more useful arrangement, for reasons the comparison table sets out.
bullets: Four assessment criteria, six marks each, twenty-four in total at both SL and HL
The deadline that governs the work is your school's, not the IB's
Data first, prose last: a graph you can defend is worth more than a tidy paragraph
A tutor may question, teach and give feedback; the student writes every word
Market rates for specialist IB science support run roughly AED 200-450 per hour

ib-chemistry-ia-help.programmesIntro: Investigation skills are built across the IB continuum, not in DP1. The programmes below are described by what each one does to a student's ability to design a fair test, record a measurement honestly and say what the data does not show.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: DP Chemistry is where the Scientific Investigation sits. One independent investigation is assessed internally against four criteria and carries twenty marks in every hundred at Standard and Higher Level alike, which means an SL student and an HL student are writing to the same rubric even though the HL student has more syllabus to draw on. The remaining marks come from the written papers, so the investigation is the one component finished months before the examination window.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools the DP Chemistry investigation is typically launched late in DP1 and submitted in internal drafts across the first half of DP2. Because the May session is the one almost every UAE school sits, the practical work tends to land either side of the winter break and the first drafts collide with January mocks. Ask your school's DP coordinator for the internal timeline in writing; it is the only date that actually governs the work.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences assesses inquiry and design, and processing and evaluating, as separate criteria with their own descriptors. A student who has been taught to write a hypothesis with a reason, identify a controlled variable and comment on the reliability of their own method arrives in DP1 already holding most of the investigation skill set. A student who has only ever followed a worksheet method does not, and that gap is the single most common reason a bright DP1 chemist stalls.
programmes.countryNote: The UAE runs a large MYP cohort feeding into DP, and many families move between curricula mid-school. A student arriving into MYP 5 from an IGCSE or CBSE background has usually met practical write-ups as fixed-format exercises rather than as open investigations. Four to six sessions on experimental design in MYP 4 or 5 costs a fraction of rescuing an investigation under deadline two years later.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. A CP student taking DP Chemistry sits exactly the same investigation as a full Diploma candidate, but usually with less timetabled study time around it and a reflective project competing for the same weeks. Planning backwards matters more here, not less, because there is no slack anywhere in the term.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision is thinner across the UAE than DP provision, so a CP student taking Chemistry is often one of a very small group in their school and may be the only one at Higher Level. That tends to mean less peer discussion of the investigation and fewer worked examples in circulation, which is precisely the gap one-to-one teaching fills.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP inquiry is where the habits start: predicting, changing one thing at a time, recording what happened rather than what was supposed to happen. None of it is assessed externally and none of it appears on a transcript, but the student who learned at nine that a result which contradicts the prediction is interesting rather than wrong is the student who later writes a real evaluation instead of an apology.
programmes.countryNote: Most UAE IB schools run the full continuum on one campus, so a family choosing a PYP school is often choosing the DP their child will eventually sit. If Chemistry at Higher Level is a plausible destination, ask at the primary stage how many periods of science the upper PYP and MYP years actually get, and whether the laboratories are shared with the secondary timetable.

ib-chemistry-ia-help.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is the subject of this page, but internally assessed coursework runs through every DP subject a UAE student takes, and the deadlines overlap. The notes below say what each one demands and where its marks leak away.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The Scientific Investigation is twenty-four marks across four criteria and twenty per cent of the grade at both levels. Marks are lost most often in Data analysis: raw tables without uncertainties in the headings, processing that stops at an average, and graphs with no error bars or no attempt at a gradient. Organic reaction mechanisms and equilibrium dominate the written papers, so an investigation built on kinetics or on an equilibrium shift also pays twice.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The same four-criterion investigation, the same twenty per cent, but with biological variation to contend with. Students who take five measurements of a living system and then report a mean to four decimal places lose Evaluation marks they never knew existed. Statistical treatment is the differentiator: a standard deviation and a sensible comment on sample size reads as scientific maturity to a moderator.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics investigations usually produce cleaner data than Chemistry ones and are judged accordingly. A linearised graph is close to expected, so a student who plots raw against raw and fits a curve by eye has already capped Data analysis. Uncertainty propagation through a multi-step calculation is where Physics candidates separate from each other, and it is a teachable skill rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The mathematical exploration is twenty marks and a different beast: no laboratory, no apparatus, and a personal engagement expectation that punishes a topic lifted from a list. For a Chemistry student, AA HL is the route most UAE and UK medicine and engineering admissions tutors expect to see, and the overlap with Chemistry is real in rates, logarithms and equilibrium constants.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI carries the same exploration requirement but with statistics and modelling at its centre, which makes it the friendlier partner for a Chemistry student whose investigation leans on regression and correlation. Check prerequisites before choosing: some engineering and physical-science programmes still specify AA, and switching route in DP2 is close to impossible.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: ESS sits across the sciences and individuals-and-societies groups and carries its own internally assessed investigation. Chemistry students often find the environmental framing easier to design around, because a fieldwork or secondary-data investigation can be completed without competing for laboratory time. The risk is a question so broad that no trend emerges from the data at all.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: SEHS investigations attract students who want a human physiological measurement rather than a bench reaction. The ethical and consent requirements are stricter as a result, and a UAE school will usually require written approval before any participant is tested. Build that approval step into the timeline; students routinely lose a fortnight waiting for it.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The Computer Science solution is a developed product with documentation rather than an experiment, but the planning discipline is identical: a client, success criteria agreed in advance, and evidence of testing against them. Chemistry students taking CS often use their own investigation data as the dataset, which is efficient provided the two write-ups remain genuinely separate pieces of work.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The TOK essay and exhibition are not science, but they consume the same DP2 weeks as the Chemistry investigation and are marked externally. Families planning a support block almost always underestimate this collision. A student who schedules the TOK essay and the Chemistry draft in the same ten days will do one of them badly.

ib-chemistry-ia-help.regionsTitle: Where in the UAE this comes up, and what changes by emirate
ib-chemistry-ia-help.regionsIntro: Laboratory access, term pressure and the number of Chemistry teachers in a department all vary by emirate and by school size. These notes describe what families in each place actually run into during an investigation term.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest IB pool in the country, with 227 private schools and seventeen curricula under KHDA and seven further schools opening for 2026-27, three of them IB. Large Dubai DP cohorts mean a Chemistry department of several teachers and generally decent bench access, but also fixed laboratory timetables booked weeks ahead.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. DP cohorts are often smaller than Dubai's, so a Higher Level Chemistry set can be a handful of students sharing one teacher, and an investigation question outside that teacher's own specialism gets less scrutiny before submission.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves curricula, courses and assessment methods as well as fees. Many Sharjah families commute into Dubai schools, which turns a 4pm laboratory slot into a two-hour round trip and makes after-dinner online sessions the only workable option.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. The IB provision is thinner than in Abu Dhabi city, so a student needing Higher Level Chemistry support frequently cannot find anyone locally who has taught the current guide. This is the clearest case for live video delivery rather than a search within driving distance.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education is regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which also approves tuition fees, curricula and assessment methods. RAK appears in no competitor page in this market. Families here typically have one or two realistic school options and almost no local specialist Chemistry tuition market at all.

regions.name: Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in these three emirates. DP Chemistry is offered in very few schools, and students often travel to Sharjah or Dubai for it. Online one-to-one is not a second-best arrangement here; it is the only way to reach a specialist in the subject at the right level.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's IB cohort is about seven per cent of the emirate's private-school pupils, which still makes it one of the largest DP populations in the Gulf. Students we support sit DP Chemistry at schools including those below. Internal draft deadlines differ by several weeks between them, which is why we plan from your school's calendar rather than a generic one.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain IB World Schools
schoolClusters.note: ADEK-regulated schools in the capital run smaller DP sets than Dubai's, and a Higher Level Chemistry group of five or six students is common. Students we support sit DP Chemistry at schools including those listed here, and several have told us their investigation was launched in the same fortnight as their TOK exhibition.

sections.heading: What the Scientific Investigation is, and what the twenty-four marks are for
paragraphs: A DP Chemistry student submits one independent scientific investigation. It is marked by the subject teacher against four published criteria, each worth six marks, giving twenty-four in total, and it contributes twenty per cent of the final Chemistry grade at Standard Level and at Higher Level alike. That last point surprises most parents: the Higher Level student has roughly half again as much syllabus to learn and sits a longer paper, but the investigation weighting is identical.

The four criteria are Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation. They are not four sections of a document, although students treat them that way. Research design marks are earned by the methodological decisions a student can justify, which means a clearly identified independent and dependent variable, a stated and controlled set of other variables, and a range chosen because it will generate a trend rather than because it fits the apparatus. Data analysis marks live in the treatment of the numbers: recorded raw data with units and uncertainties, processing that goes beyond an average, and a graphical representation that actually supports the claim being made.

Conclusion asks for an interpretation of the student's own results compared against the accepted chemistry, with a source cited for the comparison value. Evaluation asks what the method's real weaknesses were and what a better version would look like, and this is the criterion where honest work outscores polished work. A student who identifies a systematic error they genuinely suspect, explains its direction, and proposes a specific correction will beat a student who lists three generic improvements about repeating the experiment more times.

The table below sets out the criteria with their marks and the failure that costs the most in each. It is the piece of information no page competing for IB Chemistry IA help in the UAE currently publishes at all, and it is the first thing a family should read, because it tells you what to look at when your child hands you a draft and asks if it is any good.

sections.heading: The investigation counted backwards from your school's draft deadline
paragraphs: Every family that asks for help with a Chemistry investigation asks the same first question in a different form: is there still time? The answer depends entirely on which milestone has already been passed, not on how many weeks remain. A student ten weeks out with no question is in more trouble than a student three weeks out with clean data, because data takes bench time and bench time is the one resource that cannot be compressed.

So the planning runs backwards. Fix the school's internal draft deadline first, in writing, from the coordinator. Then place the practical work far enough before it that a failed first attempt is survivable, because the first attempt usually does fail in some respect: the concentration range gives readings too close together, the reaction is too fast to time by hand, or the balance resolution swallows the mass change. Students who allow one spare laboratory session for the repeat finish calmly. Students who do not, do not.

The IB's own assessment timetable sits behind all of this, and it is the part that cannot move. The May session is the one almost every UAE school sits, and marks for internally assessed work have to be with the IB well before results are issued, which is why schools set internal deadlines that feel early. No IB session or results date is published on this page: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so confirm every IB date with your school's DP coordinator or on ibo.org directly rather than trusting a figure found on a tutoring site.

The milestone table below is the version we actually plan sessions from. Weeks are counted back from the school draft deadline, not from the examination. Where a row says what should exist, it means a physical artefact a parent could look at, because an IB Chemistry IA deadline is missed one invisible week at a time.

sections.heading: Where Chemistry investigations actually lose marks
paragraphs: The failures are consistent enough to list. The most common is a research question that cannot produce a trend: too broad to constrain the variables, or with a range so narrow that every reading sits inside its own uncertainty. A student investigating reaction rate across three concentrations has three points, and three points do not establish a relationship. Five or six well-spaced concentrations with repeats at each is a different piece of work entirely, and the difference is decided in week one, not in the write-up.

The second is uncertainty treatment, and it is the clearest single separator in IB Chemistry HL data analysis. A burette reading carries an uncertainty. A balance carries one. A thermometer carries one. Those uncertainties have to appear in the raw table headings, be propagated through every calculation, and end up as error bars on the graph. Students who add a sentence saying that equipment has limitations, without ever carrying a number through, lose marks in Data analysis and then lose more in Evaluation because they have no quantitative basis for judging whether their result and the accepted value genuinely disagree.

The third is a conclusion that answers the hypothesis instead of the data. If the trend flattens at high concentration, say so and explain it; do not report a straight-line relationship because that was the prediction. Examiners reward a student who notices that their own numbers misbehave. The fourth is an evaluation built from a template: repeat more trials, use more accurate equipment, control the temperature better. Those sentences appear in thousands of drafts and earn almost nothing, because none of them is tied to an observed feature of this student's own results.

The fifth is specific to this market. UAE schools run tight laboratory timetables and many DP Chemistry sets share benches with IGCSE classes. A student whose method needs an hour of undisturbed bench time, three times over, may be designing an investigation their own school cannot host. Discovering that in week eight rather than week two is what turns a manageable piece of coursework into the eleven-day emergency this page opened with.

sections.heading: Choosing a Chemistry IA research question a UAE school lab can host
paragraphs: Question choice is where the most marks are won for the least effort, and where the least help is usually available. A subject teacher with twenty investigations to supervise can give each student a few minutes of feasibility discussion. That is enough to catch an obviously impossible plan and not nearly enough to turn a vague interest into a question with a measurable variable and a sensible range.

The practical constraint in UAE schools is apparatus and time rather than imagination. Controlled-temperature work needs a water bath that may be shared across three year groups. Anything involving a spectrophotometer depends on whether the school owns one and whether DP students are allowed on it unsupervised. Reactions producing gas need either a gas syringe or a mass-loss method, and the balance resolution decides whether mass loss is detectable at all. These are answerable questions, and the answers belong in week one.

The alternative routes are legitimate and underused. A database investigation using published thermodynamic or kinetic data can score full marks if the processing and evaluation are genuine, and it removes bench time from the critical path entirely. A simulation-based investigation is similarly acceptable provided the student treats the model's assumptions as part of the evaluation rather than as a disclaimer. Neither route is a soft option: the Evaluation criterion gets harder, not easier, because the student has to interrogate someone else's data collection instead of their own.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may touch and what only the student may
paragraphs: This is the part of the market that deserves scrutiny. Research into the UAE tutoring landscape in October 2026 found a provider openly selling finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is an academic-integrity breach, a malpractice trigger for the student rather than for the seller, and the consequence falls on a sixteen-year-old. Any offer of a completed piece of assessed coursework should be treated as a reason to walk away, whatever the price.

The honest boundary is not vague, and it is not restrictive either. A tutor may teach the chemistry, explain uncertainty propagation, ask why a range was chosen, point at a graph and ask what it shows, read a draft and say which criterion is weakest, and send a student away with a list of decisions to make. A tutor may not type into the student's document, dictate sentences, supply a method to copy, process the data on the student's behalf, or hand over a finished section. Everything in the submitted file must be the student's own work, produced by the student.

UAE schools take this seriously and the regulators do too. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours are required to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document, as this was press-reported. The practical implication for parents is simple: your child's own Chemistry teacher is not the right person to pay for private help on the investigation that same teacher will mark.

The table states our boundaries as a list a parent can hold us to. Nothing in it is a marketing position. It is what IB academic-honesty rules require, written out so that a family can tell the difference between teaching and the thing that gets a Diploma withheld.
