sections.heading: Moderation and grade boundaries: the two things nobody can tell you in advance
paragraphs: IB internal assessment moderation is widely misunderstood by families and occasionally by schools. The school marks its own cohort against the criteria, submits a sample to the IB, and a moderator reads that sample to judge whether the school applied the standard correctly. Where the school has been generous, marks come down; where it has been severe, marks go up. The adjustment is applied at cohort level, so a single student's mark can move because of how their classmates' work was marked, not because of anything in their own.

The practical consequence is counterintuitive. A high teacher-awarded mark is not a result, it is a prediction, and a parent who treats it as banked may get an unpleasant surprise in July. The only defence is work that is strong on its own terms: a research question with a real variable in it, data that was genuinely collected, and an evaluation that names the method's limitations honestly. Moderators are reading for whether the criteria were met, and work that plainly meets them is hard to adjust downwards.

Grade boundaries are the second thing nobody can promise. They are set after marking is complete, by senior examiners reading the evidence of how the cohort performed on that particular paper, which is why they move between sessions. Any tutor who offers to tell you what a 7 will require next summer is describing last year's boundary or inventing one. The honest version is a range from recent sessions, with the warning that it is history rather than a target, and a plan built on being clear of the line rather than near it.
bullets: A teacher-awarded internal mark is provisional until moderation is complete
Adjustments apply across a cohort, not to an individual student's file
Boundaries are set after marking, from the evidence of that session's scripts
Plan for comfortably inside a band rather than for the edge of it

sections.heading: What an examiner-badged tutor costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Examiner experience is the single largest premium in this market, and most pages competing for this search publish no number at all. Three of the six main competitors quote no price whatsoever, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The table below is the market, in AED, with each figure attributed to whoever published it. It is not an IB Gram price list.

Read it as five tiers with five different things being sold. At the bottom you are buying company and patience, which drills practice questions adequately and reads a markband poorly. In the middle you are buying someone who has taught the course and marked class work against the criteria, which covers most Standard Level needs. At the top you are buying scarcity plus a claim, and the claim is the part worth interrogating before you pay the difference.

For context, Dubai's school fees were frozen for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package, announced in May 2026, so the tutoring line is the one in a UAE family's education budget that is still moving. IB Gram's own answer to the pricing question is a free trial lesson of 45 minutes, one per family and with no card details taken, followed by a written quote for the hours actually proposed. Rates depend on subject, level and tutor, and quoting a single number for all of them would be dishonest.

sections.heading: Why this is taught online, and what that does to an exam-year plan
paragraphs: IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one online IB tuition over live video. There is no in-home service anywhere in the Emirates; that option exists only in India. The honest reason is the shape of the specialist market. There are a limited number of adults in this country who have taught Higher Level Chemistry to the current guide and marked work against its criteria, and the chance that one of them lives twenty minutes from a particular villa in Al Ain or Ajman is small.

The format also suits what examiner-informed teaching actually involves. Most of the value is in reading a marked script together: the student's own paper on screen, the criteria beside it, the tutor annotating as the reasoning is traced. That works better shared on a screen than passed across a kitchen table, and it leaves a recorded artefact the student can revisit the night before a paper. The same session can pull up a past-paper question and a markband in seconds.

In an exam year, the scheduling argument becomes the decisive one. A visiting tutor consumes an evening at both ends, which is why so many of them insist on a two-hour minimum: the travel has to be worth someone's time. An online slot can be 45 minutes on a Tuesday and 90 on a Saturday, moved after Iftar during Ramadan, and held while a family is travelling. During the final twelve weeks, that flexibility is what keeps a plan alive.

sections.heading: Academic honesty gets stricter, not looser, when a tutor has marked papers
paragraphs: Somewhere in this search results page is a provider selling finished internal assessments. One of them publishes a price for them. That is not tutoring; it is malpractice under the IB's academic-honesty rules, and the consequences land on the student, not the seller. A candidate found to have submitted work that is not their own can lose the diploma. No tutor who has actually moderated coursework would go anywhere near it, because they have seen what detection looks like from the other side of the desk.

The permitted line is clear and we will put it in writing. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain what a criterion is asking for, discuss a research question the student has proposed, rehearse a method, and comment on a draft the student has produced. A tutor may not supply sentences for an internal assessment, rewrite a paragraph of an Extended Essay, hand back a finished exploration, or sit beside a student and dictate. Where the boundary is reached, the session stops and we say so.

There is a disclosure side too. Your child's coordinator may ask whether outside help was used, and the right answer is the true one: tuition in the subject, with feedback on the student's own work. Schools are untroubled by that. What troubles them is work whose register changes halfway down a page. Keeping drafts, dated, is the student's own best protection, and it costs nothing. If a provider ever suggests that the disclosure question has a clever answer, treat that as the end of the conversation rather than as advice.
bullets: Permitted: subject teaching, criteria explanation, method rehearsal, feedback on the student's own draft

sections.heading: Results day, enquiry upon results, and the November decision
paragraphs: Results arrive through the school first and then to candidates, and the hours after that are busier than most families expect. Three decisions can be sitting on the table at once: whether to ask for a grade to be looked at again, whether to enter the November session, and whether a university offer still stands. Each has its own deadline, and the first two are short.

An enquiry upon results is the formal route for asking the IB to review a mark, and it is submitted by the school rather than by a parent. There are different categories of enquiry, there is a fee, and there is a window that closes quickly after results are released. We do not publish the date, because the IB sets it per session. What we tell families to do is ask the coordinator for the exact deadline in writing before results day, so the decision is made on evidence rather than in a rush.

The November session is a real option rather than a consolation. It gives a candidate roughly a term to rebuild one or two subjects while the rest of the diploma stands, and an examiner-informed read of the original script is the most useful input to that decision. Before committing, check what the university offer actually requires and whether it will hold for a January result, because the answer varies by institution and by country. Check too which components are retaken and which carry forward, since that decides whether the term's work is a whole course or two papers.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the figure we will not publish
paragraphs: A UAE-recognised secondary certificate is a separate piece of paperwork from an IB diploma or a set of IGCSEs, and it is what a UAE university or a federal employer asks to see. The Ministry of Education equivalency process converts a foreign qualification into that recognition. It is not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or speeds up, and no amount of tuition is required for it.

The British-track requirements are published and specific. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five subjects. One page currently ranking in this market tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects; the published figure is five, and getting that right matters more than any marketing line on the page.

For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB diploma there is a points threshold, and this page will not print a number for it, because we have not read one on the ministry's own site. Open the file in the final year, ask the school registrar which documents they issue and which you must attest yourself, and verify the current requirement at the official channel rather than from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in the same marking term
paragraphs: A UAE Diploma student is not only a Diploma student. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the federal position behind that is that private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies whatever else they offer. These lessons sit on the same timetable as Higher Level Physics, in the same week as an internal assessment deadline.

The rules around them are more specific than most parents realise. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and schools are advised that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

For tutoring, two constraints follow. Material is tightly controlled: using different or additional content for these subjects without prior permission from the ministry is prohibited, so a tutor works with the school's own scheme rather than importing a syllabus. And teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education need the appropriate approval from the regulator to teach those subjects, which is a credential worth asking about specifically. The planning point is simpler: when a Diploma family builds a revision block, these subjects are already in the week, and pretending otherwise is how a plan collapses in March.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: A message saying Chemistry Higher Level, Paper 2 technique, mocks in January is worth three messages saying help with science. Name the subject, the level, the board where it is not the IB, the session your child is sitting, and what the last marked piece of work came back as. That is enough to know whether a specialist is free.

process.title: Free 45-minute trial lesson
process.description: One per family, with no card details taken beforehand and no obligation afterwards. A specialist in that subject and level works through a recent piece of marked work with your child, over live video. You get a short written read on what the marks say, whether or not anything is booked after it.

process.title: A plan counted backwards
process.description: Before hours are agreed, we write down the dates that are already fixed: the school's internal deadlines, the mock window, the entry deadline and the session. The plan then works backwards from those rather than forwards from today, which is the difference between buying hours and buying a sequence.

process.title: Weekly sessions with session notes
process.description: A fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor, and a short note after each lesson saying what was marked, which command terms were misread and what the student is practising next. The notes are the record you use to judge whether the hours are working.

process.title: Review at the mock, and again at twelve weeks
process.description: Two scheduled points where the plan is reopened rather than continued by default: when mock papers come back, and twelve weeks before the first paper. Frequency, subject mix and session length all change at those reviews, and sometimes the honest recommendation is fewer hours in one subject and none in another.

whyPoints.title: Marking experience stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Examiner or moderator experience appears on a tutor profile only where it has been evidenced to us, with the component and the level named. Where a tutor has no marking history, the profile says nothing rather than reaching for a vaguer word. You can ask which session an appointment covered before the first paid lesson.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is the plan
whyPoints.description: Hours are planned backwards from entry deadlines, school submission dates, the mock window and the session itself. That is why this page is built as a calendar and not as a list of benefits. A plan that ignores the deadline it is working towards is a diary of lessons rather than a strategy.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed
whyPoints.description: Each AED rate on this page carries the name of whoever published it and the month we read it. Nothing here is presented as an IB Gram price except the free trial, and that comes with its conditions stated: 45 minutes, one per family, no card details. Statistics without a source do not appear.

whyPoints.title: A teaching service, in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains criteria, rehearses methods and comments on the student's own draft. A tutor does not produce assessed work in any form, at any price, and will stop a session that drifts towards it. In a market where one provider sells finished internal assessments, that boundary is worth stating plainly.

whyPoints.title: Honest unavailability
whyPoints.description: Some subject and level combinations have no specialist free in a given week. When that happens we say so and give you a realistic date, rather than putting a generalist in the slot. A Higher Level paper taught by someone who has not taught it wastes the hours and the window at the same time.

faqs.question: What does it actually mean when a tutor is described as an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: It should mean the IB appointed that person to mark a specific component in a specific session. Appointments are made session by session and carry confidentiality obligations. Assistant examiners mark scripts, team leaders check their examiners' standard, and moderators sample internally assessed work from schools. Ask which component, which level and which session, and ask what evidences it. The badge does not mean advance sight of papers, knowledge of boundaries, or any influence over who marks your child. On this site, a tutor is only described as an examiner where that appointment has been evidenced to us.

faqs.question: Can a tutor with marking experience tell us what the grade boundaries will be?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who offers to is either quoting history or inventing a number. Boundaries are set after marking is finished, by senior examiners looking at how candidates performed on that particular paper, which is why they move between sessions. A useful tutor will show you the range boundaries have occupied in recent sessions and explain that it is history rather than a target. The planning consequence is practical: build towards being comfortably inside a band rather than a mark above where last year's line happened to fall.

faqs.question: Does examiner experience give a tutor early sight of the exam papers?
faqs.answer: It does not. Examination papers are secure material and examiners receive them on the same schedule as everyone else, under confidentiality undertakings they sign before any appointment begins. Someone who hints otherwise is describing something that would be a serious breach rather than a service. What marking experience does give is familiarity with how a question type has been marked in the past, which is legitimate and genuinely useful. If a provider suggests access to unreleased material, that is a reason to walk away rather than to pay more.

faqs.question: Who moderates the mark my child's teacher awards for an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: The class teacher marks the work against the published criteria, the school submits a sample to the IB, and an IB moderator reads that sample to judge whether the school applied the standard correctly. The moderator is not reading your child's file specifically; they are checking a school's marking. Where a school has been generous, marks come down across the cohort, and where it has been severe they go up. That is why a high teacher-awarded mark is a prediction rather than a result until moderation is complete.

faqs.question: Can a moderated internal assessment mark go down as well as up?
faqs.answer: Yes. Moderation adjusts in both directions, and the adjustment is applied at cohort level rather than to an individual. A student can see their mark move because of how their classmates' work was marked. The only real defence is work that plainly meets the criteria on its own terms: a research question with a genuine variable in it, data actually collected, and an evaluation that names the method's limitations rather than praising the experiment. Work like that is difficult to adjust downwards, because a moderator can see the criteria being met.

faqs.question: Which deadline in the exam year is the last one a family can still influence?
faqs.answer: The final exam entry deadline. Once entries are submitted, subject, level and session are fixed, so a Higher Level that is not holding becomes a Higher Level your child sits. It typically falls six to eight months before the first paper, and your school submits it against the board's date. The other effectively irreversible point is your school's internal submission deadline for assessed work, after which a tutor can do nothing further on that component. Everything else in the year can be adjusted.

faqs.question: How far back from the first paper does a sensible plan start?
faqs.answer: It depends on what you want the money to buy. Starting in February of the final year buys technique and timing, which is real but bounded. Starting in the first Diploma year buys the decisions that set the ceiling: the maths route, the Higher Level pattern, and a research question that can survive a failed first attempt. Most families here start after the January mocks, and the useful version of that is a diagnosis within a fortnight of the papers coming back, followed by a twelve-week block planned by paper rather than by topic.

faqs.question: What does a command term such as evaluate instruct a marker to reward?
faqs.answer: Evaluate asks for an appraisal that weighs up strengths and limitations and reaches a judgement. A marker is looking for both sides and a supported conclusion, so an answer listing only strengths sits in the lower bands however accurate it is. State asks for a name or value with no explanation. Explain asks for reasons, with each link in the chain written down. Discuss asks for competing positions, then a weighing of them. Learning these the way vocabulary is learned is one of the cheapest grade improvements available, because in a timed paper there is no time to work out the instruction.

faqs.question: Why do two answers containing the same facts score differently?
faqs.answer: Because a mark scheme rewards a particular shape of response, not the presence of correct information. A reasoning chain with one link left implicit loses the mark for that link even when the student clearly understood it. A comparison written as two separate descriptions earns the description marks and misses the comparison ones. Marks also go to units, state symbols, labelled axes and shown working, all of which are easy to omit under time pressure. This is why reading a marked script line by line usually explains a grade better than re-reading the textbook.

faqs.question: What happens to my child's script between the exam and the grade?
faqs.answer: Written papers go to an examiner with no connection to the school, who marks against a mark scheme they have been trained and standardised on, while senior examiners check samples to keep the standard consistent. Internal assessment stays with the school's mark until a moderator has read a sample. Once marking is complete, senior examiners set the boundaries for that session from the evidence of how the cohort performed, and grades are awarded. Nothing a family does during that period changes anything, which is why the work has to be finished before it starts.

faqs.question: What does an examiner-badged tutor charge in the UAE, and is the premium worth it?
faqs.answer: The top of this market is published at AED 500 to 650 and above; BartyED lists AED 650. Below that, specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and qualified subject teachers online start around AED 150 to 300 by Unitors' published rates. All figures were read in October 2026. The premium is worth paying where the claim is evidenced and the need is genuinely Higher Level technique. For Standard Level content gaps, a qualified teacher at a third of the price usually does the same work.

faqs.question: Why is this delivered online rather than by someone sitting beside my child?
faqs.answer: Because the specialist pool is national and the driving radius is not. A limited number of adults in this country have taught Higher Level Chemistry to the current guide and marked work against its criteria, and the odds that one lives twenty minutes from a particular address in Al Ain or Ajman are poor. IB Gram does not offer in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Online also suits the work itself, since most of the value is in reading a marked script together on a shared screen.

faqs.question: Where is the honesty line when the tutor has marked that component before?
faqs.answer: Exactly where it is for any other tutor, and someone with marking experience usually guards it harder because they have seen detection from the other side. Permitted: teaching the content, explaining what a criterion asks for, discussing a question the student has proposed, rehearsing a method, and commenting on a draft the student has produced. Not permitted: supplying sentences for an internal assessment, rewriting a paragraph of an Extended Essay to completion, or handing back finished assessed work. Keep dated drafts, and answer your coordinator's question about outside help specifically and truthfully.

faqs.question: Which exam dates can we diary now, and which have to come from the school?
faqs.answer: Cambridge and Pearson publish theirs. Cambridge's March 2027 series runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026 and forecast grades 27 February 2027; results reach Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. IB session and results dates come from your coordinator or the IB itself, and this page does not restate a date it cannot source.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge zone my child's centre sits in change their timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this catches families out. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the series timetable. Cambridge's guidance for exams officers states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Take the timetable from your child's exams officer rather than from a search result, and check the zone label on the document before building a revision plan around it.

faqs.question: After results, how long is the window for asking the IB to look again?
faqs.answer: Short, and set by the IB for each session. An enquiry upon results is submitted by the school rather than by a parent, there are different categories of enquiry, and a fee applies. We do not publish the deadline because it varies by session and we will not guess one. The useful move is to ask your coordinator in writing, before results day, for the exact date and the categories available. That way the decision is made on an examiner-informed read of the script rather than in a panic.

faqs.question: Does my child need Ministry of Education equivalency before a UAE university application?
faqs.answer: A UAE-recognised secondary certificate is what a UAE university or federal employer asks for, and the Ministry of Education equivalency process is how a foreign qualification becomes one. Open the file in the final year, because document collection and attestation take longer than families expect. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. Verify current requirements at the official channel; no tutoring is required for any of it.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education marks go through the same external marking as Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: No. They sit outside the IB's assessment entirely and are governed by the emirate regulator and the federal ministry instead. They are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with Standard Arabic required as the language of instruction in defined cases. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Using different or additional content without prior ministry permission is prohibited, so a tutor works from the school's own scheme rather than bringing their own material.

ib-examiner-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the date, not from the subject
ib-examiner-tutor.closingBody: If your child sits papers next session, the first useful conversation is not about subjects at all. It is about which dates are already fixed: the school's internal submission deadlines, the mock window, the entry deadline, and the session itself. Tell us those and the component you are worried about, and we will tell you honestly whether a specialist is free and what the remaining weeks can realistically change. The trial lesson is free, 45 minutes, one per family, with no card details taken. If nobody is free at the level you need, we will say so and give you a date rather than filling the slot.

intro.heading: The cost question, answered before anything else
paragraphs: Extended Essay support in the UAE is bought in hours, not in packages. Across the market, a qualified subject tutor working online quotes roughly AED 150–300 an hour, an IB or IGCSE specialist AED 200–450 and upwards, and a premium named provider AED 500–650 or more. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts the specialist band at AED 200–450+, and the in-home band at AED 180–350. Those are market figures from October 2026, quoted as the market and not as an IB Gram price list. The honest version of our own position is that the first lesson is free, the rate depends on the subject and the level of specialism the essay needs, and you will be told the number before a block is agreed rather than after.

What moves the number is not glamour. It is the subject, the research method and how late the family starts. A History Extended Essay built from printed sources sits at the lower end of the specialist band. A Chemistry essay with a laboratory component, or a Mathematics essay that needs a proof read properly, sits at the top of it, because the pool of people who can mentor it competently in the UAE is small. An essay that arrives three weeks before the school deadline costs more than the same essay started in DP1, not because anyone is profiteering, but because rescue work is denser, longer and far less likely to move a grade.

Delivery is the part worth being blunt about. Every lesson for a UAE family happens online, one-to-one, over live video, with the draft shared on screen. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is not a limitation dressed up as a feature. An Extended Essay is a document, and a document is better reviewed on a shared screen with the comment history preserved than it is across a kitchen table with a pen. It also means a candidate in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain has the same access to a Biology Extended Essay mentor as a candidate in Emirates Hills.

There is a boundary that no amount of money moves. A tutor may teach, question, model and give criterion-referenced feedback. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite paragraphs into shape, or hand over a finished piece of work. The IB treats any other hand on the text as malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student, not on the provider. One operator in this search results page sells completed Internal Assessments. Paying for that buys an academic-integrity investigation, not a grade. Say no to it, and be wary of any quote that sounds like it includes it.

So this page is built the way a parent reads it: what Extended Essay support costs in the UAE, what drives that figure up or down, what you get for it criterion by criterion, when in the two-year cycle each hour is worth most, and what to check before money changes hands. Every AED figure carries its band and its source. Every claim about the IB rubric should still be confirmed with your child's Extended Essay coordinator, because the coordinator sets the school deadlines that actually govern your calendar.

Six to twelve mentoring hours across two years is a realistic budget; twenty in the final month rarely is

ib-extended-essay-help.programmesIntro: The Extended Essay belongs to the Diploma Programme core, but the research habit it tests is built earlier and tested differently in the Career-related Programme. Where your child sits in that sequence changes what support is worth buying and what it should cost.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is one of three core requirements alongside Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. It is an independent research piece with a 4,000-word ceiling, registered in a subject the candidate is usually studying, supervised inside the school and marked externally against five criteria worth 34 marks in total. The EE and TOK matrix converts those two grades into up to three points on the final Diploma score.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma candidates sit this inside a private school system where the IB accounted for roughly 7% of Dubai's private-school roll in 2024-25, across a sector of 227 schools. That means a large absolute number of Diploma candidates but a thin spread of specialist supervisors per subject, which is exactly why families buy outside mentoring hours. Confirm your school's internal EE deadlines with the coordinator, since those, not the IB upload window, set your spending calendar.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Personal Project in MYP Year 5 is the rehearsal for the Extended Essay: a self-chosen goal, a documented process and a reflective report. Students who learn to keep a process journal here arrive in DP1 already able to write a usable reflection, which is the cheapest six marks in the Diploma core to secure.
programmes.countryNote: A good number of UAE schools run the MYP as a continuum into the Diploma, so the same coordinator often oversees both. Families who spend two or three hours on Personal Project process skills in Year 11 routinely spend fewer hours on Extended Essay rescue in DP2. Support at this stage is priced at the qualified-tutor band rather than the specialist band, which makes it the better value of the two.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP candidates complete a Reflective Project rather than an Extended Essay. It is shorter, ethics-focused and tied to the career-related study, but it is marked on the same habits: a defensible question, evidence, analysis and honest reflection. Mentoring is charged in the same bands, and the planning work transfers almost completely.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in the UAE is far narrower than DP provision, so a family looking for Reflective Project support locally often finds nobody within reach. Online delivery removes that constraint entirely: the mentor is chosen for knowing the ethical-dilemma framework, not for living in the same emirate. Ask any provider directly whether they have mentored a Reflective Project before, because many have not.

programmes.name: Pre-DP and IGCSE research skills
programmes.description: Year 10 and Year 11 students heading into the Diploma gain more from a short block on referencing, source evaluation and academic style than from early subject cramming. These are the skills behind criterion D and most of criterion B, and they are far cheaper to teach before an essay exists than during one.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE candidates move from Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE into the Diploma in the same school, and the step up in independent research is where DP1 reports most often slip. A four-hour block at the qualified-tutor band in Year 11 is the single cheapest intervention available to a UAE family planning two years ahead. It also makes the first reflection session a genuine conversation rather than an improvisation.

ib-extended-essay-help.subjectsIntro: An Extended Essay is registered in a subject, and the subject decides who can mentor it and at what rate. The routes below are the ones UAE candidates choose most often. Each note says what the essay tends to demand and where the mark loss concentrates.

subjects.name: Biology Extended Essay
subjects.description: Usually experimental or field-based, which makes the method the expensive part. Candidates lose criterion A marks for a question no controlled experiment can answer, and criterion C marks for reporting results without interrogating uncertainty. Mentoring hours are worth most before data collection starts, not after.

subjects.name: Chemistry Extended Essay
subjects.description: Laboratory access, risk assessment and the school's willingness to host the practical set the ceiling here. The commonest failure is an investigation that is really a recipe: it produces numbers but no argument. Sessions focus on building a question with a variable worth changing and a justified analytical technique.

subjects.name: Physics Extended Essay
subjects.description: Either an experiment with honest error analysis or a modelling study with defensible assumptions. Marks drain away in criterion C when a candidate presents a graph and stops. A mentor's job is to make the student explain why the gradient means what they say it means, in the subject's own vocabulary.

subjects.name: Mathematics Extended Essay
subjects.description: The hardest route to mentor well and the one with the smallest UAE tutor pool, which pushes it to the top of the specialist band. Essays fail on scope: a topic either collapses into textbook exposition or expands past anything a candidate can prove. Early question-shaping is the whole game.

subjects.name: Economics Extended Essay
subjects.description: A local research question with real data is the strongest form, and the UAE supplies plenty of them. Candidates lose marks by describing a market rather than applying a model to it, and by using a diagram as decoration. Sessions drill the link from theory to the evidence actually gathered.

subjects.name: Business Management Extended Essay
subjects.description: Primary research is permitted and often encouraged, which creates ethics and consent questions a supervisor must sign off. The frequent problem is a consultancy report with no academic argument. Mentoring turns a company case into a question a framework can genuinely test.

subjects.name: History Extended Essay
subjects.description: Source-led, and the cheapest route to mentor because the research needs no laboratory. Marks go on an unresolved historiographical debate and on narrative that never becomes argument. Candidates in the UAE working on regional topics need early help locating sources beyond the first page of search results.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature Extended Essay
subjects.description: A close-reading argument about a text or a body of language use. The usual failure is a question so broad that the essay becomes a survey. Sessions narrow the corpus until 4,000 words can do justice to it, then work on holding one analytical line through the whole piece.

subjects.name: Psychology Extended Essay
subjects.description: Almost always a literature-based study, because experimental work on human participants raises consent issues a school will rarely approve. Marks are lost when studies are summarised one after another with no critical comparison. Mentoring targets evaluation: design, sampling, ecological validity, replication.

subjects.name: World Studies Extended Essay
subjects.description: A World Studies Extended Essay takes a global issue through two subject lenses and demands genuine interdisciplinarity rather than two half-essays stapled together. It is the most interesting route and the most commonly mishandled. Expect the specialist band, because the mentor needs credible footing in both subjects.

ib-extended-essay-help.regionsIntro: The regulator changes across the seven emirates, and so does the local supply of Diploma supervisors. Online delivery means the mentor is the same wherever you sit; what differs is how much you were short of locally in the first place.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. The largest Diploma cohort in the country sits here, across a private sector of 227 schools in 2024-25. Supervisor time is still rationed per cohort, so most paid Extended Essay hours in the UAE are bought by Dubai families.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, so an Abu Dhabi family cannot simply pay their child's own supervisor for extra hours.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a far thinner spread of IB World Schools than the island. A Mathematics or World Studies Extended Essay mentor is unlikely to be available within driving distance, which is the clearest case in the country for buying the specialist online rather than compromising locally.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That makes SPEA a curriculum authority, not only an inspector. Diploma provision is modest, and several Sharjah families have a child commuting into Dubai for the programme.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. IB provision is limited, so Extended Essay candidates are often the only one in their subject at the school. Online mentoring is frequently the only route to a subject-matched reader.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like SPEA, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. RAK returned zero mentions across the competitor pages researched for this project, which is a fair measure of how little attention northern-emirate Diploma families are given.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Diploma candidates on the east coast face the longest journey to any specialist tutor pool in the country, and a 4pm in-home session is simply not purchasable. A 7pm online session in Gulf Standard Time is, at the same rate as Dubai.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market in the UAE, with effectively no local market for Extended Essay mentoring in a named subject. Families here pay the same online band as everyone else, which is the point of delivering it that way.

schoolClusters.note: The deepest Diploma provision in the country, and the cluster where Extended Essay supervision is most likely to be formalised with internal deadlines and a taught research-skills programme. Students we support attend schools in this group; the names are listed as context for the school system, not as relationships.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School – Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.note: ADEK territory, where the ethics rules on tutoring your own school's students bite hardest. Diploma cohorts are smaller than Dubai's, so a subject with four candidates may share a supervisor with no background in the research method the essay needs. That gap is what paid mentoring hours close here.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: Provision thins sharply north of Dubai, and some families commute across emirate lines for the Diploma. Verify any school's current programme authorisation on the regulator's own listing before assuming it runs the DP, because provision in this cluster changes more often than in Dubai.
schools: Sharjah American International School – Sharjah campus

ib-extended-essay-help.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as context for the UAE school system only; no affiliation, partnership or endorsement is implied, and every name should be checked against the relevant regulator's own school listing.
ib-extended-essay-help.modesIntro: Extended Essay support is sold in four recognisable shapes, and they are not interchangeable. Choosing the wrong one is the most common way a UAE family overpays: a full mentoring block bought for an essay that needed one draft read, or a single read bought for an essay with no research question yet.

modes.title: Fixed Extended Essay mentoring block
modes.description: Eight to twelve one-to-one online sessions spread from the subject decision in DP1 to the final submission in DP2, with the hours deliberately front-loaded. Priced per hour at the specialist band, agreed in advance, and bookable in halves so the budget follows the calendar rather than a sales plan. The block is the right purchase when the essay has not been started.

Two criterion-marked reads: structure, then final

modes.title: Subject tuition with Extended Essay time attached
modes.description: A weekly subject lesson for Chemistry HL or History HL, with twenty to thirty minutes of each session given to the essay registered in that subject. The best value option for families already buying subject tuition, because the mentor is already holding the syllabus context the essay sits inside and no second relationship has to be built.
bullets: One tutor, one rate, two problems addressed
Essay progress tracked against the school's internal deadlines

modes.title: Single Extended Essay draft review
modes.description: One ninety-minute read of a complete draft, returned marked against criteria A to E with a prioritised fix list the student keeps. No ongoing commitment. This is the honest purchase for a candidate who is basically on track and wants a second reader who knows the rubric, and it is how most families should start.

A fix list ordered by marks per hour of student effort

modes.title: Research-methods and data-handling block
modes.description: Three to four sessions on the mechanics: controlling a variable, treating uncertainty, evaluating a source, building a reference list, using a spreadsheet or statistical tool honestly. Bought before the research starts, it is the hours that most often prevent a second data-collection round, which is the single most expensive thing that can happen to an Extended Essay.

Source evaluation for literature-based essays
Referencing set up once, consistently, in the school's chosen style
A process journal the student can actually use for the RPPF

sections.heading: What "Extended Essay help" actually buys
paragraphs: Extended Essay help in the UAE is a mentoring relationship around a piece of work the student owns. In practice it means a subject specialist who reads drafts against the published criteria, asks the questions a supervisor has no time to ask, and tells you which marks are genuinely recoverable and which are not. It does not mean a second author, and no price buys one legitimately.

That distinction matters more here than in most markets, because the same search results page that lists tutors also lists operators selling finished coursework outright. One of them advertises completed Internal Assessments at a four-figure AED price. A family who buys that is not buying a grade; they are buying an academic-honesty investigation with the candidate's name on it. The IB's response to malpractice falls on the student, and no refund policy reverses it.

The useful question is therefore not "who will help with the essay" but "what specifically will be done in each hour, and what will my child have afterwards that they did not have before". A good answer sounds like: after this hour your daughter will have a research question with a defined variable, a method she can describe in two sentences, and three sources she has read rather than found. A weak answer sounds like reassurance.

Everything on this page is organised around that test. The rate tables show what the UAE market charges and who charges it. The criteria table shows where the 34 marks sit so you can see which hours are worth buying. The permission table shows the line a tutor may not cross. The calendar table shows when each hour is worth most. If a provider cannot be measured against those four things, the quote is not comparable to anything.
bullets: Ask what the student will hold at the end of the hour, not what the tutor will cover
Ask for feedback in writing, so the school supervisor can see it
Ask which criterion each session targets, by letter
Walk away from anything described as a completion or finishing service

sections.heading: What Extended Essay support costs across the UAE
paragraphs: The Extended Essay cost in AED that a UAE family actually pays depends almost entirely on which of six market products they buy. Three published UAE market sources and a 2026 Dubai rate survey give the bands below. A budget online tutor starts around AED 45–65 an hour and some platforms advertise from the low AED 30s; a qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150–300; an IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist sits at AED 200–450 and above; a premium named provider publishes up to AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits, which are the market norm rather than our model, run AED 180–500 once travel is inside the hour.

Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars — a currency no UAE family transacts school fees in. That is why the table below exists. It is also why each band is given with the provider model that quotes it rather than a brand name: a model-level comparison is checkable, and quoting a rival's number without its date and source URL is not fair comment.

Read the table as a ceiling and a floor, not a price list. IB Gram's own position is deliberately simple and is not in the table: the first lesson is free, the hourly figure depends on the subject and the specialism the essay needs, and you hear the number before anything is booked. Monthly packages circulating in the Dubai market give a useful sanity check — around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599–1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. If a quote sits far outside every band here, ask what explains it, in writing.

One figure deserves its own sentence. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package. Tutoring is not covered by that freeze. A family budgeting the Diploma core should assume school fees flat and support hours variable, which argues for buying a small number of well-timed hours rather than a standing weekly commitment that runs for two years.

sections.heading: Five things that move the number up or down
paragraphs: Subject is the first lever. A History or Psychology Extended Essay is literature-based and can be mentored by a wider pool, so it sits at the lower end of the specialist band. A Mathematics essay, or a World Studies Extended Essay crossing two subjects, needs a mentor with credible footing in territory few tutors hold, and the price follows the scarcity rather than the difficulty.

Method is the second. An experimental Biology or Chemistry essay carries risk assessment, equipment access and uncertainty analysis, and the mentoring hours cluster before data collection because a flawed method cannot be fixed by better prose. Literature-based essays spread their hours more evenly and cost less in total, because nothing has to be redone in a laboratory.

Timing is the third and the most expensive. Hours bought in DP1, while the question is still movable, change the essay. Hours bought three weeks before a school deadline mostly triage it. Rescue sessions are longer, denser and often need two tutors' worth of attention in one, and the marks available by then are concentrated in criteria D and E rather than C, where most of the 34 sit.

The fourth is scope. An essay already 5,200 words long needs a thousand words removed without losing an argument, which is slower work than writing them was. The fifth is what the school already supplies. If the supervisor's allocated hours are real and the internal deadlines are enforced, a single Extended Essay draft review may be the entire sensible purchase. If the supervisor is covering a subject they do not teach, the block is the honest answer. Ask the coordinator which situation you are in before you buy anything.

sections.heading: The 34 marks you are paying to protect
paragraphs: The Extended Essay criteria A to E carry 34 marks between them, and they are not evenly weighted. Criterion C, critical thinking, carries 12 — more than focus and method plus knowledge and understanding combined. Presentation carries 4. Engagement, assessed through the three reflections recorded on the Reflections on Planning and Progress Form, carries 6. Any family deciding where to spend money should start from that distribution rather than from a tutor's preferred order of work.

The practical consequence is counter-intuitive. The cheapest marks in the whole component are the engagement marks, because preparing a reflection takes under an hour and most candidates write all three in one panicked sitting at the end, which reads exactly as it was produced. The most expensive marks are in criterion C, because moving an essay from description to analysis means rebuilding paragraphs the student has grown attached to. A mentor who starts with presentation is optimising the smallest number on the sheet.

Criterion A is where UAE candidates most often lose marks before they have written a word. A research question that cannot be answered inside 4,000 words is a design fault, not a writing fault, and no amount of later support recovers the marks. This is the single strongest argument for buying one hour early rather than five late, and it is the reason the first session in any mentoring block is about narrowing the question until it has a findable answer.

Treat the table below as a map of where your money does work, and confirm the current rubric and mark allocations with your child's Extended Essay coordinator or on ibo.org before relying on them. Rubrics are revised, schools hold the authoritative version, and a page on the internet is not a substitute for the coordinator who will apply it.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do, and what only your child may do
paragraphs: This is the section that should decide which provider you pay. Under IB academic-honesty rules the Extended Essay must be the candidate's own work, supervised inside the school, with the supervisor commenting on one full draft and signing the RPPF. An external mentor sits outside that structure and so has to be more careful, not less. The useful test is whether a sentence in the final document could have originated anywhere other than the student's own keyboard.

A mentor may teach subject content, explain a criterion, model how an analytical paragraph works using a different example, ask the questions that expose a weak claim, mark a draft against the rubric, and tell a student plainly that a section is not yet analysis. A mentor may not supply sentences for the essay, restructure paragraphs on the student's behalf, correct grammar line by line, or hand back a version that has been edited into shape. The second list is not a style preference; it is the boundary between teaching and malpractice.

Line-by-line grammar correction deserves naming because it looks harmless and is not. If a tutor fixes every error, criterion D measures the tutor. The defensible version is to show the student the pattern — comma splices, tense drift in a methodology, inconsistent citation of the same source — and have the student find and fix the rest. It takes longer in the session and it is the only version that leaves the marks with the candidate.

Everything a mentor says should also be visible to the school. Written feedback that the student can forward to their supervisor protects the candidate, keeps the supervisor informed, and makes the whole relationship auditable if the school ever asks. Any provider reluctant to put their feedback in writing is telling you something about what the feedback contains.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from submission: where the hours are worth most
paragraphs: No competitor page researched for this project names a single Extended Essay milestone, which is strange, because the calendar is what determines whether support works. The dates that govern a UAE family are set by the school, not by the IB: your coordinator fixes the internal proposal, draft and final deadlines, and those sit well ahead of the IB upload. Ask for them in writing at the start of DP1 and build the budget around them.

The shape of a well-spent budget is front-loaded and tapering. One or two hours before the subject is locked, one before the first reflection session, two to four around the method, one or two on structure at the interim reflection, two on a marked full draft, one on referencing and presentation, and one rehearsing the viva voce. That is roughly six to twelve hours across two years. At the specialist band it is a planned expense rather than an emergency one.

Compare that with the pattern most families actually fall into: nothing until DP2, then eight to fifteen hours in the final month at whatever rate is available, aimed at the four presentation marks and whatever can still be salvaged in criterion C. The money spent is similar or higher. The marks protected are far fewer, and the student is more frightened. The difference is entirely scheduling.

Extended Essay supervision hours inside school are finite and usually shared across a cohort, which is why the table below separates what the school gives you from what you might buy. One note on IB dates: no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, so confirm every IB-set deadline with your coordinator or on ibo.org rather than trusting a figure found online. Cambridge and Pearson publish their own timetables, and entry deadlines there sit months before the exams — Cambridge's March 2027 series, for example, closes final entries on 27 November 2026 for a February exam window.

sections.heading: Subject choice and the research question: the decision that costs most to get wrong
paragraphs: Most expensive Extended Essay problems are decisions, not writing. Registering the essay in a subject the candidate does not study is permitted in some circumstances and is almost always a mistake, because criterion B is marked on subject-specific knowledge the student has not been taught. Registering it in a Higher Level subject the student is strong in, on a question that subject can genuinely test, removes a whole class of later difficulty for free.

The research question itself fails in three recognisable ways. It is too broad, so the essay becomes a survey and criterion C has nothing to grip. It is unanswerable with the evidence available in the UAE, which usually means a laboratory the school does not have or an archive nobody can reach. Or it is already answered in a textbook, so the essay is exposition. A single hour with a subject specialist will usually expose which of the three a draft question is.

A World Studies Extended Essay adds a fourth failure mode: two subjects placed side by side without being made to talk to each other. Done properly it is a strong route and a genuinely interesting one, and UAE-based global issues — water, labour mobility, urban heat, trade routes — supply more good questions than most candidates realise. Done badly it is two half-essays, and the mentoring cost of repairing it is higher than starting again.

The practical move is cheap. Before the subject is locked, write three candidate questions, each in one sentence, each with the evidence you would need named beside it. Take all three to one session. A specialist can tell you within the hour which has a findable answer, which needs narrowing, and which should be abandoned. That is the highest-value hour available on the whole component, and it costs the same as any other.
bullets: Register the essay in a subject the candidate actually studies
Write three one-sentence questions with their evidence named beside them
Test each against: too broad, unanswerable here, or already answered
For World Studies, make the two subjects argue with each other, not take turns

sections.heading: Online delivery, Gulf Standard Time and the Ramadan calendar
paragraphs: Every lesson for a UAE family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with the draft open on a shared screen and the feedback kept. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. The case for online delivery on this component is unusually strong, because an Extended Essay is a document: tracked comments, a version history and a recording beat a pen on a printout, and the student can revisit what was said in week three when they are editing in week twenty.

The second argument is supply. An online Extended Essay tutor is chosen for having mentored that subject before, not for living within a reasonable drive. For a Mathematics or World Studies essay in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain, the local pool is often empty, and the honest alternative to online is not in-home tutoring — it is nothing. Where a subject genuinely has no UAE-resident specialist free, the match is made with a specialist elsewhere and you are told so before booking, at the rate quoted.

Scheduling is where Gulf Standard Time does real work. UAE school days end early and traffic peaks around 6pm, which is exactly when in-home sessions have to travel. An online session at 7.30pm costs the same hour of tutoring with none of the commute, and a candidate in Sharjah is not paying for a tutor's drive from Dubai. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar timing without changing the rate, and in exam weeks they pause rather than running out of obligation.

The comparison below is the one competitor pages avoid. Only one researched page in the whole area cluster publishes any version of it, and it has three generic rows. Read it as a reality check on what each option delivers for the money rather than a claim that one is better for every family.

sections.heading: Before you pay: the permit, the regulator and the own-school rule
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone, and a figure circulating online as a specific sum is not verifiable. What a parent can do is simple and rarely done: ask to see the permit before the first paid session, and treat reluctance as an answer.

There is one rule that catches UAE families out repeatedly. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars the same arrangement. So the most tempting option — paying your child's own Extended Essay supervisor for extra hours — is the one option to decline. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document, since this has been reported in the press rather than quoted from the source here.

The regulators themselves are worth naming because almost nobody in this market does. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. SPEA regulates private education in Sharjah and approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same. The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram holds no permit, licence or endorsement from any of them and does not claim one; a tuition business with premises in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different thing entirely.
