sections.heading: What the Extended Essay does and does not do for a UAE university application
paragraphs: Parents sometimes buy Extended Essay support under the impression that the component carries weight with the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process. It does not, and nobody should sell it that way. The equivalency rules that have been published are curriculum-specific and subject-count based. For the British track, candidates must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five.

That last detail is worth holding on to, because a ranking competitor page states UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The published rule is five, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB track, no points threshold is published here, because none has been read on a Ministry of Education source. Any site quoting an IB equivalency score without that citation is guessing, and inheriting someone else's guess is how a family makes a decision on a number nobody can stand behind. Check the requirement on the Ministry's own channel or with the emirate attestation authority, and treat this page as a pointer rather than an authority. IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency or attestation for anyone.

Where the Extended Essay does earn its keep is the Diploma itself and the applications that follow it. The EE and TOK matrix converts the two core grades into up to three points on the final score, and those points decide offers at the margin. A grade E in either the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge is a failing condition for the Diploma. Universities also read the essay as evidence of independent research, which matters for competitive courses. Those are real reasons to spend on it. Equivalency is not one of them, and no tutoring is required for a regulatory process.
bullets: British track: five IGCSE or GCSE subjects at E or grade 3 minimum, Arabic and Islamic education excluded
Plus one A-Level at grade E or two AS-Levels at the same grade
American track: SAT Math 450+, and IELTS 5 / TOEFL iBT 61 / SAT reading-writing 450
IB track: verify any points figure on a Ministry of Education source before relying on it
A grade E in the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge is a failing condition for the Diploma

process.title: Tell us the subject, the stage and the school deadline
process.description: The three facts that decide everything: which subject the essay is registered in, whether a research question exists yet, and the date the school has set for the full draft. With those, we can tell you whether you are buying one Extended Essay draft review or a full mentoring block, before anyone discusses money.

process.title: Hear the rate and the shape of the plan
process.description: You are given the hourly figure, the number of hours the stage actually warrants, and which criterion each session targets. If the honest answer is that two hours will do, that is the answer. If no UAE-resident specialist in that subject is free, you are told so and told where the match would come from instead.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One introductory online session with the proposed mentor, with no payment taken and no card details asked for. It exists so the student can judge whether this person asks useful questions about their work. Bring the research question, or the three candidate questions, and treat it as the subject-choice session it usually becomes.

process.title: Work the calendar, not the panic
process.description: Sessions are booked against the school's internal deadlines rather than a fixed weekly slot, which means hours cluster before the method and before each draft and thin out in between. Feedback comes in writing after every session so the student can forward it to their supervisor and the school can see exactly what was said.

process.title: Review what the hours bought, then stop or continue
process.description: After the marked full draft, you decide whether the remaining hours are worth it. Many families stop there, having bought a referencing pass and a viva voce rehearsal and nothing more. Stopping is a normal outcome, not a failed retention; a mentoring block that runs out of useful work should end.

whyPoints.title: The rate is quoted before the sale, not after
whyPoints.description: Three of the six competitor pages researched publish no price anywhere, and one has an FAQ that asks the price and then declines to answer it. You get a number, the market bands it sits inside, and the source of those bands. If a provider will not give you a figure before a consultation, that is information about the figure.

whyPoints.title: Hours are recommended against the mark distribution
whyPoints.description: Criterion C carries 12 of the 34 marks and the engagement marks cost an hour to protect. Sessions are proposed in that order rather than in the order that fills a calendar. If the sensible purchase is a single draft review, that is what is recommended, and the mentoring block is left on the shelf.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is written down and held
whyPoints.description: Your child writes every sentence. A mentor teaches, questions, models with other examples, and marks drafts against the criteria in writing. Nothing is supplied, rewritten or edited into shape, and the feedback is sent in a form you can forward to the school supervisor. The boundary protects the candidate, which is the only person it can harm.

whyPoints.title: Subject-matched mentors rather than whoever is nearby
whyPoints.description: An Extended Essay is marked on subject-specific knowledge, so a general essay tutor cannot defend criterion B. Mentors are matched to the registered subject and to the research method, which is why a Mathematics essay in Al Ain and a History essay in Dubai are handled by different people at different points in the band.

whyPoints.title: Online, in Gulf Standard Time, with the record kept
whyPoints.description: Live video, the draft on a shared screen, feedback in writing, and sessions timed around UAE school days, the 6pm traffic peak and post-Iftar hours during Ramadan. No travel is billed because none happens. Home visits are a service offered in India, and that is stated plainly rather than implied away.

whyPoints.title: Sources named, including where we do not know
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page carries its market source and date. The permit and regulator facts come from u.ae, mohre.gov.ae and KHDA's own documents. Where a figure has not been verified — any IB session date, any IB equivalency threshold — the page says so and points you at the authority instead of guessing.

faqs.question: How much should a UAE family expect to pay for Extended Essay support?
faqs.answer: Market rates in the UAE run roughly AED 150–300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200–450 and upwards for an IB specialist, with premium named providers publishing up to AED 650. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives the specialist band as AED 200–450+. In-home visits, which are the market norm rather than our model, run AED 180–500 once travel sits inside the hour. A realistic total across two years is six to twelve hours. IB Gram's own hourly figure depends on the subject and the specialism the essay needs, and is quoted before anything is booked, after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is it better to buy a fixed block of hours or pay session by session?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the essay exists yet. If there is no research question, a block of eight to twelve sessions spread across DP1 and DP2 is better value, because the early hours change the essay rather than patch it and the sessions can be scheduled against the school's internal deadlines. If there is a complete draft and the student is broadly on track, pay for a single marked read and stop. The expensive mistake is buying a block for an essay that needed one review, or buying one review for an essay with a question nobody can answer in 4,000 words.

faqs.question: Our daughter already has a school supervisor. What are we actually paying a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Supervisor hours are allocated and shared across a cohort, and the supervisor may not teach the subject the essay is registered in. What outside mentoring adds is subject-matched reading of drafts against criteria A to E, time to interrogate the research question properly, and preparation for each reflection session. What it must not add is a second author. Ask your coordinator two questions first: how many supervision hours your child actually gets, and whether the supervisor teaches that subject. If the answers are generous and yes, a single draft review may be the whole sensible purchase.

faqs.question: Why do quotes for the same Extended Essay range from AED 150 to AED 650 an hour?
faqs.answer: Four things explain almost all of it. Subject scarcity: Mathematics and World Studies mentors are rarer than History mentors, so the band is higher. Format: an in-home visit bills travel inside the hour, which is why AED 180–500 is the home band and AED 150–450 the online one. Specialism: criterion knowledge and experience of the rubric cost more than general essay help. And positioning: a premium named provider publishes AED 650 because it can. Ask what the premium buys in writing. If the answer is a tone of voice rather than a capability, it is not worth the gap.

faqs.question: Does the price change if the research question needs laboratory data?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the reason is the stage rather than the subject. Experimental Biology, Chemistry and Physics essays need method work before any data exists: a controlled variable, a risk assessment, an uncertainty treatment the examiner will accept. Those hours sit at the top of the specialist band because the pool of mentors who can do them competently is small, and because a flawed method cannot be repaired by better prose later. Literature-based essays in History, Psychology or English spread their hours more evenly and cost less in total, since nothing has to be repeated in a laboratory.

faqs.question: Which Extended Essay subjects cost the most to support in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Mathematics is the most expensive to mentor well, because the essay has to prove something without collapsing into textbook exposition and very few UAE-based tutors have supervised one. A World Studies Extended Essay is next, since the mentor needs credible footing in two subjects and has to make them genuinely argue with each other. Experimental Chemistry and Physics follow, for the method work. History, Psychology and English sit at the lower end of the specialist band, because the research is source-led and the mentor pool is wider. Scarcity sets these rates, not difficulty.

faqs.question: We are in DP2 with eight weeks left. What can be done and what will it cost?
faqs.answer: Something useful, but less than you would hope, and the budget should reflect that. With eight weeks the recoverable marks concentrate in criterion D, the four presentation marks, and in whatever criterion C can still absorb from restructuring existing paragraphs. Realistically that is a marked full-draft read, a referencing and formatting pass, reflection preparation and a viva voce rehearsal — five to six hours at the specialist band. What cannot be bought at this stage is a better research question, which is where criterion A marks live. Starting in DP1 costs the same per hour and protects far more of the 34.

faqs.question: Is there a cheaper way to get a second opinion on a finished draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families should start there. A single ninety-minute read of a complete draft, returned marked against criteria A to E with a prioritised fix list, sits in the AED 200–450 band and carries no ongoing commitment. It tells you which marks are at risk and which are already secure, which is exactly the information needed to decide whether to buy more hours. A proofread from a budget tutor at AED 45–150 is cheaper and usually worth less, because it fixes typography without touching the 12 marks sitting in critical thinking.

faqs.question: Do Extended Essay sessions pause during Ramadan, and do we still pay?
faqs.answer: Sessions move rather than pause. UAE school hours shorten during Ramadan and families eat late, so mentoring shifts to post-Iftar timing at the same hourly rate — no premium for the unsocial slot and no charge for a week nobody studied in. Hours are billed as used, so a quieter fortnight costs less and a draft deadline landing in that month can be supported properly. Say at the outset which weeks your family expects to lose to travel, Eid or examinations, and the plan is built around them rather than around a standing weekly slot.

faqs.question: Can one mentor cover both the Extended Essay and the subject it is registered in?
faqs.answer: That is usually the best value available. A weekly Chemistry HL or History HL lesson with twenty to thirty minutes given to the essay means one tutor, one rate and one relationship, and the mentor is already holding the syllabus context the essay sits inside. It also keeps criterion B honest, because the subject vocabulary being taught in the lesson is the vocabulary the examiner is looking for. The arrangement scales up as the school's draft deadline approaches and back down afterwards, which a separate essay-only engagement does not do easily.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if the match turns out to be wrong?
faqs.answer: The free trial lesson exists to catch that before money moves. It is one introductory online session with the proposed mentor, with no payment taken and no card details requested, and its only purpose is to let the student judge whether this person asks useful questions about their own work. If the fit is wrong after a paid session, say so and a different mentor is proposed; hours are booked in small increments rather than a long prepaid block precisely so that a change costs a session, not a term.

faqs.question: How are Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge grades turned into Diploma points?
faqs.answer: The two core grades are combined through the EE and TOK matrix, which can add up to three points to the final Diploma score. Those points decide university offers at the margin, which is why a candidate sitting on 37 predicted points has a concrete financial reason to protect them. A grade E in either component is a failing condition for the Diploma regardless of subject scores. Confirm the current matrix with your child's coordinator or on ibo.org, because the rules governing the core are the school's to apply and are revised from time to time.

faqs.question: Do we need a tutor for the Extended Essay to pass UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. The published equivalency rules are subject-count based: the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. No Ministry-sourced IB points threshold has been verified for publication here, so check that requirement on the Ministry's own channel. IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency or attestation, and no tutoring is required for it.

faqs.question: Is a mentor who quotes in pounds or dollars a problem for a UAE family?
faqs.answer: It is a cost you should price in rather than a disqualification. Two of the agencies ranking for these searches quote in US dollars and one leads with pounds sterling, and a UAE card payment then carries a conversion spread and sometimes a cross-border fee on top of the headline rate. Ask for the figure in AED, ask whether it is per hour or per session, and ask what the total will be for the hours proposed. A rate quoted in the currency you actually pay school fees in is easier to compare against the AED bands on this page.

faqs.question: Can a mentor in Al Ain or Fujairah be found for a Mathematics essay?
faqs.answer: Locally, often not, and that is worth saying plainly. Al Ain sits under ADEK with far fewer IB World Schools than Abu Dhabi island, and Fujairah is supervised federally with the longest journey to any specialist pool in the country. A Mathematics or World Studies Extended Essay mentor within driving distance may simply not exist. Online delivery removes the problem: the mentor is chosen for having supervised that subject before, the session runs at 7.30pm Gulf Standard Time, and the rate is the same one a Dubai family pays, with no travel billed because none happens.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if the essay is 1,200 words over the limit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is slower work than writing those words was, so budget for it. Removing 1,200 words without losing an argument means deciding which sections carry criterion C marks and which are description that felt necessary at the time. A mentor can mark the draft against the criteria, show which paragraphs are doing analytical work and which are not, and set the priority order — but the student makes every cut themselves, because the words in the final document have to be theirs. Two hours is a realistic figure for a draft in that state.

ib-extended-essay-help.closingHeading: Start with one hour and a number you have actually been told
ib-extended-essay-help.closingBody: The useful first step on an Extended Essay is small. Write down the subject, the stage the essay has reached and the date the school has set for the full draft. Bring three candidate research questions, each in one sentence, with the evidence you would need named beside it. Take the free trial lesson, with no payment taken and no card details asked for, and let a subject specialist tell you which question has a findable answer. You will hear the hourly figure, the number of hours the stage warrants and which criterion each session targets before anything is booked. If two hours is the honest answer, that is the answer you will get.

ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.h1: IB HL vs SL Guidance in the UAE
ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.heroEyebrow: LEVEL DECISIONS FOR UAE DIPLOMA FAMILIES
ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.heroSubtitle: IB HL vs SL guidance in the UAE comes down to three concrete differences and one deadline. A Higher Level course adds taught hours, adds extension content, and in most subjects adds a whole examination paper. The deadline is the point in DP1 after which your child's level is registered with the IB and can no longer be moved by the school alone. This page sets out both, subject group by subject group, for families across the UAE. Teaching is one-to-one over live video.
heroTrustPoints: Paper-by-paper weightings compared at both levels, not described in a sentence
The level-change window dated against the DP1 calendar, not left vague
Market rates in AED attributed to the provider that published them
One-to-one teaching over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time

ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach Diploma subjects at Higher Level, which is a different job from teaching the Standard Level course well. Ask for the person who has taught the extension topics and marked the extra paper, because that is where a level decision is actually tested. All sessions run online.

intro.heading: Three differences, one deadline, and a decision that is reversible for about six weeks
paragraphs: Higher Level and Standard Level are not easy and hard versions of the same course. They are two courses with a shared core and a different assessment. The IB recommends 240 taught hours for a Higher Level subject and 150 for a Standard Level one, and that extra ninety hours is spent on extension content that does not appear on the Standard Level syllabus at all. In most subjects the Higher Level candidate also sits an additional examination paper, so the final grade is built from a different set of components.

That structure explains why the level question feels different from the subject question. Changing a subject swaps one body of content for another. Changing a level changes how many papers your child sits, what the internal assessment is expected to achieve, and which parts of the syllabus they are examined on. It also changes the shape of revision in DP2, because a Higher Level candidate is revising a broader syllabus against more papers in the same number of weeks.

In the UAE the practical problem is timing rather than understanding. Level choices are made on an option form in February or March of Year 11, before IGCSE or MYP results exist, and the first genuinely useful evidence about whether a Higher Level is the right level arrives in week three or four of DP1, when a student meets extension content for the first time. Schools leave a window of roughly four to six weeks at the start of DP1 for exactly this reason. After the school's internal cut-off, a change becomes an amendment to the IB candidate registration handled by the Diploma coordinator rather than something a parent can arrange.

There is a cost dimension too, and it is worth being plain about. A Higher Level subject that is the wrong level does not usually cost one grade; it costs weekly tutoring across two years and still produces a lower grade than the same student would have earned at Standard Level with the time reinvested. Market rates for specialist Diploma teaching in the UAE sit in a published band this page quotes with its sources, so the arithmetic of a level decision can be done properly rather than guessed at.

What follows is the comparison done component by component, the switch calendar, the question of which of three Higher Levels to let go when one has to go, the failure modes that are specific to Higher Level rather than general, and what the market charges. Where a figure belongs to a named provider it is attributed to them. Where a date depends on the IB or on your child's school, the page says so instead of inventing one, because a planning page that states an unverified date causes more trouble than one that admits the gap.
bullets: Ninety extra taught hours, extension content, and usually one extra paper
Internal assessment expectations differ by level in several subjects
A level change is normally straightforward for four to six weeks into DP1
After IB candidate registration the coordinator handles it as an amendment
Most university offers name one or two Higher Level subjects, not three

ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.programmesIntro: The Higher Level and Standard Level distinction belongs to the Diploma, but three other IB routes change what a level decision means. These are the four a UAE family may actually be choosing between.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, full award
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7, plus up to three points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. The three-Higher-Level requirement is a rule of the award, not a recommendation: a candidate who drops a fourth subject to Standard Level has not weakened a Diploma, but one who ends up with only two Higher Levels no longer qualifies for the full award.
programmes.countryNote: That rule is the hinge of most level conversations in UAE schools. A family weighing a step-down in DP1 is usually weighing it against an existing fourth Higher Level, or against moving a different subject up to keep three. The coordinator will know immediately which of those the timetable permits, and it is the first question to ask.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme courses, certificate route
programmes.description: A student may take individual Diploma courses and receive certificates for them without pursuing the full Diploma. Each course still carries a level, so the Higher Level and Standard Level decision applies, but the three-Higher-Level rule does not. The route suits students whose strengths are concentrated, or who are completing another qualification alongside.
programmes.countryNote: Not every UAE school offers the certificate route, and some that do restrict it to particular circumstances. Where it is available it changes the level conversation entirely, because a student can take two Higher Levels in the subjects that matter to a destination and nothing at Higher Level elsewhere.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject on a 1 to 8 scale, with no Core and Extended tiering of the kind IGCSE uses. An MYP 5 student therefore reaches the level decision without a public grade that signals Higher Level readiness, and the criterion profile has to do that work instead.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE continuum schools the MYP 5 subject teacher is often the DP1 teacher, which makes their view on level readiness unusually well informed. The specific question worth asking is how the student performed on the criteria that require independent inquiry, because those map most directly onto Higher Level demands.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, service learning, personal and professional skills and language development. Levels still apply to the Diploma courses within it, and the programme exists for students whose profile is deep rather than broad.
programmes.countryNote: Available at only a small number of UAE schools, so for most families it is a question to put to the coordinator rather than a live alternative. Where it exists it removes the three-Higher-Level pressure from the conversation completely.

ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.subjectsIntro: What follows is the extension, subject by subject: the specific thing the Higher Level course adds that the Standard Level course does not contain. This is the content a level decision is actually about.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level adds substantial further calculus, proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers, vectors in three dimensions and more demanding series work, plus a third paper of extended problem solving. The jump is in abstraction rather than volume, and it is the single most common mid-DP1 step-down in UAE schools.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Higher Level extends into statistical inference, matrices, graph theory and differential equations applied to modelling, with a third paper built around extended modelling tasks. Students who chose it as the lighter maths meet that third paper in DP2 and discover it is a demanding statistics qualification in its own right.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level extends wave behaviour, fields, induction and quantum effects, and assumes comfort with algebraic rearrangement under time pressure. The additional paper carries extended questions where marks turn on whether a student can carry an unfamiliar derivation several steps without prompting.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level deepens energetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, and organic mechanisms, and adds quantitative work that Standard Level treats qualitatively. Mechanism questions are where the level gap shows most sharply, because a half-remembered Standard Level mechanism scores almost nothing on a Higher Level paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth across existing themes rather than new ones, which makes the step feel manageable in term one and heavy in DP2. The volume of precise terminology roughly grows with the syllabus, and the additional paper rewards students who can apply a named process to unfamiliar data.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds quantitative content and a third paper of calculation and policy analysis. The internal assessment is three commentaries at both levels, so the level gap is concentrated almost entirely in that extra paper, which makes Economics an unusually clean step-down candidate.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Higher Level adds the written essay on a studied work and raises expectations on the comparative paper. For students whose first language is not English, the Higher Level essay is the component where the step up is felt, because it cannot be prepared for with content revision alone.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Higher Level adds a regional option and a third paper of extended essay writing under timed conditions, on top of the source paper and the world history topics. The reading load roughly doubles, and the historical investigation is unchanged, so the level decision here is almost purely about writing stamina.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Higher Level adds extensions within each approach, further research methodology and an additional paper. It is frequently chosen as a third Higher Level by students who want a Group 3 subject at depth, and the extension content on research design is where unprepared candidates lose marks.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Higher Level extends the content across all units and changes the internal assessment from a response to given material into a research project on a real organisation. That change of task, rather than the extra content, is the real difference between the levels here.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Higher Level adds abstract data structures, resource management, control and an additional paper, plus a case study released ahead of the session. Provision at Higher Level is thin across UAE schools, so availability is often the constraint before readiness is.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Higher Level requires more resolved artwork and a longer comparative study, with higher expectations on the process portfolio. The step up is measured in studio hours, which collide directly with the Extended Essay term in DP1.

ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.regionsTitle: Where Diploma cohorts sit, community by community
ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.regionsIntro: Level decisions are shaped by the size of the cohort around your child, because a school that runs one Higher Level class per subject has less room to move a student than one that runs three. These are the UAE communities where Diploma cohorts concentrate.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: A dense expatriate catchment feeding schools across Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and the Greens. Cohorts are large enough that most Higher Level classes run, so a step-down here is usually an administrative move rather than a question of whether the class exists.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: Long-established schools with mature sixth forms, several offering both A-Levels and the Diploma. The level conversation in these catchments is often a two-stage one, because a student weighing three Higher Levels is sometimes also weighing three A-Levels instead.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Villa communities with a strong school-bus culture, which puts a practical floor under session timing: a student home at 16:15 after a long route is not at their best for abstract Higher Level maths at 16:30. Evening slots work better here than afternoon ones.

regions.name: Mirdif, Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Mixed catchments with several continuum schools, so MYP 5 to DP1 transitions are common and the MYP criterion profile is readily available as evidence for a level decision. Cohort sizes vary year to year, which affects whether a class can absorb a late arrival.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha, Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Served by schools where the Diploma sits alongside a larger British-curriculum intake, so Higher Level classes can be small. A step-down request here is more likely to be answered with what the timetable allows than with what would be ideal.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island and Al Reem Island
regions.note: Newer schools with growing sixth forms and correspondingly small Diploma cohorts. Families here most often ask whether a particular Higher Level will run at all next year, which is a question for the coordinator in term two, not term four.

regions.name: Sharjah, Al Majaz and Muwaileh
regions.note: Diploma provision north of Dubai is concentrated in a few schools, and the Sharjah Private Education Authority approves curricula and assessment methods, so a school cannot add a Higher Level class mid-year because demand appeared. Plan level decisions earlier here than in Dubai.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools with large Diploma cohorts
schoolClusters.note: Where several Higher Level classes run in the same subject, a level change in the first weeks of DP1 is usually a timetable adjustment. These are the Dubai schools where Diploma numbers are large enough for that flexibility to exist.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sixth forms
schoolClusters.note: Several capital schools offer the Diploma alongside A-Levels, which means the level question is sometimes really a qualification question. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate.

Small Diploma cohorts and tighter option blocks. Where a Higher Level class cannot run, the realistic answers are a different subject in the same group, a certificate-route arrangement if the school permits one, or live online teaching to cover what the timetable cannot.
schools: The American School of Creative Science Sharjah

ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.modesIntro: Level support is not one thing. These three formats cover what UAE families ask for before the switch window closes, during a Higher Level year, and when a Standard Level subject needs consolidating rather than extending.

modes.title: Pre-deadline level review
modes.description: A short block of sessions inside the weeks when the school can still move a student between levels. The work is deliberately pitched at extension content rather than revision, because extension content is the thing the Standard Level course does not contain and therefore the thing the decision turns on.
bullets: Extension topics only, from the DP1 scheme of work
Ends with a plain written view, including when that view is to step down
Timed to finish before the coordinator's internal cut-off
Delivered online in Gulf Standard Time

modes.title: Higher Level subject teaching through DP2
modes.description: Weekly one-to-one in a Higher Level subject, following your child's own scheme of work and the school's internal assessment deadlines. The additional paper is practised from DP1 rather than discovered in the final term, which is where most of the avoidable Higher Level mark loss sits.
bullets: The extra paper practised from early DP1, not from March of DP2
Mark schemes and command terms used from the first session
Same tutor across both years where availability allows
Live video, shared screen, annotated working kept for review

modes.title: Standard Level consolidation
modes.description: For a student who has stepped down, or who chose Standard Level correctly and now wants a 7 rather than a 5. Standard Level grade boundaries reward precision over breadth, so the work is accuracy, timing and mark-scheme discipline rather than additional content.
bullets: Paper timing drilled against the real duration
Past-paper questions mapped to the Standard Level syllabus only
Internal assessment supported as feedback on the student's own drafts
Shorter, more frequent sessions where attention is the constraint

sections.heading: What the Higher Level and Standard Level labels actually change
paragraphs: Three things change, and the first is the least important. Taught hours move from 150 to 240, which parents read as the headline difference and students barely notice, because those hours are delivered inside a normal school timetable. The second change is extension content: topics that exist only on the Higher Level syllabus, which cannot be reached by studying the Standard Level material more thoroughly. The third change is assessment, and it is the one that decides grades. In most subjects a Higher Level candidate sits an additional paper, and in several the internal assessment is judged against broader expectations.

The practical consequence is that Higher Level and Standard Level fail differently. A Standard Level candidate who loses marks usually loses them on precision: a missed unit, an unexplained step, a command term answered as though it said something else. A Higher Level candidate loses them on reach, in extended questions that start from unfamiliar ground and require several linked steps without prompting. Teaching that fixes the first does not fix the second, which is why a tutor who has taught the Standard Level course well is not automatically the right tutor for a Higher Level year.

This also reframes the common worry that stepping down looks like giving up. Dropping a subject to Standard Level removes extension content and usually a paper. It does not remove rigour, and the Standard Level course is examined with the same grade descriptors on the material it covers. A student holding a 4 at Higher Level and a student holding a 7 at Standard Level in the same subject have made different trades, and only one of those outcomes helps a university application that does not name the subject at Higher Level.

The rest of this page compares the two levels where the comparison can be made concretely: side by side across the things that differ, weighting by weighting, and against the calendar that decides how long the choice stays open.
bullets: Taught hours: 150 at Standard Level, 240 at Higher Level
Extension content exists only on the Higher Level syllabus
An additional paper in most subjects, and broader internal assessment expectations in several
The two levels lose marks for different reasons and need different teaching

sections.heading: Higher Level and Standard Level, compared across what actually differs
paragraphs: The useful comparison is not a list of adjectives. It is a row-by-row look at the things that are genuinely different, with the consequence for how a week has to be organised. The table below does that, and the final column is the one worth reading first if you are deciding whether to commit to a level before the option form closes.

Two rows in it are frequently misunderstood. The grade ceiling is identical: a 7 at Standard Level is a 7, and the Diploma total treats it as such. What differs is what a 7 is awarded for, because the syllabus is narrower. And the university prerequisite row is the only place where the levels are not interchangeable at all, because an offer naming a subject at Higher Level cannot be satisfied by a 7 at Standard Level, no matter how good the grade.

The right-fit signal row deserves a caution. Prior attainment predicts Higher Level success imperfectly, and in the UAE it predicts it worse than elsewhere, because a cohort arriving from MYP has no tiered public grade and a cohort arriving from IGCSE has grades from two different boards with different tiering. Treat a strong IGCSE grade as necessary rather than sufficient evidence, and get the decision tested against actual extension content.

One row is missing from the table because it cannot be filled honestly, and its absence is worth naming. There is no reliable published figure for how many UAE Diploma candidates step down a level during DP1, because schools do not publish it and the IB reports grades rather than movements. Anyone quoting a percentage for that is quoting an impression. What school coordinators do say consistently is that the requests cluster in the same four weeks and in the same two or three subjects, which is why this page treats the decision as a scheduling problem with a known shape rather than a rare event.

sections.heading: Where the extra weight sits: assessment structure at each level
paragraphs: A level decision is partly a decision about which components your child is strongest in. Internal assessment is worth a fifth to a quarter of the grade in most subjects at both levels, which means a student who works well on a long independent task carries a meaningful part of the grade before any paper is sat. A student who performs under timed conditions and struggles with independent projects has the opposite profile, and in a Higher Level subject they face one more timed paper to work with.

The table below sets out the structure at both levels for the subject groups UAE students most often agonise over. Component weightings are published by the IB in each subject guide and are revised between syllabus cycles, so treat the figures as the shape of the assessment rather than as the final word for your child's cohort, and confirm the current weighting in the subject guide your school is teaching to.

Read the rows for the subject your child is least certain about and ask one question: is the additional Higher Level paper the kind of paper this student does well in? For Economics the third paper is quantitative policy analysis. For Mathematics it is extended problem solving with no prompting. For History it is timed essay writing on a regional option. Those are three completely different demands, and a student may be well suited to one and badly suited to another.

sections.heading: The switch calendar: how long the level decision stays open
paragraphs: Every family asks the same question in week four of DP1, and the answer depends entirely on where that week sits relative to two dates nobody publishes together. The first is the school's internal change cut-off, usually four to six weeks into DP1. The second is IB candidate registration, set by the IB and handled by the school, after which a level change is a formal amendment rather than a reshuffle. Ask the Diploma coordinator for both, by name, in writing. They are the most useful two dates of the whole programme and they are rarely in the option booklet.

The calendar below counts backwards from the final examinations. On the examination window itself this page publishes nothing, and that is deliberate: the IB's assessment pages block automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly. Secondary sources circulate windows for upcoming May and November sessions, and they may well be right, but a planning page that states an unverified date is doing harm. Confirm your child's window with the coordinator or on ibo.org.

Where a board date is genuinely sourced, this page uses it. Cambridge International publishes its key dates series by series: for the March 2027 series the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, and results are released on Direct on 13 May. That gap between entry deadline and examination is the pattern worth internalising, because the IB works the same way even though the exact dates differ.

sections.heading: Three Higher Levels, and which one to let go
paragraphs: When something has to give, it is rarely obvious which subject. Families default to dropping whichever subject has the lowest current mark, which is often exactly the wrong choice, because a low mark in a subject with a gentle extension is a fixable problem while a comfortable mark in a subject whose extension arrives in DP2 is a deferred one. The decision has four inputs and they are worth taking in order.

Start with requirements. Any subject named at Higher Level by a course your child is seriously applying to is not a candidate, full stop. Then look at where the extension content falls in the two-year sequence: subjects that front-load extension, such as Mathematics, have already shown you what the level demands by October, while subjects that back-load it, such as several Group 4 options, have not. Third, look at the internal assessment. Where the task is identical at both levels, as in Economics, a step-down costs almost nothing in work already done. Where the task changes, as in Business Management, it costs more.

The fourth input is the one families undervalue: what the freed time is actually for. Ninety hours and one paper released from a Higher Level subject are only worth having if they go somewhere. Reinvested in the Extended Essay and the two remaining Higher Levels they are often worth two or three points on the total. Absorbed into the general week they are worth nothing, and the step-down then looks in hindsight like it did not help.

Where only two Higher Levels would remain, there is a structural constraint to settle first. The full Diploma requires three, so the realistic move is a swap rather than a drop: one subject down to Standard Level and another up to Higher Level, which the timetable may or may not permit. That is a conversation for the coordinator before it is a conversation at home.
bullets: Named Higher Level requirements come off the table first
Front-loaded extension has already shown its hand; back-loaded extension has not
An unchanged internal assessment makes a step-down much cheaper
Freed hours must be reinvested deliberately or the step-down achieves little

sections.heading: Higher Level mark loss that Standard Level candidates never meet
paragraphs: Some mark loss is level-specific, and knowing which kind you are looking at is the difference between useful teaching and expensive reassurance. The first pattern is the multi-step extended question. A Higher Level paper will open from an unfamiliar context and require four or five linked steps with no scaffolding, and students who have only ever practised structured questions stall at step two. The fix is practice on genuinely unstructured problems, which is uncomfortable and works.

The second pattern is the half-learned extension topic. Extension content is usually taught late in DP1 or early in DP2, under time pressure, and students carry a partial version of it into the examination. Partial knowledge of a Higher Level mechanism, induction proof or field derivation scores close to nothing, because the marks are allocated to the steps the student cannot reach. This is the single largest avoidable loss at Higher Level and it is a scheduling problem as much as a teaching one.

The third is the internal assessment written to Standard Level scope. The task looks the same, the student writes the same kind of piece they would have written at Standard Level, and the marks that reward wider reach are simply not available to the work as scoped. A tutor can help here only in a specific way: by giving feedback on the student's own plan and drafts, explaining what the criteria reward, and sending them back to do it. Supplying text or producing the piece would be malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor.

The fourth is timing on the extra paper. A third paper changes the arithmetic of a revision week in DP2, and candidates who rehearsed two papers at full duration and the third only in fragments lose marks at the end of it through pace rather than knowledge.
bullets: Unstructured multi-step questions: practise unscaffolded problems, not more structured ones
Half-learned extension topics: the largest avoidable Higher Level loss, and a timetable problem
Internal assessments scoped at Standard Level: fixed with feedback on the student's own drafts
The third paper rehearsed only in fragments: pace, not knowledge, costs the marks

sections.heading: What a Higher Level year costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: A level decision has a price attached and it is worth doing the arithmetic before the option form rather than in February of DP2. Published market rates in the UAE sit in reasonably well-defined bands, and the table below records what named providers published in October 2026, with the provider attributed in each row. These are market figures, not IB Gram's prices. Where you need our figures, the free trial lesson and the consultation that follows are the right place to get them.

The pattern across the bands is consistent: the premium is paid for subject specialism at the level being taught, not for the format. A qualified subject tutor working online was advertised from AED 150 for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB by Unitors; TutorChase listed AED 270; Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table put specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above; BartyED listed AED 650 at the top of the market. In-home visits were priced at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by individual home tutors, with the difference largely accounted for by travel.

Set against that, the cost of a wrong level becomes legible. A Higher Level subject supported weekly for two years at mid-market rates is a substantial commitment, and if the honest assessment in week four of DP1 is that Standard Level is the right level, the step-down saves most of it and usually produces a better grade. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not a currency UAE families transact in. The arithmetic is easier when the numbers are in AED and attributed.

sections.heading: Retakes, the November session, and the level you sat
paragraphs: A level decision also has a tail, and almost nobody explains it at option-form stage. The IB runs two examination sessions a year, and a candidate who is unhappy with a result can retake. What matters for this page is that a retake is sat in the subject and at the level originally registered, so the level decision taken in DP1 still governs the position two years later. A student who wanted a Higher Level grade and sat Standard Level cannot acquire the Higher Level grade by retaking the Standard Level paper.

The retake mechanics themselves are worth understanding in outline, with the detail confirmed through the school. Candidates can retake subjects in a later session; internal assessment marks can in some circumstances be carried forward rather than resubmitted; and there are deadlines for registering a retake that sit months before the session, in the same way Cambridge requires final entries for its March 2027 series by 27 November 2026. Your child's school, or an examination centre accepting private candidates, handles the registration, and both the timetable and the carry-forward rules should be confirmed with the Diploma coordinator rather than from a tutoring site.

For families weighing a level now, two conclusions follow. The first is that there is no quiet second chance at the level question: the retake route reopens the grade, not the level. The second is that the November session gives a candidate who has a genuinely bad May a real option, which is relevant to how much risk a family wants to carry on a third Higher Level. Neither of those should be the deciding factor, but both belong in the conversation, and neither appeared on any competitor page examined for this project.
bullets: A retake is sat at the level originally registered, not at a different one
Internal assessment marks may be carried forward in some circumstances; confirm with the school
Retake registration deadlines sit months before the session, as with Cambridge's entry dates
The November session is a real fallback, but not a reason to over-reach on a third Higher Level

process.title: Tell us which level is in question, and why
process.description: The useful starting point is one subject and one worry: the mark that came back low, the topic that stopped making sense, or the offer that names the subject at Higher Level. A level review of all six subjects at once produces generalities, and generalities are what the option booklet already gave you.

process.title: A trial lesson on extension content, not revision
process.description: Free, online and deliberately pitched at a Higher Level extension topic rather than at material your child has already covered. Extension content is what the Standard Level course does not contain, so it is the only material that tests the level question properly.

process.title: A written view the coordinator can act on
process.description: After the trial you get a short note naming the topics attempted, what was fluent, where the work stopped, and whether the evidence supports the current level. It is written for the Diploma coordinator, with topics and command terms named rather than impressions offered.

process.title: Decide inside the window, with the dates in hand
process.description: Ask the coordinator for the internal change cut-off and the IB registration date in writing, then decide against them. A good decision taken after the window has closed is worth considerably less than an adequate one taken inside it.

process.title: Weekly teaching on the component that is weakest
process.description: If the level stands, work starts on whichever component the evidence pointed at: unstructured problems, the extension topic that was half-learned, or timing on the third paper. One session a week in the right place beats three spread across everything.

whyPoints.title: Extension content is the test, so that is what we teach first
whyPoints.description: A trial lesson on material your child already knows tells you nothing about a level decision. We start on an extension topic from the Higher Level syllabus, because the ability to work on content the Standard Level course does not contain is the actual question being asked.

whyPoints.title: Weightings quoted, not described
whyPoints.description: The comparison tables on this page name components and what each extra Higher Level paper demands, rather than calling the level difference significant. Component weightings are revised between syllabus cycles, so the page tells you to confirm current figures in your school's subject guide.

whyPoints.title: AED figures attributed to whoever published them
whyPoints.description: Every rate in the market table names the provider and the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family pays in.

whyPoints.title: No IB date published that has not been verified
whyPoints.description: The IB's assessment pages block automated checking, so no session or results date appears on this page. Cambridge and Pearson dates are quoted because they are sourced from the boards' own published key-dates documents, and the page says which is which.

whyPoints.title: Stepping down is a real recommendation, not a last resort
whyPoints.description: Where the evidence says a student is better placed at Standard Level with the hours reinvested in the Core and the other two Higher Levels, the written note says so, in time for the coordinator to act. An adviser who never recommends a step-down is selling hours.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online across all seven emirates
whyPoints.description: Teaching is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes, which is why a family in Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah reaches the same Higher Level specialist as one in Dubai rather than whoever lives nearby.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level just a harder version of the same Standard Level course?
faqs.answer: No. The two courses share a core, and then the Higher Level syllabus adds extension topics that do not appear at Standard Level at all. Working harder on the Standard Level material will not cover them. In most subjects the Higher Level candidate also sits an extra examination paper, and in several the internal assessment is judged against wider expectations. So the honest description is two related courses with different assessments, rather than one course at two difficulty settings. That distinction matters because it means the level decision is about content and components, not about effort.

faqs.question: How many Higher Level subjects does the full IB Diploma require?
faqs.answer: Three, with the other three taken at Standard Level. That is a rule of the award rather than a recommendation, which is why a family considering a step-down in DP1 has to check what it would leave them with. If dropping a subject would leave only two Higher Levels, the move has to be a swap rather than a drop: one subject down and another up, which the timetable may or may not allow. Students taking individual Diploma courses for certificates rather than the full award are not bound by the three-Higher-Level rule.

faqs.question: Does a 7 at Standard Level count for less than a 7 at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: In the Diploma total they are identical: both contribute 7 points. What differs is the syllabus the 7 was awarded on, and whether it satisfies a university offer. An offer that names a subject at Higher Level cannot be met with a Standard Level grade however high it is, and that is the only context in which the levels are genuinely not interchangeable. For a subject no offer names, a 7 at Standard Level is a better outcome than a 4 at Higher Level by every measure that matters, including the total.

faqs.question: How late into DP1 can my child move from Higher Level to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Usually four to six weeks, set by the school rather than by the IB, and then a second boundary at IB candidate registration later in DP1. Inside the first window it is a class move. Between the school's cut-off and registration it is possible but disruptive, because the receiving class has covered different material. After registration it becomes a formal amendment that the coordinator submits to the IB. Ask for both dates in writing at the start of DP1; they are rarely printed in the option booklet and they decide how much time you have.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subject should we drop if one has to go?
faqs.answer: Not automatically the one with the lowest mark. Take four things in order: any subject named at Higher Level by a target course is not a candidate; subjects whose extension content comes early have already shown you what the level demands, while late-extension subjects have not; a subject whose internal assessment is identical at both levels, such as Economics, is a much cheaper step-down than one where the task changes; and the freed hours need a destination, usually the Extended Essay and the remaining Higher Levels. A step-down that is not reinvested rarely helps.

faqs.question: My child has a strong IGCSE grade. Is that enough to justify Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It is necessary rather than sufficient. A strong IGCSE grade shows the student handles the content of a tiered two-year course well. Higher Level asks something different: sustained work on unfamiliar problems with no scaffolding, across extension topics that have no IGCSE equivalent. The better evidence is what happens when the student meets one of those extension topics cold. In the UAE this matters more than elsewhere, because cohorts arrive from MYP with no tiered public grade and from two different IGCSE boards with different tiering conventions.

faqs.question: Which subjects have the biggest gap between the two levels?
faqs.answer: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches has the sharpest step, because the Higher Level course adds genuine abstraction through proof, complex numbers and further calculus rather than more of the same. History roughly doubles the reading by adding a regional option and a third timed essay paper. Chemistry's extension sits in mechanisms and quantitative treatment, where partial knowledge scores close to nothing. The flattest steps are usually Biology, where Higher Level deepens existing themes, and Economics, where almost all of the difference is concentrated in one extra paper.

faqs.question: Does the internal assessment change if my child moves level?
faqs.answer: In most subjects the task itself is the same at both levels and the expectations are wider at Higher Level, so work already done is not wasted. In some, including Business Management, the nature of the task differs between levels, and a move means starting a different piece. Either way the marks already earned in class do not transfer automatically; what transfers is the student's understanding of the criteria. Ask the subject teacher specifically what happens to work in progress before the move, not afterwards.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level support cost per hour in Dubai and Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist examination-year support ran AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table reaching beyond 450. In-home visits sat at AED 180 to 350 in that table and up to 500 with independent tutors, with travel accounting for much of the difference. Those are market figures from the providers named, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Can my child retake a subject at a different level in the November session?
faqs.answer: A retake is sat in the subject and at the level originally registered, so it reopens the grade rather than the level. That is worth knowing at option-form stage, because it means the level decision does not have a quiet second chance built into it. Registration deadlines for a later session fall months ahead of the examinations, and in some circumstances internal assessment marks can be carried forward rather than resubmitted. Confirm the carry-forward rules and the registration deadline with your school's Diploma coordinator rather than from a tutoring website.

faqs.question: Is three Higher Level sciences ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, where a specific course genuinely names three. Most competitive medicine and engineering routes name two. Three Higher Level sciences means 720 taught hours in Group 4, three separate scientific investigations and a DP2 in which the Extended Essay competes with all of it for the same weeks. Where a course does require three, the right plan is about sequencing and support rather than reducing the load. Where it does not, two at Higher Level with the third at Standard Level usually produces a better total and a considerably better Extended Essay.

faqs.question: How does the extra Higher Level paper change revision in DP2?
faqs.answer: It changes the arithmetic rather than the method. Three papers in a subject means three distinct timing patterns to rehearse, and a broader syllabus to cover in the same number of weeks as a Standard Level candidate. The failure mode is predictable: candidates rehearse the two familiar papers at full duration and the third only in fragments, then lose marks at the end of it to pace rather than knowledge. Putting the third paper into full-length practice from early in DP2, not March, is the cheapest available fix.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Higher Level internal assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what the assessment criteria reward, discuss a plan, give feedback on the student's own draft and send them back to revise it. A tutor may not supply text, produce the piece or edit it to the point where it is no longer the student's own work. Every internal assessment is submitted with the student's declaration of authorship, and a breach is handled as malpractice with the consequence falling on the student. Any provider pricing per assignment rather than per hour is selling something else.

faqs.question: Our school only runs one class per Higher Level subject. Does that limit a change?
faqs.answer: It often does, and it is the main reason level requests are refused in smaller UAE cohorts. A single class per level means a step-down depends on the Standard Level class having capacity in the right timetable column, and a step-up depends on the Higher Level class having both space and a student able to catch up on what it has covered. Schools in Sharjah and the northern emirates face this most, because Diploma cohorts are smaller. Ask in term two of Year 11 which classes are expected to run, rather than in October.

faqs.question: Should the level decision wait until after IGCSE or MYP results?
faqs.answer: It usually cannot, because most UAE schools close the option form in February or March of Year 11 to build a timetable. The workable approach is to make the best decision available then, and plan deliberately for both outcomes: what changes if the grade lands above prediction, and what changes if it lands below. Then use the first weeks of DP1, while the change window is open, to test the uncertain level against real extension content. That gives you two decisions on the same question rather than one made blind.

ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.closingHeading: Settle the level while the window is still open
ib-hl-vs-sl-guidance.closingBody: A level is the one Diploma decision that is cheap to correct for about six weeks and expensive to correct afterwards. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal change cut-off and the IB registration date in writing. Test the uncertain subject against an extension topic rather than against revision, and decide on what that produces. A free trial lesson is one hour, online and one-to-one, and the written note afterwards will say plainly whether the evidence supports Higher Level. Where it does not, stepping down and reinvesting the hours is usually the stronger plan.

Each one lists the programme, the subjects and the levels they hold, so you can match a specific gap to a specific person before you book a block.

intro.heading: A holiday is the only time an IB student controls the whole week
paragraphs: During term, an IB Diploma student in the UAE has six subjects, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay, an Internal Assessment in most of those subjects, and whatever Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies their school is required to timetable alongside the Diploma. The week is full before any tutoring is added to it. A holiday is a different problem. For three days or eight weeks, depending which break you are in, nothing competes. That is why IB holiday tuition in the UAE runs on a different logic from a weekly term-time lesson: the question is not where to squeeze an hour, but what to rebuild while there is room to rebuild it.

The complication is that you do not set the dates. Private schools here are licensed emirate by emirate. Dubai answers to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

Scale makes this a planning problem rather than a detail. Dubai alone had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent of enrolment and the UK curriculum at 37 per cent. Seven more private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places. Schools on a September start and schools on an April start sit in the same community with different holidays, and a family with children in two of them plans around two calendars.

What usually goes wrong in a holiday is not laziness. It is that nobody decided what the block was for. Eight weeks of unspecified revision produces a student who has reread notes and learned nothing new. A block that works names the deliverable on day one: the Maths exploration moves from a vague idea to a tested dataset; the Chemistry student rebuilds organic mechanisms from first principles instead of memorising arrows; the DP1 student who dropped from a 5 to a 3 in Physics Paper 2 fixes the two topics that paper actually tested. Everything else is scheduling.

Lessons for UAE families run live online, one-to-one, over video. IB Gram does not make home visits to UAE addresses; that is part of what we do in India, not here. In a holiday it turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise. Families travel. A student in Al Ain in June may be in Kerala, Karachi, Manchester or Amman by July, and a tutor who exists on a screen follows them there without a new match, a new diagnosis and a new first lesson. The same format is why a Fujairah family can book a Chemistry HL specialist at all: the pool is not limited to whoever lives within driving distance of the east coast.

The rest of this page is built around the four breaks a UAE school year contains, the authorities that set their dates, what the market charges for a block in dirhams, the Cambridge and Pearson deadlines that fall outside the holidays they affect, and the academic-honesty line a tutor must not cross in the weeks when coursework finally gets finished.
