ib-holiday-tuition.programmesIntro: Each IB programme uses a break differently, because the thing at risk differs. A PYP child loses fluency. An MYP student loses the habit of writing to a clock. A DP student loses a topic they will be examined on in May. The notes below are about what a holiday does to each programme inside a UAE school year, not about what the programme is.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and reported against learner outcomes rather than examined, so nothing visible breaks over a long holiday, which is exactly why it gets left out of holiday plans. What slips is fluency: reading stamina, number facts recalled without counting, and writing at length without prompting. Six weeks without any of it shows in September. A Year 5 child who has stopped reading daily reads noticeably more slowly in week one of a new unit, and the teacher reads that as a dip in ability rather than a dip in practice.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai private schools, PYP children also carry Arabic, Islamic Education and Moral or Social Studies, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups under KHDA's rules. For most UAE families at this age the highest-value summer block is twenty-five to thirty minutes of Arabic reading three times a week, built from the school's own unit plan rather than from any substitute material.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, marked out of eight, with redrafting built into the process. That is a gentler regime than the Diploma's timed papers and it hides one specific weakness: students who have never produced finished written work under a clock. The MYP5 personal project also lands in a year already crowded with criterion tasks. Holiday time at this stage buys writing speed, notation discipline in maths and science, and the habit of reading a command term properly before answering it.
programmes.countryNote: MYP to DP summer preparation is the most requested holiday block we get from UAE families, and most of them ask a year later than they should. A student entering DP1 in late August gains more from six weeks of short timed writing in July than from pre-teaching Diploma content. The content arrives anyway in September; the clock does not arrive with it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and an Internal Assessment in most subjects. Paper weightings do the damage: a Higher Level science Paper 3 or a Maths Paper 3 carries enough of the grade that one weak forty minutes costs a band. The Diploma is cumulative too, so a topic skipped in DP1 returns in May of DP2 with interest. That is why holiday blocks in this programme are usually repair work against a named topic list rather than general revision.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma students sit the May session, and schools here run internal mocks in the winter term and again in spring. That puts a holiday on either side of the mocks with different jobs: December repairs the subject the November internal test exposed, and the spring fortnight is for full timed papers against the published mark scheme. We do not publish IB session or results dates on this page; confirm those with your school's IB coordinator.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a language-development requirement and a personal and professional skills core. A small number of UAE schools run it, and it attracts students who want Diploma-level rigour in two or three subjects with an applied strand alongside. Holiday support here usually focuses on the Diploma courses inside the timetable and on the reflective project's structure, which is the component most often left until it is late.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP cohorts in the UAE are small, a student wanting help with one Diploma course inside a CP timetable rarely finds a specialist at their own school or in their own emirate. That is the clearest case for one-to-one lessons on live video: the match is made on the subject and the level, not on who happens to live in the same city.

ib-holiday-tuition.subjectsIntro: Holiday demand is not spread evenly across the Diploma. These are the subjects UAE families book blocks in, with the specific failure a break is usually bought to fix. Each is taught at the level your child is actually entered for, because Higher and Standard are different courses with different papers rather than the same course at two speeds.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof, calculus and algebraic-manipulation route. Marks go in Paper 1, where no calculator is allowed and one shaky algebraic step ends the question. Holiday blocks here usually rebuild differentiation, integration techniques and proof structure before moving to the exploration.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use. Students who chose this route to avoid algebra are caught by the statistics content and by modelling questions that require reading a context and selecting a function. UAE universities differ on which route they expect, so check the course page before any switch.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The gap is almost never the maths. It is explaining a mechanism in words, and the unfamiliar-context question in Paper 2. Higher Level Paper 3 adds practical and data analysis, which is the component online sessions improve fastest because the work is reading graphs, errors and uncertainties.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and equilibrium calculations account for most of the lost marks we see in UAE scripts. Both respond well to a holiday block because they are procedural: a defined sequence of steps, practised until automatic. Energetics and bonding need understanding rebuilt instead, which takes longer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Students who revise by rereading retain little; the fix is structured recall against syllabus statements plus command-term practice on outline, explain and evaluate. The Internal Assessment needs a measurable variable chosen early, which is a holiday job.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation sentence at the end of a long answer are where bands are won. Higher Level adds quantitative questions. The Internal Assessment is a set of commentaries on real articles, and choosing weak articles costs more marks than writing badly about strong ones.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application is the weakness: students name a framework instead of applying it to the stimulus in front of them. Holiday blocks work through past stimulus material under time, then on the Internal Assessment's research question, which has to be answerable with evidence the student can actually obtain.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen guided analysis, and students who have only studied set texts panic at it. The individual oral needs a global issue linked to two texts and collapses without planning. Short, frequent sessions on unseen extracts suit a break better than long ones.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Receptive and productive skills are assessed separately, and the writing tasks require a text type with its own conventions. Students in UAE schools who speak English fluently still lose marks on register and text-type convention, which is teachable inside a fortnight.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Script, verb forms, and the distance between classroom Arabic and the Arabic spoken in a UAE household. This is the Diploma language course and is assessed as one, separate from the mandatory Arabic a Dubai private school must timetable alongside it.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-based Paper 1 has a fixed question structure that can be drilled, and the Internal Assessment needs a narrow question with sources the student can reach. Most lost marks come from writing narrative where the question asked for an argument.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Neither is a subject and both are usually behind. The Theory of Knowledge essay needs its prescribed title read properly; the Extended Essay needs a question narrow enough to answer in four thousand words. Process coaching only: the student is the author of every sentence.

ib-holiday-tuition.regionsIntro: Term dates, regulators and the local supply of subject specialists all vary by emirate, and the northern emirates are where the supply gap is widest. These notes cover what changes for a holiday block depending on where your child is enrolled. They are not a list of places anyone drives to, because the lessons happen on live video.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: 227 private schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent of enrolment. KHDA regulates, mandatory UAE subjects apply in every school, and both September and April starts exist here, so IB summer tuition in Dubai covers two different holiday calendars inside one emirate.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK licenses the schools and sets professional-ethics rules that bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school. A holiday IB intensive in Abu Dhabi therefore almost always means an outside tutor, and Diploma families here tend to book the December block around their school's own mock week.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller Diploma cohort and far fewer subject specialists living locally. Al Ain families travel heavily in summer, which makes a tutor who follows the time zone rather than the postcode the practical option for a long block.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: SPEA regulates, and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Because assessment methods are approved locally, internal test weeks move, and IB spring break revision in Sharjah has to be planned against the school's own calendar rather than a neighbour's in Dubai.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. A small number of international schools and almost no local Diploma specialists, so holiday blocks here run online by necessity as much as by design.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education and approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Named by none of the competitor pages we studied, which reflects how thin provision is. Families often plan summer blocks around travel out of the emirate entirely.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the Ministry of Education's supervision, on the east coast, and a long drive from most of the specialist supply in Dubai. The driving is the whole argument: a fifty-minute online session is possible here in a way a fifty-minute in-home one is not.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the country, also supervised by the Ministry of Education. Holiday support for a Diploma subject here means looking outside the emirate, and the honest version of that is a tutor on video rather than a weekly commute.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's Diploma schools run on different calendars, some on a September start and some on April, and the mandatory UAE subjects sit on top of the Diploma in all of them. December and spring blocks here are usually planned around the school's own mock week rather than the emirate's holiday dates.

Schools here hold their licence from ADEK, which sets professional-ethics rules that keep a child's own teachers out of paid tutoring. Diploma cohorts are smaller than Dubai's, so a Higher Level specialist in a minority subject is rarely free locally inside a holiday window.

Sharjah's schools work to curricula and assessment methods approved by SPEA, while schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah answer to the federal ministry. Local specialist supply thins out quickly here, which is the main reason holiday blocks in these emirates run online.

ib-holiday-tuition.modesIntro: Four shapes cover almost every holiday request UAE families send us. Pick by the length of the break and the deliverable, not by the number of hours that sounds serious. All four run one-to-one on live video, in Gulf Standard Time or whatever time zone the family is in that month.

modes.title: Summer bridge block
modes.description: Six to eight weeks, two subjects, three to five hours a week, with a named topic list agreed before the first session. Booked most for MYP5 into DP1 and DP1 into DP2. The block ends with a written handover: what was covered, what the student can now do unaided, and the two things to watch in the first month of the new term.

modes.title: Pre-mock December intensive
modes.description: Two to three weeks across the winter break, one or two subjects, built from the marked November internal paper rather than a syllabus overview. Four sessions per subject is the usual shape, with the last four days of the holiday left clear. The target is the January mock and the predicted grade that follows from it.

Two topics per subject at most

modes.title: Spring timed-paper block
modes.description: Two weeks of full papers under exam conditions, marked against the published scheme, with the distance between the student's answer and the band descriptor read out explicitly. No new content is taught. For most UAE Diploma students this is the last uninterrupted fortnight before the May session, and it is spent on technique.

modes.title: Coursework process coaching
modes.description: Short checkpoints across a break for the Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. The student brings a draft, the tutor reads it against the criteria letter by letter, and the student leaves with changes to make alone. The student is the author of every sentence; nothing else is on offer here.

sections.heading: What UAE families mean when they search for holiday tuition
paragraphs: IB holiday tuition in the UAE is one-to-one teaching booked into a school break rather than a term week, usually to rebuild a subject, bridge two programmes, or move an Internal Assessment to a real draft. A UAE school year contains four usable breaks of very different lengths, and the job changes with the length. Eight weeks is a rebuild. Three days is maintenance. Treating them the same is the most common planning error we see.

The lengths in the table are what UAE private schools typically run, not dates anyone can set for you. Each school publishes its own calendar under the licence its emirate's regulator issues, and schools on an April start break at different points from schools on a September start. Check your own school's published calendar before committing to a block, then check it again in February, because internal assessment weeks and mock windows move more often than parents expect them to.

The column parents usually get wrong is the load. A holiday is not a reason to run ten hours a week. Past about five hours of new teaching in a week, retention falls and the student begins resenting the break, which costs more in September than the extra hours bought. The pattern that holds is short, frequent and specific: four sessions a week of fifty minutes against one named topic list, with written practice between them, then a clear week before term restarts.

An online IB holiday tutor makes that pattern economic in a way a driving tutor cannot. Nobody spends forty minutes on Sheikh Zayed Road to deliver a fifty-minute lesson, so short sessions stop being wasteful, and a family that leaves the country for July keeps the same tutor in August instead of starting again with somebody new at the worst possible moment.

sections.heading: Who actually sets the holiday your plan has to fit
paragraphs: Nobody in the UAE school system answers to a single authority on term dates. Private schools are licensed emirate by emirate, and u.ae sets out the whole map: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Five bodies, one country, three different holiday calendars in a single street.

This matters for more than trivia. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, assessment methods included. A Sharjah school's internal testing calendar is therefore a locally approved document, and the mock window your spring plan is built around will not necessarily sit where a Dubai friend's does. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which closes the easiest-looking option a parent reaches for in a hurry.

There is also a federal floor under every licensed curriculum. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA requires those subjects in every private school whatever the international curriculum, with the requirement to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. A Diploma holiday plan that leaves them out is incomplete before it starts.

The practical move is to write four things down once: your school's published calendar, your emirate's regulator, the board your child is actually entered with, and your own travel plan. Most holiday plans fail because two of those four were never compared with each other.

sections.heading: The summer block: what six to eight weeks can and cannot repair
paragraphs: Summer is the only break long enough to change a grade rather than protect one. Six to eight weeks allows a full pass through a year's content with practice attached, which is why IB summer tuition in Dubai is booked most heavily by two groups: students moving from MYP5 into DP1, and students moving from DP1 into DP2. Both are transition years, and both go wrong for the same reason. The new course assumes a skill the old one never assessed.

MYP to DP summer preparation is mostly about notation, pace and formal writing. MYP marks against criteria and allows redrafting; the Diploma marks papers under time. A student who has never written to a command term against a clock finds Paper 1 brutal in October, and the repair is six weeks of short timed writing rather than more content. The IGCSE to IB Diploma holiday bridge has a sharper version of the same gap: Extended-tier algebra and Cambridge practical skills do not carry a student through Maths AA HL or a Diploma science Internal Assessment.

The DP1 to DP2 summer bridge is a different job again. By July a DP1 student has internal exam grades, two or three partly built Internal Assessments, and a clear sense of which subject is the risk. Summer is when that subject gets rebuilt from the syllabus outwards instead of patched topic by topic. Eight weeks of IB revision over the summer holiday on Chemistry HL organic mechanisms, or on Maths AA HL proof and calculus, moves a student off the boundary they have been sitting on since February.

What summer cannot do is manufacture a subject the student has not studied. Nobody builds Physics HL Paper 3 technique in six weeks from a standing start, and anyone promising it is selling the holiday rather than the teaching. Decide what the block is for, put it in writing, and judge it in September against that sentence rather than against how busy the weeks felt.

sections.heading: Winter break, the January mocks and the report that follows
paragraphs: The two to three weeks in late December are the most mispriced block in the UAE school year. They sit immediately before the January mock window in most Diploma schools, and a mock grade is what feeds the predicted-grade conversation with the university counsellor. IB winter break tutoring is therefore not general revision. It is targeted repair of whatever the November internal test exposed, in the one or two subjects where the predicted grade is genuinely at risk.

The useful input is the paper, not the percentage. A DP2 student who lost eleven marks across two Chemistry Paper 2 questions has a specific problem, equilibrium calculation or data handling with uncertainties, and four sessions can fix it. The same student told only that they got a 4 will spend the holiday rereading the whole syllabus and arrive in January with both gaps intact. Bring the marked script to the first session. Everything else about the block follows from reading it properly.

December also carries a planning job nothing else in the year has room for. Internal Assessment deadlines in DP2 cluster in the term after the mocks, and the Extended Essay is usually at or near its final internal deadline. A single ninety-minute session in the break, spent on structure, criteria and what the next draft has to show, saves weeks of drift in February. Measured against the time it takes, it is the cheapest hour in the whole two-year programme.

Keep the load light anyway. Three weeks with family in them is still a holiday, and a DP2 student who works through all of it walks into mocks tired. Two subjects, four sessions each, written work in between, and the final four days off entirely is a plan that survives contact with an actual December.

sections.heading: Spring break and the deadlines that passed months ago
paragraphs: By the spring break the decisions that matter have already been made, and most were made against a deadline nobody mentioned at the time. Cambridge's March 2027 series shows the shape plainly: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries were due 27 November 2026 and forecast grades 27 February 2027, with results on Cambridge Direct from 13 May 2027 and certificates in late June. The holiday that mattered for that series was the winter one.

Cambridge runs International GCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential that you use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your school's exams officer which zone it sits in before planning a single session around a date.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so treat the live official PDF as the only version worth planning against. IB dates are not published here: confirm the current session window with ibo.org or your school's IB coordinator.

What the spring fortnight is actually for is technique under time. Full papers, marked against the published scheme, with the distance between the student's answer and the band descriptor read out loud rather than implied. IB spring break revision in Sharjah, Dubai or Al Ain looks identical in content and differs only in when the school's own internal mock week sits, which is itself a locally approved date.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and when a holiday session can actually start
paragraphs: Ramadan reshapes a UAE study week more than any other part of the calendar, and it moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, so advice that worked two years ago may now land in a different term altogether. School days typically shorten, families eat late, and a student who was sharp at five in the afternoon in January is not sharp at the same hour while fasting. A Ramadan IB tutoring schedule that ignores this produces attended sessions and very little learning.

The answer is to move the slot rather than the content. Post-Iftar sessions, usually from around nine in the evening Gulf Standard Time, work well for Diploma students: the fast is broken, the house is awake, and concentration is genuinely available. Some families prefer the quiet hour before Suhoor for written practice instead. Either works with a tutor on live video, because no travel has to be arranged around it. Tell us which window your household actually keeps at booking rather than discovering it in week two.

Eid Al Fitr and Eid Al Adha are short, and the honest advice is usually to leave them alone. Three to five days with family is not a revision window. Where Eid holiday IB sessions earn their place is a single milestone: the Maths exploration dataset gets collected, the Extended Essay research question gets narrowed, the History Internal Assessment source list gets finalised. One session, one deliverable, then stop and let the holiday be a holiday.

Travel compounds all of it. Families leave for Eid and for the summer, and the time zone leaves with them. A block agreed in Gulf Standard Time can be rescheduled to London, Karachi, Nairobi or Toronto hours without changing tutor, which is the main practical advantage of lessons that happen on a screen rather than in a car.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies in a holiday plan
paragraphs: Almost every Diploma holiday plan we are sent leaves out the three subjects the UAE requires. In Dubai, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirement to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. These sit alongside six Diploma subjects, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, and they carry school grades that land on the report card parents then react to.

The rules around them are specific enough to change what a holiday block should contain. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arab students take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details matter for scheduling and for material. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes, and lets schools vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, so a short frequent holiday session matches the format the school already uses. And for these subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the ministry is strictly prohibited. A holiday block therefore works from your school's own scheme of work and from nothing else.

Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a credential you can ask your own school about directly. For holiday support the sensible brief is narrow: reading fluency, written register, and the specific vocabulary the school's current unit plan names.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in the weeks when coursework finally gets finished
paragraphs: Holidays are when Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay actually get finished, because term weeks have no room for sustained writing. That makes a break the point of highest temptation in the two-year programme, and it is where these search results are least honest. At least one site ranking for queries like this one sells finished Internal Assessments outright at a four-figure dirham price. Under IB academic-honesty rules, submitting that work is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

The line itself is not vague. A tutor may teach the skill the task assesses, explain the criteria letter by letter and what each band descriptor is asking for, question a method until the student finds the flaw themselves, point at a paragraph and say it does not do what the criterion requires, and model a technique on a different example. A tutor may not supply sentences, rework a paragraph into its final form, pick the research question, or hand over data the student did not collect. The author is the student, every time.

IB IA support during school holidays works best as a sequence of short checkpoints rather than one long session. The student arrives with a draft, the tutor reads it against the criteria, and the student leaves with a list of changes to make alone. Three of those across a two-week break move an exploration from criterion-level guesswork to something a school's internal marker can recognise. The record of who contributed what is cleaner this way too, which matters if a school ever asks the question.

One more boundary is worth stating plainly. No tutor here supplies past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or syllabus documents as files. Those belong to the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and reproducing them is a copyright matter rather than a grey area. We point at the official page and work from the material your school has legitimately given your child.

sections.heading: What a holiday block costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: A holiday block is priced per hour in this market, and the hourly figure is the number competitors hide. Three of the six strongest pages in these results publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The table below is the market in dirhams, with the provider that published each figure named and the month the figure was read. None of it is an IB Gram price list.

Read it as bands rather than quotes. A university student teaching online and a subject specialist with Diploma teaching experience are different products at AED 45 and AED 300, and the cheaper one is not a saving if the block has to be run again in December. The in-home row carries travel inside it, which is where a chunk of the AED 180 to AED 500 range comes from: an hour at a villa in Khalifa City is an hour of teaching plus an hour of driving, and somebody is paying for the driving.

Context helps as well. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are the fixed cost in a family budget; a holiday block is the discretionary one, and a four-week specialist block at the market's mid rate is a real decision rather than a rounding error. Price the block, not the hour, before agreeing to anything.

For our own numbers the honest answer is a conversation. What a block costs depends on the subject, the level, the number of hours and the window, and printing one figure for every Diploma subject would be inventing it. Start with a trial lesson at no charge, one lesson per subject, then ask for the whole block in writing with the session count and the topic list attached.

sections.heading: Is a holiday tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and it is regulated, and the regulation is specific. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the smart app, the website or the e-services system.

The consequence of not holding one is not hypothetical. u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MOHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, and figures circulating online could not be verified, so no amount appears on this page. The point for a parent is simpler than the law: a tutor who cannot answer the permit question has told you something useful, and a holiday block is long enough that the answer is worth having.

A tuition centre is a different legal animal from an individual. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That permit is issued to institutions with premises, not to individual tutors, which is why any page implying a regulator has vetted its tutor list is describing something that does not exist in that form.

IB Gram matches students with tutors. It does not operate a school or a training institute in the UAE, and nothing on this page should be read as a regulator endorsing it. What we can do is be plain about the rules, name the official channels, and leave you able to ask the tutor the permit question yourself before a holiday block starts.

sections.heading: Equivalency, universities and what a holiday block is not for
paragraphs: Parents often ask whether a holiday block helps with Ministry of Education equivalency. It helps with grades, and grades feed the paperwork, but no tutoring is required for equivalency and nobody should imply otherwise. The British-track rule as published is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

One detail is worth knowing before you plan an Arabic holiday block for equivalency reasons: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. A page currently ranking for UAE equivalency queries states that candidates here must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. For the American track, English proficiency is shown through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math.

For IB there is no figure on this page, deliberately. No IB points threshold for equivalency has been read on a ministry source, so publishing one would be guessing with a family's university application. Check the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate, and treat any site that quotes a confident number without citing the ministry with the scepticism it deserves.

The useful holiday work here is ordinary: get the five IGCSE subjects secure, get the Advanced Level or Diploma grades where they need to be, and keep the documents in order. Equivalency and attestation are processes the authorities run, not services a tutoring platform performs, and anyone offering to handle them for you is outside their lane.

process.title: Tell us the break and the deliverable
process.description: Say which holiday, which subjects, which level, and what you want to be true at the end of it. Chemistry HL in December, fixing equilibrium and data handling before mocks, is a brief we can staff. Some revision over the holidays is not, and it is the request that most reliably produces a wasted block.

process.title: Send the evidence first
process.description: The marked paper, the report card, the Internal Assessment draft, the school's scheme of work for the current unit. Forty-five minutes of a tutor reading that before the first session is worth more than two sessions of diagnosis, and it keeps the block working from your school's material instead of a generic revision course.

process.title: We check who is free in that window
process.description: Holiday weeks are the busiest in the year and also the weeks tutors take leave. Availability is confirmed against your exact dates before any quote. If no specialist at that subject and level is free, we say so rather than putting a generalist into a Higher Level slot and hoping.

process.title: Trial lesson, then the block in writing
process.description: One trial lesson per subject, at no charge. If it works you get the block written down: the number of sessions, the topic list, the practice set between sessions, and the price for the whole block rather than an hourly rate you have to multiply yourself and hope you guessed right.

process.title: The block runs, then hands over
process.description: Sessions happen on live video at the agreed time, rescheduled to your time zone if the family travels mid-block. At the end you get a short handover note you can give the school: what was covered, what is now secure, and what still needs watching in the first month of term.

whyPoints.title: The plan starts from your school's material
whyPoints.description: KHDA's own rule for the mandatory UAE subjects is that different or additional content needs prior permission from the ministry, and the same instinct is good practice everywhere else. A block built from your school's scheme of work and your child's marked papers beats one built from somebody's generic holiday revision course.

whyPoints.title: Every dirham figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: Each rate on this page is attributed to the provider that published it and the month it was read, and none of them is presented as our price list. No statistic appears without a source behind it. You can check the numbers yourself before deciding what a holiday block is worth to your family.

whyPoints.title: The regulator map is on the page
whyPoints.description: Which authority licenses your school, what it approves, and what that does to your holiday dates, set out in a table rather than hidden behind a form. Of the competitor pages we studied for these queries, not one names ADEK at all, and several never mention a regulator in any form.

whyPoints.title: One-to-one and live online
whyPoints.description: No driving, so a fifty-minute session is economic and a short daily pattern becomes possible. The match is made on subject and level rather than on who lives nearby, which is the difference between a Chemistry HL specialist and the nearest tutor with a free Tuesday evening.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help stops at the student's own work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria and gives feedback on a draft the student has produced. The student is the author. Any offer of finished assessed work in exchange for a fee is malpractice under IB rules, and it is the student who carries the finding, not the site that sold it.

faqs.question: Can my child take IB lessons during the UAE summer break?
faqs.answer: Yes, and summer is the block that changes most. Six to eight weeks is long enough for a full pass through a subject with practice attached, which is why most UAE families book it for the transition years: MYP5 into DP1, or DP1 into DP2. Lessons run one-to-one on live video, so a family travelling in July keeps the same tutor rather than restarting in August with somebody new. The pattern that works is three to five hours a week across two subjects, with written work between sessions and the last week left clear before term restarts.

faqs.question: How many weeks of the summer holiday should an IB student actually work?
faqs.answer: Four to six of the eight, with a clear break at either end. Starting in the first week usually fails because the student has not stopped yet, and working through the final week leaves them tired for the first unit of the new term. Within those weeks keep new teaching under about five hours. Past that, retention falls and resentment rises, which costs more in September than the extra hours bought. Two subjects, four short sessions a week, written practice between them. A block that is tolerated gets finished; one that is endured gets abandoned in week three.

faqs.question: What should a DP2 student do with the two weeks before January mocks?
faqs.answer: Work from the marked November internal paper rather than from the syllabus. A student who lost marks across two Chemistry Paper 2 questions has a specific, fixable problem; the same student told only that they scored a 4 will reread everything and arrive with both gaps intact. Pick one or two subjects, four sessions each, and put a timed question in every session. Leave the final four days of the break alone. The mock grade feeds the predicted-grade conversation with the university counsellor, which is why this short block is worth more per hour than any other in the year.

faqs.question: Do UAE school holiday dates differ between Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah?
faqs.answer: They can, and more often than parents expect. Private schools are licensed emirate by emirate, KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, and each school publishes its own calendar under that licence. Dubai also has schools on a September start and schools on an April start, so two families in the same community can be on different holidays. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves assessment methods as well as curricula, so internal test weeks move too. Check your own school's published calendar before booking a block.

faqs.question: Who approves the academic calendar my child's private school follows?
faqs.answer: The emirate's regulator, through the licence the school holds. u.ae sets out the map: KHDA oversees private education in Dubai, ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge regulates Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The IB sets windows for its own assessment sessions; it does not set your school's term dates.

faqs.question: Does my child need Arabic or Islamic Education support over the break?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and these are the subjects holiday plans forget. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. They carry school grades, and they are taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab students. KHDA also states that different or additional content needs prior permission from the ministry, so a holiday block here works from your school's scheme of work: reading fluency, written register, named vocabulary.

faqs.question: Can a holiday tutor help with an Internal Assessment due in term three?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits. A tutor can teach the skill the task assesses, explain each criterion letter and what its band descriptors demand, question a method until the student finds the flaw, and give feedback on a draft the student has produced. A tutor cannot supply sentences, pick the research question, or hand over data the student did not collect. The student is the author of every sentence. The format that works over a break is short checkpoints: draft in, feedback against criteria, changes made alone, repeat. Any site selling finished assessed work is selling the student a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Can holiday sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Diploma students it is usually the better slot. During Ramadan school days typically shorten and families eat late, so a session at five in the afternoon that worked in January is being taught to a fasting teenager. Post-Iftar, from around nine in the evening Gulf Standard Time, concentration is genuinely available; some families prefer the quiet hour before Suhoor for written practice. Because lessons are on live video, no travel has to be arranged around either window. Tell us which pattern your household actually keeps at booking rather than in week two.

faqs.question: What does a two-week IB holiday intensive cost in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Price the block rather than the hour. Market rates here run roughly AED 45 to 150 for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel included, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB specialist, as published by those providers and read in October 2026. Sixteen hours at the specialist mid-band is therefore a four-figure dirham decision. None of those are IB Gram prices; ask for the whole block in writing after a trial lesson instead of multiplying an hourly rate.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working through the holidays need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and, according to u.ae, is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. u.ae also states that individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so none appears here. Ask the tutor directly.

faqs.question: We travel for six weeks in summer, so can lessons follow a different time zone?
faqs.answer: That is the ordinary case for UAE families and it is handled at booking. A block agreed in Gulf Standard Time can be rescheduled to London, Karachi, Nairobi or Toronto hours without changing tutor, because nothing physical has to move. Tell us the dates and the destination while the block is being planned rather than halfway through, so session times are set once and stay set. Families who are away for the whole of July often prefer a four-week block in August with the travel weeks clear, which also keeps the work closer to the start of term.

faqs.question: Is the IGCSE November series a reason to use the summer holiday differently?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the preparation window sits in the summer rather than the spring. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge also runs a November series, timetabled by administrative zone. A student entered for November revises through July, August and the October half-term, with results arriving the following January: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Confirm entry deadlines with your school's exams officer, because they fall in the preceding term.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free in the holiday window we want?
faqs.answer: We say so before taking the booking. Holiday weeks are the busiest of the year and the weeks tutors also take leave, so availability is checked against your exact dates before a quote is given. If nobody at the right subject and level is free, the options are a different window, a different session pattern, or a tutor outside the Gulf time zone whose evening is your morning. What we will not do is put a generalist into a Higher Level slot and let you discover the mismatch in session three.

faqs.question: Will holiday tuition help with UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Indirectly at best, and no tutoring is required for it. For British-curriculum students the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. American-track applicants show SAT Mathematics of at least 450, and English through IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing. No verified IB points threshold is published, so confirm the IB route on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: How is holiday tuition different from weekly term-time lessons?
faqs.answer: The constraint changes. In term the question is where to find an hour between six Diploma subjects, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the mandatory UAE subjects. In a holiday nothing competes, so the block can be frequent, short and cumulative: four fifty-minute sessions a week against one named topic list, with written practice between them. That pattern is impossible in October and ordinary in July. It also means the deliverable has to be decided in advance, because a holiday with no named outcome produces a student who has reread notes and learned nothing new.

faqs.question: Should we use the Eid break for IB tutoring at all?
faqs.answer: Usually for one thing only. Eid Al Fitr and Eid Al Adha are three to five days with family in them, and treating that as a revision window produces resentment and very little learning. Where a session earns its place is a single milestone: the Maths exploration dataset collected, the Extended Essay research question narrowed, a History source list finalised. One session, one deliverable, then stop. If a subject genuinely needs rebuilding, the summer or the December break is the block for it, and the Eid days are better spent not studying.

ib-holiday-tuition.closingHeading: Pick the break, name the outcome, then book it
ib-holiday-tuition.closingBody: The holiday is the only part of a UAE school year where you decide what the week contains. Use it deliberately: one or two subjects, a named topic list taken from your school's own scheme of work, a marked paper to start from, and a written plan with an end date on it. Tell us which break, which subjects and which level, and we will confirm who is free for those exact dates before quoting anything. Lessons run one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time, or in whichever time zone you happen to be in that month. Start with a trial lesson, one per subject, at no charge.

intro.heading: Two rulebooks sit behind every home tuition decision in the UAE
paragraphs: Search for IB home tuition in the UAE and the results argue about price, hours and tutor quality. Almost none of them mention the two rulebooks a family is actually working inside. The first is the permit system: private tutoring here is licensed work, and the person teaching your child is meant to hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The second is your child's school system, where an emirate authority decides which curriculum may be taught, which subjects are compulsory beside it and how many weekly minutes those subjects take.

Those two rulebooks decide more than they appear to. They decide who may legally sit in your living room and charge for an hour of teaching. They decide whether the teacher your child already trusts is permitted to take your money at all. They decide how much of the week is committed before a tutor is booked, because Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside the Diploma in Dubai regardless of the licensed international curriculum. And at the end of Year 13 they decide what a Diploma has to become on paper before a UAE university admissions office will read it.

IB Gram's own position is worth stating before anything else. Lessons are delivered live online, one-to-one, over video, on Gulf Standard Time. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is not a workaround for the permit rules, and it is not a compromise. A Diploma student sitting Chemistry at Higher Level needs a Chemistry Higher Level teacher, not the best-qualified person willing to drive to Mirdif on a Tuesday evening in October. Online one-to-one is how a family in Fujairah gets the same specialist a family in Jumeirah gets.

The rest of this page is built to be used rather than skimmed. It sets out who may tutor privately and what to ask them for, which authority sits above your child's school and what that authority controls, how the mandatory ministry subjects are organised, what the UAE market charges and what the travel inside that charge is really worth, where the line sits on coursework, what the Ministry of Education asks for at equivalency, and which exam dates are genuinely published. Every figure carries its source. Where a date could not be verified at source, the page says so rather than guessing.

One caveat belongs at the top. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing here should be read as implying one. Schools are named because they are the system your child sits inside, not because they are clients. Where a regulator's rule is quoted, the authority is named so you can read the original instead of taking our summary of it on trust.

ib-home-tuition.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and in the UAE each stage of it sits beside a set of subjects the regulator requires. The four programmes below are described as a UAE parent meets them: what the stage assesses, and what the local school system adds on top of it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Teachers assess through units of inquiry, portfolios and an exhibition in the final year. Tuition at this stage is almost never about exam technique; it is about reading fluency, number sense and the written expression a child will need two programmes later. Parents usually come to us after a parent-teacher meeting rather than after a report card.
programmes.countryNote: A PYP school in Dubai still has to deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies to KHDA's weekly time requirement, and the Arabic strand is where PYP parents most often ask for separate support. Because there is no external paper to aim at, the useful measure is whether a child can read an unfamiliar Arabic passage aloud and answer questions on it without help.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. Students lose marks less for not knowing content than for not answering the command term in front of them. The personal project in the final year is the first piece of long independent work most students have attempted.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE families use the MYP's final year as the decision point between staying with the IB and moving to IGCSE, because a sizeable share of their neighbours' children sit Cambridge or Edexcel papers instead. That decision is worth making on the subjects a school can actually staff at Higher Level, not on reputation. The mandatory ministry subjects continue through the MYP unchanged.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries internally assessed coursework alongside the papers, and the coursework is marked by the teacher and moderated externally. The common failure is not a weak subject but a timetable collision between three internal assessment deadlines and the mock papers.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is a minority route in the UAE: in Dubai the IB accounted for roughly a 7% share of private-school enrolment in 2024-25. That is the whole reason Higher Level specialists are hard to find inside a driving radius, and the reason an online match beats a local one for subjects such as Physics HL, Economics HL and Arabic A. Equivalency paperwork then matters for UAE university applications.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by far fewer schools than the Diploma, so students on it are often the only candidate in their year taking a particular DP subject at Standard Level.
programmes.countryNote: A CP student in the UAE frequently needs exactly one thing: a specialist in the single DP course their school runs for a handful of candidates. That is the clearest case for online one-to-one tuition in the country, because the local pool for one Standard Level subject in one school is effectively nobody. Equivalency for a CP leaver should be checked with the Ministry before applications open, not after.

ib-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects UAE families ask for most, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to go. Every description is about the paper set and the coursework, because that is what a tutor can change in a term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The calculus-heavy route, and the one most UAE engineering and economics applicants are told to take. Higher Level adds an options-free but deeper syllabus and a third paper of extended problem solving. Marks go on unjustified steps and on proof questions that students treat as calculations. The exploration is where a strong mathematician often underperforms.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work, with a graphical calculator expected throughout. It is not the easy route; Higher Level statistics and the third paper's extended investigation defeat students who chose it to avoid calculus. Check the course requirement published by the universities on your child's list before switching from Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward precision with units and vector direction; students lose marks writing correct physics in the wrong notation. Higher Level extends the syllabus and adds data-analysis demands in the final paper. The internal assessment stands or falls on whether the method actually controls what it claims to control.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the usual pressure points, and the ones Higher Level students most often ask for weekly help with. The internal assessment is a design problem before it is a chemistry problem, which is why it is worth starting a year before the deadline rather than a month.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap. Students revise terminology and then lose marks on application questions set in unfamiliar contexts and on data interpretation from a study they have never seen. Command terms do most of the damage: outline, explain and evaluate each want a different shape of answer.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries more marks than students expect, and the written commentaries need real published articles rather than convenient ones. Higher Level adds quantitative demands that catch out students who chose Economics as an essay subject. Evaluation, not description, separates a 5 from a 7.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A case-study subject where marks are lost by answering in general terms rather than from the stimulus provided. The internal assessment requires genuine primary or secondary research on a real organisation, and UAE students often pick a company they cannot actually get information about.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper on unseen non-literary texts are where UAE students most often need structured practice, especially those who have moved between curricula. Higher Level adds an extended essay-length paper. Analysis of how a text works, rather than what it says, is the skill being marked.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic sits in two places at once for most UAE students: as an IB language subject and as a KHDA mandatory subject with its own ministry curriculum. First-language and additional-language students are taught separately at school and should be supported separately out of it, because the expectations and the language of instruction differ.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Few UAE schools staff this at Higher Level, so candidates are often one of two or three in a year group. The solution requires working code and documented testing, not a description of an idea, and students underestimate how long the development stage takes once school deadlines are set.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The core is where Diploma points are quietly won and lost. TOK is assessed on an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay; the Extended Essay is a supervised piece of independent research. Both are marked on the student's own thinking, which sets a hard limit on what any tutor may contribute.

ib-home-tuition.regionsTitle: Who regulates where: the emirates, grouped by authority
ib-home-tuition.regionsIntro: Tuition is delivered online everywhere below, so the practical difference between these places is not travel time — it is which authority sits above the school, what that authority controls, and how thin the local pool of IB specialists is.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA licenses the curriculum, inspects the school and sets the mandatory-subject requirements every private school must meet. It also issues the Educational Services Permit a tuition centre with premises needs. The largest school market in the country, and still a minority IB one.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff restrict paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the same school, which narrows the list of people you may legitimately hire from inside your child's school.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK, not a separate authority, which surprises families who have moved from Dubai. A smaller school list means fewer schools running the full Diploma subject spread, so a Higher Level specialist for a minority subject will almost always be matched online rather than locally.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fee and curriculum approval sitting with the emirate means the school, not a parents' group, is the reliable source on what your child will sit.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education here with the same approval powers over fees, curricula and assessment methods as Sharjah's authority, across a much shorter school list. Families here are the clearest beneficiaries of a tutor pool that is not limited by driving distance.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman. Many families commute to Dubai or Sharjah for school, so the usable tuition slot is late: after the drive home, after dinner, and often after a younger sibling's bedtime. Evening-only availability is the norm, not a request.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market in the country, which makes online delivery less a preference than the only way to reach a Diploma subject specialist at Higher Level on a weekday evening at a sensible rate.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory, on the east coast and separated from the western emirates by a mountain drive. Any model that depends on a specialist travelling to the family twice a week fails here on arithmetic alone, whatever the hourly rate quoted.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's IB schools sit inside a market of 227 private schools teaching 17 curricula, so two children on the same street can be entered for entirely different papers. Ask which programme and which year group a school actually runs at Higher Level before assuming a subject is available.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, under ADEK
schoolClusters.note: Families in this cluster name a mix of IB, British and American schools when they contact us, which is a fair picture of the emirate. ADEK's ethics rules are the reason a request for your child's own class teacher, paid privately, is one we decline rather than negotiate.

Fewer schools, longer commutes and smaller Diploma cohorts. A student can be one of three candidates in a Higher Level subject, which changes what tuition is for: not remediation, but the specialist conversation a three-student class cannot always sustain.

modes.description: A fixed hour each week in one subject at one level, with the tutor working from the school's own scheme of work and deadline list rather than a generic plan. This is what most Diploma families book first, usually in a single subject, and it is the pattern that makes a difference over two terms rather than two weeks.

The work stays the student's own throughout: the tutor teaches the technique, questions the method, and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. Nothing is supplied for insertion, and nothing is produced on the student's behalf.

sections.heading: What a UAE family is really asking for when they search for home tuition
paragraphs: The phrase means a specialist, one child and no classroom. It rarely means that someone must physically be in the house. When families explain the request, the three things they describe are a tutor who knows the exact paper their child sits, an hour that survives contact with a UAE school day, and a person they can hold to account. Travel is a means to those ends, and in this country it is an expensive one.

The market offers four ways to get there. An individual tutor who travels to the family, at the top of the published rate bands because the drive is inside the fee. A tuition centre with premises, which is a licensed business rather than an individual and needs its own permit. A group class, cheaper but fixed to somebody else's pace. Or live one-to-one online, which separates the specialist from the postcode entirely. IB Gram does the fourth, and only the fourth, for families in the UAE.

So the honest answer to the search is this. You can buy IB home tuition in the UAE in the literal sense, at between roughly AED 180 and AED 500 an hour according to published market rates, and some families will decide the physical presence is worth it. What you cannot reliably buy that way is a Higher Level specialist in a minority subject on a Tuesday evening in your own community. The IB is a 7% share of Dubai's private-school enrolment. The specialist your child needs is usually not the nearest one, and online one-to-one is how that stops mattering.
bullets: What families ask for: the right specialist, a workable hour, someone accountable
What they usually do not need: a car journey built into the hourly rate

sections.heading: Who the law permits to tutor your child privately
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work with a licence attached. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through MoHRE, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone offering private lessons without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting you a dirham figure for the penalty is quoting something that cannot be checked.

The eligible categories are wider than most parents assume. They include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The route is MoHRE's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days and no fee published.

What this means at your end is a question, not a worry. Ask any tutor you are about to pay whether they hold the permit, and ask what subject and level they actually teach rather than what they can cover. The table below sets out each category and what is reasonable to ask for before the first paid hour. It applies to a tutor at the door and to a tutor on a screen equally: the permit is about the work, not the format.

sections.heading: The own-school rule, and the offer worth turning down
paragraphs: One request comes up more than any other: can we hire the teacher who already teaches the class? It is an understandable instinct and it runs into the rules. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. This has been press-reported rather than read by us in the current ADEK policy document, so verify the exact wording with the school before relying on it.

The conflict is easy to see once it is named. The same adult would be setting the classwork, marking the assessment that feeds the report, and being paid privately by the family whose child is being marked. Add internally assessed coursework to that, where the teacher is both supervisor and moderated marker, and the position becomes untenable for the teacher long before it becomes a problem for the family. An offer that leads with your child's own teacher, privately, is an offer to put a teacher's employment at risk.

The practical consequence is small. A tutor from outside the school is better placed anyway, because they can say the unpopular thing about a topic choice or a predicted grade without a staffroom to go back to. What matters is that they teach the same syllabus and level, work from your child's actual deadline list, and never become a second marker of work the school will moderate. That is the brief we match against, and it is why we decline the own-teacher request rather than quietly route around it.

sections.heading: Which authority sits above your child's school, and what it approves
paragraphs: Five bodies cover private schools in the UAE and most search results name none of them. In Dubai, KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The part that matters for planning is what these authorities control beyond publishing an inspection judgement. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is approval over what your child studies and how it is assessed, not only over how well the school did last year. KHDA, in parallel, sets the mandatory-subject requirements every private school must meet and issues the permit a tuition centre with premises needs in order to trade.

There is a federal baseline underneath all of it. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That single rule is why an IB school in Dubai still timetables Arabic and Islamic Education, and it is the reason a tuition plan built only around six IB subjects usually misses the two the school report will also carry.

sections.heading: The ministry subjects already sitting on your child's timetable
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For an IB family this is the single most overlooked line in the week. Six Diploma subjects plus the core is already a full load, and the KHDA mandatory subjects are additional to it rather than instead of something.

The organisation rules are specific enough to plan around. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit; schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

Those language rules carry into tuition. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. And for these subjects specifically, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which is why our support here works from the school's own materials.

sections.heading: Dubai's school market in numbers, and the specialist problem it creates
paragraphs: Dubai published the figures that explain why finding an IB specialist locally is harder than the size of the city suggests. In 2024-25 the emirate's private schools taught 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum holding a 37% share of enrolment, Indian 26%, American 14% and the International Baccalaureate 7%. The market is enormous and it is also fragmented, which is a different problem from scarcity.

Growth is not changing the ratio quickly. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family budgeting tuition alongside fees, a fee freeze is the most useful planning fact of the year.

Put the two together and the practical conclusion is straightforward. In a market where the IB is a minority board spread thinly across 227 schools, the number of teachers in your community who have taught your child's specific Higher Level paper recently is small, and the number of those willing to drive to you at a sensible rate is smaller still. sections.heading: What home tuition costs in the UAE, and what the travel inside it is worth
paragraphs: Most pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and the ones that do quote dollars. Here are the published bands in dirhams, attributed, as of October 2026. Budget online tuition, often delivered by a university student, runs from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to AED 300. A visiting tutor at a UAE address runs AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is inside the fee. An IB or IGCSE subject specialist is quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and named premium tuition reaches AED 650.

These are market rates published by other providers, not an IB Gram price list. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Ask any provider in writing whether the quoted figure includes VAT before comparing two numbers.

The column worth studying is the one nobody prints: how many minutes of teaching sit inside the money. A visiting tutor billing 90 minutes in a UAE evening is covering a drive, a lift, a greeting and a settling-in period from the same fee. That is not dishonesty, it is geography, and it is why the in-home band starts above the online specialist band rather than beside it. Decide what you are buying with the difference.
