ib-home-tutor-fees.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects to families across the Emirates over live video. Each profile names the subjects and levels that tutor actually teaches, because the level is the single biggest driver of what an hour costs, and a Higher Level specialist is not interchangeable with a general maths tutor.

intro.heading: What a UAE family is actually buying by the hour
paragraphs: A parent searching for IB home tutor fees in the UAE is usually trying to answer one question: is the number I was just quoted reasonable? The honest answer is that the quote is almost meaningless on its own. Across the providers we checked in October 2026, the same hour of IB teaching was advertised anywhere between AED 45 and AED 650. That is not a market with one price. It is six different products sharing one label.

The cheapest end of the range is a university student revising alongside your child from the same textbook. The top end is a specialist who has taught one subject at Higher Level for a decade and prices scarcity. In between sit qualified subject teachers, agency-matched tutors, tuition-centre group classes and visiting tutors whose rate quietly carries a car, a petrol bill and forty minutes of Sheikh Zayed Road. Those are not variations on a theme; they buy different things, and comparing them by hourly rate alone is how families end up paying twice.

Three of the six highest-ranking pages for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do publish quote in US dollars — a currency no UAE family pays a tutor in. One page's own frequently asked questions ask what tutoring costs and then decline to answer. So the market has trained parents to expect a consultation call before a number, which is exactly the opposite of what a parent needs at the moment of searching.

This page does the opposite. It publishes the AED bands other providers advertise, names who advertises them, breaks a quote down into the drivers that move it, and shows what a fair invoice looks like line by line. Where the number depends on something only your child's school can tell you — which board sets the papers, which session they sit, how many Higher Levels they carry — the page says so rather than guessing.

One structural point before the figures. IB Gram does not operate a visiting-tutor service anywhere in the Emirates; lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a cost statement as much as a logistics one. A visiting tutor's rate includes travel the student does not benefit from, and restricts your choice to whoever lives within a sensible drive. An online hour removes both constraints: a family in Khor Fakkan and a family in Jumeirah pay for the same thing and can book the same Chemistry Higher Level specialist.

Read the rate table first, then the eight drivers, then the invoice anatomy. By the end you should be able to take any quote you are given in this market, say which tier it sits in, and name what is in the number.

ib-home-tutor-fees.programmesIntro: Fees move with the programme, not only with the subject. A Primary Years enquiry and a Diploma Higher Level enquiry are priced differently because the supply of tutors is different and the assessment load is different. Here is how each IB programme behaves on a quote.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examinations, so tutoring at this stage is about securing number sense, reading fluency and written expression before the Middle Years Programme asks for them independently. Sessions are shorter — thirty to forty-five minutes holds a younger child's attention better than an hour — and the useful work is diagnostic: finding the specific gap, not covering ground broadly.
programmes.countryNote: PYP hours are the cheapest IB hours in this market because the supply of capable tutors is wide: a strong primary teacher can teach the whole curriculum. Budget-tier providers advertise from AED 45–65 an hour and that is often genuinely adequate here. Where families overspend is buying a subject specialist for a nine-year-old. Where they underspend is buying nothing at all and arriving at MYP with a reading-age gap that then costs considerably more to close.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP runs on eight subject groups, criterion-referenced assessment in each, and the Personal Project in the final year. Marks are awarded against published criteria rather than a percentage, which is where families get caught: a child can feel competent and still score in the middle band because the response never addresses the criterion strand being assessed. That is a teachable skill and it is most of what MYP tutoring is for.
programmes.countryNote: MYP sits in the middle of the UAE fee range, around AED 150–250 an hour for a qualified subject teacher online. Two things raise it. One is MYP Mathematics in the final year, where the extended course and the Diploma entry decision collide. The other is the Personal Project, where supervision is time-intensive and some providers price it as a block rather than an hour. A tutor may coach the process and give feedback on the student's own work; the project itself belongs to the student.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against published criteria and moderated externally, and the external papers carry the rest. The Diploma is where the fee conversation becomes a budget conversation, because a family is rarely buying one subject for one term — they are buying a two-year plan with peaks around coursework deadlines and the May session.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma rates in the UAE market start where MYP ends and go considerably higher: one agency advertises IB from AED 200 an hour against IGCSE from AED 150, a UK-based agency quotes around AED 270, and premium named tutors are advertised at AED 650. The driver is scarcity at Higher Level in the sciences and mathematics. Dubai's private sector has 227 schools but the IB accounts for roughly 7% of enrolment, so the pool of people who have taught Chemistry Higher Level repeatedly is small, and small pools price upward.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by a handful of schools in the Emirates and the support students need is usually split: Diploma-course teaching on one side, structured writing and project management on the other. The reflective project is the component families most often seek help with, and the honesty rules that govern the Extended Essay apply to it in the same way.
programmes.countryNote: CP enquiries are the hardest in this market to price, for a simple reason: supply. A tutor who has taught a Diploma course inside a CP cohort is rare, so families are frequently quoted a specialist Diploma rate for the subject element and a separate block for project supervision. Ask any provider to split the quote that way rather than accepting a blended figure. If no tutor is available for the career-related element, the honest answer is to say so, which is what we do rather than inventing coverage.

ib-home-tutor-fees.subjectsIntro: Subject is the second-largest driver of the number you are quoted, and it has almost nothing to do with difficulty. It is about how many people in reach can teach that subject at that level. Here is how the common IB subjects behave when a UAE family asks for a price.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested paid hour in the Emirates and the one where rates vary most. Higher Level carries Paper 3, a longer problem-solving paper that rewards sustained reasoning rather than recall, and tutors who can teach it command a premium. Standard Level pricing is far more competitive because the supply of capable teachers is wider.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Priced slightly below Analysis and Approaches at the same level, with one exception: Higher Level Applications is genuinely scarce, because many tutors trained on the pure-maths route and are uncomfortable with the statistics and modelling weighting. Check that a tutor has taught the route your child is on before accepting a rate for either.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The clearest example of scarcity pricing in this market. Higher Level organic and energetics teaching, plus the internal assessment, puts Chemistry at the top of most providers' science rate cards. Standard Level is cheaper to buy but families frequently buy too late — after the first grade comes back, rather than before the data-based paper practice starts.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level Physics tutors are thin on the ground outside the main Dubai and Abu Dhabi school clusters, which is why a family in Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah hears either a high visiting rate or nothing at all. Online removes the geography from the price. The internal assessment, with its uncertainty treatment, is where most marks are quietly lost.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Mid-range on most rate cards, with wide supply at Standard Level and genuine competition at Higher Level. The hours families buy here cluster around the internal assessment and command-term precision in extended response questions, where a strong student describes when the question asked them to explain and loses marks they understood perfectly well.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Reasonably priced relative to the sciences because supply is broader, but the internal assessment commentaries are time-hungry and some providers charge for them in blocks rather than hours. Higher Level adds quantitative content and a third paper, which is where the rate separates from Standard Level.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: One of the more affordable Diploma hours in this market, with a caveat: the case study released ahead of the examination means a concentrated burst of hours late in the year rather than steady weekly work. Families who budget monthly across two years overpay here; a block bought at the right moment does more.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Wide supply keeps the rate competitive, though the individual oral and the Higher Level essay need a tutor who has actually assessed against the criteria rather than taught general essay writing. The component where the marks move most per hour spent is usually the comparative paper.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Priced below English A at the same level, and often the better investment for a student who is strong in content subjects but fighting the language of assessment. Productive hours go into the writing task formats and the listening component rather than general conversation practice.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: A specific UAE case. A student may be taking Arabic for the Diploma and separately sitting the Ministry-mandated Arabic the school is required to deliver. Those are different courses with different materials, and a tutor should be clear which one an hour is for before quoting. Ask the school which stream your child is placed in first.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Scarce enough in the Emirates that rates are frequently quoted at the specialist tier regardless of level. The internal assessment is a developed solution with documentation, and the supervision load is heavier than families expect, so clarify whether feedback sessions are charged inside the hourly rate or separately.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Rarely priced on a standard rate card because the work is portfolio-based: the comparative study, the process portfolio and the exhibition each need different support. Hours are usually bought in bursts around internal deadlines, and a tutor's role is critique and technical teaching, never production of the pieces themselves.

ib-home-tutor-fees.regionsIntro: Hourly rates in this market are quoted against geography, not because teaching differs between the emirates but because a visiting tutor's travel does. Online delivery flattens that. Here is what the fee conversation looks like from each emirate, and what changes once travel leaves the invoice.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest tutor supply and the widest advertised range, from budget online providers to premium named tutors at AED 650. Visiting rates here carry traffic: a 5pm slot in Jumeirah and a 5pm slot in Dubai Silicon Oasis are not the same drive, and a two-hour minimum is standard precisely because of it.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Rates track Dubai closely, but the island-to-mainland distances are longer, so travel is a bigger share of a visiting quote. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, which removes the cheapest option families often ask about first.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Lower advertised rates on average, with a catch: many Sharjah families attend schools in Dubai, so the practical session window starts after a commute home. A visiting tutor priced for Sharjah may be unavailable at the only time the child is actually free, and availability, not the rate, becomes the binding constraint.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Small tutor pool, so a visiting specialist quote often includes travel from Sharjah or Dubai and arrives above the headline market band. Online pricing is identical to Dubai pricing here, which is the whole argument for it. Ajman's private schools are supervised federally by the Ministry of Education.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Families routinely report that no Higher Level science specialist is available locally at any price, which makes the hourly comparison moot. The emirate's Department of Knowledge regulates private education here. Online delivery is what turns an unavailable subject into a bookable one without a premium for distance.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: The east coast is where travel-inclusive pricing breaks down completely: nobody is driving over the mountains twice a week for a single hour, so quotes either disappear or arrive with a minimum block attached. Ministry of Education supervision applies, and online rates here match Dubai's exactly.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest market of the seven, with most secondary students commuting to Sharjah or Dubai schools. A visiting quote is effectively a Sharjah quote plus the drive. Sessions tend to start late in the evening because of the commute, which narrows the pool of tutors willing to take the slot at any rate.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Inspected by ADEK rather than by a separate Al Ain authority, and far enough from the capital that specialist visiting coverage is unreliable. Families here most often ask for a blended plan: online weekly sessions, with heavier blocks bought around internal assessment deadlines rather than spread evenly.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the IB at roughly 7% of enrolment. Seven new private schools are opening for 2026-27, three of them IB. More IB places does not mean more Higher Level specialists, which is why subject scarcity rather than school count sets the rate.

ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, Al Ain included. Distances inside the capital are long enough that visiting quotes separate sharply from online ones, and families on Saadiyat or in Khalifa City often find the time cost of a visit outweighs the hourly saving.

SPEA regulates private education in Sharjah and approves tuition fees, curricula and assessment methods; Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there; the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Fewer IB cohorts means fewer local tutors, so rate comparisons matter less here than whether the subject is covered at all.

ib-home-tutor-fees.modesIntro: How you buy the hours changes the effective cost more than the headline rate does. Four structures are common in this market, and each suits a different point in a student's year. All of them are delivered one-to-one over live video.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, paid by the hour
modes.description: The default and the most flexible. One or two sessions a week on a fixed slot, charged per session, with no commitment beyond the next lesson. It is the right structure when you are still establishing whether the match works, and it is the only structure in which you can stop cheaply.

modes.title: Prepaid block of hours
modes.description: A set number of hours bought up front and drawn down as needed. Providers discount these because the cash comes early and the scheduling risk moves to you. The structure suits a family who already knows the tutor works and wants the rate fixed before the exam term, when demand across this market tightens.

modes.title: Intensive block before a paper
modes.description: Six to twelve hours compressed into two or three weeks, aimed at one subject and one failure mode. This is the structure that moves grades per dirham spent, and it is also where market rates rise, because every family in the Emirates wants the same fortnight. Booking the slot early costs nothing and protects the rate.

modes.title: Coursework feedback sessions
modes.description: Scheduled sessions timed to the student's own internal deadlines rather than weekly. The tutor teaches the method, reads what the student has written and gives criterion-referenced feedback that the student then acts on alone. It is the component families most want help with and the one where the honesty line matters most, so it is priced and described separately.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, tier by tier
paragraphs: An IB tutor in the Emirates is advertised at between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour as of October 2026, and the band a quote sits in tells you more than the number does. The table below groups every rate we could attribute to a provider that published it. None of these are IB Gram prices; they are the market you are shopping in, so that a quote you receive can be placed rather than guessed at.

Read the bands as products rather than as quality grades. The budget tier is typically a university student or a recent graduate working from the same textbook as the class — genuinely useful for homework supervision and primary-level consolidation, and a false economy at Higher Level, where the value of the hour comes from having taught the component repeatedly. The qualified-teacher tier is where most families land and where the price-to-outcome relationship is strongest. The specialist tier prices scarcity: one subject, one level, taught many times.

The in-home band is the one to read most carefully. The published range of AED 180–500 an hour covers the lesson and the travel together, and no provider itemises the split. A tutor driving thirty minutes each way is spending an hour of working time to deliver an hour of teaching, and that hour is in your rate whether or not it appears on the invoice. The same arithmetic explains the two-hour minimum almost every visiting tutor in this market insists on.

Monthly packages advertised in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599–1,799 for four two-hour home visits. Divide them out before comparing: eight sessions at AED 799 is close to AED 100 an hour, which places that package firmly in the budget tier whatever the headline suggests.

sections.heading: The eight things that move a quote, and by how much
paragraphs: Once you know the bands, the useful question is why the same provider quotes two families differently for apparently the same hour. Eight drivers account for nearly all of it. Each one is something you can ask about directly, and a provider who cannot explain which drivers are in your number is quoting a feeling rather than a price.

Level does the heaviest lifting. Higher Level costs more than Standard Level because the content runs deeper, the extra paper changes what practice looks like, and the supply of tutors who have taught it is narrower. Subject scarcity comes next and compounds it: Chemistry and Physics at Higher Level, Computer Science at any level, and Higher Level Applications and Interpretation all price above the market average for supply reasons alone.

Then come the operational drivers, which families underestimate. The slot matters: a 4pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is the most contested three hours of the UAE tutoring day, and a tutor with a full diary prices it accordingly. Session length matters, because a 90-minute session carries one set-up rather than two. Notice period and cancellation terms matter, because a tutor holding a slot you may not use has to price that risk somewhere. Proximity to the examination session matters most of all, and the direction of travel is always up.

The last driver is the one nobody advertises: whether the hour includes work outside the lesson. Reading a draft, marking a past paper and writing a progress note all take time. Some providers price that inside the rate, some bill it, some do it unpaid and inconsistently. Ask which, because it is often the difference between two quotes that look identical.
bullets: Ask which level the quote assumes — a Standard Level rate applied to Higher Level work will be revised later
Ask what a 60-minute session actually contains versus a 90-minute one
Ask for the cancellation notice period in hours, in writing

sections.heading: Reading a tutoring quote line by line
paragraphs: Most disputes in this market are not about the hourly rate. They are about a line on an invoice nobody explained before the first lesson. The table below is the anatomy of a tutoring quote in the Emirates: what each line should mean, whether it is reasonable, and how a parent can check it without taking anyone's word for it.

Two lines deserve particular attention. The first is any charge described as licensing, registration or permit recovery. The UAE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. There is no licensing cost for a tutor to pass on, so a line that recovers one is a margin line wearing a regulator's clothes.

The second is tax. Ask plainly whether a quoted AED figure includes value added tax and ask for a tax registration number on the invoice if one is charged. The correct treatment of tuition fees under UAE tax law is a question for the Federal Tax Authority's own published guidance, not something a tutoring company should assert on a landing page, and a provider that adds tax at the point of payment after quoting a clean hourly figure has mispriced the quote rather than discovered a tax.

Everything else on a quote should map to something you can picture. If a line cannot be explained in one sentence that names what the parent receives, ask for it to be removed before the first session rather than after the third invoice.

sections.heading: A visiting hour and an online hour are not the same hour
paragraphs: Families comparing an AED 220 online rate with an AED 320 visiting rate usually conclude the difference is AED 100. It is not. The two options differ on five dimensions that all have money in them, and only one of them appears on the invoice.

Start with elapsed time. A visiting arrangement in this market almost always carries a two-hour minimum, because a tutor who drives forty minutes each way cannot make a single hour pay. So the real comparison is not AED 320 against AED 220; it is AED 640 for a two-hour block against AED 220 for the hour you actually wanted. For a family buying one weekly session on a specific gap, that is the whole decision.

Then consider the pool. A visiting arrangement restricts you to tutors who live within a sensible drive of your address at the exact time your child is free. In Dubai that pool is reasonably deep. In Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain, for Higher Level Chemistry, it may be empty at any price. A family that needs a Higher Level specialist and insists on a visit is frequently choosing between a generalist nearby and a specialist on video, which is a decision about teaching quality dressed up as a decision about format.

The third consideration is what the hour contains. Online sessions are recorded with a shared screen, the written work stays in one place, and a parent can see the tutor's annotations afterwards without asking. The fourth is attrition: the visiting slot that depends on a drive through a 5pm Sheikh Zayed Road is the slot that gets cancelled. The fifth is scheduling flexibility during Ramadan and examination weeks, when a post-Iftar session is simple to arrange over video and much harder to arrange around a commute.

sections.heading: Where tutoring money does the most work across two Diploma years
paragraphs: A family that spends evenly across twenty-four months spends more and gets less than a family that spends in the right four windows. The Diploma is not a flat workload; it has peaks, and money applied at a peak buys marks that the same money applied in a quiet term does not.

The first window is the transition in. A student arriving in the Diploma from IGCSE, the Middle Years Programme or a national curriculum has specific, nameable gaps — algebraic fluency before Analysis and Approaches, laboratory write-up conventions before the sciences, essay structure before Language and Literature. Six to ten hours in the first term, spent on diagnosis and repair, is the cheapest intervention in the whole two years because everything afterwards compounds on it.

The second window is internal assessment season in the first year and early second year. These components carry real weight, the mark comes from criterion-referenced judgement rather than content recall, and feedback on the student's own work is exactly what a tutor is for. The third window is the mock period, where the useful spend is not more teaching but forensic analysis of the scripts the student has just produced. The fourth is the final run, where technique and timing are the only things still movable.

What this means for a budget is simple. Hold money back for the mock-analysis and final-run windows rather than committing it to a weekly slot in a quiet term, and buy blocks rather than open-ended weekly sessions in the peaks. A family with a fixed monthly figure should treat it as an annual figure divided unevenly, not as twelve equal payments.

sections.heading: Fees nobody is entitled to charge a UAE family
paragraphs: Some charges in this market are not expensive; they are illegitimate. Knowing which is which is worth more to a parent than negotiating ten per cent off an hourly rate, so this section names them and gives the source you can check each one against.

The clearest is a completed piece of coursework. One site in this search results sells finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. That is academic malpractice under the IB's own rules, the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller, and no price makes it a service. A tutor's role is to teach the method, explain the criteria and give feedback on work the student has produced; the work itself belongs to the student and must. We say this in plain words because the alternative in this search results is an essay mill, and parents deserve to be told which they are looking at.

The second is a charge for board material. Official syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables are published by the IB, Cambridge International and Pearson, and reselling them as a resource pack is both a copyright problem and a sign the provider has nothing of its own to offer. A tutor's own written practice is worth paying for. A photocopied mark scheme is not.

The third is anything framed around the regulators. Nobody can charge a family to arrange Ministry of Education equivalency, and no tutoring company performs it — the process sits with the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority, and a parent applies through the official channel. Equally, there is no permit fee to recover, no inspection fee, and no circumstance in which tutoring is required for a school progression or a university application. A provider that implies otherwise is selling urgency.

sections.heading: Why Chemistry at Higher Level costs more than English at Standard Level
paragraphs: Subject pricing in the Emirates has almost nothing to do with how hard the subject is and almost everything to do with how many people within reach have taught it at that level. This is supply-side pricing, and once a parent sees it, several confusing quotes become obvious.

Consider the arithmetic. Dubai has 227 private schools and the IB accounts for roughly 7% of private-school enrolment, which is a modest base. Of the schools running the Diploma, only some offer Chemistry at Higher Level in a given year, each with one or two teachers. The number of people in the emirate who have taught Higher Level Chemistry through a full two-year cycle more than twice is therefore small, and those people are employed. English A at Standard Level sits at the other end: the pool includes every competent English teacher in the Emirates, and competition keeps the rate honest.

Scarcity has a second effect families notice too late: availability, not price, becomes the constraint. A Higher Level Physics tutor with four free evening slots in October has none in February, which is why the same tutor quoted the same rate in both months is effectively unbookable in the second. Booking early is the only discount a scarce subject offers.

This is also where online delivery changes the economics rather than merely the logistics. A visiting arrangement limits supply to one neighbourhood. A live video session draws on every available specialist in the time zone, which means a family in Fujairah and a family in Dubai Marina face the same price for the same subject — and, more usefully, the same chance of getting one at all.

sections.heading: Tuition fees in the context of everything else the year costs
paragraphs: A tutoring fee is never assessed in isolation. It sits inside a family budget that already contains school fees, examination entries, transport and, for Diploma families, university application costs. Putting the hourly rate next to those gives it a scale, and the scale is usually reassuring rather than alarming.

The fixed point this year is school fees. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second of Dubai's economic incentives packages. For a parent planning a tutoring budget, that matters: the largest line in the education budget is not moving, so a tutoring decision this year is being made against a stable base rather than a rising one. Nothing comparable has been announced for tutoring rates, which are set by thousands of independent providers and move with demand.

Examination entries are the line families forget. A student registered through their school has entries made and billed by the school, usually months before the papers; a private candidate arranges entries through a registered centre and pays that centre's own fee schedule. Those schedules are set by the centres and are not uniform across the country, so the only reliable figure is the one your centre gives you in writing. The same applies to attestation and equivalency charges, which belong to the Ministry and the attestation authority rather than to any tutor.

The one cost worth modelling properly is the cost of a second attempt. A retake means a fresh entry, a further term of preparation and, in the worst case, a deferred university place. Measured against that, a block of eight to ten hours bought at the right moment in the first attempt is the cheaper line, which is the entire argument for spending early and precisely rather than late and broadly.

sections.heading: Entry deadlines, sessions and the price of a late decision
paragraphs: Fees respond to the calendar, so the calendar is worth counting backwards. The pattern that catches UAE families is that entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, while tutoring decisions are usually made weeks ahead of them — by which point both the useful preparation window and the cheaper slots have gone.

Cambridge International is the clearest worked example, because its dates are published. For the March 2027 series the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct from 13 May and certificates in late June. Final entries fall more than two months before the first paper. Cambridge also runs June and November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that the correct zone timetable must be used and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. That is why two cousins at different schools in the same emirate can sit the same paper at different times.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations run in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is always the document to work from rather than any date restated on a tutoring page.

For the IB itself we deliberately publish no session or results date here. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a date on a page that turns out to be wrong costs a family far more than a missing date. UAE schools sit the May session, a smaller number sit November, and your child's coordinator holds the dates that actually apply. Plan the spend against the school's internal deadlines, which are set earlier than the external ones and are the dates your tutoring calendar should follow.

sections.heading: The honesty line, and the Arabic lessons you may already be paying for
paragraphs: Two things sit at the edge of every fees conversation in this market, and both are worth more to a parent than a discount. The first is what a tutor may and may not do. The second is what your child's school is already required to deliver, which occasionally turns out to be the thing you are being quoted for.

On the first: a tutor teaches the method, explains how a component is assessed, and gives criterion-referenced feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not author any part of an assessed component, does not edit one to completion, and does not supply material that the student then submits as their own. This is not caution for its own sake. Under the IB's rules the consequence of malpractice lands on the student, and a provider who blurs the line is selling a family a risk it has not priced. When a coordinator asks whether outside support was used, the honest answer should be comfortable to give.

On the second: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited, and the language of instruction is specified per stream. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic need the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

The consequence for a fee conversation is concrete. Mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and schools may vary the lesson length provided the weekly total is met, so your child already receives a defined quantity of this teaching. For those subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited — which means a tutor cannot credibly sell a bespoke Arabic or Islamic Education curriculum. Paid support here should be revision and language confidence built on the school's own material, priced modestly, and only where the school's provision has genuinely not landed.

sections.heading: What happens if nobody is free at the hour you want
paragraphs: Every provider in this search results implies infinite availability. None has it. The scarce combinations are predictable — Higher Level Chemistry or Physics, both Higher Level maths routes, Computer Science, Visual Arts, and anything at all in a 5pm Gulf Standard Time slot during the mock season — and a family deserves to hear that before paying rather than after.

Our position is to say which of three situations applies. Either a specialist is free in the slot you want, in which case the trial lesson happens that week. Or a specialist is available at a different hour, in which case the honest trade is a 7.30pm session with the right tutor against a 5pm session with a generalist, and most families who have been through a mock period choose the former. Or nobody covers the combination, in which case we say so and do not take a booking against a tutor we cannot name.

There is one more case worth naming. Where a subject has no UAE-based specialist free, support may be delivered by a specialist elsewhere in the same working time zone, teaching the same syllabus over the same video platform. That is disclosed, not concealed behind a local-looking telephone number. It changes nothing about the lesson and it should change nothing about the rate, and a provider who hides it is hiding the one fact that would let you compare quotes properly.

Scarcity also argues for booking the examination-term slot in the quiet term. The rate does not usually move much between October and February in this market; the diary does. A slot reserved early is the only real discount a scarce subject offers, and it costs nothing to reserve.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the slot
process.description: Three facts decide whether a price is even possible: the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, and which Gulf Standard Time window your child is actually free in. A quote given without all three will be revised later, which is how families end up feeling misled by a number nobody meant dishonestly.

process.title: Send what the tutor needs to be useful
process.description: The most recent report, a marked piece of work and the school's own deadline list. A tutor who has read a mock script arrives at the trial lesson with a diagnosis rather than a questionnaire, and that is worth more than any introductory discount. Send only what is relevant — school, grades and photographs of a child are not a package to hand over casually.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: The first session is a free trial lesson, one per student, with no payment details required to book it. Treat it as an assessment of the tutor rather than of your child: does this person know the component, and can they name where the marks are going? Ask the tutor at the end what the first six sessions would cover.

process.title: Agree the structure before the second session
process.description: Settle the rate per session length, the cancellation notice in hours, whether marking time is included, and whether you are buying weekly sessions or a block. Get it in a message you can scroll back to. Nearly every fee dispute in this market comes from one of those four points being assumed rather than stated.

process.title: Review after four sessions, against something measurable
process.description: Four sessions is enough to judge. The measure is not how the sessions felt but whether a specific, named weakness has moved: a paper section, a criterion strand, a topic. If it has not, change the plan or change the tutor rather than buying more of the same hour.

process.title: Re-plan at each peak, not each month
process.description: Before internal assessment season, before mocks and before the final run, reset the plan: more sessions, fewer, different subject, different tutor. A monthly direct debit running quietly through a quiet term is the most common way a UAE family overspends on tutoring without noticing.

whyPoints.title: Numbers with a source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or authority that published it, with the month we read it. Three of the highest-ranking pages for this search publish no price at all. A parent cannot judge a quote without a benchmark, and a benchmark without a source is just another assertion.

whyPoints.title: The hour buys teaching, not driving
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. Nobody is paid for a drive down Sheikh Zayed Road, there is no two-hour minimum to make a journey worthwhile, and a family in Fujairah pays what a family in Jumeirah pays for the same specialist.

whyPoints.title: The specialist, not the nearest person
whyPoints.description: Subject scarcity is the real constraint in this market, especially at Higher Level in the sciences and maths. Removing travel from the equation means the pool is every available specialist in the time zone rather than every tutor within a twenty-minute drive of your address.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the method, explains the criteria and gives feedback on what the student has produced. Nothing is authored on a student's behalf, at any price. One site in this search results sells finished internal assessments; the penalty for that falls on the student, and no rate makes it worth buying.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before payment
whyPoints.description: Where no specialist is free for a subject, level and slot, we say so instead of booking against a tutor we cannot name. Where support comes from a specialist outside the Emirates in the same working time zone, that is disclosed rather than hidden behind a local-looking number.

whyPoints.title: No regulator borrowed as a credential
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education and MoHRE are described here because UAE parents need to understand them. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them, states none, and operates no office or centre in the Emirates.

faqs.question: What is the full range of IB home tutor fees quoted in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates run from about AED 45 an hour to AED 650, which tells you the label covers several different products. Budget online providers advertise from AED 45–65 and one platform from AED 33–52. Qualified subject teachers online sit around AED 150–300, with one agency listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and A-Level work is advertised at AED 200–450 and above, including a UK agency at roughly AED 270. Visiting tutors quote AED 180–500 with travel inside the rate. A premium provider advertises AED 650. These are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, not ours.

faqs.question: Why do two tutors quote fees AED 300 apart for the same Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: Because they are selling different hours. The lower quote is often a generalist who will teach the content competently but has not taught that component repeatedly; the higher one has, and prices the scarcity. Other differences hide inside the gap: whether the rate covers marking and draft reading, whether the slot is in the contested 4pm to 7pm window, whether travel is bundled, and what the cancellation terms are. Ask each tutor how many times they have taught that subject at that level and what the hour includes beyond the lesson itself. The answers usually explain the whole difference.

faqs.question: Can a tutor charge a licensing or permit fee on top of the lesson fee?
faqs.answer: No, because there is no cost to recover. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through the MoHRE app, website or e-services. A line on your invoice described as licensing, registration or compliance recovery is therefore margin presented as a regulatory cost. Ask for it to be removed, or treat the total as the real hourly rate and compare it that way.

faqs.question: Should a matching or registration fee appear on the first invoice?
faqs.answer: Question it. Plenty of providers in this market charge nothing until a lesson has happened, so a fee payable before any teaching takes place is worth pushing back on. If a provider insists, ask three things in writing: what the fee buys that the hourly rate does not, what it is credited against if the first match does not work, and whether it recurs if you change tutor. A one-off administrative charge that is credited against your first paid session is defensible. A non-refundable fee for an introduction is not.

faqs.question: A month with Eid in it has fewer teaching weeks. How should that change what we pay?
faqs.answer: Count sessions, not months. A monthly package priced for four or eight sessions should deliver four or eight sessions, whatever the calendar does, and a month containing Eid or a school break will simply run longer. Ask whether unused sessions roll forward and how long they stay valid. During Ramadan the school day shortens and many families move to post-Iftar slots, which is straightforward over video. The rate should not change for a post-Iftar session; if it does, you are being charged for inconvenience rather than teaching, and that is a reasonable thing to query.

faqs.question: Which parts of a tutoring fee are negotiable and which are not?
faqs.answer: Session length and structure are the negotiable parts. Most providers price a 90-minute session below two separate hours, and a prepaid block below session-by-session billing, so the same teaching costs less bought differently. Slot timing is negotiable in the other direction: a late-evening or weekend-morning session is often cheaper than the contested after-school window. What is rarely negotiable is a specialist's headline rate at Higher Level in a scarce subject, because the constraint is supply rather than margin. Trying to negotiate that usually produces a different, less experienced tutor at the price you asked for.

faqs.question: What must never appear on a tutoring invoice under IB academic-honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Any line that amounts to assessed work supplied to the student. Internal assessments, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, the Personal Project and the Career-related Programme's reflective project must be the student's own, and a tutor's legitimate role is teaching the method, explaining the criteria and giving feedback on drafts the student has written. One site in this search results sells finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. The penalty for malpractice falls on the student, not the seller, so the only safe answer is that no price makes it a purchase. If an invoice implies otherwise, that is the whole answer about the provider.

faqs.question: Is it reasonable to be charged for past papers, mark schemes or a subject guide?
faqs.answer: No. Those documents are published by the IB, Cambridge International and Pearson, and a tutor should cite and link the official source rather than resell it as a resource pack. Reproducing board material is a copyright problem, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure as well. What is worth paying for is a tutor's own written practice: question sets built around your child's specific errors, model responses they have written, and marking against the published criteria. If a materials line on a quote cannot be described as original work, ask what exactly you are buying.

faqs.question: Does anyone charge to arrange Ministry of Education equivalency, and should we pay it?
faqs.answer: Nobody should, and no tutoring company performs the process. Equivalency sits with the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority, and a family applies through the official channel. For the British track the published requirements are five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited A-Level at grade E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which is wrong. For the IB, no points figure has been confirmed on the Ministry's own site, so verify yours there or with your coordinator.

faqs.question: We were quoted a fee per 45-minute period rather than per hour. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is common and not in itself a problem, but it makes comparison harder, which is sometimes the point. Convert everything to an hourly figure before comparing quotes: AED 180 for 45 minutes is AED 240 an hour, which lands in a different tier than the headline suggests. Shorter periods genuinely suit younger students and single-topic work. For Diploma teaching, 45 minutes is tight once a past-paper question and its feedback are both in the session. Ask what a 60 and a 90-minute session cost, then compare per hour.

faqs.question: Where in the two Diploma years does tutoring money do the most work?
faqs.answer: Four windows. The transition into the Diploma, where six to ten hours spent on named gaps from IGCSE or the Middle Years Programme compounds through everything afterwards. Internal assessment season, where the mark comes from criterion-referenced judgement and feedback is exactly what a tutor is for. The mock period, where the useful spend is forensic analysis of the scripts your child has just written rather than more teaching. The final run, where timing and command-term precision are the only things still movable. Money committed to a weekly slot in a quiet term is the money families most often wish they had held back.

faqs.question: If November retakes exist, is it cheaper to wait than to pay for support now?
faqs.answer: Almost never. A second attempt means a fresh entry through the school or a registered centre, a further term of preparation, and the possibility of a deferred university place — and the preparation is harder the second time because motivation has taken a hit. Measured against that, eight to ten hours bought at the right moment in the first attempt is the cheaper line by a wide margin. A retake is a legitimate option after a result that genuinely misrepresents a student, not a budgeting strategy. Discuss the session choice with the coordinator, who holds the dates that apply to your child.

faqs.question: What is a fair fee for a one-off mock-paper review rather than weekly lessons?
faqs.answer: Expect to pay the tutor's normal hourly rate, and expect it to need between 90 minutes and two hours for a full paper. The work is reading the script, identifying whether each lost mark is content, technique or timing, and teaching the two or three patterns that account for most of them. That is the highest-value single purchase in this market, because it converts a grade you already have into a specific list of fixes. Ask for the output in writing. A review that produces only a conversation is worth less than the same hour spent teaching.

faqs.question: What should a written fee agreement say before the first paid lesson?
faqs.answer: Five things, in a message you can scroll back to. The rate and the session length in minutes, not 'an hour'. The cancellation notice in hours, and whether it applies to the tutor as well as to you. Whether marking, draft reading and progress notes are inside the rate or billed. Whether value added tax is included, and the tax registration number if it is charged. What happens to any prepaid balance if you change tutor or stop. Nearly every fee dispute in this market comes from one of those five being assumed rather than written down.

faqs.question: Does paying a higher fee actually secure a Higher Level specialist?
faqs.answer: Only if you check. Price correlates with scarcity, not automatically with experience, and the market contains confident generalists charging specialist rates. The verifiable questions are specific: which level have you taught this subject at, how many cohorts, which components have you given criterion-referenced feedback on. Be cautious of examiner claims that cannot be evidenced, and treat examiner status as irrelevant to what you are buying anyway — it implies nothing about access to marking or boundaries. A tutor who can name where the marks are going in the first lesson has already answered the question.

faqs.question: Are we paying a tutor for Arabic teaching the school already has to provide?
faqs.answer: Possibly. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, so a defined quantity is already being delivered. For those subjects the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, so nobody can sell a bespoke curriculum. Paid support should be revision on the school's own material, and priced accordingly.

faqs.question: What happens to the money already paid if we change tutor after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Sessions already taught are taught; nothing should be clawed back on either side. What matters is any prepaid balance, so settle that question before you prepay at all. Ask whether unused hours transfer to a replacement tutor, to a second subject or to a sibling, and whether they expire. A provider whose answer is that the balance is tied to one named tutor has given you a reason to pay session by session instead. Changing tutor after three or four sessions is normal and not a failure; judging the match that early is cheaper than persisting with it.

faqs.question: Why will you not quote a single fee for the whole Diploma up front?
faqs.answer: Because the honest number depends on facts we do not have yet: how many subjects need support, which levels, whether the gaps are content or technique, and how the first mock goes. A single two-year figure quoted before a trial lesson is a sales device, and it is almost always higher than what a family actually needs, because it assumes even weekly spending across twenty-four months. What we can do is name the market bands, show which windows the money belongs in, and price a specific plan after a tutor has seen a piece of your child's marked work.

ib-home-tutor-fees.closingHeading: Take any quote in this market and place it
ib-home-tutor-fees.closingBody: You now have the three things a fee conversation needs: the AED bands this market advertises, with sources; the drivers that move a quote up or down; and the lines that belong on an invoice against the ones to refuse. Use them on us as readily as on anyone else. Start with the free trial lesson — one per student, no payment details needed to book it — and ask the tutor at the end where the marks are going and what the first six sessions would cover. If the answer is specific, the rate is probably fair. If it is not, no discount makes the hour worth buying.

intro.heading: What your postcode decides, and what it does not
paragraphs: A search for an IB home tutor near me in the UAE is a search about distance. It is worth being precise about what distance actually buys. The IB Diploma is a single international syllabus: the same guide, the same command terms, the same criteria whether your child sits Paper 1 in Al Quoz or in Frankfurt. Nothing in that syllabus changes because a tutor lives two streets away. What does change with your address is the regulatory frame around the school, and almost nobody writing about tutoring in this country explains it.

Five separate bodies license private schools in the UAE. KHDA covers Dubai. ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge covers Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The powers are not identical. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so a family moving between emirates is moving between different approval regimes rather than between different inspection letterheads.

Then there is supply. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, and the International Baccalaureate accounted for 7% of that enrolment, against 37% UK curriculum, 26% Indian and 14% American. A Diploma family is therefore shopping inside the smallest of the four main curriculum groups. When the requirement narrows to Chemistry at Higher Level, or to Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the number of people within driving distance who have actually taught that course at that level thins very quickly. Outside Dubai it thins faster.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own past paper on screen. Home visiting is a service we run in India, and saying so plainly is more useful than leaving it ambiguous. The practical consequence for a family in Mirdif or Khalifa City is that the search radius stops mattering: the specialist is chosen for the syllabus, and the forty minutes that would have gone on a drive go into the lesson instead.

This page is organised around the things your location really does govern. Which authority to check before you book. Whether the person you found locally is permitted to tutor at all. Which exam timetable zone your child's centre belongs to. What the Ministry of Education asks for when an IB or IGCSE certificate has to be made equivalent for a UAE university. And what the market charges to put somebody in the room, so that the comparison with one-to-one online gets made on numbers rather than on feelings.

ib-home-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the four IB programmes a UAE family may meet, though the Diploma is where most requests land. Each note below adds the thing the UAE regulatory frame puts on top of the IB's own requirements, because the mandatory Ministry subjects and the equivalency file apply whichever programme your child is on.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme runs from ages 3 to 12 and is organised around six transdisciplinary themes rather than separate subjects. There are no external examinations. Assessment is continuous and the programme closes with the PYP exhibition, a student-led inquiry presented to the school community. Support at this stage is usually about reading fluency, number sense and the writing stamina the Middle Years Programme will assume, not about examination technique.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai private schools the mandatory Ministry subjects start here: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit on the timetable next to the PYP units, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Families searching for a tutor near them at primary age are most often looking for Arabic, and that is a different hunt from a Diploma subject.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme covers ages 11 to 16 across eight subject groups and assesses each against four published criteria, marked out of 8 and reported on a 1-7 scale. It ends with the personal project. Year 11 is where the gap to the Diploma opens: MYP criteria reward process and reflection, while Diploma papers reward precise, time-limited answers under specific command terms. Most of the work at this stage is closing that gap.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE schools run the MYP to Year 11 and then move students into the Diploma, while others switch to IGCSE for two years. Which route a school takes is settled with the emirate authority as part of its licensed curriculum, so read the school's own curriculum page and the subject detail in its inspection report before assuming the transition into Diploma Higher Level subjects is automatic.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma Programme covers ages 16 to 19: three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level carries more content and usually an additional paper. Internally assessed components are marked by the school teacher and moderated by the IB; external papers are marked by IB examiners. The Diploma total is 45 points, with up to 3 from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. The Diploma is also where the Ministry of Education equivalency question becomes urgent, because a UAE university application usually needs the certificate attested and made equivalent, and the published British-track rules do not cover the IB at all. Verify any IB points threshold on moe.gov.ae or with the school's IB coordinator before relying on a number found on a tutoring website.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is the smallest of the four programmes in this region and only a handful of UAE schools offer it. Students on it usually need help with the Diploma courses they carry, because those are assessed exactly as a Diploma candidate's are, by the same papers against the same criteria.
programmes.countryNote: Because the Career-related Programme is rare here, a tutor who has taught it is rarer still, which is the clearest small illustration of this page's argument. Searching by distance for a Career-related Programme specialist in Ajman or Fujairah is likely to return nothing at all. Searching by programme and teaching over live video returns somebody who has read the reflective project criteria.

ib-home-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses UAE families ask for most, with the levels taught and the point in the course where marks usually go. Request the level your child is actually entered at: the Higher Level syllabus is not the Standard Level one with extra homework, and a tutor who has only taught Standard Level will miss the additional content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation carry the papers. Higher Level adds a third paper of extended problem-solving and a far deeper calculus treatment. Marks go on unjustified steps, on calculator use where an analytic method was expected, and on the exploration, where personal engagement and reflection are the criteria students treat as decoration.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-rich questions. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical inference. The common failure is treating it as the easier route: the data-handling questions are long, the command terms are precise, and the exploration still has to show a genuine mathematical process rather than a survey with a bar chart attached.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The current guide is organised around structure and reactivity. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are where Higher Level separates from Standard Level. Data-based questions lose marks on uncertainties and significant figures, and the scientific investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation rather than on how impressive the apparatus looked.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward algebraic fluency; the Higher Level extensions reward careful use of the data booklet. Students lose marks writing qualitative answers to quantitative command terms, and on graph work: axes, uncertainties, gradients, and the units that belong to a gradient rather than to the quantities plotted.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, with marks sitting in precise terminology and in applying a concept to an unfamiliar organism. Higher Level adds depth in nucleic acids, metabolism and plant biology. Extended responses need a structure before the first sentence, and the scientific investigation needs a question narrow enough for the variables to be controlled.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams first: a correctly labelled, correctly shifted diagram carries most of the analysis marks. Higher Level adds the quantitative paper, where candidates lose marks on calculation conventions rather than on economics. The internally assessed portfolio is three commentaries on published news articles, each under a strict word limit that is enforced.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, techniques and theories applied to a real organisation, with a pre-released case study for Paper 1 and extension topics at Higher Level. The research project is where marks are lost: a question that cannot be answered with the data a student can actually obtain produces a weak evaluation however neatly it is written.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two papers, the individual oral, and at Higher Level the HL essay. Paper 1 is guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, which rewards practice on real advertisements, columns and infographics. The individual oral usually fails on the global issue: too broad, and the chosen extract cannot carry it.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Two distinct courses with different purposes, often confused at registration. Arabic A is for first-language speakers; Arabic B is acquisition. In Dubai private schools Arabic also runs as a mandatory Ministry subject with its own language-of-instruction rules, so a family may be supporting a Diploma course and a mandatory stream in parallel.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Assessed on an exhibition of three objects and a prescribed-title essay for Theory of Knowledge, and a 4,000-word research essay for the Extended Essay, together contributing up to 3 points on the Diploma matrix. Both are supervised by the school. A tutor's role is questioning, reading lists and criterion-referenced feedback on the student's own drafts.

ib-home-tutor-near-me.regionsTitle: Searching from these places: what changes, and what does not
ib-home-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: The emirate you search from changes the authority, the inspection framework and the attestation route. It does not change the syllabus, and with lessons over live video it does not change which tutor you can reach. Each note names the body that licenses your child's school and the practical scheduling point for families there.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes the inspection reports. Dubai holds the largest private sector in the country: 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, 7% of them on IB programmes. Evening slots from 17:00 Gulf Standard Time fill first here, so fix the weekly time early.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and runs its own inspection cycle. ADEK's professional-ethics rules also bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is worth knowing before accepting an offer that originates in the staff room.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, and a smaller IB field than Abu Dhabi island. Families here are the clearest case for choosing by syllabus: a Higher Level Physics specialist within a short drive of Asharej or Al Jimi is a thin market, while the same specialist over live video is not a market constraint at all.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone, and it is why a Sharjah school's course offer can differ from a Dubai school's on the same curriculum.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate authority. Many Ajman families commute into Sharjah or Dubai for school, which pushes the realistic start of a weekday session past 18:00 Gulf Standard Time once the return journey is counted.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education. The IB field here is very small, and the pages competing for these searches mention Umm Al Quwain not once. Online delivery is the only realistic route to a named Higher Level specialist for a family living in the emirate.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah Academy runs IB programmes; beyond a short list of schools the choice narrows quickly, and the local tutoring market narrows with it.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The east coast is the least-served part of the country for IB subject specialists, and the drive to Dubai makes a weekly in-person arrangement unrealistic for a school-night session. Lessons over live video remove the journey from the arrangement entirely.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai and the KHDA inspection file
schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend Dubai IB World Schools like these. Before booking anything, read the school's most recent KHDA inspection report: it separates attainment from progress by subject, and a subject where progress lags attainment is a different tutoring problem from one where both are low.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK
schoolClusters.note: ADEK publishes its own school profiles and inspection outcomes. Families in Khalifa City, Al Reef and Saadiyat most often ask about the Diploma sciences and about Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, which is also where the shortage of nearby specialists bites hardest.

A shorter list, and that is the point. Where an emirate has a handful of IB World Schools it also has a handful of teachers who have taught the Diploma, and the number who have taught one specific Higher Level course is smaller again. Matching over live video is what makes the length of that list irrelevant.

sections.heading: What a search for a tutor near you actually returns
paragraphs: A search for an IB home tutor near me in the UAE ranks results by distance, by advertising spend and by how well a local listing is maintained. None of those three things records whether the person has taught the Diploma course your child is entered for, at the level being sat, under the current subject guide.

That matters because the Diploma is not a local qualification. The subject guide, the command terms, the criteria and the papers are identical in Fujairah and in Frankfurt. The one genuinely local variable in teaching terms is the school's own scheme of work and its internal deadlines, and those are published to parents, not to the nearest tutor. So the distance between your front door and a tutor's front door buys travel time and very little else.

There are, though, several distances in a UAE family's situation that do matter, and none of them is the one a search engine measures. The table below sets them out. Two are genuinely physical: the examination centre and the attestation desk. Three are administrative: which authority licensed the school, which timetable version the centre works from, and which syllabus the class teacher is working through. Only the first row, the tutor, turns out to be the one where proximity adds nothing at all.

Read the table as a checklist before you contact anybody. Every row except the first can be settled from a published document in under an hour, and settling them changes the question you ask a tutor. It stops being whether they are nearby and becomes whether they have taught Chemistry at Higher Level under the current guide, and whether they have marked a scientific investigation against its criteria.

sections.heading: Which authority licensed your child's school, and what else it controls
paragraphs: Five bodies license private schools in the UAE and the first useful thing a parent can do is name theirs. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain.

The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge does the same in Ras Al Khaimah. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five cover the whole country. ADEK is named by none of the pages competing for these searches, and SPEA Sharjah appears in one of them, once.

The powers differ in a way that affects a tutoring plan. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is curriculum and fee approval rather than inspection alone. Dubai's fee position is set separately: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Dubai is also adding seven private schools for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places after a 6% rise in enrolment the year before.

What to take from this is to read your own authority's pages rather than a generic article. Note too that none of these bodies accredits individual private tutors. A tuition centre with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An individual tutor does not hold one, so any page describing its tutors as approved by one of these authorities is describing something that does not exist for individuals.

sections.heading: Why proximity runs out of IB specialists before it runs out of tutors
paragraphs: Scarcity, not quality, is the real problem with a distance-first search. The IB is a minority curriculum even in the country's largest private market: 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, against 37% UK curriculum, 26% Indian and 14% American. Every narrowing of the requirement cuts the local pool again.

Work it through. Start with teachers who have taught the Diploma. Keep only those who have taught the subject. Keep only those who have taught it at Higher Level under the current guide. Keep only those who have marked the internally assessed component against its criteria. Keep only those free at 18:00 on a school night. Then draw a twenty-minute radius around your villa. That last filter removes more people than any of the others and adds the least to the lesson.

Outside Dubai the arithmetic is harsher. Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain between them hold a small number of IB World Schools, and the pages competing for these searches mention three of those emirates not once. A family in Fujairah looking for a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist is not choosing between tutors. They are choosing between a generalist nearby and a specialist over live video.

We would rather state that plainly than imply a coverage we do not have. Where no specialist is free for a subject and level, we say so and give an expected wait, rather than putting a general maths tutor in front of a Higher Level candidate six weeks before the papers. That disclosure is the whole value of matching by syllabus: it only works if the answer is sometimes no.

sections.heading: Is the person you found nearby permitted to tutor?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful, and it is licensed. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and it is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. The official service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Eligibility is broad. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 may all apply. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so an amount quoted to you as the penalty is somebody's guess rather than a figure from the ministry.

Two conditions matter when the tutor is somebody local. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the holder's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the same school. So the offer from your child's own subject teacher, however convenient it sounds, is the one to decline. Treat the ADEK detail as press-reported and check the current policy document if it matters to your decision.

Asking to see a permit is a normal question rather than a rude one. Ask for the permit, the category it was issued under and the expiry date, and check the name matches the person who will actually teach. A tutoring business with premises and staff is a separate matter: in Dubai that needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps once initial approval is given.
