sections.heading: What the UAE market charges to put a tutor in the room
paragraphs: Rates first, because almost nobody in this market publishes them. The figures below are market rates in dirhams per hour, taken from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. They are not IB Gram's price list. They are reproduced so that the travel premium is visible rather than buried.

The pattern across the sources is consistent: a visiting tutor costs more per hour than the same tutor working over video, and the gap is roughly the journey. Bestimate puts one-to-one in-home tuition at AED 180-350, while independent home tutors advertise up to AED 500. Online bands run lower, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52 at the budget end, and Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB. TutorChase publishes AED 270 for specialist support and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end.

Monthly packages seen in the market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Set that against KHDA's position that Dubai private school fees are not rising for 2026-27: school fees are the fixed line in the education budget and tutoring is the one still moving.

IB Gram does not publish an hourly figure on this page, because the number depends on subject, level and how many sessions a week. The trial lesson is forty-five minutes, costs nothing, needs no card details and is one per student; the rate is agreed after it rather than before. Ask any provider three questions before you commit: is the quote per hour or per lesson, does it include VAT, and what is charged for travel.

sections.heading: A tutor in the room against one-to-one over live video
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search deserves, so here it is on the facts. A visiting tutor gives you presence in the room, a parent who can see the lesson happening, and a student who cannot quietly close a laptop. Those are real advantages and worth naming before the case against them.

Against them: the hourly rate carries the journey, the catchment decides the tutor pool, a 17:00 start becomes 18:30 after Sheikh Zayed Road at the wrong hour, a cancelled session wastes somebody's drive, and sessions arrive in two-hour blocks because a single hour does not pay for the travel. A two-hour block suits the economics of the trip more than it suits the concentration of a sixteen-year-old at the end of a school day.

One-to-one over live video removes the journey from both sides. The practical gains are specific. A shorter session becomes viable, so an hour of timed questions on Tuesday and forty minutes on the exploration on Thursday is affordable. The student's own script is on screen and annotated live. Written notes exist afterwards. And the tutor is drawn from everyone who has taught the course rather than everyone who lives within a drive. IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition this way, one-to-one, over live video; home visiting is a service we run in India only.

The honest limits are worth stating too. A student who will not engage with a screen needs a different plan. Very young learners need an adult in the room for the first few weeks. Practical laboratory work cannot be replicated over video; what can be taught is the data analysis, the uncertainty treatment and the alternative-to-practical technique, which is where the marks for practical work actually sit.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: the subjects your address does not excuse
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position is the same in substance: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The rules are more specific than most families expect. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students, while non-Arabs study Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary the length of a lesson provided the total weekly time is met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. One rule constrains a tutor directly: for these subjects the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the MoE, is strictly prohibited. A tutor supporting Arabic or Islamic Education should therefore work from the school's own prescribed material rather than from a private worksheet pack.

This is also the one area where a parent should ask about a credential rather than about syllabus history. Schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects. For the Diploma, remember that Arabic A and Arabic B are separate courses with separate aims, and a child may be carrying a Diploma Arabic course and a mandatory Arabic stream at the same time, assessed in two completely different ways.

sections.heading: The examination centre is the genuinely local thing
paragraphs: If one part of a proximity search deserves the word near, it is the examination centre. Your child sits the papers in a room, on a date the board sets, under a timetable version that depends on where that room is. Everything else in this process can happen over a connection.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That single sentence is the reason to ask your school's examinations officer one question in writing: which zone is this centre in?

The March series shows how far ahead the administrative dates sit. For March 2027 Cambridge publishes an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Entries therefore close roughly ten weeks before the first paper. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations run in May and June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official document rather than a date copied onto a tutoring website.

For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session, and that is as specific as this page will be. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB examination or results date here has been confirmed from the IB itself. Confirm every IB date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before planning around it. Any page quoting precise IB dates without naming where it read them is asking you to take a date on trust.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: the appointment that really does need you in the country
paragraphs: A UAE university application usually turns on a Ministry of Education equivalency certificate, and this is the part of the process where being in the country matters. It is also the part the pages competing for these searches leave almost entirely blank, which is a strange gap given how often it decides an application.

The British-track requirements are published. A student must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That five-subject rule is worth repeating, because at least one page ranking for UAE tutoring queries tells parents the figure is six.

The American track is specified differently: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no figure on this page, deliberately. The source that sets out the British and American tracks states no IB points threshold, so any IB number here would be invented. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of equivalency or attestation, and no tutoring service should claim to. What a tutor can do is check that the subject grades the file will need are the ones the student is actually on course for, which is a planning conversation best had in the first term of the final year rather than in August with results in hand. Nothing about tutoring is required for equivalency; it is a document process, not an academic one.

sections.heading: What a tutor may not do with internally assessed work
paragraphs: One page ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright. It is worth naming what that is: an academic-integrity breach, a malpractice trigger, and a risk that falls almost entirely on the sixteen-year-old whose name sits on the submission rather than on the person who took the money.

The internally assessed components, meaning the subject explorations and investigations, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition and the Personal Project, are assessed on the student's own work, and the school's supervisor signs to that effect. A tutor's legitimate role is large and specific: teaching the underlying content, explaining what each criterion rewards, asking the questions an examiner would ask of a research question, checking that a method can actually generate usable data, reviewing referencing conventions, and giving feedback on a draft the student has already produced.

The line is authorship. Sentences supplied by somebody else, a bibliography assembled by somebody else, data fabricated or borrowed, a research question handed over ready-made, a draft returned so heavily reworked that the voice has changed: all of that crosses it. So does any arrangement sold as a finished piece of coursework. A tutor who offers that has told you what else they will be casual about.

Ask a prospective tutor directly how they handle coursework and listen for a boundary in the answer. Ours is stated before anything is booked: we teach, we question, and we give criterion-referenced feedback on what the student has already produced, while the school supervisor stays in charge of the process and the internal deadlines. There is a practical reason to keep that line clean as well as an ethical one. An examiner reads thousands of scripts, and a voice that does not match the rest of a candidate's work is conspicuous.

process.title: Name the emirate and the authority
process.description: Tell us which emirate the school sits in and we will name the body that licenses it, whether that is KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the RAK Department of Knowledge or the Ministry of Education, and point you at its own published pages. It takes a minute and it changes which documents are worth reading before you book anything.

process.title: Give us the subject, the level and the guide
process.description: Subject, level, exam board and the version of the subject guide. For the Diploma that means Higher or Standard Level and whether the current guide applies. For IGCSE it means Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel and the syllabus code. These are the facts the match is actually made on, rather than the distance between two addresses.

process.title: Send one real piece of marked work
process.description: A marked paper, a draft of the exploration or the last school report tells a specialist more than a description of the problem ever does. It is also how the first lesson avoids being spent on diagnosis: the tutor arrives already knowing which topics and which command terms are costing your child marks.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: Forty-five minutes, one per student, no card details and nothing owed afterwards. It is a real lesson on real work rather than a sales call. Judge it on whether the tutor found something about your child's work that you did not already know, and on whether the student wants the next one.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: One recurring time, agreed around the school run, prayer times and the family's own evening. Sessions can move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. Written notes follow each lesson, and the plan is reviewed against the school's own assessment calendar every six to eight weeks rather than left to drift.

whyPoints.title: The authority is named, not implied
whyPoints.description: Every page we publish names the body that licenses schools in that emirate and links its own material. IB Gram holds no approval, permit or relationship from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and says so on the page. Any tutoring site implying otherwise is describing a credential that does not exist for individual tutors.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus, not by radius
whyPoints.description: The match is made on subject, level, exam board and guide, which is the only set of facts that predicts whether somebody can teach the course. Where the specialist lives stops mattering once the lesson runs over live video, and the pool producing the match is the whole of it rather than a twenty-minute drive.

The rate for your child depends on subject, level and frequency, and it is agreed after the trial lesson rather than before it.

whyPoints.title: A written boundary on coursework
whyPoints.description: The internally assessed components stay the student's own work and the school supervisor stays in charge of them. We teach the content, explain what each criterion rewards, and give feedback on drafts the student has produced. That boundary is stated before anything is booked, because the risk of the alternative falls on the candidate.

Delivery over live video is what makes a Higher Level match possible from an address three hours from Dubai.

Name the subject, the level, the exam board and the guide. Check the real deadlines: the board's entry date, the school's internal coursework dates, the equivalency file. Then choose a tutor against those facts rather than against a map. faqs.question: Will a search for an IB home tutor near me find someone who has taught my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: Usually not directly. A proximity search ranks by distance, by advertising and by how well a listing is maintained, and none of those records whether the tutor has taught the Diploma course your child is entered for, at the level being sat, under the current guide. Ask three questions instead of one: which subject and level have you taught, which version of the guide were you teaching from, and have you marked the internally assessed component against its criteria? Those answers predict a useful lesson. A postcode does not. With lessons running over live video, distance stops being a filter at all.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor we found locally is permitted to teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit, the category it was issued under and its expiry date, then check the name matches the person who will teach. The permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any amount quoted to you as unverified. A tutoring business with premises is different again: in Dubai that needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit.

faqs.question: Can my child's own class teacher tutor them privately in the evening?
faqs.answer: This is the arrangement to avoid. The MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring the holder from serving students affiliated with their own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the same school. The reason is plain once stated: the person teaching the class, setting the coursework deadlines and marking the internally assessed work should not also be paid privately by the family. Treat the ADEK detail as press-reported and check the current policy if it matters. A separate specialist, with no stake in the school's marking, is cleaner.

faqs.question: What does a home visit actually add to the hourly rate here?
faqs.answer: Roughly the journey. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts one-to-one in-home tuition in Dubai at AED 180-350 an hour and independent home tutors advertise up to AED 500, while online bands in the same research run from AED 33-65 at the budget end and AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor. The visit also tends to arrive as a two-hour block, because a single hour does not pay for the drive, so the commitment per session is larger as well as the rate. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, and not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Does living outside Dubai make it harder to find an IB specialist?
faqs.answer: By distance, yes, and sharply. The IB accounted for 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, and Dubai is the largest private market in the country with 227 schools. Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain hold far fewer IB World Schools between them, so the number of people nearby who have taught one specific Diploma course at Higher Level can genuinely be zero. That is the practical case for live video rather than a drive: the match is made from everyone who has taught the course, not from everyone inside a catchment area.

faqs.question: Which exam timetable applies to my child's centre, and why does the zone matter?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. So the only safe answer is the one your school's examinations officer gives in writing. Ask which zone the centre sits in, then work from that timetable and nothing else. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, which is a second reason to work from the live official document rather than a date on a tutoring site.

faqs.question: Is it five accredited IGCSE subjects for equivalency, or six?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement is to pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking for UAE tutoring queries tells parents the figure is six, which would change a child’s option choices for no reason at all. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority before planning a subject line-up around it.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education counted among those five subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The published guidance states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. They still sit on the timetable: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. So a student can be working hard at a subject that does not count towards the equivalency total while needing five others that do. Check that against the school's option blocks early, rather than in the final term when the combination is already fixed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor use their own worksheets for Arabic, Islamic Education or Social Studies?
faqs.answer: Not freely. KHDA's guidance on the mandatory subjects states that the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the MoE, is strictly prohibited. A tutor supporting these subjects should work from the school's own prescribed material rather than a private worksheet pack. The same guidance notes that schools must ensure all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach them, so this is the one area where asking about a credential matters more than asking about syllabus history. For Diploma Arabic A or Arabic B, the IB subject guide applies instead.

faqs.question: Why do schools run separate Arabic classes for Arab and non-Arab students?
faqs.answer: Because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction are different. KHDA's requirements state that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arabs study Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Knowing which stream your child sits in tells a tutor which content and which language to work in.

faqs.question: Is private tutoring lawful in the UAE if the lesson happens over video?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring is lawful and it is licensed. The route is the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Nothing in the published material makes the permit optional, so a provider telling you the sector is unregulated is either mistaken or hoping you will not check. Ask for the permit either way.

faqs.question: What should I send when I ask for a tutoring quote?
faqs.answer: Five things, and the quote stops being a guess. The emirate and the school, so the authority and the inspection report can be identified. The subject, the level and the exam board, with the syllabus code if you have it. The nearest real deadline, whether that is a mock, an internal coursework date or the examination session itself. One piece of recently marked work. And the two or three times in the week that genuinely work for the family. Anyone quoting without those is pricing a stranger, and the first lesson goes on diagnosis you have already paid for.

faqs.question: Should the equivalency certificate be sorted before or after results come out?
faqs.answer: Start the file before results and finish it after. The documents a family can gather early, meaning passport and residency copies, school letters, attested transcripts and the record of which accredited subjects the student is entered for, take longer than the certificate itself. Checking in the first term of the final year that the entered subjects will satisfy the published requirement is the part that actually prevents a problem. IB Gram does not submit, perform or guarantee any part of equivalency or attestation; that is the Ministry's process, and the authority's own channel is the only place to confirm it.

faqs.question: Can lessons be booked around prayer times and the school run?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth being specific when you ask. Give the two or three windows that genuinely work on a weekday, allowing for the school run, prayer times and the point at which a teenager can still concentrate. Slots run on Gulf Standard Time and start on the minute, because nobody is driving to get there, and they can move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. A shorter session is also viable without travel in the fee, so an hour of timed questions midweek plus forty minutes on coursework later in the week is a realistic pattern.

faqs.question: Dubai froze school fees for 2026-27. Does that change what tutoring costs?
faqs.answer: Not directly, but it changes the budget conversation. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. School fees are therefore the fixed line and tutoring is the variable one. Market rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33-65 an hour at the budget online end to AED 200-450 and above for specialist support, with visiting tutors at AED 180-500. Those are other providers' published figures; our rate is agreed after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: What happens if we stop after the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Nothing is owed. The trial lesson is forty-five minutes, one per student, needs no card details, and ends with written notes on what the tutor found, whether or not you carry on. If you do carry on, the weekly slot is agreed afterwards and the plan is reviewed against the school's own assessment calendar every six to eight weeks. If the match is wrong, whether on personality, pace, or a tutor who turns out to lack the Higher Level depth the course needs, say so and we change the tutor rather than asking the student to adapt.

faqs.question: Does my child have to sit the exams at a centre near us?
faqs.answer: Examinations are sat in person at a centre, and for most students that is their own school. A private candidate has to be entered through a centre that accepts external candidates, and the entry deadline sits a long way ahead of the papers: Cambridge's final entries for the March 2027 series were due on 27 November 2026, roughly ten weeks before an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Tuition can be delivered over live video from anywhere, but the entry and the room cannot. Confirm both with the examinations officer rather than assuming the school has it covered.

intro.heading: What a home tutor costs in the UAE, and what the fee is actually paying for
paragraphs: A UAE family that types IB home tutors into Google is usually three weeks past the point where they hoped the school would sort it out. A Diploma report has come home with a 4 in Chemistry HL, or a Mathematics exploration deadline has appeared with nothing written under it, and the obvious answer is to pay someone to sit beside the student. The market has an answer ready and a price attached: roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour for an in-home visit once the driving is absorbed into the fee. Almost nobody ranking for this search will print that number.

This page prints it, says where it came from, and takes it apart. The AED bands below were collected in October 2026 from UAE providers that publish their own rates and from the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. They are market figures, not ours. The IB Gram arrangement starts with one free trial lesson per subject, before any payment is taken, and the rate is agreed with you after that lesson rather than guessed from a web page. The reason to show you the market at all is so that whatever you are quoted, by us or by anybody else, can be checked against something real.

The second job of this page is to separate the fee from the teaching. An in-home hour is not an hour. A tutor who drives thirty minutes each way is committing two hours of their evening to deliver one hour of teaching, and that arithmetic is why the UAE in-home market sells two-hour minimum blocks, charges for late cancellations, and quietly narrows your choice of teacher down to whoever happens to live nearby. Live online lessons are not cheaper because they are a lesser product. They are cheaper because there is no car in them.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one tuition over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with written notes after each lesson that a parent can read. Nobody is sent to a UAE address: home visits are a service we run only in India, and saying that plainly matters more to us than winning a booking. What a UAE family gets instead is the thing a twenty-minute radius cannot supply, which is a Higher Level specialist who teaches the current subject guide and knows where Paper 2 eats marks, rather than the strongest graduate available within driving distance.

The rest of the page is arithmetic and calendars. What a month of lessons costs per teaching hour once you divide it out. What a quote has to contain before anyone can price it honestly. Which assessment components still have marks left in them in February and which have already closed. Who is legally permitted to give private lessons in the UAE, and what that permit costs, which is nothing at all. And the one boundary no fee moves: a tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on work the student wrote, and never produces that work.
bullets: In-home market rates run AED 180-500 an hour; qualified online subject rates run AED 150-300 (collected October 2026).
A published AED 799 monthly online package divides out near AED 100 per teaching hour; a AED 1,599-1,799 in-home package lands near AED 200-225.
The MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a licence fee inside a quote is a markup.

ib-home-tutors.programmesIntro: The IB runs as four separate programmes, and the price of help differs across them because the assessment load does. A Primary Years parent is buying confidence and reading fluency. A Diploma parent in the second year is buying marks against a fixed deadline, which is the most expensive hour in the UAE market.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Six transdisciplinary themes, inquiry units and an exhibition at the end of Year 6. There are no external papers, so nothing a tutor does here can be measured against a grade boundary. Value at this stage is diagnostic: finding out whether a child who looks slow in a unit of inquiry is actually struggling with reading comprehension, number bonds or the language of the task. Short, frequent sessions beat long ones.
programmes.countryNote: PYP rates sit at the bottom of the UAE band, roughly where the Bestimate budget tier lands, because the work does not need a subject specialist. The cost mistake families make here is the opposite of overspending: paying for two years of general homework help when eight focused sessions on place value would have closed the gap. Dubai alone has a large PYP cohort inside its 227 private schools, so supply is good and prices stay competitive.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, criterion-referenced marking from A to D in most subjects, and a Personal Project in the final year. Marks come from the school, not from an external board, which changes what tutoring is for: the student has to understand how their own teacher applies a criterion strand, because that is who awards the level. A tutor reads the task sheet and the rubric before touching the content.
programmes.countryNote: This is where UAE families most often buy the wrong thing. MYP has no public mark scheme to practise against, so hours spent on generic past papers convert into nothing. The useful spend is small and targeted: one or two sessions per assessment cycle, aimed at the specific criterion the report flagged. Families moving from MYP into the Diploma also underestimate the mathematics step, which is the single most common reason a UAE DP1 student needs paid help by October.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The Diploma is marked out of 45, with up to three points coming from the TOK and Extended Essay combination, and 24 points is the floor for the award. Internal Assessment carries 20% of most subject grades, which means a fifth of the result is finished long before the papers are sat.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is the expensive programme in every UAE price list, and the premium is real rather than invented: a Higher Level specialist is a scarcer person than a general maths teacher, and scarcity is what the extra AED 100 an hour buys. The IB accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, and three of the seven new schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 are IB schools, so demand for DP specialists in the UAE is growing faster than the local supply of them.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more DP courses taken alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course and a language development strand. The DP courses inside a CP are assessed exactly as they are in the full Diploma, so a CP student sitting Business Management SL needs the same paper technique as anyone else sitting it.
programmes.countryNote: CP cohorts in the UAE are small, which has a direct price effect: a tutor near you who has taught the reflective project is unlikely to exist, and a search by distance will return someone who has never seen one. This is the clearest case on this page for a national online pool rather than a local one. For the DP components inside the CP, ordinary subject rates apply; for the reflective project, expect to pay for process coaching rather than content teaching.

ib-home-tutors.subjectsIntro: Price follows scarcity, not difficulty. The subjects below are the ones UAE families pay for most often, with a note on where the marks are actually lost in each. Where a subject is hard to staff locally, the in-home market charges more for it and still offers you fewer people to choose from.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and the HL-only Paper 3, which is a 20% investigation-style paper most students meet for the first time in a mock. Marks leak out of method lines rather than answers: unjustified steps, a missing conclusion sentence, an unsupported sketch. HL AA is the most requested and most expensive single subject in the UAE market.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-heavy questions where the graphic display calculator is part of the method. Students lose marks by writing the answer the calculator gave without the command that produced it. AI SL is the quiet default at many UAE schools, and the exploration is where most of the recoverable marks sit.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Under the current guide, Paper 1 carries 36% and Paper 2 44%, with the scientific investigation taking the remaining 20%. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are where HL grades are made. Most lost marks are not chemistry errors: they are unstated assumptions, missing units and uncertainty treated as an afterthought.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The hardest subject to staff anywhere in the UAE at Higher Level. Fields, circuits and the HL extension topics reward students who can explain a mechanism in words before touching an equation. Examiners pay for reasoning, so a correct number with no stated principle behind it collects part marks at best.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A volume problem rather than a reasoning problem. Students who revise by rereading remember the content and still lose marks on command terms: outline, explain and evaluate each buy different things. Data-based questions on an unfamiliar experiment are the most trainable part of the paper and the part most students never practise.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides grades. Axes unlabelled, a shift drawn without a reason, no reference to the article in a commentary. HL adds the policy paper, which asks for calculation and evaluation in the same answer. The portfolio of commentaries is written across the course, so a family that asks for help in April has already lost most of it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen Paper 1 analysis, the comparative Paper 2 and the individual oral, with an HL essay on top at Higher Level. Strong readers underperform here because they summarise instead of analysing. Tutoring value is highest on the oral, where a global issue chosen badly limits the grade before the student opens their mouth.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, techniques and theories applied to a real organisation, with a case study released in advance for one paper. Most marks go missing in application: a correct definition of a concept followed by no link to the business in the question. The internal written work needs a researchable business problem, which is a decision best made early.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data structures and an internally assessed solution built for a real client. Paper questions on abstract data structures reward tracing by hand, which students resist. The solution is the component where UAE students most often need process help: scoping too large a product in October and running out of time in February.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic runs on two tracks in UAE schools, and families regularly buy the wrong one. Arabic A is a literature course for first-language speakers; Arabic B is an acquisition course. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, so the stream a child sits in is a school decision, not a preference.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together these carry up to three points on the 45-point scale, and both are supervised inside the school. The TOK essay answers a prescribed title; the exhibition answers a prompt with three objects. Support here is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafting, never writing, because authenticity is signed off by the supervisor.

ib-home-tutors.regionsTitle: Where the UAE in-home market concentrates, and what that means for you
ib-home-tutors.regionsIntro: In-home tutoring in the UAE clusters in a handful of communities, and the clustering is about drive time rather than wealth. The notes below describe what the local market looks like in each and what the evening logistics do to a booking. Lessons from IB Gram reach every one of them the same way, over live video.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Apartment living, the densest supply of freelance tutors in the country, and the worst parking position of any Dubai community. Tutors price the building, not the lesson: visitor parking and lift waits are why Marina quotes often carry a two-hour minimum.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Villa communities feeding several long-established IB and British schools. Supply here is good at primary level and thin at Higher Level sciences. School-run traffic on Al Wasl and Jumeirah Beach Road pushes realistic session starts past 17:00 on weekdays.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills
regions.note: The classic two-hour-block market. A tutor driving in from Deira or Sharjah will not take a single 60-minute booking, so families end up buying longer sessions than the child can concentrate through. Two shorter online sessions a week usually teach more for less.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Fast-growing, heavily rented, and poorly served by the local in-home market relative to its size. Searches by distance return general tutors rather than Diploma specialists. This is one of the communities where an online pool changes the answer rather than just the price.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha, Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Spread-out villa compounds where the distance between two bookings is itself a cost. Abu Dhabi school staff are barred by ADEK professional-ethics rules from paid tutoring of students at their own school, so the familiar teacher is not an option here.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island and Al Reem Island
regions.note: A small, high-demand pocket with a handful of schools and very few resident specialists in subjects like Physics HL or Computer Science. Rates quoted into these communities sit at the top of the national band, and availability rather than price is usually the binding constraint.

regions.name: Al Nahda and Muwailih, Sharjah
regions.note: Dense, affordable, and regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than KHDA. Many families here commute into Dubai for work, which compresses the usable tutoring window into a narrow slot between 18:00 and 20:30 on Gulf Standard Time.

regions.name: Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah
regions.note: The parts of the country the UAE tutoring market barely writes about. Local in-home supply for IB Diploma subjects is close to absent, and visiting tutors price the drive accordingly. Online delivery removes the distance premium entirely for these families.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, and the IB sits at roughly 7 per cent of that enrolment. Three of the seven new schools opening for 2026-27 are IB schools. Students we support attend schools across this cluster; the point of naming them is that boards and subject guides differ between them.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.note: Inspected by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. The practical difference for a family is staffing: ADEK professional-ethics rules prevent school staff from tutoring their own enrolled students for a fee, so paid help has to come from outside the school entirely.

Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; both approve fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, not just inspections. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education. IB provision thins out quickly north of Sharjah.

ib-home-tutors.modesIntro: Four booking patterns cover almost every request a UAE family makes. They are described here by what they replace in the in-home market, because that is the comparison a parent is actually making when they get to this part of the page.

modes.title: The weekly slot that replaces the house call
modes.description: One 60-minute lesson a week with the same specialist, on a fixed day, over live video. This is the direct substitute for the weekly visit most UAE families start with, minus the drive and minus the two-hour minimum that the drive imposes. Sixty minutes is the right length for most Diploma work; attention, not budget, is the limiting factor.
bullets: Same tutor every week, same slot on Gulf Standard Time
Written notes after each lesson, readable by a parent
No travel, so a 60-minute booking is actually possible
Reviewed every six to eight weeks against the school's reports

modes.title: Shared-screen problem sets
modes.description: The student works a past-paper question while the tutor watches the working appear, stopping at the line where the method goes wrong rather than after the answer. In a living room this needs two people leaning over one page; on a shared screen with an annotation layer it is cleaner, and the marked-up page is still there the next morning.
bullets: Method errors caught at the line, not at the answer
Marked pages saved and revisited before the next paper
Works for Maths, Physics and Chemistry calculation technique
Command-term drilling on real mark schemes the school supplies

modes.title: Short-notice cover before a school deadline
modes.description: A single session or a pair of them, booked inside a few days because an exploration draft, a commentary or an oral is due. The in-home market handles this badly: a visiting tutor has a fixed weekly route and cannot usually add a Tuesday. An online specialist in a different time zone frequently can.
bullets: Booked in days rather than weeks where a specialist is free
Priced as single sessions, with no package commitment
Aimed at one deliverable, with the rubric on screen
Feedback on the student's own draft, never text supplied for them

modes.title: Two children, one household, separate slots
modes.description: Families with a Year 11 and a Diploma student usually try to buy one tutor for both to save money, which works only when the subject and level genuinely overlap. Splitting the week into two shorter one-to-one sessions costs the same as one long visit and gives each child a specialist rather than a compromise.
bullets: Separate specialists where the levels differ, at the same total cost

sections.heading: What families actually mean when they search for IB home tutors
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in the UAE is a private teacher paid by the hour to work with one student, usually in the family's own sitting room, at a market rate of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed into the fee. That is the market, and those figures come from UAE providers publishing their own rates in October 2026 together with the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. IB Gram works the same way with one change that we state before anything else: the teaching happens over live video on Gulf Standard Time rather than in the room, and home visits are a service we run only in India.

The phrase hides a very wide range of people. The UAE regulates private tuition through a MoHRE work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the categories eligible to hold it include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A single search result page will mix a Diploma examiner with an undergraduate, and both of them may be calling themselves an IB home tutor at the same hourly rate.

So the question is never only what the hour costs. It is what fraction of the fee reaches the student as teaching. An in-home fee pays for teaching, driving, a cancellation buffer, an agency margin where one exists, and the risk that the match is wrong. Each of those is a real cost to somebody. Only the first one changes a grade.

The sections below take the fee apart line by line, then put it back together as a monthly figure per teaching hour, which is the only number that lets you compare an online package against a visiting tutor honestly. After that comes the part the price lists never mention: which hours are worth buying, and when in the UAE academic year they stop being worth anything.

sections.heading: The hourly rate is the smallest line in the bill
paragraphs: Every in-home tutoring arrangement in the UAE carries five or six charges behind the headline rate, and none of them is hidden in a sinister sense. They exist because somebody has to be paid for time spent in a car, for an evening held open and then cancelled, and for the administrative cost of replacing a tutor who has moved emirate. The problem is that they are rarely itemised, so a family comparing AED 250 against AED 180 is comparing two numbers that mean different things.

Travel is the dominant one. A tutor absorbing a 30-minute drive each way has to recover that time somewhere, and the three available levers are a higher hourly rate, a longer minimum block, or fewer students, each of which lands on the family as cost or inconvenience. Two-hour minimums are not a teaching judgement. No Diploma student concentrates productively for 120 unbroken minutes after a school day; the block exists so the journey is worth making.

Cancellation terms are the second. In-home providers typically need 24 hours or more because the slot cannot be refilled at short notice from another emirate. Online, the same tutor can usually move a Wednesday to a Thursday, and the commercial pressure to charge for the gap largely disappears. That difference is worth real money across a school year with two exam blocks, a Ramadan period and a family trip in it.

The table below sets out the stack. Treat the AED effects as the direction and rough scale the market moves in, not as a quotation: they are drawn from published UAE rate tables and package prices collected in October 2026, and your own quote should be itemised against them.

sections.heading: A month of lessons, priced the way the UAE market publishes it
paragraphs: Monthly packages are how most UAE providers sell, and they are designed to be hard to compare. One sells eight sessions, another four visits of two hours, a third quotes a range with no session count at all. The fix is one division: take the monthly figure, divide it by the teaching hours inside it, and the headline stops mattering. Done that way, the cheapest-looking package on a UAE price list is sometimes the most expensive hour of teaching on it.

The numbers in the table are all published figures, collected in October 2026, with the source named in the final column. The two package rows come from UAE tutoring providers advertising monthly plans; the three tier rows come from the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour sessions. None of them is an IB Gram price. We publish a rate after the free trial lesson, when the subject, the level and the actual starting point are known, because a figure quoted before any of that is a guess dressed as a quotation.

Two patterns show up as soon as the division is done. The first is that the in-home premium is roughly double, not marginal: around AED 200 to 225 per teaching hour against around AED 100 for the comparable online package. The second is that the specialist exam-year band is where families overspend without noticing, because the monthly figure climbs while the hours inside it often do not.

A third, quieter pattern matters more than either. Low monthly totals usually buy generalist hours. If the student needs a Higher Level physicist, four cheap hours of general science help is not a cheaper version of that; it is a different product that will not move the paper mark. Buy fewer hours of the right person rather than more hours of the wrong one.

sections.heading: Travel is a line item even when nobody charges for it
paragraphs: The clearest way to see what an in-home arrangement costs is to count minutes rather than dirhams. A lesson is a block of a tutor's evening, and the family is buying the whole block whether or not the whole block is teaching. The rows below are arithmetic, not survey data: take a stated journey, add it twice, add a few minutes for a lift and a greeting, and read off what proportion of the block was teaching.

The result explains most of the commercial behaviour in this market. At half the block spent driving, a tutor can make one visit an evening instead of two, so the rate per hour has to carry an evening's earnings. At two thirds, the only viable product is a long block or a group, which is why cross-emirate quotes arrive with two-hour minimums attached and why some providers push small groups instead. None of that is sharp practice. It is the arithmetic.

It also explains the quieter cost, which is scheduling. School runs across Dubai and Abu Dhabi push realistic start times past 17:00, and a tutor with a 30-minute drive between two families cannot offer 17:00 and 18:30 on the same evening. Families end up with the slot the route allows rather than the slot the child works best in, and a tired 19:30 Chemistry session is a poor use of AED 250.

Live online lessons remove the journey from both sides. The practical consequence is not only a lower rate; it is that two 45-minute sessions a week become affordable and schedulable, which for most Diploma subjects teaches considerably more than one two-hour block on a Thursday night.

sections.heading: The twenty-minute radius problem
paragraphs: Searching for a tutor by distance quietly changes the question from who can teach this to who lives nearby. For Year 4 numeracy those are close to the same question. For Physics HL under the current guide they are not, and the gap between them is where most of the disappointment in this market comes from.

The supply numbers make it concrete. Dubai has 227 private schools teaching 17 curricula, and the IB covers roughly 7 per cent of enrolment. A Higher Level Physics class in a UAE school is often a single group of a dozen or so students, taught by one or two teachers in the building. Draw a 20-minute radius around a villa in Dubai Hills and you have captured a handful of such teachers, most of whom are barred from tutoring their own students, and in Abu Dhabi explicitly so under ADEK professional-ethics rules.

What families settle for in that situation is predictable: a strong general scientist for a Higher Level paper, a mathematics graduate for an exploration that needs a teacher who has marked one, or an undergraduate who sat the Diploma recently and is cheaper than both. Those arrangements can work. They fail in a specific way, which is that the student gets the content right and the assessment wrong, because nobody in the room has read the current subject guide or a real mark scheme.

A national online pool changes the selection rule rather than the price. The binding constraint becomes availability in your evening window instead of availability within a drive, and for scarce subjects that is the difference between a specialist and a substitute. Where no specialist is free we say so rather than sending whoever is.

sections.heading: Which hours are worth buying, and when they stop being worth anything
paragraphs: Not every hour of tutoring has the same number of marks exposed to it. Each Diploma component has a window during which work on it can still change the outcome, and once that window closes the hour is worth very little regardless of what you pay for it. Families who get good value from tutoring are usually the ones who bought the right component at the right time, not the ones who bought the most hours.

Internal Assessment is the clearest case. In most Diploma subjects it carries 20% of the final grade, and it is written across a year under the school's own deadlines. An hour spent on an exploration in October, while the research question is still movable, can affect several marks. The same hour in late February, on a draft already submitted for authenticity sign-off, can affect almost nothing, because the student may no longer change it. That is the single most expensive timing error UAE families make.

Papers work the other way round. The marks stay available until the exam itself, so paper technique is the one thing worth buying late, and a six-week run of focused sessions before the May session is a reasonable purchase even if nothing came before it. The planning horizon column below is the practical part: it tells you how far ahead each component has to be bought to be worth buying.

Weightings move between subject guides, so confirm the split for your child's subjects with the school's IB coordinator against the current guide before planning around them. The figures shown are the common current pattern in the sciences and mathematics, where most UAE tutoring demand sits.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to give private lessons in the UAE, and what that should cost
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, not informal. The route is a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated completion time of two working days. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone providing private tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anybody.

The cost consequence is simple and useful. Because the permit costs nothing, any line in a quote that reads as a licensing, registration or compliance fee is a margin, not a disbursement. Ask what it covers. The same applies to administrative charges attached to replacing a tutor: that is a provider cost, and whether you pay it is a commercial question rather than a regulatory one.

Eligibility is wider than most parents expect, which is why the same hourly rate can buy very different people. Registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 can all hold the permit. A permit confirms that someone is allowed to tutor. It says nothing about whether they have taught a Diploma subject or seen a mark scheme.

Two boundaries are worth knowing before you book. Teachers are barred from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school under ADEK professional-ethics rules in Abu Dhabi, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction; this is press-reported, so check the current policy if it matters to your arrangement. And an operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: a centre in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of that kind, has no UAE premises, and does not present itself as endorsed by any authority named here.

sections.heading: The UAE academic year decides what you can buy, and when
paragraphs: Tutoring supply in the UAE is seasonal, and the seasons are not the ones a family expects. Demand spikes twice: once in late September when the first DP1 assessments land, and once between January and March when coursework deadlines and the March Cambridge series collide. Specialists in scarce subjects are committed for the year by about mid-October, which is why a February request for a Physics HL teacher so often returns a generalist.

The dated anchors below are board dates rather than IB dates, and that distinction is deliberate. Cambridge International runs June and November series with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Its March 2027 series runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Direct on 13 May. Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs run in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

IB session dates are not published on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and the UAE schools we work with sit the May session, so we describe it as the May session and nothing more precise. Confirm every IB date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before you plan around it, and treat any page that prints a confident IB results date without a source with suspicion.

Ramadan is the scheduling variable the price lists ignore entirely. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing, school days shorten, and an in-home arrangement that depends on a tutor crossing the city at 18:00 becomes hard to hold together. Online slots move by agreement, which in practice means a UAE family keeps its revision rhythm through the month instead of pausing it.

sections.heading: Paying more does not buy coursework, at any rate
paragraphs: There is one thing in this market that no fee should be able to buy, and it is the part some providers sell hardest. Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, the TOK essay, the Personal Project and the reflective project must be the student's own work. A supervisor signs off authenticity, schools run similarity checks, and the IB treats produced-for-you work as malpractice, which puts the whole Diploma at risk rather than one subject grade. A family paying for that is buying their child's exposure, not their marks.

The boundary is easier to hold than it sounds, because the useful work sits entirely on the legitimate side of it. A tutor can teach the skill the component tests, explain what a criterion strand is asking for, mark a practice question against a real mark scheme, ask hard questions about a research question the student chose, and read a draft the student wrote and say where the reasoning stops. All of that moves marks and all of it is permitted.

What a tutor must refuse is specific. No text supplied for insertion. No rewriting that leaves the student's voice behind. No dataset the student did not generate. No sourcing of secondary material the student then presents as their own reading. If a provider's offer sounds like a delivery date and a word count, that is a writing service, and the thing being sold is risk.

This is also where the money question and the honesty question meet. Sessions that teach technique compound: the student who learns how uncertainty is marked in one investigation carries it into every paper question that touches it. A document bought once teaches nothing and leaves a permanent record on an academic-honesty file. The cheaper option, measured across two years, is the legitimate one.
bullets: Permitted: teaching the skill, explaining a criterion, marking practice work, feedback on the student's own draft.
Not permitted: supplying text, rewriting to completion, providing data the student did not collect.
Ask any provider to state its coursework boundary in writing before the first payment.
Authenticity is signed off inside the school, so a bought document is discoverable later, not just now.

sections.heading: What to send when you ask three providers for a quote
paragraphs: Most UAE parents contact three or four providers and get three or four unusable answers, because the enquiry did not contain enough for anyone to price. A message that says my son needs help with IB maths can only be answered with a range, and a range is what comes back. Five specifics turn the same enquiry into a real quotation and, more usefully, let you compare the replies against each other.

The single most valuable item is a piece of the student's actual work: a marked paper, a returned exploration draft with the teacher's comments, a report with subject grades on it. A provider who reads it will tell you something specific in the first reply, and one who does not read it will send a brochure. That is the cheapest filter available to a parent in this market, and it costs one attachment.

The second most valuable is the slot you genuinely have. Tutoring plans fail on scheduling far more often than on teaching quality, and a tutor who is honest about 17:30 on Gulf Standard Time being impossible has just saved you a month. Say which evenings exist, in your actual time zone, including what Ramadan will do to them.

Send the same five items to everyone. Then compare the replies on how specific they are rather than on price alone, because the provider who identifies the right problem at AED 250 is better value than the one who identifies nothing at AED 180.
