sections.heading: The bills that arrive after the Diploma: equivalency and entry
paragraphs: Two costs land after the teaching is finished, and UAE families routinely meet them later than they should. The first is Ministry of Education equivalency, which is how an international school certificate becomes a UAE-recognised one for university admission and employment. The second is exam entry itself, where a student sitting as a private candidate rather than through a school pays a centre directly.

For the British track the requirements are published and specific: proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, plus five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which is worth knowing because at least one ranking UAE tutoring page states a six-subject requirement. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB there is no figure on this page, deliberately. We have not read an IB points threshold for equivalency on a Ministry of Education source, so we do not publish one. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate, and be sceptical of any tutoring page that quotes a number without saying where it came from. Equivalency is also a process a family completes with the authority, not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or speeds up.

The planning point is cheaper than the paperwork. Subject choices made in Year 11 decide whether the equivalency file assembles easily two years later, and a student who drops a subject for workload reasons can find the count short at the end. That is a thirty-minute conversation with the school in DP1, not a bill. Nothing here means tutoring is required for equivalency or admission; it is required for neither.

process.title: Send the five lines
process.description: Subject, level and programme; the school and the guide or board in use; the deadline that prompted the enquiry; one real piece of the student's work; and the evening slots that genuinely exist in your time zone, Ramadan included. That is enough for a specialist to say something useful in the first reply.

process.title: We say what we have, and what we do not
process.description: If a Higher Level specialist in that subject is free in your window, we name the match and the rate band. If nobody suitable is free, we say so rather than offering the nearest available alternative. Scarce subjects such as Physics HL and Computer Science are the ones where this happens most often.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One trial lesson per subject, arranged before any payment is taken and before any rate is agreed. Judge it on the diagnosis rather than on rapport: a specialist should finish the hour able to name which components are losing marks and which are still open to being changed.

process.title: Agree the rate and the pattern
process.description: The rate is set after the trial, when the subject, the level and the real starting point are known. The pattern follows what the student needs: one weekly slot, two shorter sessions, a short-notice block before a deadline, or separate slots for two children in the same household.

process.title: Fix the slot on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Lessons run over live video at an agreed weekly time, with written notes afterwards that a parent can read without having sat in. Rescheduling inside the same week is normally possible, because there is no journey to re-plan around and no held-open evening to pay for.

process.title: Review against the school's own reports
process.description: Every six to eight weeks, read the plan against what the school is reporting rather than against how the lessons feel. If a component has closed, stop paying for work on it. If a new one has opened, move the hours there. This is the whole of value for money in tutoring.

whyPoints.title: The AED numbers are on the page
whyPoints.description: Market bands, monthly packages divided out per teaching hour, and the source and month for each. Three of the six UAE pages that rank for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: No car in the fee
whyPoints.description: Teaching is delivered over live video, so you are not paying for driving, a two-hour minimum that exists to justify a journey, or a held-open evening. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India, and we would rather state that here than at the end of a sales call.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus, not by distance
whyPoints.description: The selection rule is who has taught this subject at this level against the current guide, and who is free in your evening window. A twenty-minute radius around a UAE villa is a poor filter for Physics HL, and pretending otherwise is how families end up with a generalist.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach the skill, explain criteria, mark practice work and give feedback on drafts the student wrote. Nobody supplies text, rewrites to completion or provides data the student did not collect. That line is published before you pay, not discovered afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Independent of every school and authority named here
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, has no UAE premises, and names schools only as context for the curricula taught in each area.

whyPoints.title: Honest about timing and availability
whyPoints.description: Specialists in scarce subjects commit for the year by about mid-October, and February requests are hard to fill at any rate. We say which window you are in, what is still buyable in it, and when the answer is that nobody suitable is free.

faqs.question: What do home tutors charge per hour in the UAE, and what does online cost instead?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market rates in October 2026 put an in-home one-to-one visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, and a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with premium named tutors quoted higher. Those are other providers' figures, drawn from their own pages and from the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, not ours. IB Gram agrees a rate after the free trial lesson, when the subject, level and starting point are known rather than guessed.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Dubai or Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India, and we state that before a booking rather than after one. The practical effect for a UAE family is a wider choice of teacher and a lower rate: the fee covers teaching rather than driving, single 60-minute lessons are possible instead of two-hour minimum blocks, and a Higher Level specialist is selected on what they have taught rather than on how far they live from your community.

faqs.question: Why do visiting tutors in the UAE quote a two-hour minimum?
faqs.answer: Because of travel arithmetic rather than teaching judgement. A tutor driving 30 minutes each way commits about 125 minutes of an evening to deliver 60 minutes of teaching, so roughly half the block is unpaid journey. At that ratio only one visit an evening is realistic, and the rate for that visit has to carry the whole evening. A two-hour block changes the ratio to under a third. No Diploma student concentrates well for 120 unbroken minutes after school, so the minimum serves the journey, not the learning.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package better value than paying session by session?
faqs.answer: Divide it out before deciding. A UAE online plan published at AED 799 a month for eight sessions works out near AED 100 per teaching hour. An in-home plan at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits lands near AED 200 to 225. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Packages are good value when the hours inside them are the right person's hours, and poor value when they lock a rate before the match is proven.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same household share one tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: Only when the subject and the level genuinely overlap, which is rarer than families hope. A Year 11 IGCSE student and a Diploma Higher Level student are sitting different papers against different mark schemes, and an hour split between them usually teaches neither properly. Online, the alternative costs the same: two shorter one-to-one slots on different evenings, each with a specialist for that level, with no second journey to pay for and no sibling surcharge. One combined review note afterwards means a parent still reads a single summary rather than two.

faqs.question: Should travel appear as a separate charge on an in-home quote?
faqs.answer: It rarely does, and that is the problem. Driving time is usually recovered invisibly through a higher hourly rate, a longer minimum block or a tight cancellation window, which is why two quotes of AED 250 and AED 180 can describe completely different arrangements. Ask for any quote split into the teaching fee, the travel position, the minimum block and the cancellation terms. If a quote also carries a licensing, registration or compliance fee, ask what it covers: the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge, so there is nothing to pass on.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does an IB Diploma student actually need?
faqs.answer: For one struggling subject, one 60-minute session a week sustains progress, and two shorter sessions usually teach more than a single long block because attention rather than budget is the limit. For a subject in difficulty with a deadline inside six weeks, two sessions a week is reasonable for that stretch and then should drop back. Buying four or five hours a week across several subjects at once rarely works: the student loses homework time and the gains are not attributable to anything. Review the pattern every six to eight weeks against the school's reports.

faqs.question: Our child takes Physics HL and nobody nearby teaches it. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics is the hardest subject to staff locally anywhere in the UAE. A school typically has one or two teachers for a small cohort, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK professional-ethics rules prevent them from tutoring their own students for a fee. A search by distance will return general science teachers and engineering graduates, who can cover content but not paper technique against the current guide. Online removes the distance filter, so selection depends on who has taught the subject and who is free in your evening window. Where nobody suitable is free, we say so.

faqs.question: May I ask to see a tutor's private tuition work permit before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a fair question. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a MoHRE work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years and applied for through MoHRE's own channels in about two working days. Working without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount with caution. Remember what the permit does and does not tell you: it confirms somebody may tutor, not that they have ever taught a Diploma subject or read a mark scheme.

faqs.question: Can my child's own class teacher tutor them privately for a fee?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi, no. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify the current wording with the school if it matters to your plan. The practical consequence is the same across the country: paid help has to come from outside the building, which is exactly why a wider pool of teachers matters more than a short drive.

faqs.question: What happens in the free trial lesson, and what are its conditions?
faqs.answer: One trial lesson per subject, arranged before any payment is taken and before a rate is agreed. The specialist works through a real piece of the student's own work rather than running an introduction, and should finish able to say which components are losing marks and which are still open to change. Judge the lesson on that diagnosis. There is no obligation afterwards, and the rate band is quoted once the subject, level and starting point are known. If the trial shows we are not the right fit for that subject, we will say so.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue through Ramadan and the summer holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing agreed week by week. During Ramadan sessions commonly move to post-Iftar timing and school days shorten, which is the point at which an arrangement depending on a tutor crossing the city at 18:00 tends to break down. Online slots move by agreement, so the revision rhythm survives the month. Summer is the cheapest and most available window in the UAE tutoring year, and the most useful thing to buy in it is transition work: MYP into the Diploma, IGCSE into DP1, or the groundwork for an exploration due in the autumn.

faqs.question: Will a tutor write or finish my child's Extended Essay if we pay more?
faqs.answer: No, at any price. The Extended Essay, the Internal Assessments, the TOK essay and the Personal Project must be the student's own work, authenticity is signed off by a supervisor inside the school, and the IB treats produced-for-you work as malpractice that puts the whole Diploma at risk. What a tutor does instead is narrow the research question, plan the reading, explain what each criterion is asking for, and give feedback on drafting the student did. If a provider's offer sounds like a word count and a delivery date, what is being sold is risk.

faqs.question: What should I put in a message when I ask three providers for a quote?
faqs.answer: Five things: the subject, level and programme; the school and which board or guide it uses; the deadline that prompted the enquiry; one real piece of the student's work, such as a marked paper or a returned draft; and the evening slots you genuinely have in your own time zone, Ramadan included. Send the same five to everybody. Then compare the replies on specificity rather than on price, because a provider who names the actual problem at AED 250 an hour is better value than one who names nothing at AED 180.

faqs.question: Is a quoted rate inclusive of VAT, and should a tutor show a TRN?
faqs.answer: Ask both questions directly and get the answer in writing. We do not publish a tax position for UAE tuition on this page, because stating one would need a Federal Tax Authority source we are not citing here. What a parent can reasonably do is ask whether a quoted AED figure is inclusive or exclusive, and whether the provider holds a tax registration number. A quote that cannot answer either question clearly is a quote you cannot compare with another one, which is reason enough to ask before the first payment rather than after it.

faqs.question: Which exam session is my child sitting, and when do entries close?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, because entry deadlines sit months before the papers. Cambridge International runs June and November series with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Its March 2027 series runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026. Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs run in May/June and November. UAE IB students sit the May session; confirm those dates with the IB coordinator, because we do not publish them.

faqs.question: We have about AED 2,000 a month to spend. Where should it go?
faqs.answer: At published market rates that is roughly eight to ten hours at the budget end, or four to six hours of an IB specialist. Spend it on one subject, not three. For content gaps and confidence, a recent high-scoring graduate near the AED 45 to 150 band is reasonable value. For a Higher Level paper losing marks to command terms, method lines and criterion wording, you need somebody who has marked work against the current guide, which is the AED 200 to 450 band. Four cheap hours of general science is not a discounted specialist.

faqs.question: How do you know the hours we are paying for are working?
faqs.answer: By reading the plan against the school's own reporting every six to eight weeks, not against how the lessons feel. Three things are checkable: whether the component the hours were aimed at has moved, whether the written notes after each lesson describe specific errors rather than topics covered, and whether the student can now do the thing unprompted. If a component has closed, stop paying for work on it. If a new one has opened, move the hours. Grades are the slowest signal available and the last one to look at.

ib-home-tutors.closingHeading: Start with the number, then check what it buys
ib-home-tutors.closingBody: An in-home tutor in the UAE costs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour at published market rates, and a meaningful share of that fee pays for a car rather than for teaching. The same one-to-one teaching delivered over live video on Gulf Standard Time removes the journey, the two-hour minimum and the twenty-minute radius that decides which teacher you are allowed to choose. Send the five lines, take the free trial lesson in the subject that matters most, and judge the diagnosis before any rate is agreed. If no specialist is free in your window, we will tell you that instead of sending whoever is.

intro.heading: Four fixed points every UAE coaching plan has to work around
paragraphs: Most families looking for IB IGCSE coaching in the UAE start with a subject and a grade. The more useful starting point is the paperwork. Your child's school holds a licence from one of four authorities, teaches a curriculum that authority signed off, timetables three UAE subjects the federal rules require regardless of that curriculum, and submits exam entries to a board on a deadline set outside the country. None of those four things is negotiable, and all four decide what an hour of coaching can usefully do. A plan built without them tends to teach the wrong syllabus at the wrong time of year, which is the most expensive mistake available in this market.

Take the licence first. If you live in Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and both of those bodies approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education. Four bodies, four published positions, and four different things a parent can look up before spending a dirham.

The curriculum mix matters next. Dubai's private sector enrolled 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with a UK curriculum taken by 37 per cent of enrolments, Indian by 26 per cent, American by 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate by 7 per cent. One building can run a British primary, a Cambridge IGCSE middle school and a Diploma sixth form at the same time. A parent therefore cannot assume the subject name on a report card maps to a single board or a single paper structure. Coaching that does not begin by reading the actual entry code is coaching aimed at an average syllabus that nobody sits.

Then the three mandatory subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies run in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA set the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the implementation point. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the two groups. Those lessons occupy real timetable minutes, calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and they sit alongside six Diploma subjects or nine IGCSEs rather than instead of them.

Last comes the calendar, which is where families usually arrive too late. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; for its March 2027 series the exam period is 3 February to 4 March 2027 and final entries are due 27 November 2026, more than two months before the first paper. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May/June and November. Coaching that begins in February for a February series has already missed the decision that mattered, because the tier and the subject list were locked in November. Working backwards from the entry deadline rather than from the exam is the single change that makes the hours count.

ib-igcse-coaching.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the four programmes a UAE household is most likely to be juggling, often two at once between siblings. Each note below says what the UAE school system adds on top of the programme itself, because that part is absent from both the IB's documentation and Cambridge's syllabus pages, and it is usually the part that decides how many hours a family needs.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel
programmes.description: Two years of externally examined subject courses, commonly eight or nine subjects. Cambridge syllabuses tier several sciences and mathematics as Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel runs its own paper structure and its own codes. Grades report as 9-1 or A*-G depending on the syllabus and series. The tier decision caps the grade available, so it is the first thing a coach checks before planning any content at all.
programmes.countryNote: In the Emirates the IGCSE years carry a second job. They build the five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 that the Ministry of Education's British track counts for certificate equivalency, and Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from that count of five. A Core entry, or a subject quietly dropped in Year 11, can narrow that file without anyone at home noticing until a university application.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment carries a fixed share of each subject grade, is marked in school and then moderated by the IB. UAE schools sit the May session. A failing condition in the core can cost the whole Diploma even when the six subject grades look comfortable, which is why the core deserves coaching time of its own.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students here still have Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies on the timetable, and their school's internal assessment deadlines rarely align with the dates in the subject guides. UAE families face a second question too: the Ministry of Education publishes its British-track equivalency rule in plain numbers but no IB points threshold that we have read on an official page, so that one has to be verified directly rather than taken from a tutoring website.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years in most UAE schools, assessed against four criteria per subject, each criterion marked out of eight, with the totals converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. There is no external paper unless the school offers eAssessment. Reports therefore speak in criterion letters, and a parent who has never seen that language cannot tell a weak criterion A from a weak criterion D, or which one a coach should attack first.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Year 5 in the Emirates is where the board decision gets taken. Some schools move students into Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE for Years 10 and 11; others carry straight through to the Diploma. The two routes need visibly different preparation, and the choice is usually settled in the spring term before any family has discussed coaching. Asking which route the school intends is a sensible question in Year 8, not Year 10.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: A transdisciplinary primary framework with no external examinations, organised around units of inquiry and reported against learner-profile attributes rather than subject percentages. Literacy and numeracy still sit underneath the inquiry, and gaps there are exactly what surface two years later in an MYP science class or a Cambridge mathematics set, by which point the fix costs far more hours than it would have done.
programmes.countryNote: Primary families in the UAE usually come to coaching for one of two reasons: a mid-year move between curricula, which is common in a population that relocates often, or Arabic as an additional language starting from nothing. Neither is a gap the school day is built to close, and both respond well to short weekly online sessions rather than long ones, since attention at that age runs out before the hour does.

ib-igcse-coaching.subjectsIntro: Nine IB subjects below, then a separate International GCSE grid, because the same subject name means different things on the two boards and at the two levels. Each note says where marks actually go missing rather than what the course contains. The content list is on the board's own website and reading it does not help you decide where to spend an hour.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-heavy route. Marks go missing in two predictable places: method marks lost because working is compressed rather than shown, and calculus questions where the candidate differentiates correctly then misreads what the question asked for. HL Paper 3 rewards students who have practised extended, structured investigations, which is a different skill from answering short questions quickly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with heavier calculator use. The common loss is interpretation rather than computation: a correct regression line with no sentence explaining what it means in context. UAE students choosing between the two mathematics routes should check the engineering and economics prerequisites at the universities they are actually applying to before deciding.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry most of the lost marks, and the internal assessment carries a fixed share of the final grade for a piece of work the student designs themselves. Coaching here splits cleanly in two: paper technique against past questions, and process coaching on the student's own investigation without any wording being supplied by the coach.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Candidates lose marks on unit consistency, significant figures and on the extended-response questions that ask them to explain rather than calculate. The data-analysis questions reward students who have handled real uncertainty figures. Over live video these are taught with a shared screen and the student's own written working photographed in, not read out.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume of content makes recall the limiting factor, and command terms decide the mark: distinguish, outline and explain each want a different shape of answer. Weak statistical handling in the internal assessment is the other recurring loss. A coach works on the student's own data and method, never on supplying text for the write-up.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation component decide grades more than definitions do. Students who can draw the diagram but cannot evaluate the policy sit several marks below their understanding. HL adds calculation under time pressure. The internal assessment commentaries are the student's own work, with a coach restricted to feedback on structure and on the economics.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper one unseen analysis are where marks swing. Candidates who have practised reading an unfamiliar non-literary text for technique rather than theme score higher. For families whose first language is not English, the gap is usually confidence with analytical vocabulary rather than comprehension.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus material carries the marks. Generic answers that could apply to any company lose exactly the marks a specific reference would have earned. HL adds the business research project. Coaching concentrates on reading the case, selecting the right tool and writing an answer that stays anchored to the named firm.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: The route a non-Arab student takes inside an IB timetable, running alongside the Arabic the school is separately required to teach. Writing and productive speaking are the usual weak points because classroom time skews to reading. Sessions are built around script fluency and the themes the course actually assesses rather than general conversation.

ib-igcse-coaching.igcseSubjectsIntro: The International GCSE grid is separate because the board changes the paper, the tier and the code even where the subject name is identical. Ask your exams officer for the statement of entry before booking anything: it names the syllabus code, and the code is what a coach needs. The examples below are the subjects UAE families request most often.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics
igcseSubjects.levels: Cambridge Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: The tier decision caps the grade, so it comes before any content planning. Cambridge mathematics is commonly entered as 0580 and Pearson as 4MA1, but confirm the code on your child's statement of entry rather than assuming. Lost marks cluster in algebraic manipulation and in multi-step problems where the first error carries through.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics
igcseSubjects.levels: Cambridge Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel single award
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and waves are the topics UAE students most often name as the problem, and the practical component is assessed in writing rather than in a laboratory for most candidates. Cambridge physics commonly appears as 0625 and Pearson as 4PH1. Coaching over video works through the written alternative-to-practical style questions directly.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry
igcseSubjects.levels: Cambridge Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel single award
igcseSubjects.description: Moles calculations and the qualitative analysis tables are where grades are made. The recall load is heavier than students expect, and the Extended tier adds content that the Core tier never covers. Confirm with the school whether a separate science or a combined science entry has been made, because the revision list differs completely.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology
igcseSubjects.levels: Cambridge Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel single award
igcseSubjects.description: A content-recall subject where structured revision beats extra teaching. Command terms decide the mark, and diagram labelling questions are reliably available marks that students leave on the table. Sessions usually run as timed past-paper work with immediate marking rather than as fresh teaching of topics already covered in class.

igcseSubjects.name: English First Language and English as a Second Language
igcseSubjects.description: Which of the two a child is entered for changes the ceiling and the paper, and UAE schools do not always explain the difference at the point of entry. Directed writing and the summary question carry a disproportionate number of marks relative to the time students give them in revision.

igcseSubjects.name: Arabic as a First Language and Arabic as an Additional Language
igcseSubjects.levels: First language and additional language routes
igcseSubjects.description: Taken as an IGCSE option by some UAE students and also required separately by the emirate rules. The grade does not count towards the five subjects the Ministry of Education's British track asks for, which surprises families every year. Sessions focus on the written paper and on script accuracy under timed conditions.

ib-igcse-coaching.regionsTitle: The seven emirates and the authority standing behind each school
ib-igcse-coaching.regionsIntro: Coaching reaches every emirate the same way, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. What changes between them is the regulator, the density of IB and IGCSE schools, and therefore how likely it is that a Higher Level specialist lives within driving distance of you. The notes below are about the school system in each emirate, not about the scenery.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: 227 private schools and seventeen curricula, regulated by KHDA, whose inspection reports and school listings are published and searchable. The deepest pool of IB and IGCSE schools in the country, and the only emirate where a parent can usually read a detailed inspection judgement on their own school before deciding where coaching money should go.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which makes the familiar offer of evening lessons from a class teacher a question worth asking about.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller set of IB and IGCSE schools than the island. Families here are the clearest case for online delivery: the subject specialist a Higher Level Chemistry student needs is rarely within a reasonable drive, and a video session removes the distance from the decision entirely.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods. Because assessment methods are approved locally, it is worth confirming with the school which board and which tier your child is actually entered for before planning a revision programme around it.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority, so there is no local inspection portal to read. Many Ajman families commute to schools in Sharjah or Dubai, which compresses the usable evening window and makes a fixed weekly online slot easier to protect than a travelling arrangement.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Fewer IB schools locally means fewer local specialists, and it is one of the three emirates that returned no mentions at all across the competitor pages we examined, so published guidance for RAK families is genuinely thin.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education. Distance from the Dubai and Abu Dhabi tutoring market is the operative fact here: a coach travelling to Fujairah prices the drive into the hour, while a video session does not. East-coast families also sit outside the cluster of exam centres, which makes private-candidate logistics worth checking early.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally, and the smallest private-school market in the country. Specialist subject coverage at Higher Level is effectively an online question. Ask the school which Cambridge administrative zone its centre sits in, because the timetable version differs by zone and Cambridge does not accept responsibility for a candidate who reads the wrong one.

schoolClusters.note: The widest mix of boards in one emirate, with several schools running an IB programme and a Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE route in the same building. Students we support attend schools across this group. Checking which route a school intends for Year 10 is the single most useful question a parent can ask at a Year 8 parents' evening.

A smaller IB and IGCSE cluster than Dubai's, under ADEK rather than KHDA. The professional-ethics position on staff tutoring their own students matters more here than anywhere else in the country, and it is the reason many Abu Dhabi families end up looking outside the school for subject support in the first place.

Schools here fall under SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Specialist Higher Level coverage thins out quickly outside Sharjah city, which is why online delivery is the practical answer rather than a second-best one.

sections.heading: What a UAE parent is actually buying when they search for coaching
paragraphs: IB IGCSE coaching in the UAE means one-to-one teaching in a named subject, at a named level, on the syllabus a particular school entered a particular child for. It is not a general tutoring service with the words IB and IGCSE added to the page. The distinction is practical rather than semantic: the Cambridge and Pearson versions of the same subject use different papers and different codes, and the Higher and Standard Level versions of an IB subject differ in content and in how much of the grade the internal assessment carries. A coach who does not know which of those applies is guessing for the first few hours you pay for.

The second thing you are buying is a timetable that fits a UAE week. School runs in this country finish late, traffic between emirates is a real constraint, the working week has a Friday shape, and Ramadan moves evening availability for a month. An hour booked at a time nobody can keep is an hour wasted regardless of who teaches it. Coaching delivered online on Gulf Standard Time removes the part of the scheduling problem caused by somebody else's drive, which is usually the part that breaks first.

The third thing, and the one almost nobody sells, is knowledge of the system your child sits inside. Which authority licenses the school and what its published report says. Which three subjects the emirate requires on top of the curriculum. What the Ministry of Education wants to see in an equivalency file. When the board closes entries. Those four facts shape a coaching plan more than any teaching method does, and the rest of this page works through them in order, with the sources named so you can check each one yourself.

sections.heading: Which authority licenses your child's school, and what that changes
paragraphs: There is no single UAE schools regulator. Private schools in Dubai answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Those five bodies are the complete map, and ADEK in particular was named by none of the competitor pages we examined in October 2026.

Knowing which one applies to you has three concrete uses. It tells you where to read an inspection judgement on your own school, which is the cheapest piece of diagnostic information available to a parent and is free. It tells you whose ethics rules govern your child's teachers, which matters if a teacher offers paid evening lessons. And in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah it tells you that the authority approves curricula and assessment methods as well as fees, so the board and tier your child is entered for were signed off locally and can be confirmed locally.

Read an inspection report for the subject detail rather than the overall band. A school rated Good overall can still have a weak judgement in secondary mathematics, and that paragraph is worth more to a coaching decision than the headline. What an inspection does not tell you is anything about your individual child, so treat a strong report as a reason to ask better questions at parents' evening rather than as evidence that extra help is unnecessary. Note also that no UAE authority approves individual private coaches: a KHDA educational services permit is issued to training institutes with premises, and any provider describing its individual tutors as regulator-endorsed is describing something that does not exist.

sections.heading: Reading a report card back to an actual exam entry
paragraphs: Dubai alone licenses seventeen curricula, and a single school can run more than one. The result is that a report card is an unreliable guide to what a child is being examined on. A Year 10 line that says Science could mean three separate Cambridge entries, a combined science entry, or a Pearson Edexcel double award. A grade written as 9-1 and a grade written as A*-G can come from the same board in different subjects. None of this is the school being unhelpful; it is what happens when international boards, local licensing and a parent's own curriculum background all meet on one sheet of A4.

The document that settles it is the statement of entry, held by the school's exams officer. It names the board, the syllabus code and the tier. With those three pieces of information a coach can plan content, pick the right past papers and tell you what the realistic grade ceiling is. Without them the first two or three sessions go on diagnosis that a single email to the exams officer would have done for free. Ask for it before you book anything, in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

For IB families the equivalent question is which level each subject sits at and when the school has set its internal assessment deadlines. The IB publishes subject guides; the school sets the internal dates, and they are frequently earlier than parents expect because the school needs marking and moderation time. An MYP report needs a third translation again: the criterion marks out of eight are the diagnostic information, and the overall 1-7 hides which of the four criteria is actually dragging the grade down.

sections.heading: The three UAE subjects that sit on top of whichever curriculum you chose
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position behind that is straightforward: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. These subjects are the floor under every IB and IGCSE timetable in the country.

The organisation rules are specific enough to matter for coaching. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arab students take Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies in the language of the school's licensed curriculum. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes.

Two consequences follow for a family buying coaching. The first is that Arabic and Islamic Education tuition in Dubai is a separate stream with its own stream rules, not an add-on to a maths hour, and your child must be supported in the group the school placed them in. The second is a constraint on material: for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A coach works from the school's own scheme and resources rather than importing an alternative syllabus, and any provider offering a richer or faster Arabic course than the school's licensed one is offering something the rules do not allow.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: what each file has to show
paragraphs: Certificate equivalency is the step that converts a school-leaving qualification into something a UAE authority recognises, and it is the single largest blind spot in the competitor pages we examined, where it returned effectively no mentions at all. For the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

Two details inside that rule change how an IGCSE programme should be built. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects, so a student carrying nine IGCSEs of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has seven candidates for the count rather than nine. And one page currently ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published five-subject rule. If you are planning subject choices around a UAE university application, count the five that will actually be counted before a subject gets dropped in Year 11.

The American track runs on test scores instead: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics via at least 450 in the SAT Maths test. For the IB Diploma we publish no points figure, because the source we read sets none and we have not read one on the Ministry's own site. Treat any tutoring page quoting an IB equivalency score without a moe.gov.ae citation with scepticism. Equivalency is also a process the Ministry runs, not one a tutoring company performs, and nobody should be charging you to arrange it on the side.

sections.heading: Counted backwards from the entry deadline, not from the exam
paragraphs: Families plan coaching from the exam date. Boards work from the entry date, and the gap between the two is where most of the avoidable damage happens. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Its March 2027 series is the clearest worked example available: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June.

Read that sequence backwards and the coaching implications are obvious. The tier and subject decisions are locked in late November, which means the evidence for those decisions has to exist in October. The school owes a forecast grade in late February, which means enough marked past-paper work has to exist by then for the forecast to be honest. A plan that starts in January has skipped both. For Pearson Edexcel, International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November, the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live PDF on its own site is the thing to check rather than any date restated on a tutoring page.

One Cambridge detail catches UAE families specifically. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the exams officer which zone your school sits in and work from that version. For IB dates, we deliberately publish none: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so every IB session, upload and results date should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator rather than taken from a tutoring website, including ours.

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to coach your child in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in this country is regulated by permit, and the position is not ambiguous. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 regarding the introduction of private tuition work permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The official service is listed by MoHRE as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any figure you see quoted for it on a tutoring page is unsourced and should be ignored. What a parent can usefully do is ask to see the permit before the first paid hour, and ask what it covers. The code of conduct attached to it bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. The familiar offer of quiet evening lessons from a class teacher runs directly into both.

A business is a different matter from an individual. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit, does not occupy premises in the UAE and does not describe itself as endorsed by any UAE authority. Permit status for the individuals who teach is a question we expect parents to ask, and the table below is the checklist to ask it with.

sections.heading: What the market charges across the Emirates, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The figures below were read from each provider's own published page in October 2026 and are presented as the market, not as an IB Gram price list. They are useful for one purpose: working out whether a quote you have been given sits inside the normal range for the format and level you are buying, or well outside it.

Four things move a quote inside those bands. Level is the obvious one, with Diploma Higher Level and IGCSE Extended commanding more than Core or Standard Level because the content depth and the marking load are genuinely greater. Format is the next, and it is the largest single factor: a coach travelling to a UAE address prices the drive into the hour whether or not it appears on the invoice. Scarcity is the third, which is why a Higher Level Chemistry hour costs more than a Year 9 maths hour in the same emirate. Proximity to the series is the fourth, and it is the one families control, because booking in October rather than April buys both a lower rate and a better choice of coach.

Monthly packages circulating in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. School fees being held does not hold tutoring rates, which are set by a private market with no fee regulator behind it.

sections.heading: A coach on live video against a coach at the door
paragraphs: Many UAE parents search for a home tutor and mean something specific: somebody sitting at the kitchen table on a Tuesday evening. That arrangement has real advantages, and it is worth answering honestly rather than talking around. A person in the room can read a distracted fourteen-year-old faster than a camera can, younger children settle into it more easily, and no part of the hour depends on the building's internet. Market rates for it in the UAE run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on level and emirate, with the travel priced in somewhere.

The costs are structural rather than a matter of preference. Your pool of coaches shrinks to whoever is within a reasonable drive, which in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain can mean a general science teacher instead of a Higher Level Chemistry specialist. The slot you are offered is shaped by somebody else's traffic rather than by your child's concentration. Written work stays on paper in the house, so nothing is readable later. And the arrangement is fragile: one relocation, one job change, and the plan restarts from scratch mid-year.

IB Gram does not offer visits to addresses in the Emirates. Home visits are a service we provide only in India, and the UAE service is one-to-one coaching over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. The case for it is not that it is cheaper, although published online rates are lower. It is that your child gets the specialist who actually teaches that paper, the session happens at an hour that works for your household rather than for a commute, and the annotated work and written feedback are there to read after the hour has finished. The table sets the two side by side.

sections.heading: The academic-honesty line on internal assessment and coursework
paragraphs: This market contains providers selling finished Internal Assessments. One we examined sells them at AED 3,750. That is an academic-integrity breach, a malpractice trigger under IB rules, and a risk carried entirely by your child rather than by the provider. A parent comparing options needs a clean way to tell a teaching service from an essay service, and the test is simple: ask what the provider will hand over. A teaching service hands over explanation, questions, marked feedback and a plan. An essay service hands over text.

Inside that boundary a coach can do a great deal that genuinely moves an internal assessment mark. Explaining what each assessment criterion is actually rewarding, and what the difference between the mark bands looks like in practice. Working through the student's own research question until it is narrow enough to investigate. Checking that a method will produce data the criteria can reward before weeks are spent collecting it. Teaching the statistical handling the student will need. Reading a draft the student wrote and giving feedback on it, which is the same thing a supervising teacher does. Explaining referencing conventions and why a missing citation is treated as seriously as it is.

What a coach does not do is author any part of the submission, supply wording to be pasted in, or edit a draft into a final version on the student's behalf. Those lines hold for the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, the MYP Personal Project, Diploma internal assessments and any IGCSE coursework component. Nor do we supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those belong to the boards, and a coach references the official source and links to it rather than reproducing it. Stating this plainly costs us a certain kind of enquiry, which we consider a feature.

process.title: Tell us the emirate, the school and the year group
process.description: The first message needs three things: where you are, which school, and which year. That tells us which authority licenses the school, whether the mandatory UAE subjects stream applies, and which board is likely to be in play. It takes a parent two minutes and saves a session of diagnosis later.

process.title: Confirm the board, the syllabus code and the tier
process.description: We ask you to get the statement of entry from the exams officer, or the subject list from the Diploma coordinator. Board, code and tier decide the papers, the content and the grade ceiling. For an MYP student we ask for the criterion marks out of eight rather than the overall 1-7 grade.

process.title: A free trial hour with the proposed coach
process.description: One hour, over live video, with the coach we think fits, before any payment and with no card details taken. You see the teaching rather than a sales call. If the fit is wrong, say so and we propose someone else or tell you plainly that we do not have the right specialist free.

process.title: A plan counted back from the entry deadline
process.description: After the trial you get a written plan that starts from the board's published key dates and works backwards: entry deadline, forecast-grade date, mock window, then the papers. It states how many sessions a week, on which day at Gulf Standard Time, and what the first four will cover.

process.title: A written review after four sessions
process.description: At four sessions we write to you with what has changed, what has not, and whether the hours should go up, down or move to a different subject. If a subject is better served by someone else, we say that. A plan nobody reviews becomes a standing order rather than a teaching decision.

whyPoints.title: The regulator map is on the page, not saved for a sales call
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education each govern different emirates, and ADEK was named by none of the competitor pages we examined. Knowing which one applies to your school tells you where to read its inspection judgement for free before you spend anything on coaching.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes before subject names
whyPoints.description: Coaching starts from the statement of entry rather than the report card, because Cambridge and Pearson set different papers for subjects that share a name, and a Core entry caps the grade before any teaching happens. A coach working from a code is planning; a coach working from a subject name is guessing.

whyPoints.title: The mandatory UAE subjects have a stream of their own
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are required in Dubai private schools whatever the international curriculum, organised in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and taught in a specified language. We coach them as their own stream, within the school's own material, because the rules do not allow substituting different content.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we do not do in the Emirates
whyPoints.description: We do not visit addresses in the UAE, hold no UAE premises or permit for a training institute, and claim no approval from any UAE authority or examination board. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Saying so costs enquiries and is still better than a parent discovering it after paying.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source and its date
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are each attributed to the provider that published them, read in October 2026, and presented as the market rather than as our price list. Where a source does not exist, such as an IB points figure for Ministry equivalency, we publish nothing and tell you where to check instead.

faqs.question: Our two children sit different boards, one on IGCSE and one in the Diploma. Can a single coaching plan cover both?
faqs.answer: Yes, but not with a single coach. The content, the papers and the assessment calendars are different enough that each child needs a subject specialist for their own board and level. What can be shared is the planning: one review conversation, one calendar covering both sets of deadlines, and sessions arranged so the household has one predictable evening pattern rather than two competing ones. Families with children on both boards usually start with the one closer to an exam series, add the second after a term, and keep both plans on the same written review cycle so hours can move between the two children when one needs them more.

faqs.question: Which authority actually licenses our school, and why should that change how we buy coaching?
faqs.answer: It depends on the emirate. Dubai schools are overseen by KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK, Sharjah by SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. It changes three things. It tells you where to read a published inspection judgement on your own school, which is free and more specific than most advice you will pay for. It tells you whose professional-ethics rules bind your child's teachers. And in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves assessment methods as well as fees, so the board and tier can be confirmed locally.

faqs.question: Dubai licenses seventeen curricula across its private schools. How do we work out which one our child is really examined on?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the statement of entry. A report card is not reliable evidence here, because one school building can run a British primary, a Cambridge IGCSE middle school and an IB Diploma sixth form at once, and a line that says Science can hide three separate entries or one combined award. The statement of entry names the board, the syllabus code and the tier. Those three facts decide which past papers are relevant, which content is on the course and what the grade ceiling is. Get them in Year 10 rather than Year 11, because the tier decision closes with the board's entry deadline.

faqs.question: The school says Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are compulsory. Does that really apply inside an IB building?
faqs.answer: It does. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA set the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the implementation point. The federal rule behind it is that private schools need not follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while still adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. In practice this means those lessons occupy timetable minutes alongside six Diploma subjects or nine IGCSEs, not instead of them, which is why revision planning has to account for them.

faqs.question: KHDA separates Arabic classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Does a coaching session have to follow the same split?
faqs.answer: It follows the stream the school placed your child in, which is effectively the same thing. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for the two groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. A coach works to the course your child is actually taking, so a non-Arab student on Arabic as an additional language is supported on that syllabus rather than on the first-language one. Moving a child between streams is a school decision, not something tutoring can arrange.

faqs.question: Our son's school teaches in English but his Islamic Education is in Arabic. Which language should a coach use?
faqs.answer: The same one the school uses, which is set by rule rather than preference. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Non-Arab students take Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies in the language of the school's licensed curriculum, so in an English-medium school that is English. If your son is in the Arab stream, his coaching runs in Arabic. If he is in the non-Arab stream at an English-medium school, it runs in English. Ask the school which stream he is in before booking, since the two are taught separately.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education want to see in an equivalency file for an IGCSE and A Level leaver?
faqs.answer: For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs rather than something a tutoring company performs or guarantees, so verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae or through your emirate's attestation channel, and be wary of anyone charging a fee to arrange it.

faqs.question: The Ministry asks for five accredited subjects. Does our daughter's IGCSE Arabic grade count towards that five?
faqs.answer: No. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count on the British track. That matters more than it sounds. A student carrying nine IGCSEs of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has seven subjects available for the count, not nine, and dropping two more in Year 11 brings the margin uncomfortably close. One page currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published five-subject rule. Count the subjects that will actually be counted before any are dropped.

faqs.question: A tutoring website quotes an IB points figure for UAE equivalency. Should we trust it?
faqs.answer: Not without checking it on an official page. The source we read sets out the British-track requirements in plain numbers and the American-track test thresholds, and states no IB points threshold at all. We therefore publish none, and we would treat any figure appearing on a tutoring site without a moe.gov.ae citation as unverified. The cost of inheriting someone else's wrong number is paid by your child's application, not by the website that published it. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator and check the Ministry's own page, in that order, before building subject choices around a points target.

faqs.question: Is the person coaching our child legally allowed to charge us in the UAE?
faqs.answer: They need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the application through its smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so ignore any amount quoted on a tutoring page. Ask to see the permit before the first paid hour.

faqs.question: A teacher at our daughter's own school has offered paid evening lessons. Is there a problem with that?
faqs.answer: There usually is. The code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition work permit bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Those rules exist because the same person would be teaching, assessing and privately charging for the same child. Treat the offer as one to decline politely, and verify the current wording against your emirate's own policy document rather than relying on a summary, including this one.

faqs.question: Our school's inspection report came back Good rather than Outstanding. Where should coaching money go after reading it?
faqs.answer: Into whatever subject area the report judged weakest at your child's phase, not into the overall band. An inspection judgement is reported by phase and by subject, so a school rated Good overall can carry a noticeably weaker judgement in secondary mathematics or in a science, and that paragraph is the most useful free diagnostic a parent gets. What the report cannot tell you is anything about your individual child. Use it to decide which subject to ask about at parents' evening, then use the subject teacher's answer to decide where an hour a week actually goes.

faqs.question: Cambridge gave our centre a zone letter. Does that really change which timetable we read?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth taking seriously. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your exams officer which zone your school sits in and work from that version of the PDF on Cambridge's own site. Revision planning backwards from a paper date is only as good as the date, and a zone mismatch can move a paper by a day or more.

faqs.question: Final entries close in November for a February exam series. What should be finished by then?
faqs.answer: The decisions, not the revision. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. By that November date the tier should be settled, the subject list fixed and the syllabus codes confirmed with the exams officer, which means the evidence for those choices has to exist in October. Forecast grades are then due 27 February 2027, so enough marked past-paper work has to exist by late February for the school to forecast honestly. A plan that begins in January has skipped both of those checkpoints.

faqs.question: Does a coaching company need a KHDA permit, and does IB Gram hold one?
faqs.answer: A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, which involves initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit, occupies no premises in the UAE and claims no endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. No UAE authority approves individual private coaches either, so a provider describing its tutors as regulator-endorsed is describing something that does not exist.

faqs.question: Can a coach look over an Internal Assessment draft, and where exactly does the line sit?
faqs.answer: A coach can explain what each assessment criterion rewards, help narrow a research question until it is investigable, check that a method will produce data the criteria can reward, teach the statistical handling needed, read a draft the student wrote and give feedback on it, and explain referencing conventions. What a coach must not do is author any part of the submission, supply wording to be pasted in, or edit a draft into a final version. The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay, the TOK essay, the MYP Personal Project and IGCSE coursework. Providers selling finished assessments exist in this market and the risk falls on the student.

faqs.question: Nobody comes to the villa, so how does an hour of coaching actually run?
faqs.answer: On live video, one-to-one, at a fixed slot on Gulf Standard Time. The coach shares a screen for working, the student writes on paper and photographs it in or works directly on the shared document, and annotated scripts and written feedback stay available after the session. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, so there is no UAE in-home option to compare on price. The practical gain is that your child gets the specialist who teaches that specific paper rather than whoever is within driving distance, which matters most in Al Ain, Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain.

faqs.question: Our daughter is on the Cambridge Core tier and wants a UAE university place. Is a Core entry enough?
faqs.answer: It depends on the grade the Core tier allows and on what the university asks for, so check both before assuming. The tier caps the grade available, which is why the Core or Extended decision is the first thing a coach examines, and it closes with the board's entry deadline rather than at the end of the course. Separately, the Ministry's British track counts five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education. Ask the school whether a tier change is still possible for the next series, and verify the university's own published entry requirements directly.

ib-igcse-coaching.closingHeading: Start with the paperwork, then book the hour
ib-igcse-coaching.closingBody: Before you compare coaches, collect four things: which authority licenses your child's school, which stream the mandatory UAE subjects put them in, which board and syllabus code appear on the statement of entry, and when that board closes entries for the next series. Those four facts turn a vague search for IB IGCSE coaching in the UAE into a specific request a specialist can answer properly. Send them to us and we will propose a coach for a free trial hour, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no card details taken. If we do not have the right specialist free, we will tell you that instead of offering a near match.

ib-igcse-home-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched to a syllabus code and a level rather than to a postcode. A Year 11 Cambridge 0620 candidate and a DP1 Chemistry Higher Level student in the same house need two different specialists, and on a video platform they can both have one on the same evening.

intro.heading: What a two-board household is really paying for
paragraphs: Most UAE families who search for IB IGCSE home tuition in the UAE are not buying one service. They are buying two, in the same month, often for two children. IGCSE support is short-horizon, code-specific work: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, a tiering decision, past papers marked against the right scheme. Diploma support runs for two years: Higher Level depth, an Internal Assessment with lettered criteria and fixed mark allocations, and a predicted grade that universities will read. One invoice, two completely different pieces of work.

The reason the compound search exists is structural. KHDA's 2024-25 figures put 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum taking 37 per cent of enrolment and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. A large share of UAE international schools teach IGCSE to the end of Year 11 and then offer the Diploma, so the same family often has one child finishing a Cambridge or Pearson series while another is three weeks into DP1. Two boards, one evening, one budget.

What that costs is answerable, and almost nobody answers it. Of the ranking pages surveyed for this cluster in October 2026, three published no price at all and the two that did quoted US dollars. So this page starts with the number. It sets out the AED bands the UAE market charges at each stage, names where each band comes from, and then explains the seven variables that decide where inside a band a particular quote lands. Those bands are the market's, not a price list of ours.

After the number comes the arithmetic that matters more: the five-year run from Year 10 through to DP2, year by year, with the point in each year where families reliably waste money. The commonest waste is not an expensive tutor. It is four hours a week in a subject the student was already passing, or a first session booked in April for a series that starts in May, or Extended material taught to a candidate entered for Core. Each of those three mistakes costs more than the gap between a mid-band tutor and a specialist one, and each is avoidable with a single question put to the school in writing.

One thing is fixed before you read further. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India. The home-tuition question is a fair one and it is answered honestly below, including what the UAE market charges for a tutor who drives to you and what that premium is paying for. The case for video is made on cost per learning hour, not on convenience.

A tutor travelling to a UAE address is priced at roughly AED 180-500 an hour once travel is absorbed
