process.title: Tell us the codes, not just the subjects
process.description: The first message that actually helps names the syllabus code for each child: 0580 Extended, 4PH1, Maths AA HL. Add the emirate and the school, because the authority above it tells us which calendar and which mandatory-subject rules you are working inside. Two children means two separate matches, and we will treat them separately from the start.

process.title: A diagnostic before a schedule
process.description: Each student gets one free 45-minute trial lesson, built around a past paper or a draft they bring. The tutor reports back on what is actually missing rather than on what the parent described. For a Year 11 heading into DP1 this is where the transition gap list comes from, subject by subject.

process.title: Confirm the tutor's permit position
process.description: Before teaching begins, tutors confirm their MoHRE private tuition work permit status and, where they teach in a UAE school, that your child is not enrolled there. ADEK's ethics rules and the permit's code of conduct both bar that arrangement, so we would rather lose a match than build one on it.

process.title: Fix the slots around the two calendars
process.description: One weekly slot per subject per child, on Gulf Standard Time, set against the school's internal coursework deadlines and the board's published entry dates. Sessions move by agreement when mocks, trips or Ramadan timing require it, including post-Iftar slots. Every session leaves an annotated document behind.

process.title: Review at the end of each term
process.description: We look at whether the hours are still earning their place. A transition block should end when the gap closes. A subject that has stabilised should drop to fortnightly or stop. The default in this market is to keep selling hours; the useful thing is to tell you when to stop buying them.

whyPoints.title: One tutor list, two specifications
whyPoints.description: Tutors name the codes they teach from, so a Cambridge 0620 candidate and a DP Chemistry HL candidate are matched to people who know the difference between descriptive organic chemistry and mechanism. The overlap between the boards is real but partial, and pretending otherwise is how a household ends up with one tutor doing half a job twice.

whyPoints.title: The regulatory detail written down, with sources
whyPoints.description: The regulator map, the permit rules, the mandatory-subject requirements and the equivalency thresholds on this page each carry the authority they came from. Where a figure has not been verified, this page says so and leaves the gap visible. That is a slower read than a confident number, and it is the only version worth planning around.

whyPoints.title: Online because the specialists are not local
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, which is how a family in Al Ain or Fujairah gets the same Higher Level specialist as a family in Jumeirah. It also means the hour you pay for is an hour of teaching rather than part of a commute. Visits to a student's address are offered only in India.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing produced that the student did not write. The boundary goes in writing before the first coursework session, for both the Diploma components and International GCSE coursework, because the risk of crossing it lands on the candidate and not on the tutor.

whyPoints.title: No accreditation we do not hold
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It is not approved, accredited or endorsed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, holds no UAE premises, and publishes no star rating it cannot evidence. The regulators are named on this page to explain the system, never to borrow their authority.

faqs.question: My daughter sits IGCSEs this year and her brother starts the IB Diploma next year — can one tutor cover both?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, within one subject, and it depends on the person rather than the subject. A Chemistry teacher who has taught both Cambridge 0620 and DP Chemistry knows that the organic chemistry at International GCSE is descriptive and the Diploma expects mechanism, and will teach them as two different courses. A tutor fluent in only one specification tends to import the wrong conventions, which costs marks in ways that look like carelessness. Across subjects you need separate matches. We would rather give you two tutors who each know one paper properly than one who is stretched across two.

faqs.question: Which UAE authority licenses a school that teaches both IGCSE and the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The authority for the emirate the school sits in, and it covers both programmes under the same licence. In Dubai that is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is the Department of Education and Knowledge. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Because one licence covers both programmes, the handover from Year 11 into Year 12 inside a single school is an internal matter with no regulator to appeal to.

faqs.question: Our school keeps mentioning an exam zone — what is that and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. In practice that means a timetable shared by a cousin abroad, or a screenshot circulating in a parents' group, is not a usable source. Ask the school's examinations officer which zone the centre is in and work from the timetable they give you.

faqs.question: Do the three Ministry subjects count towards my child's IGCSE or IB results?
faqs.answer: They are separate requirements, and they sit on the timetable regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are compulsory in Dubai private schools whichever curriculum is licensed, and the federal rule says private schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are specifically not counted among the five required GCSE or IGCSE subjects. So they are required at school and excluded from that count, which catches families by surprise.

faqs.question: How do I check that an online IB and IGCSE tutor holds a UAE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and ask what is written on it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system under the service Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Check that the name on the permit record matches the name on the tutor's Emirates ID, and if the tutor teaches in a UAE school, check which school is named. A tutor who will not discuss the permit has told you something.

faqs.question: My son's school is rated Outstanding — does that rating cover its IB Diploma teaching specifically?
faqs.answer: No. An inspection band describes the provision inspectors examined across the school at the phases they visited, against the framework in use. It does not resolve into a judgement on one subject at one level, which is usually the question a parent is really asking. Read the phase-by-phase breakdown to see whether secondary provision tracks the headline, read the teaching and assessment judgements for what they say about marking consistency, and read the recommendations, which name what the school has been asked to fix. Quote ratings only from the regulator's own site.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education count IGCSE Arabic towards the five subjects it requires?
faqs.answer: It does not. The published equivalency requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A student counting Arabic towards the total arrives one subject short. One page currently ranking for these searches tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, excluding those two. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before locking in Year 10 choices, because subject selection is hard to reverse later.

faqs.question: We are moving from Sharjah to Abu Dhabi mid-year — does the change of regulator affect anything for us?
faqs.answer: It changes who sits above the school and where a query goes. In Sharjah the Private Education Authority regulates private education and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. In Abu Dhabi the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of their own enrolled students. The examination board your child sits does not change with the emirate, but the fee-approval regime, the inspection framework and the escalation route all do. Ask the receiving school which entry point it is placing your child at.

faqs.question: Can my child's own schoolteacher tutor him privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No, and you should decline the offer if it is made. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. The conflict of interest is the point: the person teaching the class should not be paid separately to teach the same child the same content. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document, which is the authoritative source.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with an IGCSE coursework draft that they may not do with an IB Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Less than you might think, because both regimes end in the same requirement: the submitted work is the student's. For either, a tutor may teach the criteria, explain the marks attached to each, question a method and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. For neither may a tutor supply text, rewrite a section or hand over a finished piece. The practical difference is procedural. Diploma components run through the school's declaration and supervisor process, while International GCSE coursework and practical work are administered by the examination centre under the board's rules.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should my child take if the IB Diploma is the plan?
faqs.answer: Two separate questions sit inside that one. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 are required, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. For Diploma readiness, the subject list matters more than the count: a student intending Maths AA at Higher Level needs the Extended tier rather than Core, and a student heading for English A is better served by First Language English than by English as a Second Language. Decide the Diploma shape first, then count backwards.

faqs.question: Is there a UAE rule about how long a tutoring session should be?
faqs.answer: Not for private tutoring, but there is published guidance for the mandatory school subjects, and it is a useful reference point. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. For one-to-one online teaching, 60 minutes suits most secondary subjects and 45 minutes suits younger students or a focused Internal Assessment review. Longer blocks work for timed-paper practice and poorly for new content.

faqs.question: What happens to our lessons during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten, family routines shift, and evening availability changes rather than disappears. Sessions move by agreement, including to post-Iftar slots, and the rate does not change because the slot does. The planning point matters more than the timing: Ramadan often falls in the run-up to the spring and early-summer examination windows, so a revision plan built in January that ignores it will be rewritten in a hurry. Count the available weeks before the series your child is entered for, place the mock-review sessions outside Ramadan where possible, and keep the lighter consolidation work inside it.

faqs.question: No tutor covers the exact board and subject combination we need — what then?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with someone approximately qualified. For a niche combination — a Pearson 4CH1 candidate needing Higher Level-style extension work, or a Diploma subject with few UAE teachers — the match may take longer, or the available specialist may be based outside the UAE and teaching on Gulf Standard Time. Both are disclosed before you book. No competitor page we examined states a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE families to a non-UAE number without saying so, which is the version of this answer we are trying not to give.

faqs.question: Can you send us past papers and mark schemes for 0580 and the Diploma?
faqs.answer: No. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. A tutor should reference them and link the board's own page, and reproducing or redistributing them is copyright infringement, with an added malpractice exposure for anything unreleased. In a session a tutor works through a paper with your child and leaves an annotated shared document behind. If a tutor offers you a private library of mark schemes, treat that as information about how they operate rather than as a benefit.

faqs.question: Do IB and IGCSE students in the UAE get their results on the same day?
faqs.answer: No, and the gap between them can be weeks. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge's March 2027 series results are published on Direct on 13 May 2027 with certificates in late June. For the IB we publish no date at all: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so the session and results dates for your child's cohort should come from the school's IB coordinator and nowhere else.

ib-igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the codes and the emirate
ib-igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: Send us the syllabus code for each child, the school and the emirate. From that we can say which calendar you are working to, which mandatory subjects are already inside the school week, and which specialist fits the paper your child actually sits. Each student gets one free 45-minute trial lesson built around a past paper or a draft they bring, before any payment. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. If nobody on our list covers your combination, we will say so rather than fill the slot, and we will tell you what the wait looks like.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched by board, subject and level rather than by postcode, because the binding constraint in the UAE is specialist supply, not distance. Each one teaches the specification your child is actually entered for, and each one works to your school's own internal deadlines.

intro.heading: The rules sitting behind a private tutor in the UAE
paragraphs: Most searches for a private tutor end at price and availability. In the UAE, two further questions decide whether the arrangement is sound. The first is whether the person teaching your child is permitted to give paid private lessons at all: that permit is federal, issued by MoHRE, and it belongs to the individual rather than to any company. The second is which authority licensed your child's school, because that body approves the curriculum, the assessment methods and, in two emirates, the fees the school may charge.

Those two answers rarely come from the same place. Private schools in Dubai answer to KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah answers to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the Ministry of Education directly. Not one of those five bodies regulates an individual tutor. That sits with MoHRE, and the distinction is where most of the confusion on tutoring websites begins.

A household running both boards feels the system twice. A Year 10 child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel papers with codes printed on the entry sheet. A sibling in DP1 is working to Internal Assessment deadlines the school sets and an exam series the IB sets. The school owns the entry. The board owns the timetable. The Ministry decides later which certificates it recognises. A tutor who cannot say which of those three owns a given deadline will still give you confident advice, and it will be advice about the wrong one.

This page is written for the parent doing that checking. It sets out what the permit actually says and where to read it, what each regulator does and does not reach into, the KHDA rules governing Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies on your child's timetable, the five-subject rule reported for British-track equivalency, and the published market rates in AED so you can see where a quote sits. Every figure below carries the body or provider that published it and the month it was read. Where something is not verified, the page says so rather than printing a number.

One thing is stated up front, because it changes how you read the rest. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video. Home visits are part of our service in India only, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. The reason is specialist supply rather than convenience: the IB accounted for 7% of the Dubai private-school roll in 2024-25, so a Chemistry HL or Economics HL specialist is genuinely scarce, and matching by subject and level beats matching by driving distance.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.programmesIntro: Four programmes turn up in these households, often two at once. Each has its own assessment machinery and its own relationship with the UAE system: which authority licensed it, which Ministry subjects sit beside it, and what the certificate is worth when an equivalency file is eventually opened. The notes below are about that relationship rather than the brochure.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two different boards, often inside one school building. Cambridge IGCSE subjects carry four-digit codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics, with Core and Extended tiers in many subjects. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1 and runs some subjects modularly. The code on the entry sheet, not the subject name, decides which papers your child sits and which past material is relevant. A tutor who prepares a student against the wrong specification wastes a term, and neither of you finds out until a mock.
programmes.countryNote: UK curriculum schools took 37% of Dubai's private-school roll in 2024-25, the largest single share, so IGCSE tutor supply is the healthiest of any board in the country. That cuts both ways. The market is crowded with general IGCSE tutors and thin on people who can explain the difference between 0580 Extended and 4MA1 Higher Tier. Ask which code they have taught this academic year, and ask them to name the papers.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against four criteria per subject, each out of 8, and converts the total to a 1-7 grade using subject-specific boundaries. There is no external paper for most MYP students, so the mark that matters is the one a classroom teacher awards against a published criterion descriptor. Families moving from MYP 5 into DP1 often discover that five years of criterion-based marking taught the student a great deal about process and very little about sitting a timed paper under exam conditions.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai and Abu Dhabi IB schools run MYP through Year 11 instead of IGCSE, which creates a gap the equivalency route does not anticipate: there are no five IGCSE grades to count. Families planning a UAE university application from an MYP school should ask the school's coordinator what the file will actually show, and verify the position on moe.gov.ae before Year 11 options are locked.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Internal Assessments are marked by the school and moderated by the IB, so an IA mark is provisional until moderation is done. The HL and SL split changes paper count and component weighting rather than topic names, which is why a student who moves level mid-course usually needs the assessment structure retaught rather than the content. Most of the lost marks at HL are structural, not conceptual.
programmes.countryNote: The IB accounted for 7% of the Dubai private-school roll in 2024-25, and three of the seven new private schools opening for 2026-27 are IB schools, part of 16,846 new places announced for that intake. Demand for HL specialists in Chemistry, Physics, Economics and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is therefore rising faster than local supply, which is the practical argument for matching online.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examination. Progress is reported against transdisciplinary themes and learner-profile attributes, which parents often find hard to convert into a reading age or a maths level. Support at this stage is about building the number fluency and extended-writing stamina that MYP criteria will later assume, not about preparing for a paper that does not exist. The useful question for a PYP parent is what the child can do unaided, in writing, in twenty minutes.
programmes.countryNote: A PYP child in Dubai, Sharjah or Abu Dhabi also carries the Ministry subjects from the start of primary, with Arabic as a first or additional language depending on the group they are placed in. Early Arabic support is the most frequent request we see from UAE primary families, and the placement decision, Arab or non-Arab stream, determines which syllabus and which language of instruction applies.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.subjectsIntro: The IB Diploma subjects below are the ones UAE families ask for most. Each description names where marks are actually lost rather than restating the syllabus heading, because that is the information a parent cannot get from a school report. Every subject is taught against the current specification and the student's own school deadlines.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where most of the damage happens: algebraic manipulation that a graphic display calculator had been quietly hiding all year. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers and vectors. UAE engineering and medicine applicants are usually asked for AA rather than AI, so the route choice has consequences.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling carry the papers, and marks go on interpretation rather than algebra: stating what a correlation coefficient means in context, choosing the right test, justifying a model. HL financial mathematics and graph theory catch students who chose AI expecting a lighter course than AA.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics account for most lost marks at HL, and the extended-response questions reward structured reasoning rather than recall. The Internal Assessment most often fails on a research question that cannot be measured with the apparatus a school actually owns, which is a planning problem, not a chemistry one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Students who can solve the numerical question still lose the explanation marks, because command terms such as explain and justify expect a chain of causes written down in order. Electricity and fields are the recurring weak topics, and uncertainty treatment in the Internal Assessment is routinely underdone.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Marks sit in precise terminology and in data-based questions about unfamiliar experiments, which reward reading the axes before the question stem. HL option material is frequently taught last and revised least, and it shows in the Paper 3 mark.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides grades: axes labelled, equilibrium shifted the right way, welfare areas shaded and then referred to in the prose. HL Paper 3 quantitative questions are marked for method as well as answer, and the Internal Assessment commentaries need genuinely current articles with a clear syllabus link.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis is where most students underperform, because they summarise the text instead of arguing about its effect on a reader. The Individual Oral needs a defensible global issue and two extracts the student can say something structured about for ten minutes without notes.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application beats tool naming: a SWOT that leads to a decision earns marks that a labelled box never will. HL extension topics and the pre-released case study for Paper 1 reward planned preparation across months rather than a revision sprint in the final fortnight.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Object-oriented programming and the HL abstract data structures are the common failure points, along with pseudocode discipline under time pressure. The solution-development Internal Assessment needs a real client whose requirements can be evidenced, and students routinely arrange that client far too late.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic A
subjects.description: For Arabic B, marks go on productive range rather than comprehension; for Arabic A, on literary analysis in Standard Arabic. In the UAE this sits alongside the school's own mandatory Arabic provision, and the stream a child is placed in decides which syllabus and which language of instruction apply.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: IGCSE support here is organised by syllabus code, because one subject name hides two different sets of papers. Ask your child's school for the Cambridge IGCSE syllabus codes or the Pearson specification codes on the entry sheet before the first lesson. Tiering, practical assessment and grade ceiling all follow from that code.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 into Foundation and Higher Tier. The grade ceiling differs by tier, so tiering is an attainment decision with an administrative deadline attached rather than a matter of preference, and it is the school that submits it.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper rewards apparatus description, graph plotting and error reasoning, none of which is taught by reading the textbook again. Electricity and waves are the recurring weak topics, and Extended adds quantitative work on momentum and fields that Core candidates never meet.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Mole calculations and the organic families carry the Extended papers. Students who learned definitions by rote lose marks on the questions that ask for a test and its result, because both halves have to be stated to score, and only one half usually appears.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Terminology precision decides the grade more than content coverage does. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance diagrams are the standard losses, and Extended papers want the mechanism explained where Core papers accepted a description of what happens.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language (0500 / 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and the summary question are the most teachable gains available, because both are marked against stated criteria that most candidates have never actually read. Timing on the longer composition is the other common failure, and it is fixed by practice under the clock.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (0450 / 0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Case-study questions are marked for applied judgement rather than definitions. The highest-tariff questions ask for a recommendation with justification, and candidates who list advantages and disadvantages without choosing a side cap their own marks at the lower band.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.regionsTitle: The seven emirates, and who regulates schooling in each
ib-igcse-private-tutor.regionsIntro: Which emirate you live in changes who approves your child's curriculum, who publishes the inspection report and, in two cases, who signs off the fees. It does not change who regulates your tutor, because that is federal. The notes below are about the school system in each emirate, with the source named.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. It published 227 private schools and 387,441 students for 2024-25 across 17 curricula, and confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Press reporting also describes ADEK ethics rules barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school; the current wording should be checked against ADEK's own policy document.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits under ADEK alongside Abu Dhabi, so the same licensing and ethics framework applies. Families here ask about specialist supply more often than regulation: an Analysis and Approaches HL or Chemistry HL specialist is harder to find locally than in Dubai.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and, unusually, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval sitting with the emirate matters when a school changes board or adds a programme part-way through a cycle.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Ajman appears in almost no UAE tutoring content at all, which usually means families here are handed Dubai-shaped advice that does not match their own regulator.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A move from Dubai to RAK part-way through a year changes both the regulator and the approval route for a programme.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah
regions.note: Both are supervised by the Ministry of Education directly. School choice is narrower, so more families sit IGCSE subjects as private candidates or travel for a programme, which makes a tutor working online to the board's published timetable the practical option rather than the fallback.

schoolClusters.note: KHDA publishes an inspection report for each of these schools on its own site, and the rating you can read there is the only one worth quoting back at anyone. Students we support attend schools across this group, on both IB and IGCSE tracks, sometimes in the same family.

ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of these schools, and its reported ethics rules for school staff are the reason a parent should think twice before accepting private lessons from a teacher at their own child's school. Students we support attend schools across this group.

Here the regulator changes with the emirate: SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In two of those cases the authority also approves the programme and the fees.

modes.description: A concentrated block in the weeks before a Cambridge, Pearson or IB series, built around paper technique rather than new content. The published series dates decide when it starts: Cambridge's March 2027 series has an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, so a block aimed at that series begins in November, not January. Slots are not shared across siblings, because the boards are not the same and the papers are not the same.

sections.heading: What a UAE family is actually hiring when they hire a private tutor
paragraphs: A private tutor in the UAE is a person holding a permit in their own name. The federal route is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. It is not a company licence, not a teaching qualification and not a subject endorsement. A tutoring operation with premises and employed staff is a different legal animal altogether: that needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained in stages, with initial approval first and renewal requested annually before expiry.

So the phrase private tutor describes a legal arrangement rather than a standard of teaching. The eligible categories for the permit include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. A permit therefore tells you the arrangement is lawful. It tells you nothing at all about whether the person has taught Paper 2 of 0620 this year, or read an Internal Assessment against criterion wording. Those are separate questions, and only the second kind changes a grade.

An IB IGCSE private tutor in the UAE is usually being hired into a household running two assessment systems at once, which is why the question of who owns a deadline matters as much as who teaches the lesson. IB Gram matches your child to a specialist in their specification and level, and teaches one-to-one over live video. Home visits are part of our service in India only, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. What that buys is access to the right specialist rather than the nearest available adult, which is the real constraint in this market.

sections.heading: The private tuition work permit, line by line
paragraphs: The permit is documented in two places a parent can read without an intermediary. The u.ae work permits page sets out the legal basis, the eligible categories and the enforcement position. The MoHRE service page, titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, sets out the application route, lists no fee, and gives a completion time of two working days through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Two working days is the detail worth remembering, because it means a tutor who says the paperwork takes months is not describing this permit.

What the permit covers is the tutor, not the lesson format. Nothing in the published rules makes the permit conditional on teaching in a particular room, which is why a permitted tutor can teach over video. What the permit does carry is a code of conduct, and that code is reported to bar a permit holder from tutoring students affiliated with their own school. In Abu Dhabi the same ground is covered from the school's side: press reporting describes ADEK ethics rules preventing private and charter school staff from giving paid private lessons to students enrolled where they teach.

The enforcement position is stated and the penalty schedule is not. The official wording is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No figure is published alongside that sentence, so any specific amount you find quoted on a tutoring site or in a forum post is unverified. The honest answer to a parent asking what the fine is: the obligation is real, the number is not published, and the place to check is mohre.gov.ae rather than a tutoring advert.

sections.heading: Where each authority's remit stops, and who covers your tutor instead
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools across the seven emirates, and each one's remit stops at the school gate. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge does the same in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, provided they adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

Two of those authorities reach further than inspection. Sharjah's authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a materially different relationship from quality oversight: it means a school in those emirates cannot simply add a programme or change an assessment approach on its own timetable. For a family planning two years of support around a particular course, the question of whether a programme is approved to run at all is worth asking before the first tuition invoice.

None of the five regulates the individual teaching your child privately. That is MoHRE's permit, which is why no school regulator can vouch for a tutor and no tutor can borrow a school regulator's authority. The practical consequence is uncomfortable but useful: nobody inspects private tutoring the way KHDA inspects a school. There is no published band, no report and no rating to read. The checks therefore fall to you, and the next section sets out which of them can actually be completed from public sources.

sections.heading: KHDA does not approve private tutors, so what does that phrase on tutoring sites mean?
paragraphs: Three real approvals exist in this space, and tutoring marketing routinely blurs them into one. The first is the KHDA Educational Services Permit, issued to a training institute that has premises and staff in Dubai; it is granted in stages, with initial approval first, a window of up to six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. The second is KHDA approval held by school teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education, which schools are required to ensure for anyone teaching those subjects. The third is the MoHRE permit, held by an individual.

None of those three is a KHDA endorsement of a tutoring website, and none of them transfers. An institute's permit says nothing about the person who turns up on the call. A school teacher's subject approval belongs to that teacher inside that school. A MoHRE permit belongs to one individual and expires in two years. When a site tells you its tutors carry regulator backing, the useful reply is to ask which of the three it means, for which named person, and where the number can be checked. A straight answer arrives quickly; a vague one is itself the answer.

IB Gram's position is written down so it cannot drift. No UAE authority approves, licenses, accredits or endorses this platform, and no page of ours will imply one does. What we can evidence instead is narrower and more useful: which specification a tutor has taught this year, which levels, what they will show you in a trial lesson, and what they will refuse to do with assessed coursework. That is a smaller claim than regulator backing, and it is the one that survives being checked.

sections.heading: The checks a parent can make without taking anyone's word
paragraphs: Most tutoring claims are either publicly checkable or not claims at all. The permit is checkable by asking the tutor to show their own MoHRE permit record, since the permit is issued to them and costs them nothing to produce. A school's inspection outcome is checkable on the regulator's own site rather than in a provider's summary of it. Equivalency requirements are checkable on moe.gov.ae. A star rating published by a provider about itself is checkable nowhere, which is the point worth noticing about it.

Two claims deserve particular care because they are common and consequential. The first is examiner status. Current examining work is confidential and time-limited, and a provider that cannot evidence it for a named individual should not be describing anyone as an examiner, nor implying access to marking, boundaries or unreleased papers. The second is a school relationship. Supporting students who attend a school is ordinary; being a partner of that school is a specific arrangement with paperwork behind it. Lists of school logos under a heading about trust are usually the first kind described as the second.

The last check is the cheapest and the most revealing. Ask what the provider will not do. A straight answer about assessed coursework, about grade promises, and about what happens when no specialist is available tells you more about how an organisation behaves under pressure than any quantity of testimonial copy. A provider who has thought about those boundaries will answer in one sentence each. A provider who has not will change the subject to results.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: the content rule an outside tutor must obey
paragraphs: Whatever curriculum a Dubai private school is licensed to teach, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies sit on the timetable beside it. The KHDA mandatory subjects guidance sets this out as a requirement for all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with its requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For an IB or IGCSE family this is the part of the week nobody budgets tuition for, and the part most often misunderstood.

The placement rules are specific rather than general. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students. For non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies, the school's licensed-curriculum language applies.

The rule that catches outside tutors is about material, not timetabling. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor who arrives with their own worksheets for UAE Social Studies is working against that rule, however good the worksheets are. The defensible approach is to teach the student's own school material: the set texts, the school's assessment tasks, the vocabulary and script work the class is already doing, and the exam technique that sits around it.

sections.heading: Who owns which step of the exam year: the school, the board, or you
paragraphs: The single most expensive misunderstanding in an exam year is about ownership. A family can change almost nothing about an exam timetable and almost everything about preparation, yet most of the panic arrives over the parts they never controlled. Cambridge's own published key dates for the March 2027 series illustrate the arithmetic: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, while final entries are due 27 November 2026 and forecast grades 27 February 2027. The IGCSE exam entry deadline therefore falls more than two months before the first paper, and the school submits it.

There is a second administrative detail with real consequences. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used. The zone belongs to the centre, not the family, so the question to ask the exams officer is simply which zone the school is in and which timetable version the printed one at home corresponds to.

Results and appeals follow the board's own clock. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the IB, this page publishes no session or results date: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so those dates must come from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org directly.

sections.heading: Year 9 options, read against the Ministry of Education equivalency rule
paragraphs: Subject choices made at 13 or 14 decide what a Ministry of Education equivalency file can show at 18. As reported in July 2026, the British track requires a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. That is the rule an options sheet should be read against, before it is signed.

The detail that trips families up is what does not count. The same reporting states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A child taking exactly five subjects, two of which are Arabic and Islamic Education, can therefore pass all five and still not satisfy the count. At least one widely ranking tutoring page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the reported rule says; publishing the five-subject rule correctly, and telling you to verify it, is more useful than inheriting someone else's error.

Two further rows matter. On the American track, the reported requirements include English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold is published here at all, because none has been read on moe.gov.ae. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring platform performs or can promise; it is a Ministry process, and the Ministry is where it gets confirmed.

sections.heading: What private tuition costs beside a Dubai school fee that is not rising
paragraphs: Tuition spending is easier to judge next to the school fee it sits beside. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family whose largest education line is flat for a year, the question becomes what the discretionary line is worth, and that is a question the tutoring market mostly answers by refusing to publish a number at all.

Published market rates, read in October 2026, run across a wide band. Budget online tuition and university-student tutors appear from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor working online sits around AED 150 to AED 300. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists are advertised from about AED 200 to AED 450 and above, premium named tutors as high as AED 650, and an in-home visit including travel between roughly AED 180 and AED 500. Monthly packages seen include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published figures, not an IB Gram price list.

What moves a number inside that band is specificity, not branding. A generalist covering five subjects charges less than someone who teaches only Chemistry HL, and should. A private tutor in Dubai who can produce last year's 0620 Extended scripts and talk about where the marks went is pricing a different service from someone offering homework supervision. Our own position on price is deliberately not on this page: you get a free first session, then a consultation that quotes against the specification, the level and the hours actually needed.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and who actually signs the declaration
paragraphs: Every assessed component that leaves a school carries a declaration of authenticity, and the student's name is on it. For the IB, the school supervisor also signs to say the work is the student's own, which is why a supervisor asks to see drafts and asks questions about method. A paid tutor signs nothing, holds no part of that chain, and cannot transfer responsibility away from the student. That single structural fact is why coursework support has to be shaped as teaching rather than production, and it is a rule about consequences, not etiquette.

The academic honesty rules permit a great deal and forbid one thing. A tutor may teach the subject content an Internal Assessment needs, explain what a criterion is asking for in plain words, read a student's own draft and say where it is unclear, show how data should be treated, demonstrate referencing, and run the student through viva-style questions a supervisor might ask. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a section into its final form, source and structure an argument on the student's behalf, or hand over material a student then presents as their own thinking.

This market contains providers that cross that line and advertise it as a service, complete with a price. The consequence of buying it does not land on the provider. It lands on a student whose diploma is at risk, in a process the family cannot appeal on grounds of having paid for help. So the position here is stated in the open: no assessed component is written, completed or rewritten by anyone working through IB Gram, and a tutor who is asked to do it says no and tells us. Families who want that service are better served elsewhere, and we would rather lose the booking.

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: The first thing we ask for is the specification each child is entered for: 0580 or 4MA1, HL or SL, Core or Extended. It is printed on the entry sheet or the school's subject letter. Matching on a subject name alone is how a student ends up well prepared for the wrong papers, and nobody notices until a mock.

process.title: A free first session, and the condition attached to it
process.description: The first 30-minute session is free, once per student, and no card details are taken to book it. It is a working lesson rather than a sales call: the tutor teaches something, then tells you what they found. If the match is wrong, say so and we match again at no cost to you.

process.title: A plan counted backwards from published dates
process.description: You get a plan built backwards from dates the board has published, not from a generic term structure. Where a date is not published or not verified, and every IB session date falls into that category here, the plan says so and points you at your school's IB coordinator rather than guessing.

process.title: Written feedback after every session
process.description: Notes go out after each lesson: what was taught, what the student got wrong, what to do before the next slot. Parents read the same notes the tutor keeps. Progress is reported against the school's own marking criteria rather than a score we invented for the purpose.

process.title: What we say when nobody is free
process.description: Some subject and level combinations have thin coverage, HL sciences in particular. When no specialist is free at the time you want, we tell you the likely wait instead of filling the slot with a generalist, and you decide. Asking for the code up front is what makes that disclosure possible early.

whyPoints.title: Sources, not assertions
whyPoints.description: Every regulator rule, permit detail and AED band on this page is attributed to the body or provider that published it, with the month it was read. Where a figure is unverified, including IB session dates and any Diploma points threshold for equivalency, the page says so rather than printing a number that looks authoritative.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the specification
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to the code on the entry sheet and the level, so the papers they prepare for are the papers your child sits. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are treated as different qualifications here, because they are: different codes, different tiering, different practical arrangements.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches, reads and gives feedback on work the student produced. No assessed component is drafted, completed or rewritten by a tutor. We publish that because the alternative is sold openly in this market, and a parent deserves to know which kind of provider they are talking to.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that matches the UAE week
whyPoints.description: Lessons sit in Gulf Standard Time around school hours, prayer times, Eid and the Ramadan timetable, with post-Iftar slots available. Families who travel between the UAE and abroad keep the same tutor and move the slot rather than starting again with someone new.

whyPoints.title: No regulator is claimed as a sponsor
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education and MoHRE are described on this page because they shape your options. Not one of them approves, licenses or endorses this platform, and no page of ours will suggest otherwise. What we claim instead is checkable in a trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor teaching my child in the UAE need a permit, and what should I ask to see?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a MoHRE work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is issued to the individual, granted free of charge for two years, and applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. Because it belongs to the tutor personally and costs them nothing, asking to see their own permit record is a reasonable request and an easy one to meet. A tutor who cannot produce it, or who describes a long and expensive licensing process instead, is not describing this permit.

faqs.question: KHDA does not approve individual tutors, so what are tutoring websites referring to?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three different things. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes that have premises and staff in Dubai, granted in stages and renewed annually. Schools must separately ensure that their own teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. And MoHRE issues the private tuition permit to individuals. None of the three is a regulator endorsement of a tutoring website, and none of them transfers to whoever joins your video call. Ask which one is meant, for which named person, and where the reference can be checked.

faqs.question: Can a teacher at my child's own school take them for paid private lessons?
faqs.answer: Treat that offer with caution. Press reporting describes ADEK ethics rules preventing private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. The current wording should be checked against ADEK's own policy document rather than a news summary. Beyond the rules, there is a plainer problem: the person teaching the class, setting the assessment and being paid privately for the same content is holding three roles that conflict.

faqs.question: Does the private tuition permit still apply when the lessons happen over video?
faqs.answer: The permit attaches to the tutor rather than to the room. Nothing in the published rules makes it conditional on teaching in person, which is why a permitted tutor can teach online. What does follow the tutor into a video lesson is the code of conduct attached to the permit, including the restriction reported around students affiliated with their own school. For a parent the useful consequence is that the permit question and the delivery question are separate: ask about the permit, then ask separately how the lesson is actually taught and what the student writes on.

faqs.question: How long is the MoHRE private tuition work permit valid, and what does it cost the tutor?
faqs.answer: The published position is that the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. The MoHRE service page for it lists no fees and gives a completion time of two working days, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Two points follow. A tutor who adds a permit fee to your invoice has the position wrong, because there is no fee to pass on. And a two-year validity means a permit shown to you can be out of date, so the issue date is worth a glance alongside the name.

faqs.question: Can a university student in Dubai hold the same tutoring permit as a qualified teacher?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the most useful thing to understand about the permit. The eligible categories published on u.ae include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. A permit therefore confirms that the arrangement is lawful. It says nothing about subject depth, exam-board familiarity or experience of marking. Those have to be checked separately, which is why the question that actually predicts a grade is which specification and level the tutor has taught this year.

faqs.question: Do the five IGCSE subjects counted for Ministry equivalency have to include Arabic?
faqs.answer: Reporting from July 2026 states the opposite: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. The British-track requirement reported is a pass in five accredited subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. The practical risk is a child entered for exactly five subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before options are signed, because this is reported guidance rather than a Ministry page.

faqs.question: Why can't my child's Arabic and Islamic Education classes be combined with the other group?
faqs.answer: Because the two groups are following different curricula in different languages. The KHDA mandatory subjects guidance requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arab students follow the school's licensed-curriculum language. Knowing which stream your child sits in decides which syllabus any outside support should follow.

faqs.question: May an outside tutor use their own worksheets for UAE Social Studies?
faqs.answer: They should not. The KHDA mandatory subjects guidance states that for these subjects the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. That makes an imported worksheet pack a problem regardless of its quality. The defensible approach is to work from the school's own material: the set content, the school's assessment tasks, the vocabulary and script practice the class is already doing, and the technique that sits around them. If a tutor offers you their own Social Studies curriculum, that is a reason to ask more questions, not fewer.

faqs.question: Who decides whether my child is entered for IGCSE Core or Extended?
faqs.answer: The school decides and submits the entry, because the school is the exam centre. What a family controls is the evidence brought to that conversation and the timing of it. Tiering sets a grade ceiling, so a capable candidate entered at the lower tier cannot reach the top grades however well they perform on the day. Bring mock scripts rather than impressions, and raise it before the centre's internal cut-off, which sits ahead of the board's own final entry date. For Cambridge's published March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 against an exam period beginning 3 February 2027.

faqs.question: Our exam timetable has a zone number printed on it - does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used. The zone belongs to the centre, so ask the exams officer which zone the school sits in, then check that the printed timetable at home is that version. It is a two-minute question that removes one of the few genuinely unrecoverable errors in an exam year.

faqs.question: We are moving from Dubai to Ras Al Khaimah mid-year - which authority takes over?
faqs.answer: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah, so oversight passes from KHDA to it. The difference is not only the name on the inspection report. Ras Al Khaimah's authority, like the Sharjah Private Education Authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a wider remit than quality oversight alone. For a mid-year move, ask the receiving school which programmes it is approved to run at your child's year group, and confirm how coursework already completed and any exam entries already submitted will be carried across.

faqs.question: What may a paid tutor do with an Internal Assessment draft, and where is the line?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the content the work needs, explain what a criterion is asking for, read the student's own draft and say where it is unclear or unsupported, show how data should be handled, demonstrate referencing, and ask the viva-style questions a supervisor might ask. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a section into final form, build the argument on the student's behalf, or hand over material the student then presents as their own. The school supervisor signs the authenticity declaration and the student's name is on it, so the responsibility never moves to the tutor.

faqs.question: Does Dubai's school-fee freeze for 2026-27 change what private tuition costs?
faqs.answer: Not directly, because the two are set by different people. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Tuition rates are set provider by provider and move with demand, particularly in the weeks before a series. What the freeze does change is the comparison: with the largest education line flat for a year, the discretionary line is easier to judge, and a published, sourced rate band is easier to argue with than a vague quote.

faqs.question: Nobody was available for my son's HL option subject last year - how is that handled now?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Coverage is thinnest in HL sciences and in the less common language and option combinations, and it tightens further in the weeks before a series. When nobody suitable is free at the time you want, you get the likely wait and the alternatives: a different weekly slot, a different start date, or a narrower piece of work with someone who covers part of the requirement. An IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi for a mainstream subject is usually quick; a Diploma HL option subject at 5pm on a Tuesday may not be.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take an IGCSE sibling and a Diploma sibling in the same week?
faqs.answer: Sometimes within a single subject area, but we do not treat it as the default. An IB Diploma tutor in the UAE teaching Chemistry HL and a specialist in Cambridge 0620 Extended are doing related but different jobs, with different papers, different mark schemes and different internal deadlines. Where one person genuinely covers both, we will say so. Otherwise the household gets two specialists on one shared schedule, with one point of contact and one monthly summary, so nobody is reconciling two providers against two exam calendars every term.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the code on the entry sheet
ib-igcse-private-tutor.closingBody: If one thing from this page is worth keeping, make it the first question: which specification is my child entered for, and who owns the next deadline on it? With that answer, matching takes less guessing and a plan can be counted backwards from a date somebody has actually published. Tell us the board, the subject codes and the level for each child in the house, and we will tell you who is free, when, and what we cannot cover. The first 30-minute session is free, once per student, with no card details taken, and lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Distance is the one variable that stopped mattering
paragraphs: A parent typing IB IGCSE tuition near me is usually answering a practical question: who can reach us, and when. That question made sense in 2015, when a tutor's reach was the radius of a car journey after Maghrib. It makes much less sense now. The binding constraint on a UAE tutoring plan is not kilometres. It is the date printed on an examination timetable, and the number of teaching weeks left between tonight and that date. Those weeks are the resource that runs out.

This page is built on that arithmetic. It sets out the IGCSE and IB Diploma years as two calendars that share one household, names the entry deadlines and results dates the boards themselves publish, and counts backwards from each of them. Where a date is sourced, the source is named. Where a date is not verifiable, the page says so rather than inventing one, because a wrong date on a revision plan costs a family far more than a missing one.

The delivery model is simple and worth stating before anything else. IB Gram matches students to specialist tutors and lessons run one-to-one over live video. Home visits are part of what IB Gram offers in India; they are not offered anywhere in the Emirates. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation. A family in Al Reef looking for a Chemistry HL specialist should not be restricted to the handful of people who happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of Al Reef.

There is a second reason the online format suits this particular search. Most UAE households running both boards at once need two tutors on two different timetables, often for two children with different school-day end times. Matching that by geography means compromising on subject depth. Matching it by syllabus and by available slot means the Year 11 Cambridge Physics hour and the DP2 Maths Analysis hour can sit in the same evening without anyone getting into a car.

What follows is organised as a countdown rather than a brochure. The series tables come first, then the handover between IGCSE results and the first Diploma year, then the daily clock, the market rates other providers publish in AED, the coursework ceilings and who owns each internal deadline, the examination-zone trap that catches private candidates, and the Ministry of Education equivalency file that should be opened before results day rather than after it.

One more thing is worth saying at the top, because it shapes every number below. The rates quoted on this page are what other UAE providers have published, each attributed and dated. They are not IB Gram's price list. A figure quoted before anyone knows the subject, the level, the board and how many teaching weeks remain is a guess with a currency symbol in front of it, and a family comparing quotes deserves a reference band rather than a sales number.
