faqs.question: What is the IB mathematical exploration and how is it different from a written paper?
faqs.answer: The exploration is an individual piece of written mathematics, 12 to 20 pages long, that every DP maths student produces in both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, at SL and HL. It is worth 20 per cent of the subject grade, marked out of 20 by the class teacher against five criteria, then moderated by the IB. A written paper tests technique under time pressure against a mark scheme. The exploration tests whether a student can choose a mathematical question, develop it correctly, communicate it clearly and reflect on what the result does and does not show. No amount of past-paper practice improves it.

faqs.question: How long is the maths exploration allowed to be?
faqs.answer: The IB gives a page range rather than a word count for mathematics: 12 to 20 pages, including graphs, tables and diagrams. That differs from the Extended Essay, which has a 4,000-word limit, and from several science internal assessments, which have word ceilings. The maths IA page limit is not a target to reach; a tight 13-page exploration with real mathematics in it scores better than a 20-page one padded with background and screenshots. If a document is running long, the usual cause is material that belongs in an appendix or does not belong at all, and criterion A rewards conciseness directly.

faqs.question: Which of the five IB maths IA criteria is hardest to score well on?
faqs.answer: Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six marks and is the hardest to recover, because it is largely decided by the topic. Mathematics has to be relevant and commensurate with the level sat, so an HL student whose topic cannot carry HL content has capped the mark before writing begins. Criteria C and D, personal engagement and reflection, carry three marks each and are the most commonly left near-empty, particularly by students who transferred from systems that never asked for either. Those two are usually the cheapest marks to recover late, because they need thinking rather than new mathematics.

faqs.question: My son has chosen a topic but there is no mathematics in it yet. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Treat that as the normal starting position rather than a problem. Most topics arrive as an interest, not as a question, and the work of the first session is turning it into something with a calculation at the centre. A tutor asks what would have to be measured, modelled or derived for the topic to produce a result, and whether the mathematics that requires sits inside the course at the level sat. If it does not, the topic gets narrowed or swapped while that is still cheap. Doing this before any writing is the single highest-value hour in the whole process.

faqs.question: How many marks does personal engagement carry, and what actually earns them?
faqs.answer: Personal engagement is criterion C and carries three of the 20 marks. It is not a statement that the student finds the topic interesting, which is what most first drafts offer. It credits evidence that the student made decisions and acted on them: choosing this data rather than that, trying an approach that failed and changing it, collecting something themselves, adapting a standard method to their own question. The marks come from visible decisions inside the mathematics, not from a paragraph of enthusiasm at the start. A tutor can teach a student to notice and record those decisions, but cannot manufacture them afterwards.

faqs.question: Our school allows one draft to be reviewed. What may a tutor say about it?
faqs.answer: Anything that is feedback rather than production. A tutor can say that criterion B is losing marks because variables are never defined, that the conclusion does not answer the stated aim, that the reflection sits in one paragraph at the end instead of where the results arrive, or that the central calculation is correct but unexplained. What a tutor cannot do is supply replacement wording, correct the document line by line, or hand over a version to be copied. The submitted text has to be the student's own, and the student signs a declaration to that effect before it goes anywhere.

faqs.question: Is a spreadsheet regression enough mathematics for Analysis and Approaches HL?
faqs.answer: On its own, no. Criterion E asks whether the mathematics is commensurate with the level of the course, and a regression line produced by software is below what Analysis and Approaches HL covers, however accurately it is presented. It could be a legitimate starting point if the exploration then develops the underlying mathematics: deriving the least-squares result, examining the assumptions, extending to a model the software does not fit. For Applications and Interpretation the same regression can sit much closer to the centre of the work, provided the interpretation and the critique of fit are genuinely present.

faqs.question: Can an exploration topic be about something local to the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and local data often produces a stronger exploration than a borrowed international data set, because the student can explain where the numbers came from and what their limits are. Metro ridership patterns, summer temperature and humidity series, school-run traffic timings, residential service charges, desalination volumes and prayer-time variation across the year have all carried real mathematics. What matters is not the subject matter but whether the data supports mathematics at the level sat, and whether the student can say why they chose this question. Novelty earns nothing by itself under any of the five criteria.

faqs.question: How many sessions does exploration support usually take?
faqs.answer: Four to six, in most cases, spread across the weeks the school's internal dates define rather than booked evenly. Session one tests the topic against criterion E and the level sat. Session two fixes the mathematics the topic needs. The remaining sessions work through the criteria as the document grows, and the last one is a read-back before the school's final date. A student who already has a near-complete document may need only one or two sessions, and a student with no topic in DP2 may need more. A tutor should tell you the expected number before the block starts.

faqs.question: What does the authenticity declaration my daughter signs actually commit her to?
faqs.answer: It commits her to the statement that the work submitted is her own and that any material from other sources is acknowledged. In practice that means every line of mathematics and every sentence of commentary originated with her, sources are referenced, and no part of the text was supplied by anyone else. Teaching, questioning and feedback on her own work sit inside that; receiving wording to paste in does not. The consequence of a false declaration falls on the student, which is why we will not provide text for submission however the request is framed, and why we say so before a family books.

faqs.question: Does the mark my child's teacher gives for the exploration stand as the final one?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. The class teacher marks the exploration against the five criteria, and the IB moderates by sampling work from the cohort. Moderation can move a cohort's marks up or down where the school's marking has been generous or severe relative to the standard. That has two consequences for families. First, a mark reported at school is provisional until the session results are issued. Second, arguing about a single mark with the teacher is rarely useful; the better use of time before the internal deadline is making sure each criterion has something in it to credit.

faqs.question: We are in Sharjah and the school has no DP maths specialist free. What are the options?
faqs.answer: This is common outside Dubai and more common again in Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain, where DP cohorts are small. Because every UAE session runs over live video, the match does not depend on who lives nearby: a Sharjah student taking Applications and Interpretation HL can work with a tutor who has marked AI HL explorations wherever that person is based. Where nobody in the exact route and level is free in the window you need, we say so rather than substituting a tutor who teaches the other course, and we give you the earliest date we can genuinely cover.

faqs.question: Does the exploration mark matter for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not as a separate item. Equivalency looks at the qualification and its grades, and the exploration mark is scaled into the subject grade rather than reported on its own. The British-track requirements are published: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. No IB points threshold has been read on an official Ministry source, so none is quoted here. Check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation channel directly, and note that equivalency is a government process no tutoring provider performs or guarantees.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the exploration timetable in a UAE school?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten during Ramadan and the rhythm of the day moves, so the hours a student expected to use for writing often are not there. Sessions move to the post-Iftar evening, which suits exploration work better than new syllabus content: reading a draft, fixing notation and building reflection hold up well in a late slot. The planning point is earlier than Ramadan itself. If your school's draft or final date falls close to it, the writing has to be substantially done before the month starts, and that is worth confirming with the DP coordinator in advance rather than discovering in week two.

faqs.question: How does one-to-one video work for an exploration full of graphs and working?
faqs.answer: The document and the files are the lesson, so a shared screen is the natural way to work on them. The student opens the write-up alongside the graphing file or spreadsheet and the tutor annotates while reading, which is easier than two people leaning over one laptop. Handwritten working is joined by pointing a phone camera at the page or photographing it before the session, and many DP students already write directly into a tablet. Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the UAE school week, and each one ends with a written note of the next step for the student.

ib-math-ia-help.closingHeading: Start with the topic, not the deadline
ib-math-ia-help.closingBody: If your child is in DP1 and a topic is due, that is the hour worth buying: a session that tests whether the question can carry 20 marks at the level they sit changes what the final mark can be. If the deadline is close and a document already exists, a criterion read-back will tell you honestly which marks are still in reach and which are not. Either way the first lesson is free, no card details are taken, and we will tell you the number of sessions we think it needs before you commit to any of them. Send the route, the level, the school and whatever internal dates you have.

intro.heading: The May session is fixed; everything around it in the UAE is not
paragraphs: IB May session exam preparation in the UAE sits between two calendars that were never designed to meet. One belongs to the IB: internally assessed components finished and submitted months ahead, then a fixed window of written papers, then results. The other belongs to your child's school and to the authority that licenses it — the Knowledge and Human Development Authority in Dubai, the Department of Education and Knowledge in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those bodies decide term dates, mandatory lessons and fee approvals. Not one of them decides an exam date.

That split is what most families discover late. A regulator approves curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods inside a school, and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah it approves tuition fees as well. None of them marks a Paper 2, moves a submission deadline or publishes a grade boundary. A revision plan built on the school term calendar, or on an inspection band, will therefore miss the dates that actually decide the grade. The plan that works runs on the IB's clock while respecting the constraints the emirate imposes: mandatory subject minutes that do not pause for revision, Ramadan falling inside the final stretch, and a school year that in some UAE schools does not begin in September at all.

Scale matters here too. Dubai alone had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment against 37% for UK curricula and 26% for Indian ones. Seven new private schools join Dubai's 2026-27 intake — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — adding 16,846 places after a 6% rise in enrolment during 2025-26. A Diploma cohort is a minority inside a very large private-school market, which is exactly why a Higher Level specialist for a narrow subject is harder to find locally than a general maths tutor, and why online matching changes the arithmetic.

IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform, not a school and not a tuition centre. Support for families in the UAE is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around school hours, prayer times and, during Ramadan, around Iftar. Home visits are something we arrange only in India; nobody is sent to an address in the Emirates. For a May candidate that model is usually the stronger one anyway, because it decouples the choice of tutor from the drive time between their building and yours.

This page is built around the system your family has to work inside: which authority answers for your school, which lessons the Ministry requires alongside the Diploma, who is legally permitted to coach your child, what the market charges in the final term, and what paperwork begins only after results arrive. It does not publish an IB exam or results date. The IB sets those, they can be revised, and the reliable source is your school's Diploma coordinator or ibo.org — not a tutoring page. Cambridge and Pearson dates quoted below are taken from each board's own published key-dates documents and attributed.

ib-may-session-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: Four IB programmes run in UAE schools, and only one of them ends in the May written session. Knowing which one your child is in decides whether exam preparation means papers and timed practice, or whether it means project criteria, portfolios and the transition into the Diploma two years early.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internally assessed component finished well before the papers, and most carry two or three external papers in the May window. The final score runs to 45 points, 42 from subjects and up to 3 from the core.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma cohorts overwhelmingly sit the May session because the local academic year ends in June or July, so the papers land in the final term rather than in the middle of one. That is also the term in which mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons continue under KHDA rules, so the revision week a family imagines is usually shorter than the one the timetable allows.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of 8 per criterion, with no external written session in most UAE schools. The Personal Project in the final year is the assessed piece families worry about most. Results are reported on a 1-7 scale derived from criterion totals rather than from papers.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP student in a UAE school has no May session to prepare for, but the year 11 cohort is choosing Diploma subjects in the same months the year 13 cohort sits papers. Getting Maths Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation right at that point removes most of the Higher Level crisis two years later, and it is the cheapest intervention on this page.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no graded external assessment, finishing in the Year 6 exhibition. Reporting is descriptive rather than numerical, which makes it hard for families to see where a child sits against a standard. The useful signals are reading fluency, number facts and written structure.
programmes.countryNote: PYP families in the UAE meet the mandatory-subject rules earliest: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies run alongside the programme from the start, in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Support at this stage is about literacy and number security, not exam technique, and no May session applies.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller cohort studying at least two Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and a language development component. The Diploma courses are externally assessed in the same sessions as full Diploma subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Where a UAE school offers the Career-related Programme, candidates sit the same May papers for their Diploma courses as full Diploma students, which surprises families who assumed the route was entirely internal. For Ministry of Education equivalency purposes, treat the certificate as something to verify directly with the attestation authority rather than assuming parity with the full Diploma.

ib-may-session-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: Subject choice decides where final-term hours earn marks. The notes below describe what each course actually assesses and the point at which UAE candidates most often lose marks, so you can decide which two subjects deserve the hours rather than spreading them across six.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with Higher Level adding a third paper of extended problem solving. Marks go on unjustified steps and on method marks never claimed because working was done mentally. Candidates who moved from MYP without an algebra rebuild lose most in the non-calculator paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy problem solving. The calculator is central, and marks are lost by reporting an answer without the model, the units or the degree of accuracy asked for. Higher Level adds significant statistical inference that is often met for the first time weeks before the papers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity, fields and nuclear physics, with a data and experimental strand running through the papers. The recurring loss is explanation questions answered with a formula instead of a causal chain, and graph questions where gradients are quoted without units.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Organic chemistry at Higher Level is where UAE candidates most often stall, because mechanisms must be reproduced rather than recognised. Multiple-choice paper marks depend on arithmetic discipline under time pressure.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, molecular biology, genetics, ecology, physiology and the Higher Level extensions. Content volume is the trap rather than difficulty: marks are lost on command terms, where a question asking for an outline is answered with a description and the mark scheme's required points never appear.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with diagram accuracy carrying marks in every paper. Higher Level adds quantitative questions and a policy paper that rewards evaluation over description. Candidates lose marks by drawing a diagram and never referring to it in the written answer.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, marketing, operations and finance, with a pre-released case study for the externally assessed paper. The habitual loss is tool-dropping: naming a framework without applying it to the stimulus, and answering evaluation questions with a list of advantages and disadvantages.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis, a comparative essay on studied works and an individual oral built on a global issue. Marks are lost in the unseen paper when a candidate summarises content instead of analysing how meaning is constructed through structure, register and form.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Arabic runs both as a Diploma language option and as a Ministry-mandated subject in UAE schools, and those are different courses with different expectations. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects and a prescribed-title essay, graded A to E and contributing with the Extended Essay to the bonus points. A grade E in either core component is a failing condition for the Diploma, which makes it the highest-leverage small piece of work in the programme.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay in a chosen subject, supervised inside the school and assessed externally. It must be the candidate's own work from the first research question to final submission; a tutor's role is questioning, method coaching and feedback on the student's draft.

ib-may-session-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: Which authority answers for your child's school changes the paperwork, the inspection language and the person you escalate to — and it does not change the exam at all. The notes below set out what each emirate's position means for a family preparing for the May session.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, publishes the mandatory-subject requirements and confirmed no private school fee increase for 2026-27. IB Diploma exam preparation in Dubai still runs on the IB's own submission and paper windows, not on KHDA's calendar.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Families booking an online IB tutor in Abu Dhabi should read that rule before asking a class teacher for help.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits under the same Abu Dhabi authority as the capital, so the licensing position and the staff ethics rules are identical. The practical difference is supply: fewer IB World Schools means fewer local Higher Level specialists, and a live-video slot is often the only way to reach one for a narrow subject.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone, and it is worth knowing when a school changes a course offering mid-programme for a cohort already entered for the May session.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah returned zero mentions across every competitor page researched for this project, which tells you how thinly the northern emirates are served by tutoring content.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, so escalation runs to the Ministry rather than to an emirate-level authority. For a Diploma family this mostly matters for equivalency and attestation enquiries, which are federal in any case and start only once certificates are issued.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools also sit under the federal Ministry of Education. Distance from the Dubai and Abu Dhabi school clusters makes a tutor travelling to an address impractical even where a family wants it, which is why one-to-one lessons over live video are the realistic route to a subject specialist here.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Umm Al Quwain completes the federal Ministry of Education group alongside Ajman and Fujairah. The regulator map for UAE private schools is therefore five bodies, not seven, and a page that names only KHDA has described Dubai rather than the country.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's Diploma cohort is spread across schools in Emirates Hills, Al Barsha, Dubai Festival City, Mirdif and the Jumeirah corridor, all licensed by KHDA. Students we support sit the May session from these schools; a tutor working with them uses the school's own internal deadlines rather than a generic revision calendar.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain IB World Schools
schoolClusters.note: The capital's Diploma schools cluster around Khalifa City, Al Bateen, Al Raha and Saadiyat, all licensed by ADEK. Students we support attend schools in this group, and the ADEK ethics position on staff tutoring their own students is the single most useful thing a capital family can know before the final term.

IB provision thins quickly north of Dubai, with SPEA licensing Sharjah's private schools and the federal Ministry of Education covering Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families here often travel into Dubai for school, which is why an evening live-video slot usually beats any arrangement involving a second commute.

ib-may-session-exam-preparation.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named here as context for the UAE system and the students we support; no affiliation, endorsement or partnership with any school or school group is implied.
ib-may-session-exam-preparation.modesIntro: Three formats carry almost all final-term work, and the right one depends on how many weeks remain and whether the problem is content, technique or confidence. All three are delivered one-to-one over live video at a Gulf Standard Time slot.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the final two terms
modes.description: One or two sessions a week per subject, following the school's own scheme of work, with timed questions set between lessons. This is the format that fixes content gaps, because it gives a week between diagnosis and the next check. It is also the cheapest per mark gained, since nothing has to be re-taught twice under pressure.
bullets: Session notes after every lesson naming what was tested and what was missed
Timed question sets drawn from the student's own subject guide, not a generic pack
Pacing anchored to the school's internal submission dates
Slot held weekly in Gulf Standard Time so it survives a busy term

modes.title: Paper-by-paper intensive block
modes.description: A fixed block of hours bought for one subject in the weeks before the papers, organised by paper rather than by topic. The hours go on technique: command terms, mark-scheme language, time per mark and the specific question types that have been costing marks. Useful when content is broadly known and execution is not.
bullets: Each session built on one paper format and its mark allocation
Full past-paper sections attempted under timed conditions, then marked with the student
A written list of recurring error types, carried from session to session
Quoted as a block of hours so the family can see the total before committing

modes.title: Core and internal-component review clinic
modes.description: Short sessions on Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and subject internal assessments, where the work is the student's and the tutor's job is questioning and feedback. Because a grade E in a core component is a failing condition for the Diploma, a handful of hours here can protect more than a term of subject revision.
bullets: Feedback on the student's own draft, in their words, never rewritten by the tutor
Criterion-by-criterion reading so the student can see where marks sit
Research-question and method coaching before the writing begins
A clear record of what was discussed, available if the coordinator asks

sections.heading: What the May session actually is, and why a UAE cohort sits it
paragraphs: The May session is the IB's main examination series, and it is the one almost every UAE Diploma cohort sits, because the local academic year ends in June or July. That timing puts the written papers in the final term rather than the middle of one, which is convenient for the school and brutal for revision, since the same weeks carry mandatory lessons, end-of-year school business and, in most years, Ramadan. A session is not only the papers. It includes internally assessed components submitted and uploaded by the school weeks or months earlier, the core components, and the entry itself, which is filed by the school's Diploma coordinator rather than by the family.

That last point is where families lose control without realising it. Nobody at home submits an entry, changes a level from Higher to Standard or registers a subject. The coordinator does, within windows the IB sets, and once a level change window has closed it has closed. The single most valuable email a parent can send in the autumn term is a short one asking the coordinator to confirm, in writing, the school's internal deadlines for every internally assessed component, the date by which a level change must be requested, and the school's own mock window. Those three facts turn a vague plan into a dated one.

A smaller group sits the November session instead, usually retake candidates or students at schools on a different year pattern. Retaking is a real route rather than a failure, but it is a separate registration with its own deadline, and the decision is better made with the coordinator in the days after results than left for a month. This page does not publish IB session or results dates. The IB sets them, they can be revised, and the only sources worth trusting are your coordinator or ibo.org.

sections.heading: Which authority answers for your school, and what it does not control
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools across the seven emirates. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education plays a supervisory role in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits at emirate level there.

What none of them does is run the assessment. The IB sets the submission windows, writes the papers, marks the externally assessed components, moderates the internal ones and publishes the results. An emirate authority can license a school, inspect it, approve its fee and require subjects alongside the licensed curriculum. It cannot move a deadline your child has missed, re-mark a paper or tell you what a grade boundary will be. Treating the regulator as the escalation route for an assessment problem wastes the two weeks in which something could still have been done inside the school.

Where the regulator does matter for exam preparation is in everything surrounding the papers: the term calendar, the mandatory lessons that keep running, the staff conduct rules that decide who may coach your child privately, and the inspection report that tells you something about the school without telling you anything about your candidate. Read the report for what it is, a school-level judgement published in a particular year, and then ask subject-level questions of the department. The table below separates the two jurisdictions so nothing is escalated to the wrong desk.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects and the minutes they take out of a revision week
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Diploma family that is not a footnote. These lessons continue through the exam term, they sit inside the school day, and they are the reason the revision week a parent imagines is shorter than the one the timetable actually allows.

The arithmetic is worth doing once. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Multiply the units your child's school timetables across Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies and you have the block of school time that is not available for Higher Level revision, whatever the exam calendar says. Families who plan around that number stop treating the school day as flexible and start protecting evening and weekend hours deliberately.

There are rules about how those classes run, and they matter if you are thinking about outside support. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited — so outside support here means working with the school's own material, never substituting a tutor's.

sections.heading: Two candidates, one household: the IB May session beside the IGCSE series
paragraphs: Plenty of UAE families have a Diploma candidate and an IGCSE candidate in the same spring. The two boards do not share a calendar, a zone system or an entry process, and assuming they do is how a deadline gets missed. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The IB's own session dates must come from your coordinator or ibo.org.

Cambridge's March series shows exactly how far ahead an entry sits. For March 2027 the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry deadline is more than two months before the first paper. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used.

Pearson's published dates make the same point from the other direction. The November 2026 final International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, which is why any date on a tutoring page should be read as indicative and checked against the board's live timetable. For a two-candidate household the practical move is a single shared calendar with one row per board and a named person responsible for each entry.

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to coach your child before the papers
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 regarding the introduction of private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure appears on this page; a number circulating online could not be verified against any official source. The honest position is that the permit is required and operating without one carries consequences the Ministry has not itemised publicly.

The rule that catches families in the final term is a different one. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against the current ADEK policy document, but the direction is clear: the obvious shortcut — paying your child's own subject teacher for exam coaching — is the one route to avoid. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again, needing a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram is a matching platform with no UAE premises, and makes no claim to hold that permit.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the deadline is close, and what the coordinator declares
paragraphs: The weeks before the May session are when the pressure on academic honesty peaks, and they are also when the boundary is clearest. Assessed work must be the candidate's own. A tutor may teach the content, explain what a criterion is asking for, question a line of reasoning, point out that a conclusion is not supported by the data, and read a draft the student wrote and give feedback on it. A tutor may not author any part of it, supply text to be pasted in, edit a piece to completion, or hand over a worked version of an exploration for the student to copy.

This is not a house style. The IB's academic-honesty rules make outside authorship a malpractice matter for the student, with consequences that can reach the award of the Diploma itself, and the student's own supervisor and coordinator sign authenticity declarations at submission. A family paying for support in the final term should understand that the declaration is made about work the student produced, and that any help which cannot survive the coordinator asking about it is help that should not have been given. Keeping session notes and dated drafts protects the candidate, not the tutor.

There is a commercial dimension too. One provider ranking for these searches sells finished internal assessments outright, at a published price. That is an integrity breach, an expulsion risk for the student and a liability for the family that pays for it. The useful test before buying anything in the final term is simple: ask what the student will have done by the end of the engagement. If the answer is that work will be handed over rather than produced, the engagement is not tutoring. IB Gram's position is the narrow one — teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own work, and nothing beyond it.
bullets: A tutor may teach content, model method and give feedback on the student's own draft
A tutor may not author, supply or edit to completion any assessed component
Supervisors and coordinators sign authenticity declarations at submission
Keep dated drafts and session notes so the student's process is evidenced

sections.heading: What is already banked before the first paper, and what is still movable
paragraphs: By the time a UAE candidate walks into the first paper, a meaningful share of the Diploma score is already decided. Internally assessed components have been submitted, marked by the school and sent for moderation. The Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay are gone. Creativity, Activity, Service is complete or it is not. Those marks can still move slightly through moderation, but no amount of revision in April changes what was uploaded in February. Knowing which parts are banked tells you where the remaining hours should go, and it stops a family spending the final term on work that cannot be improved.

What is still movable is everything the external papers carry, and in most subjects that is the larger share of the grade. The highest-return work in the last weeks is almost never new content. It is the mark-scheme behaviours: reading the command term before answering, allocating time by marks rather than by how interesting a question looks, showing the step that earns the method mark, labelling a diagram so the written answer can refer to it, and finishing the paper. Candidates routinely lose more marks to unfinished papers and mis-read commands than to topics they never understood.

The core deserves a specific mention because of how it fails. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are graded A to E, and a grade E in either is a failing condition for the Diploma regardless of subject scores. That makes a handful of hours spent on a core component, early enough to matter, one of the highest-leverage decisions available — and it is the opposite of where most final-term money goes. If a family can fund only a small amount of support, the question is not which Higher Level subject is weakest. It is whether anything in the core is at risk.
bullets: Internally assessed components are submitted and moderated long before the papers
A grade E in Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay is a failing condition
Most final-term marks are won through command terms and timing, not new content
Unfinished papers are a bigger loss than unlearned topics for most candidates

sections.heading: What exam-term support costs in the UAE market, and what the number includes
paragraphs: Three of six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in. The figures below are market rates in AED read from providers' own published pages and from a Dubai tutoring cost table in October 2026. They are not an IB Gram price list. Our model is a trial lesson at no charge first, then a quote for the specific subject, level and number of hours, so you see the total before anything is committed.

Read the bands as a map of the market rather than a menu. Budget online tutoring starts low because the tutor is often a university student rather than a subject specialist; EdFlik publishes rates from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit higher, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A tutor travelling to an address costs more again, because travel is inside the rate: Bestimate's Dubai table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350, and home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level rates run AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 for premium named tutors.

The number that decides the bill is not the hourly rate, it is hours times weeks. A single Higher Level subject at one hour a week for a twelve-week final block is twelve hours; at the specialist mid-band that is a four-figure sum in AED, and three subjects is three times it. Monthly packages seen in the market run from AED 799 a month for eight online sessions to AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Ask any provider three questions before paying: is the rate per 60 minutes or per lesson, what the quoted figure says about VAT, and what happens to unused hours. For context on the wider household budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package.

sections.heading: A tutor at a UAE address against one-to-one online, for a May candidate
paragraphs: Parents search for a tutor who will come to the house, and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. A tutor travelling to a UAE address is a real market: Bestimate's Dubai figures put it at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with travel priced into the rate. It works best for younger children, for families who want a visible adult presence during the session, and in dense school catchments where a tutor can reach several households in an evening. Those are genuine advantages and this page is not going to pretend otherwise.

IB Gram does not operate that way in the Emirates. Home visits are arranged only in India; in the UAE every lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The reason is the one that matters most to a Higher Level candidate weeks from papers: the choice of tutor stops being limited by driving distance. A family in Fujairah or Al Ain gets a Chemistry Higher Level specialist on the same terms as a family in Emirates Hills, instead of whoever happens to be within a twenty-minute drive. For a narrow Diploma subject in a market where the IB accounts for 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, that difference decides whether a specialist is available at all.

The second reason is time. A 4pm slot with travel built in consumes an evening at both ends; a 6pm video slot consumes an hour. In the final term, when a candidate needs a short session the night before a paper or an unplanned hour after a disappointing mock, the format that can be moved is worth more than the format that feels more formal. Screen sharing also means past-paper work is annotated live and kept, so the student has the marked attempt afterwards rather than a memory of it.

sections.heading: Equivalency and attestation: paperwork that starts after results, not before
paragraphs: Families often ask what they should be filing for a UAE university while revision is under way, and the answer is usually nothing. Ministry of Education equivalency works on issued certificates, so the file is assembled after results, not during preparation. What can be done in advance is knowing what the Ministry counts and which documents the school issues on request, so the post-results weeks are administration rather than discovery. IB Gram describes the process and points to the official channel; it does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and nobody should be charged for implying otherwise.

The sourced requirements are the British and American tracks. For the British curriculum, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. That five-subject rule is worth stating precisely, because a competitor page ranking for UAE searches tells parents six IGCSE subjects are required. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

No IB points threshold appears on this page. The reporting that sources the British and American figures states no IB equivalency score, so publishing one would mean inventing it. If your child is applying to a UAE institution with an IB Diploma, verify the requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate, and ask the university's admissions office directly in the same week. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for attestation or for admission, and any provider implying that it is has invented an urgency that the regulatory process does not contain.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the session
process.description: Send the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, which session your child sits and which emirate the school is in. The last two matter: they decide the term calendar, the mandatory-subject load and the authority that licenses the school. A paper your child has already sat in a mock is the most useful attachment.

process.title: We match a subject specialist, not a generalist
process.description: Matching is by subject and level first and by availability second, because a Higher Level paper is not taught well by someone covering six subjects. If the specialist for a narrow Diploma subject is outside the UAE, we say so before the trial rather than after, and we give you the Gulf Standard Time slot they can hold.

process.title: A trial lesson at no charge, one subject
process.description: One lesson, one subject, no payment, so you can hear how the tutor explains something your child has already struggled with. Ask for the permit record and ask how a mark scheme would be used in a normal session. If the match is wrong, say so and we match again rather than asking you to persist with it.

process.title: Build the plan backwards from the session
process.description: The tutor works from your child's own subject guide and the school's internal deadlines, not a generic revision calendar. Get those dates from the coordinator in writing first: internally assessed component deadlines, the level-change window and the mock dates. The plan then assigns hours to papers rather than to topics in the order a textbook lists them.

process.title: Review at the fourth session, not at the end
process.description: By the fourth session there should be written evidence of what has been tested and what is still being missed, and a marked timed attempt you can read. If that evidence does not exist, the engagement is not working and the honest response is to change it then, while there are still weeks left in which a change can pay off.

whyPoints.title: The regulator facts are cited, not remembered
whyPoints.description: Every regulatory statement on this page traces to u.ae, KHDA's published guidance or MoHRE's own service listing, and the IB dates we will not publish are the ones no automated source could confirm. A page that shows where a fact came from is one you can check before acting on it.

whyPoints.title: One-to-one, online, and said plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are arranged only in India. Several providers in this market conceal non-UAE delivery behind a foreign phone number; stating the model up front means you are not discovering it at the first lesson.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is narrow and stated
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nobody authors an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay for a candidate. A provider ranking for these searches sells finished coursework; that is the practice this page exists to argue against.

whyPoints.title: Prices are attributed to whoever published them
whyPoints.description: AED bands on this page are quoted from named providers and a dated Dubai cost table, so you can see what the market charges rather than a figure invented to look competitive. Our own number comes after the trial lesson, quoted for the subject, level and hours you actually want.

whyPoints.title: Availability limits are disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based specialist is free for a narrow Higher Level subject at your slot, we say so and offer the specialist who is, wherever they are based. Indian Standard Time runs ninety minutes ahead of Gulf Standard Time, which makes an evening UAE slot straightforward to hold.

faqs.question: Which exam session do IB Diploma students in the UAE normally sit?
faqs.answer: Almost all UAE Diploma cohorts sit the May session, because the local academic year ends in June or July and the papers therefore land in the final term. A smaller group sits November, usually retake candidates or students at schools on a different year pattern. The session covers more than the written papers: internally assessed components are submitted and uploaded weeks or months earlier, and the entry itself is filed by the school's Diploma coordinator. This page does not publish IB session or results dates, because the IB sets them and can revise them. Confirm every date with your coordinator or on ibo.org.

faqs.question: Our school runs an April-to-March year. Does that change which session our child sits?
faqs.answer: Not usually, but it changes where the revision block falls. UAE schools on an April-start year still enter candidates for the main session; the difference is that the final push happens early in a new school year rather than at the end of an old one. KHDA accounted for April-start schools separately when it set the implementation date for mandatory-subject requirements, which tells you this pattern is real in Dubai rather than theoretical. The practical risk is continuity: a change of subject teacher across the year boundary in the middle of a revision plan. Ask the school which staff carry the cohort through to the papers.

faqs.question: Does KHDA or ADEK set the IB exam timetable?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. They license schools, inspect them, approve fees in some emirates and require subjects alongside the licensed curriculum. The IB writes the papers, sets the submission windows, marks and moderates the components and publishes results. That means a missed internal deadline cannot be escalated to the regulator, and no authority can tell you a grade boundary in advance. Escalate assessment problems inside the school, to the Diploma coordinator, and quickly.

faqs.question: Who submits my child's exam entry, the family or the school?
faqs.answer: The school. The Diploma coordinator files entries and level changes within windows the IB sets, and once a window closes it stays closed. Nothing is submitted from home. The most useful thing a parent can do in the autumn term is email the coordinator asking for three things in writing: the school's internal deadlines for every internally assessed component, the latest date a change between Higher and Standard Level can be requested, and the mock window. Those three dates convert a vague intention to get help into a plan with hours attached to specific weeks.

faqs.question: How many weeks of one-to-one support does a May candidate realistically need?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the problem is content or execution. A content gap needs a week between diagnosis and the next check, so weekly sessions across the final two terms are the efficient shape, and that is roughly twenty to twenty-four hours per subject. Execution problems — command terms, timing, unclaimed method marks — respond to a shorter block of eight to twelve hours organised by paper rather than by topic. What rarely works is three subjects at once in the last fortnight. Pick the two where marks are most recoverable and protect the core components first.

faqs.question: Where does Ramadan fall against the May session, and can lessons move after Iftar?
faqs.answer: Ramadan falls inside the final revision stretch for a May candidate in most recent years, and school timetables shorten while energy drops in the late afternoon. Sessions can move to post-Iftar slots, and for many families that is the most productive hour of the day. Because lessons run over live video rather than requiring anyone to travel, a 9pm Gulf Standard Time slot is as workable as a 5pm one. Agree the Ramadan pattern before the month starts rather than rescheduling week by week, and keep one weekend morning for full-paper work under timed conditions.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons continue through the exam term?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the requirement does not pause for revision. KHDA calculates the instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, lets schools vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. Work out how many units your child's timetable carries and treat that as school time unavailable for Higher Level revision. Planning around the real number, rather than an imagined free timetable, is what makes evening hours get protected.

faqs.question: My child's own teacher has offered paid exam coaching. Is that allowed?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and a teacher tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tutor permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy document, but the direction is unambiguous. There is also a plain conflict of interest: the person marking the mock should not be paid privately to prepare the candidate for it.

faqs.question: How do we check that a tutor is permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask them, before the first paid session, and ask any platform the same question about the person it matched you with. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system under the service Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look over an internal assessment before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read a draft the student wrote and give feedback on it: explain what a criterion is asking for, question whether a conclusion follows from the data, point out an unexplained method. A tutor cannot author any part of it, supply text to be inserted, or edit it to completion. Supervisors and coordinators sign authenticity declarations at submission, and the declaration is about work the student produced. Keep dated drafts and a record of what each session covered, so the student's own process is evidenced if anyone asks. Help that could not survive that question should not have been given.

faqs.question: Is a school's inspection rating a guide to how my child will do in May?
faqs.answer: Only loosely. An inspection rating is a school-level judgement published in a particular year by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Department of Knowledge, built from evidence across phases and subjects. Your candidate sits an individually assessed set of papers in six subjects plus the core. A strong overall rating can sit alongside a weak department, and the reverse happens too. Read the report for what it names about teaching in the relevant phase, then ask the subject department directly about Higher Level outcomes, staffing continuity and when mocks are marked. That conversation is more predictive than any band.

faqs.question: Our other child sits IGCSEs in the same spring. How do we plan two sets of exams?
faqs.answer: Build one household calendar with a row per board and a named person responsible for each entry, because the calendars do not align. Cambridge runs June and November series with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that the correct zone timetable must be used. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For the March 2027 Cambridge series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 for an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. IB dates come from your coordinator.

faqs.question: What does exam-term one-to-one support cost in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run from AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 where a tutor travels to an address, AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and AED 500 to 650 and above at the premium end. Those figures are published by EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, Bestimate, TutorChase and BartyED respectively, not by us. The number that decides your bill is hours times weeks. IB Gram quotes after a trial lesson at no charge, for the subject, level and hours you want.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram arrange for a tutor to visit our address in Dubai or Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. Every lesson for a UAE family is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time; a tutor arriving at an address in the Emirates is not part of what we arrange, and visits are something we organise only in India. The trade is deliberate. Online matching removes driving distance from the choice of tutor, so a Higher Level specialist for a narrow subject becomes reachable from Fujairah or Al Ain on the same terms as from Emirates Hills. Screen sharing also means past-paper work is annotated live and kept for the final fortnight.

faqs.question: When does the equivalency paperwork start, and will my child need it for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: It starts after results, because Ministry of Education equivalency works on issued certificates. What you can do earlier is learn what each track must show and which documents the school issues on request. The British-track rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. The American track requires IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 in reading and writing, and SAT Math 450. No IB points figure appears here; verify that on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: No Higher Level specialist is free at our Gulf Standard Time slot. What happens then?
faqs.answer: We tell you before the trial rather than after, and offer the specialist who is free, wherever they are based. UAE supply is genuinely thin for narrow Diploma subjects, which follows from the IB being 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment against 37% for UK curricula. Indian Standard Time runs ninety minutes ahead of Gulf Standard Time, so an evening UAE slot is straightforward for a Mumbai or Delhi specialist to hold week after week. If nothing fits at all, we say that too. Nobody is better served by a generalist booked into a Higher Level paper six weeks out.

faqs.question: Can we try a lesson before committing to a block of exam-term hours?
faqs.answer: Yes. The first lesson is one subject, one session, at no charge and with no card details taken, so the only thing you are committing is an hour. Use it on something your child has already failed to understand once, because how a tutor handles that is the only reliable signal available before money changes hands. Ask how a mark scheme would be used in a normal session, and ask to see the permit record. If the match is wrong, say so and we match again rather than expecting a family to persist with a tutor who does not fit.

ib-may-session-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Get the dates from the coordinator, then book the hours
ib-may-session-exam-preparation.closingBody: IB May session exam preparation in the UAE works when it is dated. Email your child's Diploma coordinator for the internal component deadlines, the level-change window and the mock dates, and you will know within a day which weeks are actually available. Then send us the subject, the level and the emirate, and we will match a specialist who can hold a Gulf Standard Time slot through to the papers. The first lesson is one subject at no charge, lessons run one-to-one over live video, and the student's assessed work stays entirely their own. If no specialist is free at the hour you need, we will say so before you pay for anything.

intro.heading: The mock is a school exam that behaves like a public one
paragraphs: A mock exam in an IB school is written, timetabled, marked and graded by the school. The IB does not set it, does not see it and does not record it. That single fact explains most of what families find confusing about mock season in the UAE: why two Dubai schools can give the same subject a different paper in the same week, why a 5 at one school reads like a 4 at another, and why an IB mock result can be both the most useful piece of evidence a family will ever get and a poor predictor of the final grade.

What mock season does own is the prediction. Schools build an IB predicted grade from the mock mark, classwork, internal assessment drafts and the subject teacher's judgement, and those predictions reach universities months before the real papers are sat. A conditional offer from a British university, a place held at a Canadian or Australian institution, a scholarship shortlist at a UAE university: each of them reads a number that the mock largely produced. Mock season is an admissions event dressed as a revision event, which is why the families who treat it as a rehearsal tend to underfund it.

The cost question follows from that. Mock-season hours in the Emirates sell in two different shapes. Pre-mock hours are revision work: coverage, pacing, practice under timed conditions. Post-mock hours are diagnosis: reading the marked script, separating content gaps from technique gaps, and rebuilding a plan for the terms that are left. Pre-mock hours are bought by more households. Post-mock hours are, per hour spent, usually the better purchase, because the script tells a tutor exactly where the marks went and removes the guesswork a pre-mock plan has to carry.

Published market figures give the arithmetic its numbers. Rates in the UAE run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and AED 650 at the premium end. Those are the providers' own published bands, read in October 2026, and they describe the market rather than an IB Gram price list. A post-mock script audit for one Higher Level subject is typically two to three hours of work. The same money spread thinly across six subjects in the fortnight before a paper buys very little in any of them.

This page is written for the parent deciding what to fund. It covers who owns each part of a mock result, where mock season falls in a UAE school year, how a mock mark becomes a prediction, what the market charges for each mock-season product, the difference between spending before and after the papers, and the things no budget buys at all. Everything IB Gram delivers to families in the Emirates is one-to-one over live video. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and nothing here should be read as an offer to send anyone to a UAE address.
