ib-mock-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: A mock looks different in each IB programme, and so does what a mock-season budget can sensibly buy. These are the three programmes UAE schools run, what the school is measuring in each, and what a family should expect the resulting mark to be used for once it is issued.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where mock season carries real weight. Schools run a full timetabled set of IB Diploma mock papers, usually in the first year of DP2, marked against the IB mark schemes the department holds. The mark feeds the prediction, and the prediction feeds every university conversation that follows. Six subjects, three of them normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay running in parallel, means a DP2 mock fortnight is the most compressed assessment window of the two years.
programmes.countryNote: Most UAE Diploma schools follow an August-to-June year and enter candidates for the May session, which puts the main mock window in late November or December and results in January. Schools on an April-to-March year, a pattern some Indian-curriculum-linked schools in Dubai and Sharjah retain for other sections, sit mocks on a different internal calendar. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the school's own mock dates rather than assuming the regional norm.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP has no external examination until the optional eAssessment at MYP 5, so a school's MYP mock is a practice run at on-screen examinations and criterion-based tasks rather than a dress rehearsal for a public paper. Marks come back against criteria A to D with a level from 1 to 8 in each, not as a percentage, and a parent reading an MYP mock report for the first time usually needs the criterion letters translated before the result means anything.
programmes.countryNote: In the Emirates, MYP 5 is also the year many families decide between continuing to the Diploma and moving to IGCSE at a different school, and a mock result is often the evidence that decision rests on. Schools in Dubai and Abu Dhabi offering both routes publish internal thresholds for Higher Level entry. A mock below those thresholds is worth a conversation with the school before it becomes a subject-choice form.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP runs no mock examinations. Assessment is continuous, and the programme closes with the PYP Exhibition rather than a paper. Families searching for mock preparation at this stage are almost always preparing for something else: an entrance assessment at a selective school, a CAT4 or similar baseline test, or the transition into MYP. Naming the actual assessment changes what useful preparation looks like, and it changes the cost.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four British curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. That expansion is reshaping entrance-assessment pressure in the primary years across the emirate. A PYP family facing a selective assessment is buying test familiarisation, not mock exam preparation, and the two are priced and planned differently.

ib-mock-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: Mock papers punish different things in different subjects, and a script audit is only worth paying for if the tutor knows which failure the paper is designed to expose. These are the subjects UAE families most often bring to us after mock results land, with what the marked script usually shows.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Mock scripts in AA lose marks to unjustified steps rather than wrong answers. Method marks go missing where working is compressed, and the Higher Level non-calculator paper exposes algebraic fluency that a calculator has been hiding all term. The toolkit and the exploration run alongside, so a December mock often arrives mid-exploration.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI scripts fail on modelling and interpretation, not on computation. Students produce a correct regression and then write nothing about what it means in context, which is where the marks sit. Graphical calculator technique is examinable in itself, and a mock is usually the first time a student discovers their own calculator is slowing them down.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The mock separates students who can recall a relationship from students who can apply it to an unfamiliar situation. Data-analysis questions on uncertainty and graph gradients are routinely left half-answered, and extended-response questions lose marks for describing a phenomenon when the command term asked for an explanation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics dominate the lost marks on a Chemistry mock, with Higher Level students losing most on multi-step calculations where one rounding decision propagates. Scripts also show a pattern of unused data booklet pages: students who never practised with it under timed conditions do not reach for it in the hall.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology mocks reward precise terminology and punish approximate description. Marks are lost where a student writes around a term instead of using it, and in data-based questions where the answer restates the trend rather than accounting for it. Higher Level scripts show the extra load of the additional Higher Level material most clearly in timing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks, and incomplete axes or unlabelled shifts cost them silently. Paper 1 essays lose marks on evaluation rather than theory, and real-world examples are either absent or generic. Higher Level policy and calculation questions need practice under time, which a mock usually proves has not happened yet.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward students who use the stimulus material and penalise those who answer from textbook theory alone. Mock scripts commonly show tool-based questions where the tool is applied correctly but never linked back to the business in the case, which is exactly where the higher mark bands begin.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis is where mock marks disappear: students summarise the text instead of analysing how it produces meaning. Paper 2 comparative essays lose structure under time. The Individual Oral and the Higher Level essay sit outside the mock, so a mock grade is a partial picture of the subject.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-based questions have a mark allocation most students have never counted, and mock scripts show time spent unevenly across it. Essays lose marks for narrative rather than argument, and Higher Level regional-option answers show the thinnest content coverage, because that material is often taught last.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Mock scripts show studies recalled without the detail the question needed, and evaluation points that name a limitation without explaining its effect on the conclusion. Research-methods questions in the Higher Level paper are frequently the lowest-scoring section on an otherwise competent script.

ib-mock-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: Mock dates, term calendars and the authority that answers for the school all change as you move between emirates. These notes cover what actually differs for a mock-season plan, rather than listing places a tutor could drive to, because sessions are delivered online.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The densest Diploma cohort in the country and the tightest mock calendar, with most schools examining in late November or December and issuing results in January. Families searching for mock exam preparation in Dubai are usually working to a predicted-grade conversation already scheduled for the spring term, so the diagnosis window is short.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Diploma schools here sit mocks on a similar November-to-December pattern, but the capital's traffic and the spread between Khalifa City, Saadiyat and Al Reem make evening scheduling the real constraint. An online slot after the school run removes the drive from both sides of the lesson, which matters in a fortnight with no spare evenings.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: A smaller IB cohort alongside a large British and Indian curriculum sector, and an emirate whose authority approves curricula and assessment methods as well as fees. Households here frequently have one IB candidate and one IGCSE candidate sitting internal examinations in overlapping weeks, which changes how a single budget has to be split.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Under the same Abu Dhabi authority as the capital, with fewer Diploma schools and a correspondingly thin local pool of Higher Level specialists. For a subject such as Physics HL or Economics HL, an online match is often the only route to a tutor who has actually taught the paper being audited.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised federally rather than by an emirate authority, and the IB cohort is small. Mock calendars follow each school's own internal planning, so the dates a neighbour in Dubai quotes are not transferable. Confirm the window with the school before booking any block of hours.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Returned zero mentions across the researched competitor pages for this query, which tells you how much attention the northern emirates get. Online delivery makes the local tutor count irrelevant to what a family can book.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, with the smallest IB presence of the seven emirates. Travel between Fujairah and the western emirates rules out any visiting arrangement for a weekly session, so a mock-to-final programme here is an online commitment or it is nothing.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai carries the largest Diploma cohort in the country, and its schools set their own mock papers and their own boundaries. Two students in neighbouring communities can sit different papers in the same subject in the same week and come away with grades that are not comparable. Students we support attend schools including those below.

Capital-region Diploma schools answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which licenses and accredits private schools in the emirate. Mock timetables are set internally and often cluster in the same fortnight across several schools, which is why specialist availability tightens sharply in December.

A smaller IB cohort spread across several authorities, with many households running an IB candidate and an IGCSE candidate at once. Mock weeks for the two boards rarely align, so the practical question is which child's internal examinations get the funded hours first.

Each of the three below is delivered one-to-one over live video, and each answers a different question.

Every lost mark is classified: content not known, content known but not retrieved under time, command term misread, working not shown, or question misallocated against its mark tariff. The output is a written plan naming the topics and the techniques, in the order they should be addressed across the remaining terms.

sections.heading: What a mock exam is in an IB school, and who owns every part of the mark
paragraphs: An IB mock is a school assessment from first page to final grade. The department chooses or writes the paper, often assembling it from released IB papers it holds legitimately or from a commercial question bank. The school sets the date, runs the room, marks the scripts, picks the boundaries that turn a raw mark into a number from 1 to 7, and decides what goes in the report. No part of that process passes through the IB, and no mock mark appears on any certificate.

That matters for two practical reasons. The first is comparability: a 5 awarded by one Dubai school and a 5 awarded by another are not the same measurement, because the papers differ and the boundaries differ. Parents comparing notes across a community WhatsApp group are comparing two different tests. The second is appeal: there is no external route to challenge a mock grade, because there is no external body involved. The only conversation available is with the department that set it.

The one output that does leave the building is the prediction. Predicted grades are submitted by the school and read by universities, and mock exam marking is the largest single input to them in most departments. So the honest description of mock season is this: the grade itself is disposable, the marked script is valuable evidence, and the prediction is the thing with consequences. A family funding mock exam preparation should be clear which of the three they are trying to influence, because the three need different work and different money.

sections.heading: Mock season in a UAE school year, and the dates that belong to the school
paragraphs: The UAE Diploma calendar is reasonably uniform. Most schools run an August-to-June year, enter candidates for the May session, and place the main mock window in late November or December so that scripts can be marked over the winter break and results issued in January. A second mock, or a set of subject-level assessments standing in for one, often lands in February. Schools on an April-to-March year sit the sequence on a different internal timetable entirely.

None of those dates are set by the IB, which is exactly why they vary between schools in the same community. The IB owns the examination session; the school owns the mock, the internal deadlines around it and the date predictions are finalised. For planning purposes this is good news: mock dates are knowable months ahead by asking the Diploma coordinator, and they are the dates a tutoring budget should actually be built around.

We do not publish IB examination or results dates on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so every date in this project would be second-hand, and a wrong examination date is the one error on a planning page that can cost a family something real. Confirm the session window and the results date with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org directly. Cambridge and Pearson publish their own key dates, which is why the IGCSE side of a household's calendar can be pinned down with more confidence than the IB side.

sections.heading: The prediction is what mock season is really selling
paragraphs: An IB predicted grade is the school's formal estimate of the final result, submitted to the IB and used by universities to decide what offer to make. Departments differ in how they weigh the inputs, but a Diploma mock sat a term before predictions are finalised is almost always the heaviest piece of evidence on the table. It is the only data point produced under examination conditions, and it is the only one a department can defend to a parent with a script in front of them.

This is where mock exam preparation stops being an academic question and becomes a financial one. The gap between a predicted 5 and a predicted 6 can be the gap between an offer and a rejection at a competitive course, and the work that closes it has to happen before predictions are submitted, not after. Families who discover the mechanism in March have already missed the window the mock opened in December.

What follows is a realistic map, not a promise. No tutor can commit to moving a grade, and any provider who offers to is making a claim they cannot stand behind. What a tutor can do is tell you, from the marked script, which of the lost marks are recoverable in the time available and roughly how many hours each class of error usually takes to fix. That is the information a spending decision needs, and it is the information the mock has just handed you free of charge.

sections.heading: What mock exam preparation costs in the UAE, product by product
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible competitor pages for this cluster publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. The figures below are the market's own published numbers in AED, read in October 2026, attributed to the provider that published them. They are not IB Gram's prices. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, because the honest quote depends on the subject, the level and how many hours the script audit says are needed.

The useful move is to stop comparing hourly rates and start comparing products. A mock exam preparation cost of AED 250 an hour means one thing for a diagnostic audit that runs for three hours and produces a written plan, and something quite different for an open-ended weekly arrangement that runs for two terms. Multiply the rate by the realistic number of hours before judging whether it is expensive, and compare the total against what the subject is worth to the application.

Two figures are worth holding in mind while reading the table. The permit that allows an individual to tutor privately in the UAE is issued free of charge for two years, so nothing in a rate reflects a licensing cost. And KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's economic incentives package. School fees were held; tutoring rates were not, and nothing obliges them to follow.

sections.heading: Before the mock or after it: where the same money does more work
paragraphs: Take a household with AED 2,000 to spend on one Diploma subject and a mock four weeks away. There are five places that money can go, and they are not equivalent. The pre-mock options buy work planned on incomplete information: the student's own account of what they find hard, which is reliably wrong in at least one direction, and a teacher's general comment. The post-mock options buy work planned on a marked script, which is the only document in the whole process that says precisely where the marks went.

Spending after the mock also costs nothing in opportunity. The mock grade itself is already recorded and cannot be changed, so the hours are aimed entirely at the final result and the prediction conversation that precedes it. Spending before the mock competes with the student's own revision time in the fortnight when that time is scarcest, and a badly timed block of lessons in that window can reduce the mark it was bought to raise.

The pre-mock case is strongest in one specific situation: a named, already-diagnosed content gap, where a term of work was missed through illness, a school move or a late subject change. There the tutor is not guessing, the gap is known, and four weeks is enough to close a defined piece of syllabus. Outside that case, the better sequence for most UAE families is a modest pre-mock block for pacing, then the real money held back for the fortnight after the scripts come home.

sections.heading: Inside a post-mock script audit: what three hours should produce
paragraphs: A script audit is a specific piece of work, and a family paying for it should know what to expect back. The tutor reads the marked paper alongside the mark scheme and classifies every lost mark into one of five categories. Content not known is the first and the most expensive to fix. Content known but not retrieved under time is the second, and it responds to practice rather than teaching. Command term misread is the third, and it is often the cheapest fix on the whole script.

The fourth category is working not shown, where the student had the right idea and the marker could not award it. On a Mathematics or Physics script this is frequently the single largest block of recoverable marks, and it is a habit rather than a knowledge gap. The fifth is mark-tariff misallocation: eighteen minutes spent on a four-mark question and six on a twelve-mark one. A student can lose a grade boundary to that alone while knowing the entire syllabus.

The output is a written plan that ranks the categories by marks available against hours required, names the topics in the order they should be revisited, and states plainly which of the lost marks are not recoverable in the time left. That last line is the part families value most and the part marketing copy usually omits. An audit that reports only good news has not been done properly, and a plan with no stated cost in hours is not a plan.
bullets: Bring the marked script, the mark scheme if the school released it, and the teacher's comment sheet
Expect the five error categories named and counted, with marks attached to each
Expect an explicit statement of what cannot be recovered before the session
Expect the plan in writing, so the next tutor or the student can work from it

sections.heading: Six reasons a mock grade and a final grade diverge
paragraphs: Families treat the mock as a forecast and are then surprised in both directions. The divergence is structural rather than mysterious. The first reason is coverage: at mock time, most Diploma courses have not finished the syllabus, so the paper tests a subset and the real paper does not. The second is boundaries: a school picks its own, often deliberately severe ones, to produce a useful shock. A mock sat against harsh boundaries understates where a student actually stands.

The third reason is internal assessment. By mock season an exploration or investigation may be a draft, so its contribution to the mock grade is an estimate, while in the final grade it is a moderated mark with a fixed weighting. The fourth is Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which sit outside the mock entirely and carry points of their own in the Diploma. A mock cannot see them, so it cannot model the total.

The fifth is marking: a school department marking its own students' papers in a fortnight is doing a different job from a moderated international marking operation, and consistency differs accordingly. The sixth is the student: five months separate the two sittings, and a DP2 cohort in February is not the cohort that sat in November. Taken together, these six explain why a mock is best read as a diagnostic instrument and worst read as a prediction of the final number. A student who sat a severe paper on a partly-taught syllabus in November is not being measured against the thing they will actually sit, and a family that reads the mock grade as a forecast is budgeting against the wrong number.

sections.heading: Who answers for the school that sets the mock
paragraphs: Five separate authorities regulate private schools across the seven emirates, and parents frequently assume one of them has oversight of mock examinations. None does. The authorities license schools, inspect them, and in several emirates approve fees, curricula and assessment methods at the institutional level. The content of an internal mock paper, the boundaries applied to it and the prediction that follows are departmental decisions inside the school.

Knowing which authority answers for your school is still useful. It tells you where the published inspection report lives, who approves a fee increase, and which body to escalate to if a school's internal assessment practice looks wrong at a level beyond the department. In Dubai that is KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools.

One further point belongs here, because it affects who may legally coach your child through mock season. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

sections.heading: Mock-script work over live video against a tutor who travels
paragraphs: A fair comparison has to be made on the work, not on a slogan. Reading a marked script with a student is a document-centred activity: the paper needs to be visible to both people, annotated as the conversation moves, and kept afterwards. A shared screen with a photographed or scanned script does that at least as well as a paper on a table, and it does one thing a table cannot, which is save the annotated version for the student, the next session and the final revision term.

The market also prices the two differently, and mock season magnifies the gap because a family is usually funding more than one subject at once. Published UAE in-home rates run from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced into the number, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Across three subjects and a dozen hours each, that difference is the whole budget for a fourth subject.

The decisive factor is the pool. A Higher Level Physics script needs someone who has taught and marked that paper, not whoever is free within a twenty-minute drive of your community. An online IB tutor in the UAE is matched on the subject, the level and the Gulf Standard Time slot, which is why a family in Al Ain or Fujairah can book the same specialist as a family in Jumeirah. To be plain about it: IB Gram delivers one-to-one online tuition to families in the Emirates, and offers home visits only in India.

sections.heading: What a mock-season budget cannot buy, and the line a tutor will not cross
paragraphs: No amount of money buys a grade, and any provider willing to promise one has told you something important about how they operate. A tutor cannot change a recorded mock mark, cannot influence the boundaries a department chose, cannot alter a prediction once it is submitted, and cannot compress two terms of missing content into a fortnight. A provider who agrees with all four of those and then quotes you a number is quoting honestly.

There is also a firm boundary around assessed work. Under IB academic honesty rules, an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project must be the student's own work, and the coordinator signs a declaration to that effect. A tutor may teach the skills, discuss the method, question the reasoning and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor must not supply text, rewrite sections to a finished standard, or hand over assessed material. One provider in this market openly sells finished internal assessments; that is a malpractice trigger for the student, and the student carries the consequence, not the seller.

Two further things sit outside what tutoring can deliver. Ministry of Education equivalency and attestation is a process families complete through the official channel, and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it. And access arrangements in examinations, such as extra time, are applied for by the school's examinations officer against evidence, on the board's own timetable. A tutor can tell you the application exists and that it has a deadline; the school is the only party who can file it.

process.title: Send the marked script, not the grade
process.description: A number tells a tutor almost nothing; a marked paper tells them everything. Photograph or scan every page, including the ones with no comments on them, and send the teacher's feedback sheet alongside. If the school has not released the script, ask for it. Most departments will share it with a parent who asks directly.

process.title: A free trial lesson on the weakest paper
process.description: The first session is free and runs on the real material rather than a sample worksheet. The student works through two or three questions from their own script while the tutor watches how the answer gets built. That half hour usually identifies the failure pattern faster than any amount of discussion about it.

process.title: Match on the subject, the level and the hour
process.description: Matching runs on three things: the exact subject and level, the component the script says is weakest, and a slot that works in Gulf Standard Time. Evening and weekend slots are the ones mock-season families need, and they are the ones that fill first in December and January. Book the slot before the results arrive if the dates are known.

process.title: The audit, then the written plan
process.description: Two or three hours produce a classified error list and a ranked plan: what to fix, in what order, and how many hours each class of error usually takes. The plan states what is not recoverable in the time left. A family can act on it with us, with the school, or with another tutor entirely.

process.title: Weekly hours, reviewed against the school's own next assessment
process.description: From January the work runs weekly against the plan, and progress is judged by the school's next internal assessment rather than by anyone's impression. If the next assessment shows no movement, the plan changes or the hours stop. Sessions pause for internal assessment deadlines and school trips without losing the block.

whyPoints.title: The script is the brief
whyPoints.description: Lessons start from your child's own marked mock paper and the mark scheme, not from a textbook chapter order. That is the difference between tutoring aimed at a syllabus and tutoring aimed at the marks a specific student actually lost in a specific paper.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with their source and date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the month it was read. Three of the six most visible pages in this cluster publish no price at all. A family cannot budget against silence, so we publish the market and quote our own only after a trial.

whyPoints.title: Specialist by subject, not by proximity
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level Chemistry script needs a Chemistry teacher who has marked that paper. Online matching means the pool is every available specialist in your Gulf Standard Time slot rather than the handful living within a short drive, which matters most in Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary is written down
whyPoints.description: What a tutor may and may not do with an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay is stated on the page rather than left to interpretation. Teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own draft: yes. Producing assessed material: never, in any subject.

whyPoints.title: Online, one-to-one, timed to Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: Every session is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, including after-Iftar slots during Ramadan and weekend mornings in mock season. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and that is stated plainly on every UAE page rather than buried in a footnote.

faqs.question: Who writes the IB mock papers my child sits at a UAE school?
faqs.answer: The school does. A subject department either writes the paper or assembles it from released IB papers and commercial question banks it holds legitimately. The school also sets the date, runs the room, marks the scripts and chooses the grade boundaries. The IB is not involved at any stage and never sees the result. This is why two schools in the same Dubai community can examine the same subject in the same week with different papers and different boundaries, and why comparing a mock grade across schools tells you very little.

faqs.question: What does mock exam preparation cost for one IB subject in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which product you are buying. Published UAE market rates run AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above at specialist tier, read October 2026. A post-mock script audit is two to three hours, so AED 400 to 1,350 per subject. A pre-mock revision block of six to ten hours lands between AED 900 and 3,000. A weekly programme from January to the exam term is twelve to sixteen hours. Those are market figures, not IB Gram prices; we quote after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is it better value to pay for help before the mocks or after the results?
faqs.answer: After, for most students. Before the mock, a tutor is planning on the student's own account of what they find difficult, which is reliably wrong in at least one direction. After the mock, the marked script says exactly where the marks went, so the same hours are spent on diagnosed problems instead of suspected ones. The exception is a student with a known content gap from illness, a school move or a late subject change, where four weeks of defined teaching before the paper is worth more than diagnosis afterwards.

faqs.question: Does a poor mock grade change the prediction a UAE school sends to universities?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because the mock is normally the heaviest single input to a predicted grade. It is the only assessment sat under examination conditions and the only one a department can defend to a parent with a script on the table. Classwork, internal assessment drafts and teacher judgement also feed in, and departments weigh them differently. The practical consequence is that work aimed at the prediction has to happen between mock results and the date predictions are finalised, which in most UAE schools is a window of a few weeks in January and February.

faqs.question: How long does a post-mock script audit on one paper actually take?
faqs.answer: Two to three hours for one subject, including the tutor's reading time before the session. The paper is read against the mark scheme and every lost mark is classified into one of five types: content not known, content known but not retrieved under time, command term misread, working not shown, or time misallocated against the mark tariff. The session then produces a written plan ranking those categories by marks available against hours required, and stating which marks are not recoverable in the time remaining. A Higher Level paper with three components can take the full three hours.

faqs.question: Our daughter scored a 4 in her Higher Level mock. What is realistically movable before the final papers?
faqs.answer: A 4 that was close to a 5 usually has two causes on the script: one or two topics that are genuinely not known, and a whole-paper technique problem affecting every question. Both are addressable across two terms, and the technique element is often the larger block of marks. In our experience that combination takes somewhere between sixteen and twenty-four hours on the subject, with the first three spent on the audit. Nobody can commit to a grade, and any provider who does is promising something they cannot control. What the script can tell you is where the available marks are.

faqs.question: Do UAE schools mark mocks to the same grade boundaries the IB uses?
faqs.answer: No, and most do not try to. A department picks boundaries from an earlier session, or sets its own, frequently choosing severe ones deliberately so that a mock produces a useful shock in November rather than a comfortable one. IB boundaries are set per session after marking, so no school can know them in advance. This means a mock grade understates or overstates a student's position depending on the department's choices, and it is one of the main reasons a mock and a final grade diverge.

faqs.question: Can we fund mock preparation for three subjects without the cost running away?
faqs.answer: Yes, by buying audits across all three and hours in only one or two. Three script audits at specialist tier is roughly AED 1,200 to 4,000 at published market rates, and it produces a ranked list of where the recoverable marks actually are across the whole Diploma. Very often two of the three subjects turn out to need technique work the student can do alone with a checklist, and the third needs real teaching hours. Buying the diagnosis first is what stops a budget from being spread evenly and thinly across six subjects.

faqs.question: When do IB mocks usually take place in Dubai and Abu Dhabi schools?
faqs.answer: Most Diploma schools in both emirates run an August-to-June year and place the main mock window in late November or December, so scripts are marked over the winter break and results are issued in January. A second mock, or subject assessments standing in for one, often falls in February. None of those dates are set by the IB, so they vary between schools in the same community. Ask the Diploma coordinator for your school's own mock calendar; it is knowable months ahead and it is the calendar a tutoring budget should be built around.

faqs.question: Is a mock result worth paying to have re-marked by someone outside the school?
faqs.answer: There is no formal route to challenge a mock grade, because no external body is involved, so a private re-mark changes nothing on the record. What a second reading of the script does buy is information: a specialist reading the paper against the mark scheme can show where marks were available and not awarded, which is useful evidence for a conversation with the department. Frame it as a diagnostic audit rather than an appeal. If the aim is genuinely to contest marking, the conversation belongs with the subject teacher and the coordinator.

faqs.question: Should we spend on mock preparation now or save the money for the final term?
faqs.answer: Split it, with the larger share in the window straight after mock results. The final six weeks can protect pacing and drill the highest-weighted paper, but they cannot build coverage that was never there, and they compete with the student's own revision time. The January to February window has neither of those problems: the plan is evidence-based, the prediction has not yet been finalised, and there is enough term left for new teaching to land. Holding everything back to the exam term is the most common budgeting error we see in UAE households.

faqs.question: What should we ask the Diploma coordinator once mock results come out?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Which boundaries were used, and from which session. Whether the paper covered the full syllabus or only the taught portion. What weight the mock carries in the prediction for each subject. When predictions are finalised and submitted. And whether the marked scripts can come home. The last one matters most, because without the script a family is working from a number. Departments generally release scripts to a parent who asks directly, and the paper is the only document that says where the marks actually went.

faqs.question: Does mock preparation do anything about internal assessment marks that are already banked?
faqs.answer: Not for work already submitted; a submitted internal assessment is finished. Where a draft is still in progress, a tutor can teach the criteria, discuss the method and give feedback on what the student has written, and the student then revises their own work. A tutor must not supply text or bring a piece to a finished standard, because an internal assessment has to be the student's own work and the coordinator signs a declaration to that effect. One provider in this market sells completed assessments outright; the student carries the malpractice consequence, not the seller.

faqs.question: Is group mock revision at a Dubai centre cheaper than one-to-one hours?
faqs.answer: Per hour, almost always. Centres quote per head for groups of two to four, and that sits below one-to-one rates. The trade is that group work cannot run on your child's own marked script, which is the one asset mock season hands you. A workable combination is a one-to-one audit to find the specific lost marks, then group hours for the content that is common to the whole cohort. Ask the centre how many students are in the group and whether the hours are per student or per session before comparing anything.

faqs.question: My son freezes under timed conditions rather than on the content. Can mock work fix that?
faqs.answer: It is one of the more tractable problems on a script, and it shows up clearly in the marking pattern: strong early answers, then a collapse in the final third, or eighteen minutes on a four-mark question. The fix is structural rather than psychological in most cases, built from mark-per-minute discipline, a fixed question order and practice at full paper length rather than in question sets. Six to ten hours of timed work usually changes the pattern. A student whose difficulty is genuine examination anxiety needs the school's counsellor as well, not a tutor alone.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for our subject during UAE mock season?
faqs.answer: December and January are the tightest weeks of the year for Diploma subjects, and for a narrow Higher Level option there may be nobody available in your Gulf Standard Time slot. We say so rather than substituting a generalist. The options then are a different slot, including early mornings before school, a later start once the first wave of mock-season bookings clears, or a tutor based in India teaching online at a UAE-friendly hour. Whichever applies, you are told which before any hours are booked.

ib-mock-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Start with the script, then decide what to fund
ib-mock-exam-preparation.closingBody: Mock season hands a UAE family one genuinely valuable document, and it is not the report card. It is the marked paper. Send it in, take the free trial lesson on whichever component looks weakest, and get a written audit that names the recoverable marks, the hours each class of error needs, and the marks that are gone. Then decide what to spend, with evidence in front of you instead of a rate card. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and nothing on this page is an offer to send a tutor to a UAE address.

intro.heading: The MYP year that decides the certificate is already half spent by January
paragraphs: MYP eAssessment is the IB's on-screen and portfolio-based route to the IB MYP Certificate, sat in Year 5 by students who are usually 15 or 16. It is not a smaller version of the Diploma examinations. The certificate is built from eight results: on-screen examinations in language and literature, individuals and societies, sciences and mathematics, an interdisciplinary on-screen examination, two externally moderated ePortfolios, and the Personal Project. Half of those results are not examinations at all. They are coursework assembled across the school year. By the time a parent in Dubai or Abu Dhabi notices that revision has not started, two of those portfolios may already be fixed.

That is why this page is organised as a countdown rather than a service list. Preparation for an on-screen examination can genuinely start eight weeks out, and often does. Preparation for a Design ePortfolio cannot: the investigation, the development of ideas and the evaluation had to exist before the school's internal upload date, and no amount of April tutoring creates evidence retrospectively. The same holds for the Personal Project, which is moderated externally on a report and process journal extracts describing work already carried out over months.

UAE families hit a second complication on top of that. Most MYP schools here sit the May session, which runs into the hottest stretch of the school year and, in several years, through Ramadan. Half-terms sit differently from the UK calendar. Mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons occupy timetable space KHDA requires Dubai schools to protect, so a Year 5 student carries more taught subjects than a British Year 11 peer. And a student in Sharjah may be commuting 50 minutes each way to an IB school in Dubai, which decides what time a weekday session can realistically start.

What a tutor can do here is narrower than most tutoring pages admit and more useful than parents expect. A tutor can rehearse the two-hour on-screen interface until it stops being a distraction and the student is reading the task instead of the software. A tutor can read an ePortfolio against the subject-group criteria and name the band each piece of evidence currently sits in. A tutor can teach a student how to plan a Personal Project report, how to reference it, and how to show process rather than describe it. A tutor cannot write any part of a student's Personal Project, and under IB academic honesty rules must not try.

Everything below is meant to be acted on this week. The calendar table counts the year backwards in weeks rather than dates, because internal school deadlines differ by school and the IB's own administrative dates should be read from your coordinator, not from a tutoring page. The criteria table shows where the marks in each criterion actually go. The rates table publishes what the UAE market charges with each source named and dated, because three of the six competitor pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. If the session is eight weeks away, skip to the last section and start there.

ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.programmesIntro: MYP eAssessment sits in the middle of a continuum, and the decisions made in Year 5 shape what a student can take in the Diploma. These four entries describe where your child is, what sits either side of it, and what each stage means specifically for a family planning in the UAE.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, assessed internally against four criteria per subject, each worth up to eight marks. There are no external examinations until Year 5. Grades 1 to 7 are awarded from criterion totals using boundaries the school applies, which is why a report card grade can move without any change in test scores: the criteria sampled that term were different.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools run the MYP alongside the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons their regulator requires, so a Dubai MYP timetable carries more taught subjects than the same programme in Europe. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes, which is the pressure most MYP Year 4 and 5 timetables absorb.

programmes.name: MYP Year 5 eAssessment
programmes.description: The externally assessed year. Candidates sit on-screen examinations in language and literature, individuals and societies, sciences and mathematics, plus an interdisciplinary on-screen examination, and submit ePortfolios in language acquisition and in one of arts, design or physical and health education. The Personal Project is moderated externally. Schools register candidates, so entry is a school decision a parent should confirm early rather than assume.
programmes.countryNote: The May session is the one most UAE MYP schools sit, which puts the examination window in the final term and the ePortfolio deadlines a full term before that. Families who have moved mid-year, which is common across Dubai and Abu Dhabi, need to check whether portfolio evidence from a previous school transfers at all; in most cases the receiving school's own internal deadlines govern.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at higher or standard level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment is predominantly external, with examination papers carrying most of the grade. The step up from MYP is not content volume but assessment type: students move from criteria-marked tasks to mark-scheme-marked papers, and the habits that earned criterion C marks do not automatically earn Paper 2 marks.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai added schools offering the IB for 2026-27 among seven new private schools, and IB programmes account for 7 per cent of Dubai private pupils against 37 per cent on UK curricula, so a UAE MYP student often sits in a year group where most peers are heading to A-Levels instead. MYP to DP transition support in June and July, immediately after results, is when subject-level choices are still reversible.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary learning across six transdisciplinary themes, ending in the PYP exhibition. There is no external assessment. Its relevance to eAssessment is indirect but real: students who come through PYP are used to being assessed on process and reflection, which is precisely what an ePortfolio and the Personal Project journal reward, while students arriving from a test-driven system often under-document.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run the full continuum on one campus, so a student may reach Year 5 having never sat an externally set paper. That is the gap worth closing in the autumn term of Year 5 rather than the spring: the first timed two-hour on-screen sitting should not be a shock, and in a continuum school it frequently is.

ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.subjectsIntro: The eAssessment route splits the eight MYP subject groups into two very different kinds of preparation. On-screen subjects reward timed rehearsal; ePortfolio subjects reward documentation discipline months earlier. Here is what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to go missing.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A two-hour on-screen paper on unseen text and media extracts. Marks are lost on criterion B when students summarise a text rather than analyse how its features produce an effect, and on criterion D when the comparative question is answered as two separate descriptions with no point of contact between them.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Source-based tasks on unfamiliar material, with concepts supplied in the stimulus. Students who have revised content and not command terms stall here: the paper rewards evaluating source reliability and applying a concept, and penalises retelling the source. Practising with sources no one has pre-taught is the only preparation that moves criterion C.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Data interpretation, experimental design and scientific reasoning on scenarios the student has not met. Criterion B marks go to method and variable control stated precisely; criterion D to explaining a scientific application and its implications. Students trained only on recall of topic content tend to score in the middle bands and plateau there.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: MYP maths on-screen examination tasks move from routine procedure to unfamiliar real-world modelling within the same paper. Marks go missing in criterion D, where the real-world context is treated as decoration rather than answered, and in criterion C, where working is not communicated well enough for a moderator to follow the reasoning.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary Learning
subjects.description: MYP interdisciplinary examination preparation is the component families most often discover late. It asks students to draw on two disciplines to address one problem, and it is graded on disciplinary grounding and on synthesis. Neither improves by revising two subjects separately, which is why targeted practice linking two named subjects is needed.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: An externally moderated portfolio across listening, reading, speaking and writing at the student's phase. It is assembled in school across the year. The common failure is phase mismatch: evidence produced at a lower phase than the one entered, which caps the achievable band regardless of how strong the individual pieces look to a parent.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Process and product together: investigation of an artistic context, development of skills, a created work, and an evaluation. Students regularly submit a strong final piece with thin process evidence and score below their ability, because criterion B rewards documented development and not the finished object.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The design cycle in full, from inquiry and analysis through developing ideas and creating a solution to evaluating it against a specification the student wrote. It is the least recoverable component in the set. Once the internal upload date passes, no amount of MYP ePortfolio feedback can add the missing development stage.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowledge of health concepts, planning for performance, applied performance and reflection. It is the ePortfolio most often chosen late by students who dislike Arts and Design, which usually means the planning and reflection evidence is thinner than the performance evidence and the grade sits below expectation.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: A self-directed project with a goal, a process journal and a report, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting. MYP Personal Project coaching can teach structure, referencing and how to evidence process. A tutor may not supply content, write the report or edit a student's Personal Project into shape; doing so is malpractice under IB rules.

ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.regionsIntro: MYP provision is not spread evenly across the seven emirates. Where a family lives decides how many schools offer the programme within a reasonable commute, what time a weekday session can start, and whether online delivery is a preference or the only realistic option.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha South, Dubai
regions.note: The densest IB cluster in the country, with full continuum schools within minutes of one another. Session slots from 16:30 work for most families here, though Sheikh Zayed Road congestion between 17:00 and 19:00 makes a 16:30 online start noticeably easier to keep than a 18:00 one.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim, Dubai
regions.note: Villa communities feeding established IB and British schools. School runs finish early, so 15:30 and 16:00 slots are usable here in a way they are not further out, which matters in the eight-week on-screen sprint when two sessions a week are needed.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba, Mirdif and Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: Continuum schools serving families spread across a long east-west axis. Commutes of 35 to 50 minutes are normal, so Year 5 students often arrive home after 16:30 and a 17:30 or 18:00 session fits better than an earlier one during ePortfolio term.

regions.name: Al Raha, Khalifa City and Al Bateen, Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Where most Abu Dhabi IB families sit. An online MYP tutor in Abu Dhabi solves the specific problem here: the capital has far fewer MYP-experienced subject teachers than Dubai, and the bridge crossing makes a cross-city match impractical on a weekday.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK alongside Abu Dhabi, with limited MYP provision in the city itself. Families here either travel towards Abu Dhabi for school or accept that subject-specialist support for Year 5 eAssessment is only available over video, which is the normal arrangement.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by SPEA, which approves curricula and assessment methods as well as fees. One continuum school and a sizeable number of Sharjah-resident students commuting into Dubai, who lose 90 to 100 minutes a day to the crossing and cannot add travel to a tutor on top.

regions.name: Ajman and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. No MYP school within a short drive, so students who want the programme commute south. Evening sessions after 19:00 are common here and are the only slot that works in practice.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah
regions.note: RAK private schools answer to the Department of Knowledge, Fujairah to the Ministry of Education. Both appear in none of the competitor pages researched for this market. MYP families here are served online by default, and scheduling is the easiest part of the arrangement.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB continuum and IB programme schools
schoolClusters.note: Students we support in Year 5 come from across this group. Programme authorisation and the year groups entered for eAssessment change from year to year and from campus to campus, so confirm with the school's MYP coordinator or the IB's own school finder before assuming your child will sit it.

ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. That rule is the reason an independent online match is the clean route for a capital family, rather than an arrangement through the school.

MYP provision thins sharply north of Dubai. Sharjah has a continuum school; Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah have none within a short commute, which is why families in those four emirates are the most dependent on video delivery for any subject specialism.

ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named only as context for where MYP cohorts sit in each area. No affiliation, sponsorship or endorsement is implied, and programme offers change year to year, so verify current provision with the school or the regulator.
ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.modesIntro: Four ways families use MYP support through the certificate year. They are not packages competing for the same budget; they occupy different parts of the calendar, and a family that starts the right one at the wrong time usually pays for the wrong thing.

modes.description: One or two live video sessions a week in a named subject group, running from the start of the year. This is the only mode that can influence an ePortfolio grade, because it overlaps the months in which portfolio evidence is produced. It is also the cheapest way to hold a weak subject, measured over the full year.

sections.heading: What IB MYP eAssessment preparation in the UAE actually covers
paragraphs: IB MYP eAssessment is the IB's externally assessed route to the IB MYP Certificate, taken in MYP Year 5. It has two halves that need completely different preparation. Four subject groups plus interdisciplinary learning are examined in two-hour on-screen sittings. Four subject groups are submitted as externally moderated ePortfolios. The Personal Project is moderated separately and is compulsory for the certificate. Service as Action is a participation requirement the school records rather than a graded component.

The IB MYP Certificate requirements are worth knowing precisely, because parents frequently assume a pass is a pass. The certificate is awarded on eight results, with a points total and a minimum grade in each result, and a satisfactory record of Service as Action. The exact threshold and the way the eight results are counted should be read from your school's MYP coordinator, who works from the current IB handbook for the session your child is entered for. Schools also have the option of entering candidates for individual course results rather than the full certificate, which is a different outcome with different consequences for the Diploma that follows.

What that means for preparation is a split timetable. On-screen components respond to the last two months. ePortfolio components do not respond to them at all. Every planning decision below follows from that one asymmetry, and the single most common expensive mistake UAE families make is booking an intensive block in March for a Design grade that was already settled in January.

sections.heading: The Year 5 calendar, counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: This is the table nobody else in this market publishes. It counts the certificate year backwards in weeks rather than in dates, and that choice is deliberate. Internal deadlines differ by school, the IB's administrative dates for a given session are published to coordinators, and a tutoring page that prints an IB date it has not verified is worse than useless. Weeks-before is a planning model you can map onto your own school's calendar in ten minutes with the coordinator's deadline list in front of you.

Read it with one question in mind: which components are still open at the point you are reading this. If the session is 24 weeks away, all eight results are still movable. At 12 weeks, the ePortfolios are usually closed or closing and only the on-screen components and the final Personal Project polish remain. At four weeks, only the on-screen examinations are in play, and the honest advice is to stop adding subjects and rehearse the two or three that carry the most risk.

The two rows families most often miss are the registration row and the interface row. Registration is a school action, not a parent action, and the subject list locks months before the session; a student who wanted to switch from physical and health education to arts discovers too late that the portfolio evidence does not exist for the new choice. The interface row looks trivial and is not. A student who has never used the exact on-screen environment loses the first fifteen minutes of a two-hour paper learning where the tools are.

sections.heading: An on-screen examination is a different examination, not a paper on a laptop
paragraphs: The two-hour on-screen format changes what the paper can ask. Stimulus material can be audio, video, interactive data or a long scrollable source set, so the reading load arrives in a different shape and cannot be skimmed the way a printed insert can. Answers are typed, which rewards students who can structure a response before they start typing and punishes those who write to find out what they think. There is no margin to annotate, no space to sketch in, unless the task provides a tool for it.

MYP on-screen examination practice therefore has to be done on screen. Printing past tasks and completing them on paper trains the wrong skill. The specific habits worth building are: reading the whole task set before answering anything, because the scrollable format hides the shape of the paper; allocating minutes per task in advance and sticking to them; typing a two-line plan at the top of a long response and deleting it at the end; and using the full stimulus, since the examination is designed so that an answer written without the source cannot reach the top bands.

The third issue is physical and nobody mentions it. Two hours of screen reading in a room that may be at 24 degrees with the air conditioning running is tiring in a way a printed paper is not. Students who have only ever done 40-minute class tests arrive at task four with their concentration gone. The fix is rehearsal volume, not technique: three or four full-length timed sittings across the final eight weeks, scheduled at the time of day the real session runs, so stamina and timing are already solved before the content revision has to carry anything.

sections.heading: ePortfolio subjects are won in term one
paragraphs: Four of the eight results come from portfolios, and portfolios are evidence. A moderator reads what the student recorded while working, not what the student can now explain about the work. This is the single most consequential difference between MYP eAssessment and the examination-led systems most UAE parents went through themselves, and it is why a capable student can finish Year 5 with a strong on-screen profile and a Design grade two bands below it.

The pattern repeats across all four portfolio subjects. In Design, the development of ideas stage is where marks sit, and students jump from a brief to a finished product with nothing in between. In Arts, criterion B rewards documented development of skills, so a beautiful final piece with three photographs attached scores below a modest piece with a full process record. In language acquisition, the trap is phase: evidence produced at a lower phase than the one entered caps the band whatever its quality. In physical and health education, planning and reflection are consistently thinner than performance evidence.

MYP ePortfolio feedback has to arrive while the evidence can still be produced, which in practice means a fortnightly cycle from the start of the year to the school's internal upload date. The work in each cycle is narrow: take what exists, map each piece to its criterion, say which band it sits in and what the next band needs, and let the student produce it. A tutor who adds a paragraph, redraws a diagram or rewrites an evaluation has crossed from teaching into producing assessed work, and the student carries the consequence.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the component with the longest runway and the shortest recovery window. It is moderated externally on a report and extracts from a process journal, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting. A school supervisor oversees it. The student signs an academic honesty form. Everything about its design assumes the work was done gradually, and a journal reconstructed in one weekend in March reads exactly like a journal reconstructed in one weekend in March.

MYP Personal Project coaching that is worth paying for covers method. Narrowing a goal from something unachievable to something a 15-year-old can actually finish alongside eight subjects. Building the habit of a short journal entry each week, dated, including the decisions that went wrong. Research skills and referencing, so sources are recorded as they are used rather than reconstructed from a browser history. Report structure, so the report evidences process rather than narrating a story. And a plain explanation of what the academic honesty form the student signs actually commits them to.

The boundary is not a formality. Under IB academic honesty rules, assessed work must be the student's own. A tutor may teach, question, model with a different example, and give feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor may not supply content for a student's Personal Project, draft sections, rewrite the report or edit it to a standard the student could not reach alone. One competitor ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright; that is malpractice, it puts the student's result at risk rather than the seller's, and no part of our model touches it. We say this on the page because parents are entitled to know where the line is before they book, not after.

sections.heading: MYP criteria A to D, read the way a moderator reads them
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, giving 32 raw marks per subject which convert to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. Parents see the 1 to 7 and nothing else, which makes a report card almost unreadable as a diagnostic. A student at grade 4 might be at band 6 on knowledge and band 2 on the real-world application criterion, and the only useful tutoring plan is the one that knows which.

The criterion names differ between subject groups, which adds to the confusion. Criterion A is some form of knowing and understanding almost everywhere. Criterion B is investigating, inquiring and analysing, or organising, depending on the subject. Criterion C is communicating or thinking critically. Criterion D is the application criterion: applying mathematics in real-world contexts, reflecting on the impacts of science, or thinking critically about a text. Ask the school for the criterion-level breakdown rather than the grade, and the conversation about MYP criteria A to D stops being abstract.

The practical point is that bands move for different reasons. Criterion A moves with retrieval practice. Criterion B moves with planning on paper before starting. Criterion C moves with subject vocabulary drilled as vocabulary, because precision of terminology is what the descriptors reward. Criterion D moves with one habit: answering the context before answering the maths or the science. Students who write the context sentence first, then the working, pick up the band they have been missing for two years, and it takes weeks rather than terms.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no hourly figure at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. So here is the market in dirhams, with the sources named and dated. These are market rates observed in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. Our own arrangement starts with one 30-minute trial lesson at no charge, with no card details taken, and a rate quoted for the specific subject group and session load after that.

The pattern across the market is consistent. Budget online tutoring, usually university students, sits between AED 45 and AED 150 an hour: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits carry the travel premium, AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, and TutorChase publishes AED 270. At the top, BartyED lists AED 650.

For a MYP Year 5 family the useful read is load rather than rate. One weekly session in a single weak subject group across the full year costs less in total than an intensive block in the final term, and it is the only spend that can affect a portfolio grade. The expensive pattern is the opposite: nothing until March, then two sessions a week in four subjects, of which only the on-screen ones can still move. MYP Year 5 tutoring in Dubai is cheapest when it starts in September and narrowest when it starts in March.

sections.heading: MYP eAssessment or IGCSE in Year 11: the decision UAE families actually face
paragraphs: This choice is usually made by the school rather than the family, but plenty of UAE parents face it directly, either because they are choosing between two schools or because a mid-year move has put it on the table. The honest comparison is not which qualification is harder. It is which assessment model suits the student and which administrative calendar the family can live with, because the two systems run on very different deadlines and the consequences of missing one are not the same.

The IGCSE side of the comparison can be stated with verified dates, and that is worth doing because it shows how early entry deadlines sit. Cambridge International runs June and November series, with a March series in some zones: for March 2027 the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026 and forecast grades 27 February 2027, with results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is the kind of operational detail that decides outcomes and appears on none of the competitor pages in this market. For MYP, the equivalent risk is not the timetable but registration: the subject list locks months out, and the ePortfolio subject cannot be changed afterwards.

sections.heading: The regulator, the tutoring permit and the mandatory UAE subjects
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools across the UAE, and only one of them appears with any regularity on competitor pages. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there; both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not just inspection sits with the emirate. The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Private tutoring itself is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with a two working day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anyone.

The third piece is the one that squeezes a Year 5 timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and prohibits combined classes outright. Standard Arabic is required as the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students, instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and any different or additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission. A MYP student therefore carries these lessons on top of eight subject groups, which is why the realistic weekly tutoring load is one subject, not three.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what the MYP does and does not do for a UAE university application
paragraphs: Parents often assume the IB MYP Certificate functions as a school-leaving qualification for Ministry of Education equivalency. It does not. Equivalency is assessed on the qualification a student leaves school with, which for an MYP student means the Diploma, or IGCSE and A-Levels if the family changes track. The MYP matters to that application indirectly and substantially: Year 5 results are what a school uses to place a student at higher or standard level in the Diploma, and the subject levels decided in July are what a university prerequisite list will later read.

The British-track requirements are published and worth stating exactly, because at least one page ranking in this market publishes the wrong subject count. Students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. On the American track, English proficiency requires IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB Diploma there is no points threshold any page should be quoting, including this one. Our sources do not include a figure read from the Ministry's own pages, so we are not publishing one. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly, and note that equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring service performs, guarantees or expedites. No tutoring is required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling urgency.

sections.heading: If the session is eight weeks away: triage, Ramadan and the Gulf Standard Time clock
paragraphs: Eight weeks out, the honest advice is to stop planning and start narrowing. The ePortfolios are closed or closing, so they are not where the time goes. Pick the two on-screen components carrying the most risk, usually the one with the weakest Year 4 criterion profile and the interdisciplinary examination, which is the component most often left unpractised. Run one full timed sitting in each during the first week. The two scripts tell you more about where the marks are going than six weeks of topic revision would, and they set the baseline the rest of the block works from.

Then build a MYP eAssessment revision timetable the student actually keeps. Two sessions a week, each one a full task set or half a paper under time, with the feedback written against criteria rather than topics. No new content after week six. Interface rehearsal in the final fortnight, twice at minimum. And a deliberate decision about what is being dropped, because a student attempting to improve five on-screen components in eight weeks improves none of them measurably.

Scheduling in the UAE has its own constraints and they are not minor. During Ramadan, school days shorten and concentration shifts; sessions move to post-Iftar slots, typically from 20:30, and that works better than forcing an afternoon slot nobody is awake for. Half-terms sit differently from the UK calendar, so a revision block planned on a UK timetable will collide with a UAE school holiday. Everything is scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, which also means a tutor matched outside the UAE teaches inside your evening rather than theirs. Where no UAE-based specialist is free for a niche subject group, the match is an IB-experienced tutor elsewhere teaching online in GST, and we say which before you book rather than after.
