sections.heading: What the MYP does and does not do for Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which the UAE Ministry of Education recognises a foreign school certificate, and it bites at the end of secondary school rather than at the end of MYP 5. The Personal Project is not a school-leaving qualification and nobody attests it on its own. What it can do is sit on an application as evidence of independent research, which some admissions readers value and none of them require.

The British-track requirements are published and specific. Students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which is a detail at least one ranking competitor page gets wrong.

The American track turns on test scores rather than subject counts: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test. Those figures come from reporting on the Ministry's clarification published in July 2026, and the same source states no IB points threshold at all.

That silence matters. No IB equivalency points figure in this project has been read on moe.gov.ae, so none is published here, and any tutoring site quoting one should be asked where it came from. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates — describe it, cite the authority, and apply through the official channel. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission, or for progression into DP1.

For a family in MYP 5 the practical consequence is sequencing. The equivalency file belongs to the end of Year 13 or Grade 12, not to this year. What belongs to this year is the project, the MYP subject grades the school reports, and the decision about whether your child continues into the Diploma Programme or moves to an A-Level or American pathway — because that choice, not the project, determines which equivalency route eventually applies.

sections.heading: Online project supervision support versus an in-home tutor in the UAE
paragraphs: The honest comparison starts with what the UAE market charges. Rates surveyed from published UAE provider pages in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45–150 an hour at the budget and university-student end, AED 150–300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180–500 for an in-home one-to-one visit with travel included, AED 200–450 and above where IB or IGCSE specialism is required, and AED 500–650 or more at the premium end. Those are market figures from other providers, not our price list.

Monthly shapes circulate too. Published packages seen during research included around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599–1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts monthly spend for a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240–600 at the budget end, AED 600–1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000–2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Dated figures from a named source beat a vague promise.

Where an in-home visit loses on a project specifically is tutor pool, not quality. A Personal Project in Design, Arts or Sciences needs somebody who knows that subject group's criteria, and the number of such people living within a reasonable drive of a given UAE address is small — much smaller in Al Ain, Ajman or Fujairah than in Dubai. Travel time is also real money: a Dubai school-run window can absorb forty minutes each way, and that sits inside the rate.

IB Gram delivers UAE tuition as one-to-one online lessons over live video; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For project work that is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise. The journal and the draft are on a shared screen, the plan is written in the session, the specialist is chosen by subject group rather than by postcode, and a 4pm slot and an 8:30pm slot cost the same. The first session is a free trial lesson.

process.title: Tell us the school, the emirate and the report deadline
process.description: The three facts that shape everything: which school, which regulator it answers to, and the date the report is due. We also ask which MYP year your child is in, because a Year 11 student at a school that switched to IGCSE at Year 10 has no project to submit and should not be buying support for one.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the goal and criteria on screen
process.description: The first session is free and it is diagnostic. The student brings the learning goal, the success criteria and the process journal as they currently stand. By the end of the hour you know which criterion is actually weak, roughly how many hours it needs, and whether the deadline you are working to is realistic.

process.title: A plan mapped to your school's own milestone dates
process.description: We lay the school's published dates for the three recorded meetings and the report deadline over the project, then work backwards. That produces the session pattern — weekly through the autumn, blocks before each meeting, concentrated in the final six weeks — rather than a generic weekly slot that peaks at the wrong time.

process.title: Weekly one-to-one sessions in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Lessons run over live video at a time that survives a UAE school week, around the mandatory-subject periods that cannot move. Each session ends with the student writing their own journal entry while the call is still open, so the evidence for criterion B accumulates as the work happens rather than being reconstructed in March.

process.title: A review before each recorded supervisor meeting
process.description: Before every one of the three documented meetings, the tutor reads the journal, lists the questions a supervisor is likely to ask, and rehearses the answers. The student walks in able to account for their own decisions, which is the point of the meeting, and the academic integrity form is checked for anything unsigned.

process.title: Report-stage review, then an honest stop
process.description: In the final weeks the work is criterion C and the format limit. The tutor reads the student's draft back with questions attached; the student makes every change. When the report is submitted the project work ends, and any continuing support moves to the subject groups your child carries into DP1 or Year 12.

whyPoints.title: The criteria taught as strands, not as a summary
whyPoints.description: Most project support explains that there are three criteria. We teach the seven strands behind them, because that is the level at which marks are awarded and lost. A student who can name what criterion A strand ii asks for can check their own work against it, which is the only version of this that keeps working after the sessions stop.

whyPoints.title: Built around the UAE school system, not around a generic IB page
whyPoints.description: Which emirate your school sits in changes who approved its calendar, how much a deadline can move, and who at the school may legally be paid to coach your child. We ask those questions before quoting a plan, and we name the regulators — including ADEK and SPEA, which almost nothing else in these search results mentions at all.

whyPoints.title: An academic-honesty line we state in writing
whyPoints.description: Sessions produce teaching, questions and feedback on the student's own work. No text is supplied, no part of a product is built, no journal entry is composed for them. We say this on the page and we hold it in the session, because the sites selling finished coursework in this market are exposing the student, not themselves.

whyPoints.title: Chosen by subject group, not by driving distance
whyPoints.description: A Design project and a Sciences project need different specialists. Online delivery means the pool is the whole network rather than whoever lives twenty minutes from your address, which matters most in Al Ain, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah, where IB provision is thin and local subject specialists are genuinely scarce.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are surveyed from other providers' published pages in October 2026 and labelled as such. Three of six competitor pages reviewed publish no price at all and two quote US dollars. Knowing the market before you talk to anyone is worth more than a discount, and the first lesson with us is free.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based specialist is free for a particular MYP subject group, we say so and offer the alternative — a specialist from our wider network joining the same live-video session — rather than taking the booking and hoping. Nothing in these search results discloses a coverage limit, and a disclosed limit is more useful than a silent one.

faqs.question: What is the MYP Personal Project and which school year does it fall in?
faqs.answer: It is an independent project completed in the final year of the Middle Years Programme, MYP 5 — Year 11 in most British-system UAE schools and Grade 10 in most American-system ones. The student chooses a learning goal rooted in a personal interest, creates a product, builds success criteria for it, keeps a process journal, meets a supervisor three recorded times and submits a report. The school assesses that report against three criteria worth eight marks each and reports a 1–7 grade. There is no external examination paper, which is why the deadline tends to be underestimated until the spring term.

faqs.question: Which criteria is the Personal Project marked against and how many marks does each carry?
faqs.answer: Three criteria, each marked out of eight, for 24 in total. Criterion A is Planning, carrying three strands: stating a learning goal and linking it to a personal interest, naming a product with appropriate success criteria, and presenting a clear detailed plan. Criterion B is Applying skills, with two strands on how Approaches to Learning skills served the goal and the product. Criterion C is Reflecting, with two strands on the impact of the work and the evaluation of the product against the stated criteria. The school converts the total into a 1–7 grade using the published project boundaries. Confirm the detail against your school's copy of the IB Projects guide.

faqs.question: How long can the report be, and does the bibliography count towards the limit?
faqs.answer: A written or electronic report runs 1,500 to 3,500 words. Oral formats such as a podcast and visual formats such as a film run 13 to 15 minutes. The bibliography and the appendices sit outside the limit, so citing properly and including journal extracts costs nothing in word count. If a student is over the limit the fix is structural rather than cosmetic: background sections no criterion asks for are the first to go, not individual adjectives. Check the current limits for your child's cohort with the MYP coordinator, since schools hold the authoritative version of the guide.

faqs.question: What is the process journal actually meant to contain?
faqs.answer: Dated evidence of thinking as it happened: decisions and why they were made, sources consulted, obstacles hit, skills practised, and what changed as a result. It is not a diary of hours worked and it is not written up at the end. Criterion B awards marks for how Approaches to Learning skills were applied, and that evidence has to exist in the journal before it can appear in the report. A journal with four entries, three of them from the opening weeks, is the most common reason a strong product still produces a mid-range grade. Extracts from it go into the report's appendices.

faqs.question: What does the MYP academic integrity form actually require?
faqs.answer: It records that the project developed under proper supervision. The student and the supervisor sign it, and it documents the supervisor meetings — a minimum of three across the project. Its purpose is evidential: a school facing a question about whether work is a student's own can point to a dated journal and a signed record of meetings. A project that appears fully formed late in the year with an unsigned form and a thin journal has no such trail. Ask your child's coordinator for the school's own version of the form at the start of the year rather than discovering it in February.

faqs.question: Where does a tutor's help stop and malpractice begin on this project?
faqs.answer: A tutor may explain what a criterion strand asks for, point to where a draft does not yet answer it, teach the skill a product needs, and ask the question that exposes a gap. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure a draft on the student's behalf, build any part of the product, choose the journal extracts, or compose journal entries. The working test: if a session ends with something on the page the student could not explain to their supervisor unprompted, the line has been crossed. An authentication failure lands on the student's result, not on whoever sold the help.

faqs.question: Does my child's project get moderated by the IB or only marked inside the school?
faqs.answer: The school marks it and standardises across supervisors so that grading is consistent. Where a school registers candidates for the IB MYP certificate, the personal project is submitted to the IB for moderation as part of that registration. Many UAE schools run the MYP without registering for the certificate, in which case the grade stays internal and appears on the school report only. Which applies to your child is a question for the MYP coordinator, and it is worth asking, because it affects how early the school's internal deadline sits before the grade is published.

faqs.question: My child's school is in Abu Dhabi under ADEK — does the regulator set the project deadline?
faqs.answer: No. The project deadline is set by the school's MYP coordinator, not by ADEK. What ADEK controls is the licensing and accreditation of the school itself, and press reporting also describes ADEK professional-ethics rules prohibiting private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. That second point is the one that affects a project term directly: if a supervisor offers paid extra hours, check the position first. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document rather than relying on a press summary, including this one.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies continue through the project term?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed for. KHDA calculates the weekly requirement on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson, and schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies — combined classes are strictly prohibited. Those periods are not spare capacity for project work. Plan the project around them, and expect assessment weeks in those subjects to collide with at least one milestone.

faqs.question: Will a UAE university accept the MYP on its own, or does my child need the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The MYP is not a school-leaving qualification, so it is not what a university admits on. Admission and Ministry of Education equivalency both work from the end-of-secondary certificate: the IB Diploma, A-Levels, an American high school diploma with the required test scores, and so on. The Personal Project can sit on an application as evidence of independent research, which some readers value and none require. The decision that matters in MYP 5 is which pathway your child continues into, because that determines the equivalency route. Check current requirements on moe.gov.ae rather than on any tutoring site.

faqs.question: Does a tutor we pay for project support need a UAE permit, and what should it say?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted online as unverified.

faqs.question: Can we pay our child's own school supervisor for extra project hours?
faqs.answer: Be careful. The MoHRE private tuition work permit's code of conduct bars a permit holder from serving students affiliated with their own school, and press reporting describes ADEK rules prohibiting Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled where they teach. Beyond the regulatory position there is an assessment problem: the supervisor marks the project, so paid coaching from the same person compromises the judgement the school relies on. Support from outside the school keeps the marking clean and the paper trail simple. Verify the current rules with the school and with ADEK.

faqs.question: What does Personal Project support cost an hour in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: Rates surveyed from published UAE provider pages in October 2026 run roughly AED 45–150 an hour for budget and university-student tutoring online, AED 150–300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180–500 for an in-home visit with travel included, AED 200–450 and above where IB specialism is required, and AED 500–650 or more at the premium end. Monthly packages seen included about AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' figures, dated and attributed, rather than our price list. Our first lesson is free, and the plan is quoted after that diagnostic session.

faqs.question: Our report deadline falls just after Ramadan — how do families plan around that?
faqs.answer: Shorten the school day, and the work that gets displaced is always the independent work. Treat the Ramadan weeks as reflection and report time rather than product-building time, because reduced hours and shifted energy suit reading a draft better than running an experiment or filming. Sessions can move to post-Iftar slots, and in Gulf Standard Time that is straightforward for an online lesson. The practical move is to pull the product completion date forward into January so that the final stretch is criterion C work, which is lower-intensity and far more forgiving of a disrupted timetable.

faqs.question: The product is behind schedule with six weeks to the report. Is it salvageable?
faqs.answer: Usually, but not by building faster. Marks come from the report, and the report is assessed on planning, skill application and reflection rather than on how impressive the product is. With six weeks left the priority is a product complete enough to evaluate against the stated success criteria, then a report that accounts honestly for what was planned, what was applied and what the student learned. A scaled-down product evaluated rigorously scores better than an ambitious one abandoned mid-build with nothing to reflect on. Scope reduction is a legitimate decision and should be recorded in the journal.

faqs.question: Does the Personal Project make the Diploma Programme Extended Essay easier?
faqs.answer: It makes the machinery familiar. Both are single long independent pieces with an allocated supervisor, recorded reflection sessions and an integrity declaration, so a student who has kept a real process journal already knows what reflection evidence looks like and why dated entries matter. The content demand is different: the Extended Essay is a 4,000-word academic research piece within a DP subject, and it is marked against its own criteria rather than the project's three. Students who struggled with criterion A planning in MYP 5 are the ones who need early Extended Essay support in DP1.

faqs.question: Who covers a Personal Project in a subject area no UAE-based tutor lists?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and then we offer the alternative rather than taking the booking regardless. If no UAE-based specialist is free for a particular MYP subject group — Design and the Arts are the usual pinch points — a specialist from our wider network joins the same live-video session instead, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time so nothing about your week changes. Nothing else in these search results discloses a coverage limit at all, and several providers route UAE families to numbers outside the country without saying so. A stated limit is more useful than a silent one.

ib-myp-personal-project-help.closingHeading: Start with the deadline, not with the search
ib-myp-personal-project-help.closingBody: Find the date your child's report is due, work backwards to when the product has to be finished and when the plan has to be real, and you will know immediately whether this is a planning job or a triage job. Bring that date, the current learning goal and the process journal as it stands to a free trial lesson, and we will tell you which criterion is actually weak and roughly how many hours it needs. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around your school's calendar. If no specialist in your subject group is free, we will say so.

ib-myp-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work in Middle Years Programme subject groups rather than in single exam syllabuses. Each is matched by subject group, MYP year and the specific criterion holding a grade down, and each works from your child's own task sheets and criterion-marked returns rather than a generic workbook.

intro.heading: What you are really paying for when you hire an MYP tutor
paragraphs: An IB MYP tutor in the UAE sits in the middle of the market, and the reason is structural rather than a discount. Online one-to-one support for a Middle Years Programme student runs roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour at the qualified-subject-tutor tier. Unitors publishes IGCSE support from AED 150 and IB support from AED 200, while Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. A Diploma Programme Higher Level specialist costs more because an external paper is coming. For most MYP students, no external paper is coming at all.

That changes what the money buys. A Diploma tutor is hired against a syllabus with published papers, weightings and grade boundaries. An MYP tutor is hired against four criteria, each marked out of eight, which a classroom teacher applies with professional judgement and reports as a single number from 1 to 7. The useful question is not what an hour costs. It is which of the four numbers on your child's last report is holding the grade down, and whether an hour a week is the right instrument for that particular problem. A parent who can read a criterion profile buys fewer hours and gets more out of each one.

Five variables move an MYP tutor cost in practice: the subject group, the MYP year, whether the student is in the eAssessment cohort, how many subjects are in scope, and how specialised the match has to be. Design and extended mathematics in MYP 4 and MYP 5 are thin specialisms anywhere in the Emirates, so they price above Individuals and societies or Language acquisition. A single criterion repaired in MYP 2 might take six sessions and nothing more. An MYP 5 student sitting on-screen examinations in two subject groups is a different budget entirely, and should be planned as a block rather than an open-ended weekly commitment.

Delivery is the part families want straight, so here it is. Every lesson IB Gram arranges for a UAE family runs live online, one-to-one, over video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the school run, prayer times and, in Ramadan, around Iftar. Home visits are a service offered only in India. The honest case for online here is not price. It is that a Sharjah family gets a Design specialist who has actually marked criterion B of the design cycle, rather than the nearest generalist who can reach Al Majaz by half past four on a Tuesday.

What follows is the arithmetic, in the order a parent needs it: how an MYP grade is assembled, what the UAE market charges for each kind of support, what moves that number, how online MYP tuition compares with the in-home model on rate and on tutor pool, MYP 5 counted backwards from the May session, the Year 10 fork between staying in the MYP and moving to IGCSE, and where the mandatory UAE subjects sit alongside all of it. Where a figure comes from a published source, the source is named. Where a date is unverified, the page says so plainly.

ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: The MYP is a five-year programme with a feeder below it and a decision above it, and the cost of support changes sharply between those stages. These four blocks are what a UAE family is actually buying across the middle of school, with the local wrinkle each one carries.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The feeder, and where most of the habits the MYP marks are first set. PYP has no grades and no criteria, which is exactly why MYP 1 can feel like a cliff: a student who has never been marked against a descriptor meets four of them at once. Support here is rarely subject tutoring. It is reading stamina, written structure and number fluency.
programmes.countryNote: Full-continuum schools in the Emirates run PYP straight into MYP 1, so the step is softer. Students arriving from a British or Indian primary into MYP 1 at a UAE international school meet criterion marking cold, usually in the first November report, and that report is where most MYP enquiries to us begin.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, years one to three
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, a minimum of 50 teaching hours in each per year, and integrated sciences rather than separate Biology, Chemistry and Physics. Assessment is entirely internal. The marks that move most here belong to criterion C and criterion D: communicating clearly, referencing consistently, and producing a reflection that cites evidence instead of feelings.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest and most useful place for a UAE family to buy hours. Six to ten sessions at the AED 150 to AED 250 band, spent on referencing and research questions, transfer across all eight subject groups and across the next four years. Most families here instead wait for MYP 5 and pay the eAssessment-year rate for the same lesson.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, years four and five
programmes.description: Sciences split into separate disciplines, mathematics splits into standard and extended, and the Personal Project runs across MYP 5 alongside everything else. Schools that offer MYP eAssessment enter students for two-hour on-screen examinations and moderated ePortfolios. Subject choice here closes options above it, which is why the hours bought in MYP 4 matter more than their price suggests.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE schools licensed for the MYP stop at MYP 3 and move the cohort onto Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE in Year 10. If yours does, the tutoring you need changes from criterion coaching to code-specific paper work on 0580, 0625 or 4MA1, and entry deadlines start to matter. Ask the coordinator which route the cohort takes before you book anything.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The destination for most MYP 5 students in the Emirates: six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Rates roughly double against MYP, because the work becomes examination craft against published papers and weightings, and because Internal Assessment supervision falls in an exam year.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to DP transition is where UAE families most often overspend, by buying Diploma hours in September of DP1 when the gap could have been closed in August for less. Extended mathematics in MYP 5 is the honest entry point for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches; standard mathematics points towards Applications and Interpretation.

ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: MYP subject groups are not exam syllabuses, so a tutor is matched to the group and to the criterion, not to a code. These are the groups UAE families ask about most, with what each one assesses and where the marks actually leak.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language, each out of eight. Students who read well often sit on 5s because criterion B organisation and criterion C conventions are marked separately from insight. The repair is structural: thesis placement, paragraph function and quotation handling, rather than more reading.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Phase placement is the hidden variable. A student parked a phase below their real level collects comfortable 7s that mean nothing, and one placed a phase above collects 3s that panic a parent. Check the phase on the report before buying hours, then target the productive skills, which carry the lower marks.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, thinking critically. Criterion B asks for a research question narrow enough to answer and sources evaluated for origin and purpose. Most lost marks here are process marks, not knowledge marks, and process is teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.levels: MYP 1-3 integrated · MYP 4-5 Biology, Chemistry, Physics
subjects.description: Criterion B inquiring and designing and criterion C processing and evaluating are where UAE science cohorts lose most. Writing a testable hypothesis with a scientific rationale, controlling variables explicitly, and evaluating a method against its own limitations are the three habits that move a 4 to a 6.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion C is communicating in mathematical form and criterion D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts, and the second is where strong calculators collapse. The extended course in MYP 4 and 5 is the route towards Analysis and Approaches, and it is the subject families most often leave too late.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The hardest MYP group to staff in the Emirates. Marks sit in the documented design cycle: a stated problem, a research-backed specification, annotated development work, and a testing plan written before the product exists. A generalist who has never marked criterion B of a design folder cannot help with it.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Assessed on investigating, developing, creating and evaluating, with the process journal carrying far more weight than parents expect. For ePortfolio candidates in MYP 5, the recorded process is the evidence. A tutor here coaches documentation and artistic intention; the work itself stays entirely the student's.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Often the quietest grade on a report and the easiest to lift, because criterion A knowing and understanding and criterion D reflecting are written tasks on anatomy, training principles and performance analysis. Students who perform well in the hall frequently under-write the theory.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary Units
subjects.description: Two subject groups assessed together against their own criteria, with an on-screen interdisciplinary examination for eAssessment candidates. Students treat it as an extra piece of work rather than a distinct skill, which is why it so often reports a band below the contributing subjects.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the MYP in UAE private schools and reported separately from the subject groups. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, with different curriculum expectations and languages of instruction, so the right stream matters more than extra hours for most families.

ib-myp-tutor.regionsTitle: Where MYP cohorts actually sit across the seven emirates
ib-myp-tutor.regionsIntro: The MYP is concentrated in a small number of full-continuum schools, which is why a neighbourhood tutor search for a Middle Years subject group so often fails. Here is what the map looks like emirate by emirate, and what it means for matching and for timing.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest MYP market in the country, inside a private sector of 227 schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25, of which International Baccalaureate programmes accounted for 7 per cent of enrolment. MYP tutoring in Dubai is the one place a subject-group specialist might also live nearby, though Design remains thin.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Fewer MYP cohorts than Dubai and spread much further apart, from the island out to Khalifa City and Al Raha. MYP tutoring in Abu Dhabi is where the online case is strongest: a 4.30pm slot survives a Corniche commute only in theory, and ADEK's ethics rules bar a teacher from paid tutoring of students at their own school.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: ADEK-regulated like the capital, with a handful of international schools and almost no local pool for MYP 4 and 5 sciences or extended mathematics. Families here are usually choosing between a generalist in the city and a subject-group specialist on screen, and the criterion profile should decide it.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by SPEA, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so an MYP timetable in Sharjah can differ from a Dubai one in genuinely material ways. Evening slots after the Dubai commute home are the normal pattern for working parents here.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority, with one established IB continuum school and a lot of cross-border enrolment into Sharjah and Dubai. Session timing has to absorb a long school run, which in practice means starting no earlier than 5pm.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education is regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. MYP numbers are small enough that a specialist in a thin subject group almost certainly does not live in the emirate, and no amount of local searching changes that.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under federal Ministry of Education supervision, with the smallest international cohort of the seven emirates and effectively no local MYP tutoring market. The mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirements still apply here exactly as they do in Dubai.

schoolClusters.note: The schools below run IB programmes in Dubai and are where most MYP enquiries to us originate. Several run the full continuum from PYP through MYP to the Diploma; read your own school's published inspection report for the phase and subject detail before deciding where hours should go.

A mixed cluster, and the mix is the point. Some schools here run the MYP to Year 11; others take the cohort into Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE at Year 10. Students we support attend both kinds, and the tutoring brief differs completely between them.

Thin on MYP cohorts and thinner still on resident subject-group specialists, which is why online matching does most of the work north of Dubai. Session timing in this cluster is built around the commute home rather than around the school bell.

ib-myp-tutor.modesIntro: MYP support works better as a defined block with a stated target than as an open weekly subscription, because the thing being fixed is usually a criterion rather than a syllabus. These are the three shapes UAE families use, all delivered online and one-to-one.

modes.title: Weekly criterion clinic
modes.description: One hour a week against one named criterion in one subject group, working from the student's own marked returns and task sheets. The target is set at the start from the report profile, and reviewed after six weeks against the next criterion-marked piece. This is the standard MYP 1 to 3 shape and the cheapest useful thing on this page.

modes.title: MYP 5 eAssessment block
modes.description: A fixed block of sessions across the spring term for students entered for on-screen examinations and ePortfolios. Two hours on screen under timed conditions is its own skill, separate from classroom criterion work, so the block practises it directly. Scope is set to two subject groups at most, because three rarely leaves enough homework time.

modes.title: Personal Project process coaching
modes.description: Fortnightly sessions across two terms of MYP 5, aimed at the three criteria the project is assessed on: planning, applying skills and reflecting. The coaching is about narrowing a goal, setting product criteria, keeping a dated process journal and reading the descriptors. The report and the product stay entirely the student's own work.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP tutor is actually hired to do
paragraphs: An MYP tutor is hired to move a criterion mark, not to cover a syllabus. Middle Years grades come from four criteria per subject group, each awarded out of eight, summing to 32 and converted to the familiar 1 to 7. Nothing in that chain involves an external examiner for most students. So the job is to find which of the four marks is low, work out whether it is a knowledge problem or a process problem, and fix the smaller of the two. That is a narrower brief than Diploma tutoring, and it is priced accordingly.

This is why the first conversation should be about a report, not about a timetable. A student on 7, 6, 4, 4 in Sciences has a communication and evaluation problem and needs perhaps eight sessions. A student on 4, 4, 6, 5 has a content and design-of-inquiry problem and needs something different. Both show a 5 on the report. A provider who quotes hours before seeing the profile is guessing, and guessing in this programme is expensive because it defaults to general revision, which is the one thing a mid-band MYP student usually does not need.

The second thing an MYP tutor does is protect the decisions above MYP 5. Subject choice in MYP 4, the standard or extended mathematics route, and whether the school takes the cohort into eAssessment or into IGCSE all narrow what is available in the Diploma. Hours spent making those decisions well are worth more than hours spent on content. A tutor who can explain what extended mathematics does to Analysis and Approaches eligibility is giving you something no worksheet provides.

What an MYP tutor is not hired to do is produce work. The Personal Project report, the ePortfolio tasks and every criterion-marked piece must be the student's own. A tutor teaches, reviews, marks against the descriptors and gives feedback. Any provider in this market offering a finished piece of assessed work is offering malpractice, and the student carries that risk, not the provider.

sections.heading: How an MYP grade is built: four criteria, 32 marks, one number
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group is assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, each marked out of eight. The four marks sum to 32, and the school converts that total into the 1 to 7 reported grade using the boundary table the IB publishes for the programme. The criterion names change between subject groups, which is the detail that confuses parents: criterion A is Knowing and understanding in Sciences, Analysing in Language and literature, and Knowing and understanding again in Individuals and societies. The letters are constant; the meanings are not.

The practical consequence is that two students with the same reported grade can need opposite interventions. A profile of 7, 7, 3, 3 and a profile of 5, 5, 5, 5 can both land on a 5. The first is a student who knows the material and cannot communicate or evaluate it; the second is evenly mid-band and needs a different kind of work. Ask the teacher for the criterion marks, and where the subject uses strands within a criterion, ask which strand was awarded. That request costs nothing and changes what you should buy.

Top-band descriptors in the MYP reward transfer and judgement rather than recall. A 7-8 band in criterion A usually requires terminology applied accurately in an unfamiliar situation. A 7-8 in criterion D usually requires a judgement supported by evidence on both sides with limitations named honestly. Students lose these marks for predictable reasons: describing instead of applying, reflecting on feelings instead of evidence, and treating referencing as presentation rather than as a marked requirement. All three are teachable inside a term.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs in the UAE, line by line
paragraphs: Online one-to-one MYP support in the UAE sits in the qualified-subject-tutor band, roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour as of October 2026. The published reference points are these: Unitors advertises IGCSE support from AED 150 and IB support from AED 200; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 at the budget online tier; Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 350 and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above; BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are the market's numbers, published by those providers, not an IB Gram price list.

Monthly packages circulating in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Read a package with two questions: do unused sessions carry forward, and does the rate change if you drop from two subject groups to one? A month containing Eid, half-term or a school trip has fewer usable weeks than the invoice assumes.

Context matters for judging any of this. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under a Dubai economic incentives package, so a tutoring line is the part of the education budget still moving. Against a school fee, two MYP sessions a week for a term is a small number; against the alternative of three subject groups tutored simultaneously for a year, it is the difference between a plan and a panic. sections.heading: The five things that move an MYP tutor cost
paragraphs: Subject group is the first variable, and it moves the price more than most parents expect. Design, extended mathematics and Arts for the ePortfolio route are thin specialisms across the whole country, so they price at the upper end of the band or above it. Individuals and societies, Language and literature and Physical and health education are the opposite: a strong pool, a lower band, and a realistic chance of a match inside a week. Nobody advertises this difference, but it is the single biggest driver of a quote.

MYP year is the second. MYP 1 to 3 support is generic enough that a good teacher in any humanities or science background can deliver it, and it prices accordingly. MYP 4 and 5 narrows to the specific course and, for eAssessment cohorts, to the on-screen format. The third variable is scope: one subject group at one hour a week is a budget; three subject groups is a different thing entirely and usually a sign that the problem is study habits rather than subject knowledge.

The fourth is urgency, and it is the one families control and routinely surrender. Six sessions booked in October against a named criterion cost less and achieve more than fifteen booked in April against a deadline. The fifth is match specificity: a tutor who has marked the criterion you care about, in the subject group you care about, at the MYP phase your child is in, costs more per hour and fewer hours in total. The arithmetic usually favours the specialist, but not always, and the report profile is what decides.

Two things should never appear on an MYP invoice. One is a premium for a named examiner, because the MYP is internally assessed for most students and examiner status is not a relevant credential here. The other is a charge connected to a tutor's permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a licensing fee passed to a parent is not a real cost.

sections.heading: Online MYP tuition against the in-home model
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real market in the Emirates and worth describing honestly. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500, with travel priced inside that number. Monthly in-home packages advertise at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Families choose it for the obvious reason: a younger student concentrates better with someone in the room, and a parent can see what happened. For MYP 1 and MYP 2 in particular, that is a legitimate preference and not a mistake.

The costs are travel and pool. Twenty to forty-five minutes each way across Dubai or Abu Dhabi at school-run hours is normal, and it is paid for either in the rate or in the slot that keeps slipping. The deeper constraint is who is reachable. An in-home search returns the tutors who live within driving distance of your community, which for Design in MYP 5 or extended mathematics may be nobody at all. Shortening the list to the geographically convenient is how a mid-band criterion problem gets handed to a generalist.

IB Gram delivers to UAE families as one-to-one online tuition over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the Emirates; home visits are an India-only service. The case for that model here is specific rather than general: the pool becomes national and international rather than local, the slot starts when the student sits down, screen sharing lets a criterion descriptor and a marked task sheet sit side by side, and the session leaves a written record the student can re-read. Those four things matter more in a criterion-marked programme than in a paper-based one.

sections.heading: MYP 5 counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools that enter students for MYP eAssessment sit the on-screen examinations in the May session, and almost everything that determines the result happens months before it. The sequence runs: a Personal Project proposal agreed with a supervisor early in MYP 5, eAssessment registration closed by the school, a process journal kept in real time, ePortfolio coursework finalised and uploaded in the spring, the Personal Project report submitted, then the examinations themselves. Each of those has an internal school deadline, and the internal deadline is the one that binds a family.

This page does not publish specific IB session or results dates. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a wrong date on a page like this is worse than no date, so the table below gives the sequence and the typical window and leaves the calendar to your MYP coordinator. Ask for the internal deadline list in September of MYP 5 and put it on a wall. Schools publish it; families routinely do not read it until the first one has passed.

Counting backwards changes what you buy and when. If ePortfolio tasks close weeks before the examinations, then Arts, Design, Language acquisition and Physical and health education support belongs in the autumn and early spring, not in the revision run-up. If the Personal Project report is due in the spring term, the planning and process-journal work belongs in the first term, when it is cheap and unhurried. Students who leave both to the same eight weeks pay specialist rates for work that is now too late to do properly.

One honest note on the result itself. The IB MYP Certificate requires results across eight components, including the interdisciplinary examination and the Personal Project, with a minimum total of 28 points from a possible 56 and a minimum grade in each, alongside the service as action requirement. Confirm the current requirement with your coordinator, because programme requirements are revised. No Diploma place in the Emirates depends on it, which is worth knowing before anyone buys crisis hours in April.

sections.heading: MYP or IGCSE at Year 10: the decision that changes your tutoring bill
paragraphs: A large share of UAE schools licensed for the MYP run it to MYP 3 and then move the cohort into Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE for Years 10 and 11. Both routes are legitimate and both lead into the Diploma, but they produce completely different tutoring briefs. MYP 4 and 5 work is criterion coaching spread across the year with internal deadlines. IGCSE work is code-specific: syllabus 0580 or 4MA1 in mathematics, 0625 in physics, with specimen papers, mark schemes, tier decisions and entry deadlines that sit months before the exam.

The deadline difference is the one that catches families. Cambridge's March 2027 series, for example, had final entries due on 27 November 2026, with the exam period running from 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February and results on Direct on 13 May. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November series, with June 2026 results issued to centres on 19 August 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong zone timetable. None of that machinery exists in the MYP.

For tutoring, the honest advice is to buy against what the student sits. If Year 10 begins an IGCSE syllabus, past-paper work and command-term fluency become the point, and a tutor who cannot name the syllabus code is the wrong tutor. If the student stays in MYP 4 and 5, criterion repair remains the point and past papers barely exist. The expensive mistake is hiring IGCSE-style drilling for an MYP student, which produces a well-drilled child whose criterion C mark has not moved.

Equivalency sits above both routes rather than inside them. The federal British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one accredited A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure; the sourced number is five. No IB points threshold for equivalency has been confirmed on the Ministry's own pages, so treat any quoted IB figure as unverified and check moe.gov.ae directly.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: No UAE private school runs the MYP on its own. Federal rules require private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed for, and in Dubai the KHDA mandatory-subject requirements apply to every private school whatever the programme. Those subjects appear on the report alongside the eight MYP subject groups, and they are frequently the grades a parent least understands and most often tries to solve with paid hours.

The structural detail matters before any money is spent. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic are required to hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited, which is a real constraint on what any tutor can legitimately bring to a session.

The practical sequence for a parent is therefore: confirm which stream your child is in, confirm the weekly minutes the school is delivering, and only then decide whether extra hours are warranted. A non-Arab student placed in a first-language Arabic class does not have a tutoring problem; they have a placement problem, and the school fixes it at no cost. Where tuition genuinely helps is vocabulary and script fluency for additional-language learners, and that work sits comfortably in the AED 150 to AED 250 band.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what an MYP tutor must refuse
paragraphs: The MYP is almost entirely internally assessed, which makes the honesty boundary sharper here than in an examination programme. Criterion-marked tasks, ePortfolio pieces and the Personal Project report are all submitted as the student's own work, and a teacher who suspects otherwise escalates it as a programme matter. The exposure sits with the student. A provider who crosses the line keeps the fee; the child carries the consequence, which can reach the loss of a result.

Here is the line in plain terms. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain a criterion descriptor, mark a draft against the descriptors and say precisely why a strand sits in the 3-4 band rather than the 5-6 band. A tutor may teach how to narrow a goal, how to keep a dated process journal and how to reference consistently. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph into its final state, hand over material that is then submitted, or take a piece of assessed work from first draft to finished. Those are different activities, not points on a spectrum.

This market contains providers who sell the second thing. One site found in research for these pages advertises finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger under IB rules, and a page that quietly competes with it on price is making the same offer in softer words. IB Gram does not take that work, and if a session drifts towards it the tutor stops and says why.

Two practical tests for a parent. First, ask what the student will produce between sessions: an honest answer names the student doing the work. Second, ask whether the tutor will work from the school's own task sheet and rubric, because a provider planning to supply content has no use for either. A tutor who asks to see the marked return before quoting hours is working the right way round.

sections.heading: The regulator, the inspection band, and whether you need a tutor at all
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools across the seven emirates, and which one covers your school changes what information you can get for free. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does so there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The emirate authorities do more than inspect. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the regulator approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits at emirate level rather than federally. Published inspection reports name strengths and weaknesses by phase and often by subject, which is free diagnostic information about the teaching your child is already receiving. Read the one for your own school before buying anything: a reported weakness in middle-phase science assessment practice tells you something a tutor cannot.

Two regulatory points bear directly on hiring. Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-based: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any circulating figure as unverified. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and it operates no office or centre in the Emirates. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific licence for a specific thing. Any provider describing its tutors as regulator-approved is describing something that does not exist in that form.

process.title: Send the report, not the timetable
process.description: Share the latest criterion marks for the subject groups in question, and the marked return if you have it. Ten minutes reading a profile of 7, 6, 4, 4 tells us more than an hour discussing availability. If the school reports strands within a criterion, include those too.

process.title: A trial lesson before any commitment
process.description: One session, no package attached, with the tutor marking a piece of the student's own work against the descriptors and explaining the band. You get a written note afterwards naming the criterion to target. If the match is wrong, say so and we change it rather than absorbing it.

process.title: A scope and a price for that scope
process.description: We quote against the number of subject groups, the MYP year and the weeks available, and we say which market band that sits in. If a thin subject group means a specialist in another time zone, you hear that before booking, along with the hours that actually overlap Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Six weeks, then a real review
process.description: The target is one criterion and the test is the next criterion-marked piece from the school. At six weeks we either name the next target or tell you the hours are no longer earning their place. Stopping on time is part of the service, and a tutor who never recommends it is not reviewing anything.

process.title: Replan at each MYP decision point
process.description: Subject choice in MYP 4, standard against extended mathematics, eAssessment or IGCSE, and the summer before DP1 are the four moments worth an unhurried conversation. Each one changes what is available later, and each is cheaper to get right in advance than to repair afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-first, not syllabus-first
whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched to the criterion holding the grade down, in the subject group it sits in, at the MYP phase the student is in. The brief starts from your school's own marked return and rubric, which is the only document that says what went wrong.

whyPoints.title: Published numbers, named sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or table that published it, with the month it was read. We do not present market bands as our own prices, and we do not publish a statistic without the number, the date and where it came from.

whyPoints.title: A national pool rather than a local one
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means a Design or extended mathematics specialist can be matched to a family in Fujairah or Al Ain as easily as in Jumeirah. The alternative is choosing from whoever is reachable by car, which in thin subject groups means choosing a generalist.

whyPoints.title: Hours that end
whyPoints.description: MYP support is planned as a block with a target and a review date, not an open subscription. We would rather tell you at week six that the criterion has moved and the hours can stop than keep a slot running because it was already in the calendar.

whyPoints.title: A clear honesty line
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, mark against descriptors and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not supply sentences for a Personal Project report, an ePortfolio task or any criterion-marked piece, and they will say so in the session if the question moves that way.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for the UAE week
whyPoints.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time around the school run and prayer times, shift to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan, and compress into intensive blocks in the long breaks when that suits the family better than a thin weekly hour.

faqs.question: How much does an IB MYP tutor cost per hour in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Market rates for online one-to-one MYP support run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour at the qualified-subject-tutor tier. Unitors publishes IB support from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 350 and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, while budget online providers advertise from AED 33 to AED 65. Those are the market's published numbers, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. We quote after a trial lesson and a conversation about scope.

faqs.question: Why does MYP tutoring cost less than Diploma Programme tutoring?
faqs.answer: Because the work is different. A Diploma Higher Level tutor is paid for examination craft against published papers, weightings and boundaries, and for Internal Assessment supervision in an exam year. Most MYP students sit no external paper at all; their grades come from four criteria a teacher applies in class. The specialism is narrower and the available pool is wider, so the hourly band sits lower. The exceptions are MYP 5 eAssessment candidates and thin subject groups such as Design or extended mathematics, where rates climb towards the Diploma band because very few tutors have marked that work.

faqs.question: My child's MYP report shows 5s in every criterion. Is that worth paying to fix?
faqs.answer: A flat profile of 5s usually means a student who understands the material and loses marks on the criteria that reward structure and judgement, typically C and D. That is a cheaper problem than it looks. Six to eight sessions on referencing, research-question framing and evidence-backed evaluation often move two criteria by a band without touching content. Ask the teacher which strand within each criterion was awarded, then buy hours against that strand. Paying for general subject revision when the profile is flat is the most common wasted spend we see in this programme.

faqs.question: How many criterion marks make up an MYP subject grade?
faqs.answer: Four criteria lettered A to D, each marked out of eight, giving 32 marks per subject group. Your school converts that total into the 1 to 7 grade on the report using the boundary table the IB publishes for the programme. Criterion names differ by subject group: criterion A is Knowing and understanding in Sciences and Analysing in Language and literature. Two students reported on the same 5 can have entirely different profiles, which is why the four numbers behind the grade matter far more than the grade itself for planning any tutoring.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for tutoring in MYP 1, or should we wait until MYP 4?
faqs.answer: MYP 1 to 3 is where the cheapest useful hours are. Criterion habits, such as referencing, framing a research question and writing a reflection that cites evidence, transfer across all eight subject groups and across five years. Buying them at AED 150 to AED 250 an hour in MYP 2 is better value than buying the same lesson in MYP 5 at the eAssessment rate with a deadline attached. Waiting is defensible when the profile is even and the student self-manages. It gets expensive once criterion C and D marks are already drifting.

faqs.question: What does MYP eAssessment involve, and does it need separate preparation?
faqs.answer: MYP eAssessment is the optional external route in MYP 5 that leads to the IB MYP Certificate. It combines two-hour on-screen examinations in subject groups such as Language and literature, Sciences, Mathematics and Individuals and societies, an interdisciplinary on-screen examination, and moderated ePortfolios in Language acquisition, Arts, Design and Physical and health education. It does need its own preparation, because answering on screen under timed conditions is a separate skill from classroom criterion work. Confirm with your MYP coordinator which route your school runs, since many UAE schools do not enter students at all.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP Personal Project without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. The project is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, and the report and process journal must be the student's own work throughout. A tutor can teach how to narrow a goal, how to set product criteria, how to keep a dated process journal and how to read the descriptors. A tutor must not supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph into its final state, or hand over material that is then submitted. Any provider offering a finished piece of assessed work is offering malpractice, and the student carries that risk.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do UAE MYP families usually book?
faqs.answer: One a week in a single subject group is the normal start in MYP 1 to 3, which at market rates lands around AED 600 to AED 1,000 a month. MYP 4 and 5 families often run one to two, and eAssessment candidates covering two subject groups two to three. More than three hours a week across subjects rarely helps a Middle Years student, because MYP work is set daily and the limiting factor is usually homework quality rather than teaching time. Start at one hour, set a target, and review after six weeks.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package cheaper than paying per session for MYP support?
faqs.answer: Packages advertised in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Per hour, the online package is often the cheaper unit. The risk is paying for a month containing Eid, half-term or a school trip, when several slots cannot be used. Ask two questions before committing: do unused sessions carry forward, and does the rate change if you drop from two subject groups to one? A package with neither answer in writing is a liability.

faqs.question: Our school teaches the MYP to Year 9 then switches to IGCSE. Which tutor do we hire?
faqs.answer: Hire against what the student sits, not what the school calls the programme. If Year 10 begins a Cambridge or Pearson syllabus, the work becomes code-specific, on 0580, 0625 or 4MA1, with specimen papers, tier decisions and entries closing months before the series. If the student stays in MYP 4 and 5, the work stays criterion-based and past papers barely exist. The transition term is the part worth paying for: command terms, mark-scheme language and timed papers are genuinely new, and six weeks of bridging usually covers the gap.

faqs.question: Does the MYP count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is assessed on the leaving certificate, not on Middle Years results, so the MYP itself is not what gets attested. For the British track, federal guidance requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. No IB points threshold has been confirmed on the Ministry's own pages, so treat any figure quoted elsewhere as unverified and check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation channel directly.

faqs.question: Are we paying twice if we hire an Arabic tutor the school already provides?
faqs.answer: Possibly, so check what the school is required to deliver first. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum is licensed, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is counted in 40-minute units. If your child is in the correct stream and the weekly minutes are being delivered, extra hours are a choice. If the stream is wrong, raise it with the school, which fixes it at no cost.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups do UAE families most often ask for help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and Sciences lead, mostly on criterion C and criterion D rather than content: processing data, evaluating a method and writing a reflection that uses evidence. Language and literature comes next, usually on criterion B organisation and criterion C conventions. Design is the quietest request and the hardest to staff, because its criteria reward a documented design cycle that few generalists have marked. Language acquisition requests cluster around phase placement, where a student sits a phase below or above what the report profile actually suggests.

faqs.question: Can MYP lessons move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes. Schools shorten the teaching day in Ramadan, so a 4pm slot that worked in January is usually wrong in it. Most UAE families move MYP sessions to after Iftar or to weekend mornings and keep the same tutor rather than the same time. Plan it a fortnight ahead, because every family reschedules in the same week and the good evening slots go first. The same thinking applies to the long summer break, where two intensive weeks often achieve more than eight thin ones spread across a term.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if no UAE-based MYP specialist is free?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a generalist. Thin subject groups, including Design, extended mathematics in MYP 5 and Arts for the ePortfolio route, sometimes have no UAE-resident specialist available in the slot you want. The options are then a specialist in another time zone whose working hours overlap Gulf Standard Time, a different slot with the right person, or a wait with a date attached. The rate quoted is the rate for the match you accept, and we do not bill a specialist rate for a generalist.

faqs.question: How do we tell a cheap MYP tutor from a bad one?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions. Which criterion are you targeting, and what does its top band actually require? What will my child produce between sessions, and how will you mark it? And will you work from the school's own task sheet and rubric rather than a generic workbook? A tutor at AED 150 who answers all three well is better value than one at AED 350 who answers none. Ask also whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years.

ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the criterion, then talk about money
ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step on an MYP enquiry is not a price. Send the latest report with the criterion marks for the subject groups you are worried about, and a marked piece of work if you have one. We read the profile, name the criterion that is costing the grade, and tell you how many sessions that usually takes and which market band it sits in. The first lesson is a trial with no package attached, and the tutor marks a piece of your child's own work against the descriptors so you can judge the match on evidence. Everything runs live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we offer only in India.

This page counts that year backwards from the last paper: when the entry closes, when the coursework decision has to be made, when timed papers start.
