ib-november-session-exam-preparation.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma subjects at Standard and Higher Level and work with second-attempt candidates as well as first. For a November entry you want the specialist for the exact paper that went wrong, not a generalist who covers the whole subject at surface depth.

intro.heading: What a November entry really asks of a UAE family
paragraphs: The IB runs two examination sessions a year. Almost every IB World School in the UAE sits the May one, because the academic year here starts in late August or September and finishes in June. That single fact is why November candidates in this country feel so isolated. The school calendar, the mock timetable, the revision clubs and the teacher availability are all built around May. A student entered for November is working against the grain of the building they sit in, and the plan has to be built deliberately rather than inherited from the year group.

Three groups of students end up in a November session. The largest is retake candidates: a result arrived in July, one or two subjects came in below what a university offer required, and the next available sitting is November. The second is students who transferred in from a school on a southern-hemisphere calendar, where November is the ordinary session and May is the odd one. The third, smaller group is students whose Diploma was not awarded on the first attempt because of a failing condition rather than a low total, and who need specific components resat.

Each of those three starts from a different place, and the preparation differs accordingly. A retake candidate already knows the syllabus and is fixing identifiable damage, usually concentrated in one or two papers. A transfer candidate may be mid-course and needs the content taught, not revised. A student resitting to satisfy a Diploma condition needs the narrowest plan of all, aimed at a single component and a single threshold. Buying the same weekly package for all three is how families spend money without changing an outcome.

The hard part is not the teaching. It is the sequence. Between a July result and a November paper there is a summer holiday, a new school term with its own coursework deadlines, an entry deadline that closes long before anybody feels ready, and in some cases a decision about whether an Internal Assessment is carried forward or re-submitted. Miss the entry window and no amount of tutoring matters. Leave the coursework decision until the autumn and the school may have no time left to process it.

So this page is a calendar first and a tutoring page second. Everything below is ordered by when it has to happen, counted backwards from the last paper rather than forwards from today. Where a date can be verified from a board's own published page, it is here with the source named. Where it cannot — and the IB's own session dates are the clearest example — the page says so and tells you exactly whom to ask instead of printing something that might be wrong.
bullets: November is the IB's second session; UAE schools overwhelmingly sit May, so local support is thin in the autumn term
Retake, transfer-in and condition-resit candidates need three different plans, not one package
The entry deadline, not the exam date, is the first date that can actually be missed
Carried-forward versus re-submitted coursework is a decision with a school-side deadline attached
Lessons here are one-to-one and online, so the specialist for a single failing paper is reachable from any emirate

ib-november-session-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: The November session belongs to the Diploma Programme, but a UAE family rarely deals with the DP in isolation. Siblings sit the MYP, primary children are in the PYP, and a minority of schools run the Career-related Programme. Here is how each sits against a November plan.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run 1 to 7 per subject with up to three bonus points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. The Diploma carries conditions as well as a total, which is why a student can hold a respectable score and still not be awarded the Diploma. A November entry is almost always about a specific component rather than a general lift.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the DP is a minority curriculum by volume and a strong one by reputation. International Baccalaureate students were around seven per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on UK curricula, and three of the seven new private schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 are IB schools. A November candidate therefore sits in a school where May is the default and where autumn-term teacher attention is already committed to the next DP2 cohort.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked A to D with published level descriptors, plus the Personal Project in the final year. Schools may opt into on-screen eAssessment for an external certificate; many UAE schools do not, and award school-based grades instead. Confirm with your coordinator which route your child's school takes, because it changes whether an external session window applies at all.
programmes.countryNote: Families with a DP2 retake candidate often have an MYP sibling in the same house, and the two calendars collide badly. MYP internal deadlines cluster in the autumn term in most UAE schools, exactly when a November candidate needs the quiet hours. Where both children need support, splitting the weekly slot so the November candidate holds the protected evening and the MYP student takes a weekend hour is usually the version that survives December.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and a language-development requirement. Students take DP subject courses alongside the career-related component, which means the same subject examinations and the same session structure apply to the DP courses inside a CP.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is rare in the UAE and a CP student needing a November entry for a DP course is rarer still. If that is your situation, the coordinator conversation matters more than anything on this page, because the career-related component sits on the school's own calendar while the DP course examinations sit on the board's. The two are not synchronised and nobody will synchronise them for you.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no external examinations, ending in the Grade 5 Exhibition. There is no PYP session, no entry deadline and no results day, so nothing in a November calendar applies to a primary child directly.
programmes.countryNote: It is listed here for one practical reason. In UAE households where an older sibling is preparing for a November session, the primary child's routine is the first thing that gets sacrificed, and a Grade 5 Exhibition that lands in the same term is genuinely demanding for a ten-year-old. Families who plan both calendars together in September rather than triaging in October tend to keep the younger child's work intact.

ib-november-session-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: A November entry is diagnosed by paper, not by subject. The notes below name where second-attempt marks are usually recovered in each subject, because that is the only question worth asking before a block of hours is booked.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Second-attempt marks in AA usually sit in method rather than knowledge. Candidates lose them in calculus manipulation under time pressure, in proof questions where the structure is not written down, and in the HL Paper 3 extended response where the early parts are gettable and get skipped. Rebuild the calculator-free paper first; it is where the gap between a 4 and a 5 most often lives.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI punishes poor reading more than poor algebra. Marks go in statistics questions where the test is chosen correctly but the conclusion is not written in context, in financial and modelling questions where units drift, and in HL matrices and graph theory left unpractised. A retake plan here is mostly timed technology-based questions with the written interpretation marked strictly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are where the second attempt is usually won. Paper 1 multiple choice rewards recall that decays over a summer, so it needs rebuilding early rather than revising late. Paper 2 extended response loses marks on state symbols, significant figures and explanations that describe an observation without naming the cause.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Candidates repeating Physics usually lose marks in the same three places: unit and prefix handling, graph work where a gradient has to be interpreted rather than calculated, and the explanation questions that need a chain of cause and effect in order. Mechanics and fields reward a rebuild; modern physics topics reward targeted recall work in the final month.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology is the subject where a November candidate most often discovers the problem was command terms, not content. Describe, explain, outline and suggest carry different mark expectations and a strong student who answers all four the same way plateaus. Data-based questions in Paper 2 are the most recoverable marks on a short timeline.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks that are either earned cleanly or lost entirely: axes labelled, curves named, the new equilibrium marked. Evaluation is the other half. A retake plan concentrates on the fifteen-mark questions, where a correct explanation without a judgement caps the mark, and on HL Paper 3 policy calculations.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case study is the examination. Candidates repeating Business Management usually need less theory and more disciplined application to the pre-released material, with tools selected deliberately rather than listed. Quantitative items — ratios, break-even, cash-flow forecasts — are reliable marks that a second attempt should bank first.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis is where second attempts move, because it can be practised intensively without rereading the whole course. Paper 2 comparative essay depends on texts already studied, so a November candidate works from existing notes. The individual oral is internally assessed and sits on the school's calendar, not the session's.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic matters twice over in the UAE: as a Diploma subject and as a Ministry-mandated subject running alongside the licensed curriculum. For a Diploma retake, productive writing under time and the unseen text response are the recoverable areas. Written accuracy is marked against published descriptors, so targeted correction work converts faster than general practice.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be named, dated and used, not gestured at. Candidates lose marks by describing a study accurately and failing to link it to the question's demand. A second attempt usually needs a tightened bank of studies — fewer, better known — plus deliberate practice on the extended response command terms.

ib-november-session-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: Where your child sits changes who regulates the school, how a late or private entry is handled, and how far a family is from any local DP specialist in the autumn term. Lessons here are online, so the emirate changes the context rather than the access.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, with 227 private schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25. The deepest pool of IB schools in the country, which also means the most competition for DP teacher time in the autumn when the new DP2 cohort absorbs it. An IB Diploma retake in Dubai is common enough that coordinators know the process well.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so an IB retake tutor in Abu Dhabi is almost always external to the school by design rather than by preference.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. Fewer IB schools and longer distances mean a November candidate here has very little chance of finding a subject specialist locally for a single failing paper. This is the clearest case in the country for taking the lesson online rather than taking whoever is nearby.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah families commute into Dubai for school, which pushes the realistic start of an evening session later than parents expect.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A November session candidate in Ajman frequently attends school in Dubai or Sharjah, so the plan has to survive a commute at both ends of the day.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like SPEA, approves curricula and assessment methods as well as fees. The IB footprint is small, and a retake candidate here is often the only one in the school, which makes an external plan the default rather than a supplement.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory on the east coast. Distances are real and the number of DP specialists resident in the emirate is very small, so online delivery is not a compromise here — it is the only way a specific Paper 3 specialist is reachable at all.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market in the country. Families often look across the border to Sharjah or Dubai for schooling, and a November candidate's evening slot has to be set after the commute home rather than at the time the timetable suggests.

schoolClusters.note: The schools where a November entry is most likely to be processed without friction, simply because the coordinators handle enough DP candidates to have seen it before. Ask the coordinator directly what the school's internal deadline is for a November registration; it will be earlier than the board's.

ADEK territory, where school staff may not take paid private tutoring of their own enrolled students. Families here are used to external support as a matter of policy, and the practical question is only whether the external tutor knows the specific paper rather than the subject in general.

A thinner IB map across SPEA, the RAK Department of Knowledge and the Ministry of Education. A November candidate in this cluster is frequently the only one in the year group, which makes the school's willingness to process a second-session entry worth confirming in writing early.

ib-november-session-exam-preparation.modesIntro: A November plan has four distinct phases and they do not all want the same format. These are the shapes families actually book, in the order they usually book them.

modes.title: Single diagnostic session on the returned results
modes.description: One session, before anything else is agreed, spent on the statement of results and the component breakdown rather than on teaching. The output is a written list of which papers cost marks and which topics inside them, ranked. Families who skip this step tend to buy hours for the subject that feels worst rather than the paper that scored worst, and those are often different.

modes.title: Summer intensive block
modes.description: The weeks between results arriving and the new term starting are the only uncontested hours in a November plan. An intensive block here rebuilds content while nothing else competes for the evening. Two or three sessions a week through the summer does more than one session a week through a crowded autumn term, and it costs the same per hour.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the autumn term
modes.description: From the start of term to the first paper, a protected weekly hour per subject, moving from content to timed questions as the weeks close. This is the phase where a November candidate competes with the school's own DP2 timetable for attention, so the slot has to be fixed and defended rather than rearranged weekly.

modes.title: Coursework review sessions on the student's own work
modes.description: Where a component is being re-submitted rather than carried forward, sessions work on what the student has already produced: criterion by criterion, against the published descriptors. The tutor teaches the criteria and questions the student's reasoning. The student is the author throughout, and the school submits through its own process.

sections.heading: What the IB November session is, and who in the UAE actually sits it
paragraphs: The IB examines twice a year. The May session is the one almost every UAE school uses, because the academic year here runs from late August to June. The November session exists for schools on a southern-hemisphere calendar and for candidates who, for one reason or another, are sitting papers outside their school's ordinary cycle. A November session candidate in the UAE is therefore an exception inside their own building, and that is the single most useful thing to understand before planning anything.

Most UAE November candidates are retake candidates. The pattern is familiar: results arrive in July, a university offer needed a 6 in Chemistry HL and a 5 came back, and the next sitting is November. Some are students who moved from Australia, New Zealand, South Africa or Argentina mid-course and whose school enters them in the session they started in. A smaller number are resitting specific components because a Diploma condition was not met — a failing grade in a Higher Level subject, or a core requirement — rather than because the total was low.

What those students share is a timetable nobody around them is following. The school's mock season is built for DP2 students sitting in May. The revision sessions, the past-paper clinics and the teacher's free periods are allocated to that cohort. A November candidate who waits to be swept along with the year group will be preparing on their own in October with no plan. The work of this page is to replace that drift with a sequence, and the sequence starts from the last paper and counts backwards.
bullets: Retake candidates: fixing one or two identified papers, syllabus already known
Transfer-in candidates: mid-course, needing content taught rather than revised
Condition resits: narrowest plan of all, aimed at a single component threshold

sections.heading: The November year, counted backwards from the last paper
paragraphs: Every family plans forwards from today and every exam calendar works backwards from the paper. The table below is the second version. Timings are given relative to the first paper rather than as dates, because the IB's own session windows are not reprinted here and because your school's internal deadlines will sit earlier than the board's anyway. Take the relative positions, put your child's actual paper date at the right-hand end, and the diary writes itself.

Two rows matter more than the rest. The registration row is the only one with a hard edge: if the school does not pass the entry to the IB in time, the November session simply does not happen for your child, and every hour bought before that point is wasted. The coursework row is the one families forget. Whether an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge component is carried forward from the first attempt or re-submitted is a decision with a school-side process behind it, and the school needs notice.

The rest of the sequence is about not doing things in the wrong order. Content rebuild comes before exam technique, because practising papers on topics the student cannot yet do produces demoralising marks and no learning. Timed papers come in the last six to eight weeks, when there is enough content in place for a mark to mean something. The final week adds nothing new. Families who compress this and start timed papers in month one usually arrive in November with a thick folder of low scores and no diagnosis.

sections.heading: Reading the statement of results before you buy a single hour
paragraphs: A statement of results is not one number. It carries a grade per subject, the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay grades, the bonus-point outcome and, through the school, a component-level breakdown. That breakdown is the whole diagnosis. A 4 in Physics HL built from a weak Paper 1 and a respectable Paper 2 is a different problem from a 4 built the other way round, and the two need different tutors, different hours and different exercises.

Ask the coordinator for the component marks before booking anything. Then look for three patterns. First, a single paper far below the others, which usually points at a format problem — timing, command terms, multiple-choice recall — rather than a knowledge gap. Second, a flat profile across all papers, which points at content and takes longer to fix. Third, an internally assessed component dragging a strong externally assessed profile, which is a coursework conversation and not a revision one.

This is also where an honest conversation about reach belongs. A one-grade move on a single paper over a full autumn term is a reasonable target for most committed students. Two subjects moving two grades each, from a standing start in September, with the same school workload continuing, is not a plan — it is a hope with invoices attached. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child. What a good diagnostic gives you is a realistic answer before the money is spent.

sections.heading: What November preparation costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Most pages in this market refuse to publish a number. The table below is the market, assembled from rates those providers published themselves and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. They are not IB Gram's prices and they are not quoted as ours. They exist so you can tell whether a quote you have been given sits inside the normal range or outside it, and so you can budget before you start rather than after.

Two things drive the number more than anything else. The first is specialism: a tutor who teaches one subject at Higher Level and knows the paper structure costs more per hour than a generalist, and for a single failing paper the specialist is usually cheaper overall because the plan is shorter. The second is format. A visiting tutor's travel time is inside the hourly rate whether anyone says so or not, which is why in-home bands sit above online bands for the same level of expertise, and why two-hour minimums are normal for visits.

Cost in context helps too. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package, so the tuition line in a household budget is the part that moved this year, not the school fee line. A November plan priced at two subjects for one weekly hour each across an autumn term is a real number worth writing down before the first session rather than discovering in November.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one versus a visiting tutor for a second-attempt candidate
paragraphs: Parents in the UAE search for a home tutor because that is the phrase the market has used for twenty years, and it is a fair question to ask. A visiting tutor who sits at the kitchen table has real advantages for a young child: presence, attention, no device between teacher and student. For a sixteen-to-nineteen-year-old repeating a Higher Level paper, the balance tips the other way, and it tips on availability rather than on preference.

The constraint is arithmetic. A visiting tutor can only teach the families inside a reasonable drive, and the number of IB Diploma specialists for any one paper who happen to live within that radius is small — in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain it is frequently zero. A November candidate does not need a tutor who covers Physics. They need the one who knows why Paper 1 multiple choice collapsed and what to do about it in nine weeks. IB Gram delivers that as one-to-one tuition online, over live video, to every emirate; home visits are a service offered only in India.

There is a second, quieter advantage for a retake plan. Online sessions leave evidence. The paper is screen-shared, annotated during the lesson and kept, so the student revisits the marked version a week later rather than remembering a conversation. For a candidate whose whole plan is built on diagnosing and fixing identified damage, that written trail is the plan's memory. The table sets the two formats side by side on the things that actually differ.

sections.heading: Why an entry deadline sits months before the paper
paragraphs: Families routinely discover the entry deadline after it has closed, because it is counter-intuitive: the exam is in November, so surely the paperwork is in October. It is not. Boards build timetables, print papers, allocate centres and distribute materials internationally, and all of that work runs off the entry list. The list has to be closed long before the first candidate sits down.

The IB's own session dates are not printed on this page, for a specific reason given below, so the worked example here comes from the two boards whose dates are published and verifiable. Cambridge International's March 2027 series shows the shape plainly: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, and final entries were due on 27 November 2026 — more than two months before the first paper, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Direct from 13 May. Pearson Edexcel's International GCSE November 2026 series runs to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Two further details from Cambridge's own guidance are worth knowing even if your child sits the IB, because they describe how exam administration works everywhere. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The lesson transfers directly: the timetable that matters is the one your child's centre is given, not the one a parent downloads.

sections.heading: Coursework on a second attempt, and exactly where the honesty line sits
paragraphs: For a repeating candidate the coursework question arrives early and it has two parts. The first is procedural: is the component carried forward from the first attempt or re-submitted for the new session? That is a rules question for the DP coordinator, decided once and recorded, and it has a school-side deadline attached. The second part is the one that gets families into trouble, because a re-submitted piece is being improved under time pressure by a student who has already been disappointed once.

The IB's academic-honesty rules do not soften for a retake. The work must be the student's own, and malpractice findings can cost a candidate the Diploma rather than a few marks. There is a market in this region that sells finished assessed work at a price; one researched provider advertises completed Internal Assessments. Buying that is not a shortcut, it is an expulsion risk carried by the student, and no legitimate tutor should go near it.

What a tutor may do is substantial, and it is where the marks actually are. Teaching the assessment criteria letter by letter, with their mark allocations, so the student knows what each one rewards. Asking the questions an examiner would ask about the student's own method and data. Pointing out that a criterion has no evidence behind it yet. Explaining what a command term requires. The student remains the author of every sentence, and the school submits through its own process. The table below draws the line task by task.

sections.heading: Results, equivalency and the university calendar after a November sitting
paragraphs: A November candidate's results arrive well after the August cycle that most university admissions systems are built around, and that gap is the thing to plan for in September rather than in January. Before entering, establish in writing what your child's target universities will do with a result that arrives late: hold the offer, defer entry by a year, move to a January intake, or require a fresh application. Admissions offices answer that question readily by email, and the answer changes whether a November entry is the right move at all.

The UAE adds its own step. Secondary certificates used for local university admission go through Ministry of Education equivalency, and the published requirements are curriculum-specific. For the British track, the Ministry's requirements as reported in July 2026 are five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing, with at least 450 in SAT Mathematics.

For the IB there is no points figure on this page, and that is deliberate. The equivalency requirement for the Diploma has to be read on moe.gov.ae or confirmed with the emirate's attestation channel, because at least one competing page in this market publishes a subject count for IGCSE candidates that does not match the Ministry's own published rule. Equivalency is a process the Ministry performs, not something a tutoring platform performs or expedites, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. Open the file early, because document attestation takes longer than families expect.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in a repeat year
paragraphs: A UAE student repeating Diploma subjects is still a student in a UAE school, and the Ministry-mandated subjects do not pause for a retake. Private schools in the country are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with those requirements due to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

The organisational detail matters for planning an evening. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

Two practical consequences follow. First, these periods sit in the school day and cannot be traded away to make room for retake revision, so the time has to come from the evening and the weekend instead. Second, for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, so support here means working with the school's own material rather than importing a substitute scheme. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

sections.heading: The three ways a November plan actually fails
paragraphs: The first failure is administrative and it is the most common. Nobody confirms the entry. The family assumes the school is handling it, the school assumes the family has decided, the deadline passes quietly and the discovery happens in October. Fix it by getting the registration confirmed in writing by the coordinator, with the subjects and levels listed, and by treating that email as the start of the plan rather than a formality after it.

The second is diagnostic. Hours are bought for the subject that feels worst rather than the paper that scored worst, and three months later the student has had thirty sessions on content they already knew while the actual problem — timing on Paper 1, command terms in extended response, a collapsed internal assessment mark — is untouched. The cure is the component breakdown and a diagnostic session before any package is agreed. It costs one hour and it reorders everything after it.

The third is scheduling, and it is the one families underestimate. A November candidate is carrying a full school timetable, the Ministry-mandated subjects, the autumn term's own deadlines and, in many households, a commute between emirates. A plan built on five evenings a week survives about three weeks. Two protected slots that actually happen beat four that get cancelled, and the summer block exists precisely so the autumn plan can be light enough to hold. Build the schedule around what will still be true in week eight.
bullets: Confirm the entry in writing, with subjects and levels, before buying hours
Diagnose by component, not by subject, and do it before the package
Protect two slots that will hold rather than planning five that will not
Put the heavy content work in the summer, while nothing competes for it

process.title: Send the statement of results and the component marks
process.description: Share the statement of results, the component-level breakdown from the coordinator and the target the result has to reach, with the university or offer condition behind it. That is enough to say honestly whether November is the right session and which papers the hours should go to.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson with the subject specialist
process.description: One session with the tutor who would actually teach the plan, not a sales call. It is spent on the weakest paper, so you see how the tutor works on the real problem. No block of hours is agreed before that lesson has happened and you have decided it was useful.

process.title: Fix the calendar backwards from the paper
process.description: Put the first paper at the right-hand end, then mark the registration confirmation, the coursework decision, the school's internal deadlines and the start of the timed-paper phase. The weekly slot is chosen after the commute home, on Gulf Standard Time, and written down as fixed.

process.title: Run the summer block, then the term plan
process.description: Content rebuild in the weeks before term, two or three sessions a week while nothing competes. From the start of term, one protected hour per subject per week, with marked work between sessions, moving to full timed papers in the last six to eight weeks.

process.title: Review at session six, and change the tutor if it is not working
process.description: Six sessions is enough evidence to judge. If the marked work is not moving and the student cannot say what changed, the match is wrong and a different specialist is arranged. That is a normal outcome, not a complaint, and it is better found in week six than in week sixteen.

whyPoints.title: A calendar, not a package
whyPoints.description: The plan is built from the entry deadline and the school's internal dates backwards, because those are the dates that can actually be missed. Families get the sequence in writing at the start, including what should be finished before the timed-paper phase begins.

whyPoints.title: Paper-level specialism, reachable from any emirate
whyPoints.description: Because lessons are online, the tutor is chosen for the specific paper that lost marks rather than for living nearby. In Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain that is the difference between a specialist and whoever is available.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before invoices
whyPoints.description: The first hour reads the component breakdown and produces a ranked topic list. If that reading says the gap is not reachable by November, you are told so before a block of hours is sold, and the sensible alternative is discussed instead.

whyPoints.title: Clear academic-honesty boundaries, stated first
whyPoints.description: On a second attempt the coursework pressure is real. The boundary is set in the first session: criteria taught, reasoning questioned, evidence gaps named, and the student the author of every sentence. Work is submitted by the student through the school's own process.

whyPoints.title: Sources named, dates you can check
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to whoever published it and dated. Cambridge and Pearson dates are cited to the board's own page. IB session dates are not printed here at all, because they could not be verified from the IB, and a wrong date is worse than no date.

whyPoints.title: Independent, with nothing to protect
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any school, school group or examination board. That means the advice can be that November is the wrong session for your child, or that one subject is worth the hours and the second is not.

faqs.question: What exactly is the IB November session, and which students in the UAE sit it?
faqs.answer: The IB examines twice a year, in May and in November. UAE schools almost all use the May session because the academic year here runs from late August to June. November candidates in this country fall into three groups: retake candidates fixing one or two subjects after a July result, students who transferred in from a school on a southern-hemisphere calendar where November is the normal session, and students resitting specific components because a Diploma condition was not met. All three are exceptions inside their own school, which is why the preparation has to be planned deliberately rather than inherited from the year group.

faqs.question: My son's school only enters candidates in May. Can he still sit papers in November?
faqs.answer: That is a question for the DP coordinator and it should be asked early, in writing. Registration for an IB session is submitted by the school, not by the family, so the school's willingness and its internal deadline govern everything. Many UAE coordinators have handled November entries before, particularly in Dubai where the IB cohort is largest. Some schools in the smaller emirates will not have, and the conversation takes longer. Ask what the school's own cut-off is for a November registration, get the subjects and levels confirmed in an email, and treat that email as the start of the plan.

faqs.question: How long is the gap between a July result and a November paper, and what should fill it?
faqs.answer: Roughly four months, and the shape of it matters more than the length. The first three weeks go to diagnosis: the component breakdown from the coordinator, read paper by paper, turned into a ranked list of topics. The summer weeks before term are the only uncontested hours in the whole plan, so heavy content rebuilding belongs there, two or three sessions a week. Once term starts, the school timetable, the Ministry-mandated subjects and the autumn deadlines compete for every evening, so the term phase should be light, fixed and focused on timed papers rather than new content.

faqs.question: If only one subject went wrong, does the whole Diploma have to be taken again?
faqs.answer: No. A candidate can be entered for individual subjects in a later session rather than repeating the whole Diploma, and that is the usual shape of a November entry from the UAE. What varies is the coursework: whether an internally assessed component is carried forward from the first attempt or re-submitted for the new session is decided under IB rules by your coordinator, and it has a school-side deadline. Get that decision made and recorded about five months before the paper, because leaving it to the autumn term can leave the school without enough time to process a re-submission.

faqs.question: Can the same Internal Assessment be used again for a second attempt?
faqs.answer: Sometimes it is carried forward and sometimes a new or revised piece is submitted, and the answer is set by IB regulations as applied by your school's coordinator rather than by preference. Ask the question explicitly and get the answer in writing, because the two routes imply very different autumn terms. If a component is being re-submitted, the student is producing improved work under real time pressure, and that is exactly the situation in which academic-honesty boundaries have to be clear before the first session rather than discovered afterwards.

faqs.question: Will a November result arrive in time for a September university start?
faqs.answer: Often not, and that has to be established before entering rather than afterwards. November results are released well after the August cycle most admissions systems are built around. Email the admissions office of each target university and ask what they do with a result that arrives late: hold the original offer, defer entry by a year, move to a January intake, or require a new application. The answers differ by university and by country, and they frequently change whether a November entry is worth doing at all. Treat that email thread as part of the decision, not as paperwork afterwards.

faqs.question: Does a second-attempt grade replace the first one on the certificate?
faqs.answer: Ask the coordinator for the current rule as it applies to your child's registration, because how results from more than one session are recorded and reported is governed by IB regulations rather than by anything a tutoring platform can state on your behalf. What matters practically is what the receiving university sees and uses, and that is a question for the admissions office in writing. Both answers should be in hand before the entry is confirmed, because together they determine whether sitting again changes the outcome your family actually cares about.

faqs.question: How many subjects can realistically be prepared for one November sitting?
faqs.answer: Two is normal and sustainable alongside a full school timetable. Three is possible for a transfer-in candidate whose whole programme is on the November cycle, because then the school day is working with the plan rather than against it. For a retake candidate carrying DP coursework, Ministry-mandated subjects and a commute, three subjects at a meaningful depth usually means four or five evening sessions a week, and plans of that size tend to collapse in about three weeks. Two protected slots that actually happen beat four that get cancelled.

faqs.question: What do UAE families actually pay per hour for second-session support?
faqs.answer: Market rates published in this region, read in October 2026, run from about AED 45-150 an hour for a generalist tutor online, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB Diploma specialist. A visiting tutor sits higher because travel is inside the rate, roughly AED 180-500, usually with a two-hour minimum. Named or examiner-level tutors are advertised up to AED 650. Those are other providers' published figures, not IB Gram's prices, and they are here so you can tell whether a quote you have been given is normal.

faqs.question: The summer holiday sits in the middle of our plan. Should sessions stop?
faqs.answer: The opposite. The weeks between results arriving and the new term starting are the most valuable hours in a November plan, because nothing else is competing for them. That is where content rebuilding belongs, at two or three sessions a week, so the autumn term can be light enough to survive alongside school. Because lessons are online, a family travelling in summer keeps the same tutor and simply agrees a different clock for a few weeks. Families who pause through the summer and start in September are, in practice, planning a ten-week preparation rather than a four-month one.

faqs.question: Why does this page describe the November timetable without printing its dates?
faqs.answer: Because the IB's own session dates could not be verified from the IB for this page, and a wrong exam date is worse than no exam date. Secondary sources circulate windows for upcoming sessions, but ibo.org is the only source that should govern a family's diary, alongside your school's DP coordinator, who receives the timetable your centre will actually use. The Cambridge and Pearson dates quoted on this page are different: those boards publish them openly and each one here is cited to the board's own page. Ask your coordinator for the session dates and put those in the diary.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education equivalency file care which session my child sat?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is about the certificate and the grades, not about the month the papers were sat, but the timing matters practically because a late result means a late file. For the British track the Ministry's published requirements are five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at E. The Diploma requirement should be read on moe.gov.ae or confirmed with the emirate's attestation channel. Equivalency is the Ministry's process, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies still take timetable space in a repeat year?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and in Dubai KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies in all private schools. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Those periods sit inside the school day and cannot be traded for retake revision, which is why the extra hours have to come from the evening and the weekend, and why the summer block matters so much.

faqs.question: What is a tutor allowed to do with a second-attempt coursework piece?
faqs.answer: Teach the assessment criteria letter by letter with their mark allocations, ask the questions an examiner would ask about the student's own method and data, point out where a criterion has no evidence behind it yet, and explain what each command term requires. What a tutor must never do is supply sentences, data or analysis that then appear in the submission. The student is the author throughout and the school submits through its own process. There is a market in this region selling finished assessed work; that is a malpractice risk carried by the student, and it can cost the Diploma.

faqs.question: Is a private candidate entry possible if the school will not register him?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether an authorised IB school near you accepts external candidates for the session, and that is a question to put to schools directly and early rather than to assume either way. Some centres take external entries and some do not, and the ones that do have their own deadlines and conditions. Start by asking your child's current school, then approach other IB schools in the emirate. If no route exists for November, the honest conversation is about the next available session and what the extra months should be used for, which is a better outcome than discovering the problem in October.

faqs.question: How quickly can a specialist for one specific paper be matched, and what if none is free?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days once the component breakdown has been shared, because the request is specific: a Higher Level tutor for one named paper rather than a general subject tutor. Where no specialist is free for the hour a family needs, you are told that rather than offered a near-match, and the options are a different time slot, a different start date, or a tutor outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time. Coverage is thinnest for minority subjects and for Higher Level Paper 3 work, and the honest version of that is worth more in September than in October.

ib-november-session-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Start with the component marks, not with a package
ib-november-session-exam-preparation.closingBody: An IB November session plan lives or dies on two things: an entry confirmed in writing, and a diagnosis made at paper level before any hours are bought. Send the statement of results and the component breakdown, take the free trial lesson with the specialist who would actually teach the plan, and fix the calendar backwards from the first paper. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered online on Gulf Standard Time, to every emirate. If the reading says the gap is not reachable by November, you will be told that before anything is sold, and what to do with the extra months instead.

ib-online-tuition.tutorsIntro: The cards below are IB subject specialists rather than generalists with a timetable to fill. Each is matched to one syllabus at one level, teaches live over video, and starts with a trial session so you can judge the diagnosis before you buy a single paid hour.

intro.heading: The hour is the unit, so start by pricing the hour
paragraphs: Everything in IB online tuition in the UAE is sold by the hour, and the hour is where every honest question lives. A parent in Jumeirah and a parent in Khalifa City are both handed a figure - AED 180, AED 300, AED 500 - with no account of what sits inside it. Of the providers currently ranking for this search, three publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family pays school fees in. So the first job of this page is arithmetic: what the market charges, in dirhams, and what the money is buying.

The second job is harder. Price in tutoring does not track effort; it tracks scarcity. A Standard Level Biology hour is inexpensive because a great many people can teach it. A Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches hour in the fortnight before an Internal Assessment deadline is expensive because the pool of people who can read a student's exploration, find the modelling error and explain it inside forty minutes is small - and smaller still within a one-hour drive of any particular villa. Live online delivery changes that arithmetic, which is exactly why it changes the price.

The third job is to say plainly what we sell. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send anyone to a UAE address; home visits are part of our India service only. That is not a hedge about quality. It is the reason a family in Fujairah can book a Chemistry HL specialist at all, instead of choosing from whoever happens to live twenty minutes away. A table further down costs both formats over a full term, travel and cancellations included, and lets the numbers make the argument.

What this page does not do is quote an IB Gram rate card by subject. Rates move with level, with the week of the year and with how scarce the specialist is, and a page that pretends otherwise is either stale or quietly wrong - one ranking provider contradicts its own prices within a single page. Every AED figure below is a market figure, read in October 2026 from what UAE providers publish and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. Where our own model comes up, we point at the free trial lesson and the conversation that follows it.

Read what follows as a budget rather than a brochure. There are sections on what a sixty-minute session contains minute by minute, on what the family side costs once, on which ten hours return the most marks, on how the Gulf Standard Time slot you ask for changes the tutors you can afford, and on what a tutor is permitted to do with an Internal Assessment. There is also the part no competitor prints: what happens to your money when you cancel, pause or stop altogether.
bullets: Published market rates, October 2026: roughly AED 33-150 budget online, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject teacher, AED 200-450+ for an IB specialist
Advertised packages: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, against AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits
A 5pm Gulf Standard Time slot competes with the British school day; an 8pm slot does not, and the rate reflects it

ib-online-tuition.programmesIntro: The IB runs as four separate programmes, and the cost of help differs across them far more than most price lists admit. A primary hour and a Diploma Higher Level hour are not the same product, do not need the same frequency, and should not carry the same rate. Here is what each one asks for in the UAE.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examinations, so tuition here is almost never about exam technique. It is about number fluency, reading stamina and writing at length - the three things that quietly decide how a child copes in Year 7. Sessions are short, usually forty-five minutes, and weekly consistency matters far more than hours bought. This is the cheapest band in the market and the one where a careful generalist is genuinely enough.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the PYP year carries a load the programme itself does not set. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA builds instructional time around a 40-minute lesson unit. Many non-Arab families first ask for help here, not in maths, and the request lands years before anyone mentions the Diploma.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against criteria A to D in every subject, marked out of eight each, and that is where families lose ground without noticing. A student can know the content and still score a 4 because the task asked for analysis and received description. Tuition in the MYP is mostly criterion translation: reading the task sheet, naming what the criterion wants, and practising the form of answer that earns it. Fortnightly often beats weekly at this stage.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Year 11 is the fork in the road for UAE families. Some schools run MYP to Year 11 and then the Diploma; others switch pupils to IGCSE for Years 10 and 11. The two routes leave different gaps at DP1, and the September hours needed to close them differ. Ask the school which route your child's cohort is on before buying any block of hours.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where the money goes. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the Internal Assessment in each subject - all on deadlines set by the school months before the May session. Specialist hours cost the most here because the specialist pool is narrow: somebody who teaches Physics HL and nothing else is rarer, and more useful, than somebody who teaches all three sciences.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma families buy hours in two bursts: September to February for coursework, then the eight weeks before the first paper. Market rates are tightest in that second window, which is the argument for fixing a slot in January rather than April. Confirm the session dates with your school's IB coordinator and on ibo.org; we do not publish IB exam dates we cannot verify.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Fewer schools run it than the Diploma, so finding help is a matter of unbundling it: the DP courses inside the CP are taught by the same specialists who teach them in the Diploma, and the reflective project needs supervision of process rather than subject content.
programmes.countryNote: Because the CP is less common in the UAE, local in-home coverage for it is thin to non-existent in most communities. This is one of the clearest cases where live online tuition is not a compromise but the only realistic route to a subject specialist, and the hourly rate is the standard DP rate rather than a premium.

ib-online-tuition.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects UAE families book most often, with what the hour is actually spent on in each. The rate differences between them are not arbitrary: they track how many people can teach the thing well and how concentrated the marks are in the parts students get wrong.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most expensive routine hour in the Diploma, because the HL pool is small and the content is unforgiving. Hours go on calculus, proof and the modelling demanded by the exploration. Students who switched from MYP maths usually need three or four hours just on algebraic fluency before the HL content can land at all.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Cheaper to staff than AA and often the better route, but the statistics and the graphical-display-calculator work catch students out. The AI exploration lives or dies on whether the data set is real and the model is justified. Maths AA and AI are not interchangeable for university entry, so the route choice is worth an advisory hour on its own.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks are lost in two places: the algebra inside a physics question, and the written explanation that asks why rather than how much. HL adds the options and a heavier data-analysis load. An hour here is usually half method teaching and half marking a past-paper question live, with the markscheme open on the shared screen.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics absorb most paid hours, and the Internal Assessment absorbs the rest. The HL specialist pool in the UAE is thin outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi, which is where live online delivery changes what a family can actually buy rather than just how it is delivered.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content is learnable from the guide; the marks sit in command terms and in data-based questions on Paper 2 and Paper 3. The cheapest useful hour in the sciences, and the one where a careful non-specialist can still help, as long as the Internal Assessment work goes to somebody who has supervised scientific investigations before.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation phrasing decide grades more than content recall. The three commentaries in the portfolio are where most support is bought, and they are also where the honesty line matters most: the tutor reads the student's draft and names what is missing, and the student writes every sentence.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, techniques and theories applied to a real organisation, plus an Internal Assessment that depends entirely on the quality of the chosen research question. Two hours spent on narrowing that question in October saves a family six hours of rescue work in February, which is the cheapest trade available in the subject.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral, Paper 1 guided analysis and the HL Essay need different skills, and students often prepare for all three the same way. An hour here is close reading plus timed writing, with the extract on the shared screen and the annotation done by the student while the tutor watches and intervenes.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A subject where live screen sharing is genuinely better than a tutor in the room: the code, the error and the terminal are all visible to both at once. Hours go on the solution development in the Internal Assessment and on the paper-based theory students neglect because the programming feels like the real work.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
subjects.levels: Ministry streams and IB Language B or ab initio
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the IB in UAE private schools and almost never mentioned in a tutoring price list. Handwriting means the student writes on paper under a phone camera or on a tablet with a stylus. Arab and non-Arab streams follow different expectations, and KHDA requires them to be taught in separate classes.

ib-online-tuition.regionsTitle: Where the family is, and what it does to the price
ib-online-tuition.regionsIntro: On a live video lesson your postcode stops deciding which tutor you can have and starts deciding only which slot suits the household. That is a bigger change in some emirates than others. Here is what the local picture does to availability, to timing and to what families end up paying.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest local tutor pool in the country and the highest in-home rates, because travel across Sheikh Zayed Road at 5pm is priced into the hour whether or not it is itemised. Online, Dubai families mostly buy the same specialists as everyone else and simply get more choice of slot.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Many families commute into Dubai schools, so the school day ends late and the realistic slot is 6pm or later. SPEA regulates private education in the emirate and approves fees, curricula and assessment methods, which is why a Sharjah school's calendar can differ from a Dubai one.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK licenses and accredits the private schools here, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school. For families on the islands and in Khalifa City that rules out the obvious shortcut and makes an independent specialist the normal route.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with fewer IB schools than the capital and a correspondingly thin local pool of Higher Level specialists. The in-home premium is highest exactly where the choice is smallest, which is the clearest arithmetic case for live online one-to-one in the country.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Diploma specialists in the emirate are scarce, and a visiting tutor for a niche HL subject is often simply unavailable at any rate rather than expensive.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula and assessment methods. RAK families routinely find that the nearest subject specialist is an hour and a half away, so the online rate is the only rate that holds.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory on the east coast, with the longest distances in the country between a family and an IB specialist. Online delivery removes travel from the invoice entirely, and the only remaining constraint is agreeing a Gulf Standard Time slot that suits the household.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the UAE and the one every competitor page ignores. Local in-home coverage for Diploma subjects is close to nil; live online one-to-one puts a UAQ family on exactly the same specialist list as a Dubai Marina family.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai had 227 private schools teaching 17 curricula in 2024-25, with 387,441 students enrolled and the IB at a 7% share. Seven more schools open for 2026-27, three of them IB, adding 16,846 places. Students we support in Dubai sit the Diploma at schools of this kind.

ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools across the emirate, including Al Ain. Families here mix IB and British curriculum schools, and a Diploma student in Al Ain often has a shorter school day but a longer drive to any specialist.

SPEA regulates Sharjah, RAK's Department of Knowledge regulates Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The IB footprint is smaller here, which is precisely why online access to subject specialists matters more.

ib-online-tuition.schoolDisclaimer: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform: the schools named above are context for where students on this page study, and no affiliation, endorsement or partnership with any of them is implied.
ib-online-tuition.modesIntro: Four patterns cover almost every UAE family that buys IB online tuition. They differ in what they cost per month and in what they are good for, and picking the wrong one is the most common way a tutoring budget gets wasted. Choose the pattern first, then the rate.

modes.title: Fixed weekly slot, one subject
modes.description: Sixty minutes a week on the same day at the same Gulf Standard Time, for one subject at one level. The standard arrangement and the one that produces visible movement in a term, because the student has something to do between sessions and the tutor has marked work to react to.
bullets: Four hours a month, around AED 800-1,200 at mid-market specialist rates
A written note after each session saying what was covered and what was set
The slot is held for the term, which matters more than the rate in exam season
Reviewed at the half-term against the student's own marked school work

modes.title: Two students, one screen
modes.description: Siblings or classmates on the same subject and level share a slot and split the cost. Each child gets roughly half the direct attention and the same named specialist, which is a sensible trade for content revision and paper technique and a poor one for anything individually assessed.
bullets: Cost per student roughly halves; attention per student roughly halves too
Both students must be within a grade or so of each other to work
Not used for Internal Assessment work, which is individual by rule
Useful for IGCSE pairs sitting the same board and the same tier

modes.title: Document clinic for the IA, EE and TOK
modes.description: A longer session, usually ninety minutes once a fortnight, built around a draft the student has already written. The document is on screen, the criteria are beside it, and the tutor names what is missing against each one. The student makes every change afterwards, in their own file.
bullets: Booked a fortnight apart, so there is time to act between readings
Criteria read out in full before any comment on the text
Feedback is spoken and summarised in notes, never typed into the student's document
Your school's academic-honesty policy and deadlines take precedence over ours

modes.title: Hour bank for the final eight weeks
modes.description: A block of hours bought for the run-up to the papers and drawn down as the student needs them, paper by paper. Flexible when study leave makes a fixed slot impossible, and the only pattern that reliably survives an exam timetable.
bullets: Ten hours at mid-market rates sits around AED 2,000-3,000
Agree the expiry date in writing before paying for the block
Sessions booked against specific papers, not against days of the week
Usually sits alongside, not instead of, the standing weekly hour

sections.heading: What a sixty-minute IB online tuition session actually contains
paragraphs: A good hour of live online one-to-one has a shape, and you can hear it from the next room. The first five minutes are not teaching: they are the tutor finding out what happened since last week, which piece of marked work came back, and what the student could not do. Skipping that is how an hour gets spent on the wrong topic at full price.

The middle of the session splits roughly in half. One part is teaching - a method worked slowly on a shared screen, with the student writing it out rather than watching. The other part is practice under observation: a real past-paper question, attempted by the student while the tutor watches the working appear and interrupts at the point the error is made rather than after it. That second half is the part a recorded course cannot do, and it is most of what the hourly rate is for.

The last ten minutes set the week. A specific task, a specific deadline, and a note the parent can read. Where there is no task, the next hour starts from the same place as this one, and you pay twice for the same ground. The practical test of whether an hour was worth AED 250 is whether anything existed at the end of it that did not exist at the start: a corrected script, a written method, a task in the student's own handwriting. If three sessions pass with nothing written down at either end, the hour has become a conversation, and a conversation is not what the rate is for.

sections.heading: Why the same online hour sells for AED 150 and for AED 500
paragraphs: The bands below are what UAE providers published in October 2026, read from their own pages, plus the in-home range in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. They are market figures, not IB Gram prices. What the table shows is that the word online explains almost none of the spread. Three other things do: who is teaching, what the hour is allowed to contain, and how scarce that person is in the slot you want.

At the bottom of the range you are buying supervision. A university student or a generalist works through the textbook, checks homework and answers questions. For a Year 8 who has fallen behind on fractions, that is the correct purchase and paying more would be waste. At the top you are buying diagnosis: somebody who has taught that syllabus at that level, who can read a script and name the three marks the student keeps dropping, and who can do it inside forty minutes. Those are different products with a shared job title.

Treat the premium band with particular care. Rates above AED 500 are usually marketed on examining history, and examiner status is only worth paying for if it can be evidenced and if it is current. No tutor, however experienced, has access to unreleased papers or boundaries, and anybody implying otherwise is selling something they should not. Ask what the hour contains, ask what the last five students at that level were working on, and compare that with the band below it before paying the difference.

sections.heading: A term of twenty-four sessions, costed in both formats
paragraphs: This is the comparison the question deserves. Parents searching for home tuition in the UAE are not wrong to want a tutor in the room, and the honest answer is not that the format is bad - it is that a term of it costs more than the rate card suggests, and that the price buys a smaller choice of teacher. IB Gram delivers one-to-one online, so we have an interest here; the table is built from published market figures rather than from our opinion, and the arithmetic is reproducible.

Two lines do most of the work. The first is minimum session length: a visiting tutor rarely comes for less than ninety minutes, because a shorter visit does not repay the drive, so you buy the minimum rather than the amount of teaching your child actually needs. The second is the pool. A visiting tutor must live within a reasonable drive of your community; an online specialist only has to be awake at your Gulf Standard Time slot. For Standard Level Biology in Mirdif that difference is small. For Higher Level Chemistry in Al Ain or Fujairah it is the difference between a specialist and the nearest available adult.

Nothing here says a tutor in the room is worthless. Younger children, students who will not sit still for a screen, and families who want the household to see the lesson happen all have a real case for it. What the lines below show is the full cost of that case, including the hours lost when the Dubai evening peak decides whether five o'clock means five o'clock. sections.heading: What the family side costs, once
paragraphs: Every online tuition page assumes the household is already equipped, and most UAE households nearly are. Still, the first session goes better when three things are sorted beforehand, and the total one-off outlay for a family that owns a laptop is usually under AED 300. The figures below are indicative UAE retail ranges read in October 2026, not charges from us, and they vary by retailer.

The item that makes the most difference per dirham is a wired headset with a microphone. Laptop speakers and a laptop microphone produce an echo the tutor has to talk over, and an hour of that is exhausting for a fifteen-year-old who is already behind. After that comes a way for the student to write rather than type. Maths and science working has to be seen as it appears, so either a stylus and tablet, or the free version: prop a phone over the page, share its camera, and write on paper as normal.

The last requirement costs nothing and gets ignored most often. A room with a door, and a household agreement that the hour is not interruptible. Sessions taken at the kitchen table with a younger sibling in the room are the single most common reason a paid hour returns nothing, and no amount of specialist expertise fixes it. Agree the hour with the family, not only with the student. One more thing belongs in the preparation rather than the shopping: the last marked piece of school work, scanned and sent across before the session starts, so the first five minutes go on the diagnosis instead of on uploading a photograph. Families who do that get noticeably more out of the same sixty minutes, at no extra cost whatever.

sections.heading: Session length, frequency, and where more money stops buying marks
paragraphs: Families usually ask how many hours a week. The better question is what shape those hours take, because the same monthly spend produces very different results depending on how it is cut. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session put a budget tutor at AED 240-600 a month, a mid-market tutor at AED 600-1,200, and a specialist in an exam year at AED 1,000-2,000 or more. Those are the envelopes most UAE families are working inside.

Within that envelope, two separated hours generally beat one double session for teaching, and one long session beats two short ones for coursework. The reason is simple: teaching needs gaps for the student to attempt something and fail at it, while a draft needs an uninterrupted run at the data, the method and the criteria. Families who book ninety minutes weekly for ordinary term-time teaching are paying for minutes the student stopped absorbing at about the fifty-minute mark.

There is also a point where buying more hours is the wrong purchase altogether. If a student cannot name what they got wrong in the last school assessment, the next hour should be diagnostic rather than additional. And if three subjects are weak, two hours a week on one subject will move that subject while the other two drift. One properly fixed subject a term is a realistic outcome at one hour a week; three subjects fixed at once is not, at any rate. The cheapest sequencing is usually to take the subject with the most marks at stake first, finish it, and then move the same slot onto the next one rather than splitting the week three ways from the start.

sections.heading: Gulf Standard Time is the line in the price nobody prints
paragraphs: Gulf Standard Time is UTC+4, and that single fact quietly decides what an hour of IB online tuition costs a UAE family. A 5pm slot in Dubai is 1pm in Britain in winter, which is the middle of the British school day, so experienced British classroom teachers cannot take it at any price. By 8pm Gulf Standard Time the same teachers are free. The specialist pool available to you is not fixed; it is a function of the clock you ask for.

The slots UAE families want most are also the scarcest. School runs finish, homework starts, and everybody asks for 4pm to 7pm. That window has the deepest competition among local families and the shallowest supply of international specialists, so it carries a premium that has nothing to do with teaching quality. Shifting a Higher Level session to 7.30pm or 8pm typically widens the choice of teacher and eases the rate for exactly the same hour.

Timezones also decide which currency you are quoted in. North American pools find a UAE late-afternoon slot comfortable in their own morning, which is why so many of them compete for the 4pm to 6pm window and quote in dollars. Indian specialists are 90 minutes ahead of Gulf Standard Time, so both the early and late UAE slots sit in a normal working evening for them, which is why supply is deepest and the specialist rates at the lower end of the band come from there.

sections.heading: If you can only buy ten hours, here is where they go
paragraphs: Most families do not have an unlimited budget, and the useful skill is not finding the cheapest hour but spending ten of them where the marks are concentrated. Three or four of those hours belong to the Internal Assessment at draft stage. The IA carries a fifth of the final grade in most Diploma subjects - confirm the current figure for your child's subject in the school's copy of the subject guide - and it is the only component where a second reader can look at the actual work before it is submitted.

Three more hours belong to the single paper the student is weakest at, spent on real past-paper questions marked live rather than on re-reading notes. Two hours belong to technique: command terms, timing, and what a markscheme rewards as opposed to what feels like a good answer. The remaining hour is best held back for the week before the first paper, when a student usually knows exactly what they are frightened of and an hour aimed at that is worth three aimed at everything.

What returns least is content revision the student could do alone from the guide, and what returns nothing at all is an hour booked without a piece of real marked work in front of it. Where a family can buy only a handful of hours, we say so at the trial lesson rather than selling a weekly slot that will not fit the budget to the end of the term. Ten well-aimed hours beat twenty unaimed ones, and that is not a sales line - it is why the diagnosis comes first.
