process.title: Send us the dates, not just the worry
process.description: The school's term dates, the conference dates, the benchmark window and - in Grade 5 - the Exhibition presentation week. Four dates and a sentence about what is going wrong is enough for us to say honestly whether paid hours are the right answer and when they should start.

process.title: Bring the two numbers the school already has
process.description: A reading band or standardised score with the date it was taken, and a piece of your child's unedited writing. Those cost nothing, they exist in almost every UAE primary, and they tell a tutor more in five minutes than a paid diagnostic does in an hour.

process.title: A free first lesson, one per family
process.description: One introductory one-to-one session at no charge, before any payment is taken and with no card required. For a primary child it is as much about whether the child will talk to this adult as about the subject. If the answer is no, we try a different tutor rather than asking you to persist.

process.title: A dated block, with a finish line
process.description: We write the plan as a number of sessions ending at a specific school date - the January benchmark, the mid-year conference, Exhibition presentation week. Open-ended primary tuition is how families end up paying for months after the gap closed.

process.title: Review against the school's next measurement
process.description: Not against our own assessment. When the next dated school number arrives we compare it to the one we started from and decide together whether to continue, change shape or stop. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we will say so when it is the right one.

process.title: If no specialist is free, we say so
process.description: For narrow primary requests - Arabic as a first language at lower primary, for instance - the right tutor is sometimes not available for the slot you need. We will tell you that and offer a waiting list rather than putting a generalist in front of your child and charging for it.

whyPoints.title: The plan is dated, not open-ended
whyPoints.description: Every primary plan we write ends at a date your school set: a benchmark window, a conference, a presentation week. It makes the hours countable in advance and it makes stopping a normal decision rather than an awkward conversation.

whyPoints.title: Session length is set by the child's age
whyPoints.description: Twenty-five to forty-five minutes for primary, twice a week rather than once, because fluency and recall build on frequency. No travel is involved, so splitting a weekly hour into two costs nothing extra in time.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated on the page, not in the small print
whyPoints.description: One-to-one lessons over live video into every emirate, timed to Gulf Standard Time. Visiting tutors are a service IB Gram runs in India only. You will not find a promise of a doorstep visit anywhere on this site for a UAE address.

whyPoints.title: Figures are attributed or absent
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page belongs to the provider that published it, read in October 2026. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no star rating and no IB examination date, because none of those could be sourced to a standard we would want quoted back at us.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary is published
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, model and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not produce Exhibitions, Internal Assessments or essays, and they do not supply board papers or mark schemes as downloads. At primary level that boundary is a habit being taught, not a legal formality.

whyPoints.title: No regulator is claimed as a sponsor
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA and the federal Ministry of Education are described on this page because they shape your child's school. None of them approves, accredits or endorses IB Gram, and any provider telling you a regulator has approved its individual tutors is describing something that does not exist.

faqs.question: Does an IB PYP home tutor in the UAE actually come to the villa, or is the lesson on video?
faqs.answer: The lesson is on video. IB Gram delivers one-to-one PYP tuition over live video into every emirate, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and visiting tutors are a service we run in India rather than in the Emirates. We use the phrase home tutor because it is what parents search for, and the honest translation is a tutor who works with your child at home over a screen. For a primary child the practical gain is that one weekly hour becomes two shorter sessions, since nobody is paying for a drive across Dubai between families at five in the evening.

faqs.question: There is no PYP examination, so what is there to plan a tutoring calendar around?
faqs.answer: Four things, all of which your school already publishes. The reading assessment in the first weeks of term one. The two parent-teacher conferences. The standardised benchmark window most UAE primaries run, commonly in January. And in the final year, Exhibition presentation week. Those are the dated items a primary plan is built from. Collecting them takes one email to the class teacher, and it converts an open-ended worry into a finite block of sessions with a review point. Without them, support gets bought in reaction to a report comment, which is the most expensive way to buy it.

faqs.question: When in the UAE school year should primary support actually start?
faqs.answer: September, in most cases. A UAE primary year contains roughly thirty genuinely teachable weeks once the settling fortnight, the winter break, Ramadan, Eid and the school's own assessment weeks are taken out, and the longest uninterrupted run of them is the block from September to mid-December. A reading or number gap needs about twenty-four short sessions, and there are only two points in the year where twenty-four useful weeks still exist. Starting in April is not a shorter version of the same plan; it is a different plan with narrower aims, and it should be described that way.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the PYP Exhibition should we bring in a tutor?
faqs.answer: About ten, counted back from your school's presentation week. The sequence that works is question at ten weeks, sources at eight, notes at six, structure at four, rehearsal in the last fortnight. Families who come to us two weeks out are asking for help with slides, which is the only thing still movable at that point and the least valuable. Ask the PYP coordinator for the presentation date in September rather than February - it is set by the school, not by the IB, and in several years of the cycle the research weeks land across Ramadan.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge Primary Checkpoint and when is it sat?
faqs.answer: It is an external test at the end of the Cambridge primary stage, and Cambridge publishes test series in March, May and October each year, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint on the same windows. Several UAE schools run Cambridge primary provision alongside or instead of a purely school-based programme, so some PYP families meet it on transfer. The school enters candidates and the entry closes well before the tests are sat. If your child's school runs it, ask which series and which administrative zone timetable applies, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Grade 3. How far away is her first externally dated examination?
faqs.answer: Between one and five years, depending entirely on the pathway. If her school runs Cambridge primary provision she may meet a Checkpoint series within a year or two. If she stays in the MYP, the first externally marked qualification is years away and the MYP's own assessment is largely school-based before that. If she moves to a British track, the first binding date is a Year 11 entry deadline. The useful thing to know now is that the date which actually cannot move is an entry deadline, not an examination, and that the school submits it rather than the parent.

faqs.question: Which deadline does a Grade 5 family really need in the diary?
faqs.answer: Exhibition presentation week, and nothing else. It is the only hard date in the Primary Years Programme and your school sets it, so it is not published anywhere you could look it up. Everything else in the exit year arranges itself around it: the research block sits in the ten weeks before, rehearsal in the final fortnight, and the MYP transition conversations before and after. The second date worth having is the first graded task in MYP 1, which usually arrives within six weeks of the new year starting and is where criterion marking first becomes real.

faqs.question: Does the Primary Years Programme produce a certificate the Ministry of Education will attest later?
faqs.answer: No. The PYP produces school reports, a portfolio and an Exhibition, not an externally awarded qualification, so there is nothing from the primary years for an attestation authority to act on. What matters later is the school-leaving qualification: the published British-track rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. Verify any requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority, because no tutoring provider performs or guarantees equivalency.

faqs.question: How does the shortened Ramadan school day change a primary tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: It moves it later and makes it shorter. Primary children are mostly not fasting, but the household rhythm shifts: later dinners, later bedtimes, and a flat stretch in the late afternoon when very little is going in. The slot that works is the hour after Iftar, at thirty focused minutes rather than sixty. Content should change too - Ramadan weeks are poor weeks for new material and good ones for consolidation, so recall practice, reading aloud and revisiting written methods that are nearly secure. Ramadan moves earlier each year, so check where it falls before planning a term.

faqs.question: What should we ask for at the first parent-teacher conference of the year?
faqs.answer: Three things, with dates attached. Which reading instrument the school uses and what the band means in months or years behind. Whether a standardised benchmark is sat, and in which window. And whether the teacher's concern is comprehension, language or attention, because those have different remedies and only one of them is helped by subject tuition. Ask when each number was taken - a reading age from April is a different thing from one taken in September. Those answers are free, they exist in almost every UAE primary, and they are better than any paid diagnostic.

faqs.question: How much does primary one-to-one tuition cost per hour in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to 650 an hour. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52 online; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150; Bestimate's Dubai table puts a tutor travelling to the address at AED 180-350, with the wider home market to AED 500; specialists run AED 200-450 and above, and BartyED at AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. At primary level the hourly rate is also the wrong unit - two twenty-five minute sessions a week is a different purchase from one long hour.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book primary hours in September than in May?
faqs.answer: The rate does not change. The weeks do, and at primary level the weeks are what you are buying. September buys the longest uninterrupted teaching block in the UAE year, roughly twelve or thirteen weeks before the winter break, with a child who is not yet tired and a school that is still introducing new content. May buys the tail end of a year, with reports written and attention gone. Primary demand in the Emirates peaks after term one reports and again before Exhibition season, which means most families buy in the two windows with the fewest usable weeks left.

faqs.question: When did Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies become compulsory in Dubai primary timetables?
faqs.answer: The subjects have long been required, but KHDA's current requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. That date is why the subjects may look different from an older sibling's experience. KHDA counts instructional time in a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length as long as the weekly total is met, and advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Arab and non-Arab groups must also be taught in separate classes for these subjects.

faqs.question: Our move from Dubai to Abu Dhabi happens in January. How should that change the primary plan?
faqs.answer: Expect three changes. The regulator changes from KHDA to ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. The calendar changes, because conference and report dates in Abu Dhabi schools often sit a fortnight off the Dubai pattern, and your child may arrive after the benchmark window has passed. And the paperwork matters more than families expect: reports and transfer documents from a school you have left are harder to get afterwards, so collect them before the move rather than after. Online tuition itself continues unchanged in the same slot.

faqs.question: Is a parent allowed to help with the PYP Exhibition, and where does that help stop?
faqs.answer: Helping is expected; doing is not. A parent can talk through whether a question is answerable, drive a child to a library, listen to a rehearsal and ask awkward questions. A parent should not choose the question, find the sources, take the notes, structure the argument or tidy the writing into something the child could not have produced. The Exhibition is the first piece of work a primary child owns end to end, and the boundary set here is the same one that governs Internal Assessments and Extended Essays years later. Settling it early is worth more than the marks involved.

faqs.question: What happens if no primary specialist is free for the slot we want?
faqs.answer: We say so and offer a waiting list. Narrow primary requests are the ones most likely to run out of coverage - Arabic as a first language at lower primary, for instance, or Islamic Education for the Arab stream, where KHDA also requires school teachers of those subjects to hold approval from the authority. The alternative on offer across this market is a generalist put in front of a seven-year-old at a specialist rate, which we would rather not do. We will also tell you honestly when the useful answer is a timetable conversation with the school instead of paid hours.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching my eight-year-old over video need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-based. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website or e-services. Anyone providing private lessons without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: If we only have twelve weeks before the summer break, what can realistically change?
faqs.answer: Automaticity, and little else. Twelve weeks of two short sessions is about twenty-four sessions, which is enough to move reading fluency, number bonds or a written method from shaky to secure, because those respond to frequency. It is not enough to change comprehension or extended writing, which develop over years rather than terms. The honest plan for a short run is to pick one measurable thing, work on it daily or near-daily, and hand the summer a child who no longer has to think about it. Then start the next block in September, where the long weeks are.

ib-pyp-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with four dates, not with an hourly rate
ib-pyp-home-tutor.closingBody: Send us your school's term dates, the two conference dates, the benchmark window and - if your child is in the exit year - Exhibition presentation week. We will tell you honestly whether paid hours are the right answer for the gap you are describing, when they should start, how many of them the calendar can usefully hold, and which school date they should be reviewed against. The first one-to-one lesson is free, one per family, with no payment taken and no card required beforehand. Lessons run over live video into every emirate, at a time that survives the school run and bedtime, and nobody is sent to a UAE address.

ib-pyp-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach primary-age children: reading, early number, written English and the mandatory UAE subjects that sit beside the units of inquiry. They are primary practitioners rather than Diploma specialists working downwards, because a Chemistry HL teacher and a Year 2 reading teacher are not the same job at any price.

intro.heading: Nobody prices primary tuition, so start with the hour
paragraphs: Search for an IB PYP tutor in the UAE and you will find agency pages that name a price for the Diploma, mention the Primary Years Programme in one line, and move on. That is not an accident. Secondary tuition sells itself on a number: a grade, a paper weighting, a university offer. Primary tuition has none of those, so the people selling it fall back on adjectives. A parent is then asked to pay AED 200 an hour on faith, for a child who cannot report back on what happened in the lesson.

This page takes the opposite approach. It starts with the hour as a unit, publishes what UAE providers advertise for primary work, and sets out what should be inside a 45-minute session, minute by minute, so you can check afterwards whether you got it. Every AED figure here was read from another provider's own page or from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price. We quote after the trial lesson, once somebody has actually met the child and knows whether thirty minutes twice a week beats forty-five minutes once.

The PYP changes the arithmetic in a way parents are rarely told. There is no external IB examination in the Primary Years Programme, no grade boundary to chase and no internal assessment to supervise. What a tutor is working on instead is narrow and measurable: decoding, reading fluency, number fact recall, handwriting stamina, written sentence structure, and the English of a child who is learning the language of instruction at the same time as the content. Those things respond to short, frequent, well-aimed sessions. They respond badly to a sixty-minute block at the end of a long school day.

The UAE adds a second layer that no generic primary tutoring page covers. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA's own guidelines require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, specify the language of instruction for each group, and prohibit any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission. A family budgeting for primary tuition is usually budgeting for two different things: the PYP subject groups, and an Arabic stream that may be the real reason the reports look uneven.

The scale is worth holding in mind while you read the numbers. Dubai alone had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with IB programmes accounting for 7% of enrolment and UK curriculum schools 37%. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them running International Baccalaureate programmes, creating 16,846 new places. More PYP classrooms are opening than there are PYP-experienced teachers living within driving distance of them. That single fact is why IB PYP tutor searches in the UAE increasingly end in a live video lesson rather than a car journey.

ib-pyp-tutor.programmesIntro: The PYP runs from age three to age twelve, and the three stages inside it buy very different things. Early years work is about language and play; lower primary is about fluency; the final years are about independence and the Exhibition. The fourth row below is the year after, because the cost of leaving a PYP-to-MYP gap unclosed is the one most families discover late.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme, Early Years
programmes.ageRange: Ages 3-6 - FS1 to Year 1, or Pre-KG to Grade 1
programmes.description: Play-based inquiry, oral language, phonological awareness and early number. Children at this stage are building the sound system of English and the idea that a numeral stands for a quantity. There is no written assessment worth tutoring towards. What one-to-one time does buy is talk: a patient adult who listens to a three-year-old finish a sentence, names objects precisely, and plays the same counting game until the quantity is held without counting.
programmes.countryNote: Across the UAE, Early Years classes are often the most linguistically mixed rooms in the school, with children arriving from five or six home languages. A child who is quiet in FS2 is frequently not behind but silent in a second language. Short, twice-weekly sessions in English, with a parent in the room, are usually enough to tell the difference before a label is attached.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme, Lower Primary
programmes.description: The fluency years, and the ones where paying for tuition changes the most per dirham. Decoding becomes automatic or it does not. Addition and subtraction facts move into recall or they stay on fingers. Handwriting either becomes fast enough to keep up with thinking or it becomes the thing that limits it. A tutor here works on a named skill, not on a topic, and the skill either moves in six weeks or the diagnosis was wrong.
programmes.countryNote: This is also where the UAE Arabic streams begin to separate children sharply. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabic as a first language and Arabic as an additional language, with different curriculum expectations and a different language of instruction, so a Year 3 child placed in the wrong stream can look weak for two years for reasons that have nothing to do with ability. Ask the school which stream your child sits in before buying any Arabic hours.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme, Upper Primary and the Exhibition
programmes.description: Inquiry gets longer, writing gets structured, and the programme ends with the PYP Exhibition: an extended, largely self-directed piece of collaborative inquiry presented to the school community. The skills under test are research, self-management, communication and reflection. The work must be the student's own, and that boundary is where most of the honest value in Exhibition-year tutoring sits: process coaching, questioning, planning and reflection prompts, with nothing produced for the child.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools run the Exhibition across a long spring window, usually finishing before the summer break, and a child juggling it alongside the mandatory UAE subjects has four or five deadlines running at once for the first time. PYP Exhibition support in this market is mostly about calendars and research questions, not content. Families who book it as a writing service are buying something a tutor may not honestly supply.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, first year
programmes.description: The year after the PYP, included here because the gap is a cost. MYP Year 1 introduces subject-specialist teachers, eight subject groups and criterion-based marking with four criteria, A to D, per subject. A child who wrote beautifully about a central idea at primary suddenly has to write to a criterion descriptor against a strand. The adjustment is a skill, it is teachable, and it is cheaper to teach in Term 1 than in Year 9.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE families change school at this point, often moving from a PYP primary into a British Year 7 heading for IGCSE or into an American middle school. Each of those three destinations demands something different on day one. The transition table further down this page sets out which gap costs most to close late for each route, and roughly how many sessions families typically book.

ib-pyp-tutor.subjectsIntro: The PYP organises learning into six subject groups inside transdisciplinary units of inquiry, which means a parent rarely sees a subject named on its own. The list below splits the programme back into the things a tutor can actually diagnose and move, and adds the mandatory UAE subjects that sit alongside it in every licensed private school.

subjects.name: Language - reading and decoding
subjects.levels: Early Years to the Exhibition year
subjects.description: Phonic knowledge, blending, vowel teams, polysyllabic decoding and then fluency measured in words per minute with accuracy. PYP reading support is diagnostic before it is remedial: a child who guesses from first letters needs something different from a child who decodes accurately but slowly. Both look identical on a report that says 'developing'.

subjects.name: Language - writing and sentence structure
subjects.description: Sentence boundaries, clause joining, tense consistency, paragraphing, and writing to an audience. Inside the units of inquiry children write explanations, reports and reflections. Marks are rarely the issue; legibility, speed and structure are. Handwriting stamina is treated here as a mechanical skill with its own practice, not a personality trait.

subjects.name: English as an additional language
subjects.description: Academic vocabulary, listening comprehension, question forms, and the specific gap between playground English and the English of a summative task. In UAE classrooms this is the most frequently misread difficulty of all, because a confident speaker can still be two years behind on the written academic register the unit assessment requires.

subjects.name: Mathematics - number
subjects.description: Counting and cardinality, place value, number facts to 20 and then to 100, the four operations, fractions and decimals. The PYP maths tutor's first job is almost always fact fluency: a child who still counts on to add is spending working memory on arithmetic that the reasoning task needs. Recall is built by short daily practice, not long sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics - measurement, shape and space
subjects.description: Units and conversion, perimeter, area, angle, position, transformation and the reading of scales. This strand is where the UAE's mixed-curriculum intake shows most: a child arriving from a metric-only primary and a child arriving from a school that taught imperial units are both correct and both stuck. Diagnosis takes one session.

subjects.name: Mathematics - pattern, function and data handling
subjects.description: Sequences, rules, early algebraic thinking, tables, pictograms, bar charts, mean and chance. Data handling carries most of the maths inside the units of inquiry, so a child who cannot read a chart loses marks in a science or social studies task rather than a maths one. That is why the report looks confusing to parents.

subjects.name: Science inside the units of inquiry
subjects.description: Living things, materials, forces, earth and space, and the inquiry skills around them: predicting, fair testing, recording and concluding. Tutoring here is rarely content delivery. It is teaching a child to write what they did and what it showed, in order, which is the part of the summative task that most often loses credit.

subjects.name: Social studies inside the units of inquiry
subjects.description: Human systems, continuity and change, place and resources. Units of inquiry support at this level means teaching a child to turn a central idea into questions they can actually research, then into notes in their own words. Copying from a website is the default behaviour of a ten-year-old; replacing it is a teachable skill.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Script formation, letter joining, short vowels, high-frequency vocabulary and listening. KHDA requires this to be taught separately from the first-language group because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. An Arabic as an additional language tutor works to the scheme the child's own school uses, since additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: Reading fluency in Standard Arabic, diacritics, grammar and extended writing. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for this stream and for Islamic Education for Arab students. Support is pitched at the school's own scheme of work and the mandatory instructional time it is given each week.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.levels: Muslim students, Arab and non-Arab streams
subjects.description: Set content comprehension, memorisation technique and written answer structure. The Arab stream is taught in Standard Arabic and the non-Arab stream in the school's licensed-curriculum language, in separate classes. Tutoring is comprehension and recall support within the school's own material rather than any additional syllabus.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning - self-management and research
subjects.description: Planning backwards from a deadline, breaking a long task into days, note-taking, source checking and reflection. These are the skills the PYP names explicitly and that nobody times or grades, which is exactly why they are the cheapest thing to fix before the Middle Years Programme arrives with four assessment criteria per subject.

ib-pyp-tutor.regionsTitle: Where PYP families are, emirate by emirate
ib-pyp-tutor.regionsIntro: The PYP is concentrated in Dubai and Abu Dhabi and thin everywhere else, which is the practical reason a driving radius is the wrong way to choose a primary tutor. The notes below are about supply: how many primary IB classrooms sit in each emirate, and what that does to a family's options at four o'clock on a weekday.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest PYP pool in the country and the only emirate with a published mandatory-subjects framework at this level of detail. A PYP tutor in Dubai is also the most contested 5pm slot in the UAE, because Marina, Al Barsha and Emirates Hills families all want the hour after the school bus.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of children enrolled at their own school, so a PYP tutor in Abu Dhabi is by design somebody outside your child's classroom. Khalifa City and Yas commutes push sessions later.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a far smaller set of international primary classrooms. Families here routinely find that the nearest teacher with real PYP experience is an hour's drive each way, which prices a visiting tutor out before the lesson starts. One-to-one primary tuition over live video removes the drive from the invoice.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Assessment methods being approved at emirate level matters at primary: ask the school what it actually administers before paying for anything described as test preparation.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education is regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. The international primary pool is small and concentrated, so mid-year transfers are common and so is the Arabic-stream placement problem that follows a transfer.

regions.name: Ajman and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. Families often commute into Sharjah or Dubai for an international primary place, which means a 3:30pm finish becomes a 5pm arrival home. Two thirty-minute evening sessions a week fit that reality; a sixty-minute block does not.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Also under federal Ministry of Education supervision, and the thinnest international primary provision in the country. Almost every enquiry here is either a transfer gap or an Arabic stream question, and almost none of it can be served by anybody living within half an hour of the house.

regions.name: Dubai's villa communities
regions.note: Arabian Ranches, Mudon, Town Square and the Dubailand belt send children to primary schools fifteen to thirty minutes away by bus, which routinely lands a seven-year-old home after 4pm. The practical consequence is that the usable primary tuition window in these communities is roughly 4:30pm to 6pm, Gulf Standard Time.

schoolClusters.note: Children we support in Dubai come from schools across the emirate's IB primary provision, spread between Al Barsha, Emirates Hills, Mirdif and the Al Quoz and Garhoud corridors. Programme authorisation changes year to year and by year group, so confirm with the school, or against the IB's own programme listing, which stages it currently runs.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi, Al Ain and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: Outside Dubai the primary IB map is sparse and spread wide, which is why families in Khalifa City, Al Ain and Sharjah so often end up matched to a teacher in another emirate or another country. Check the current programme and year groups directly with each school before assuming a stage is offered.

ib-pyp-tutor.modesIntro: Primary tuition is bought in the wrong shape more often than at the wrong price. A sixty-minute weekly hour is the default on every agency site and the worst fit for a child under nine. The three patterns below are the ones that actually hold attention, and each is delivered one-to-one over live video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot.

modes.title: Two thirty-minute sessions a week
modes.description: The default for ages five to nine and for anything involving fluency. Reading accuracy, number fact recall and handwriting speed are built by frequency, not duration: the same total minutes split across two days beats one long session because the child is still fresh and because there is a second chance in the same week to fix what did not stick. It also survives a cancelled day without losing the week.

modes.title: One forty-five-minute weekly session
modes.description: Suits ages nine to twelve, where a longer arc of work is sustainable and where a single session can hold a diagnosis, teaching, independent practice and a reflection. This is the usual shape for upper primary maths, extended writing and units of inquiry support, and it is the shape the minute-by-minute table on this page describes. Sixty minutes is available and rarely advisable before Year 7.

modes.title: A short diagnostic block, then a decision
modes.description: Four to six sessions bought as a block with one purpose: finding out what is actually wrong. Most families arrive with a report comment rather than a diagnosis, and the gap between 'needs to develop confidence in mathematics' and 'cannot recall number bonds to 20 under time pressure' is the difference between a year of tuition and a term of it. At the end of the block you get a named skill list and an honest recommendation, including no further sessions.

sections.heading: A primary hour and a Diploma hour are not the same purchase
paragraphs: An IB PYP tutor in the UAE costs less per hour than a Diploma specialist, and the gap is wider than most parents expect. Providers advertising primary work in this market publish figures from roughly AED 45 an hour at the student-tutor end to around AED 250 for an experienced primary teacher online, while the same sites quote AED 200 to AED 450 and upward for IB Diploma subject specialists. Every figure in the table below was read from another provider's own page, or from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price.

The reason for the gap is supply rather than difficulty. Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level needs a teacher who has taught that syllabus and marked against it; the pool is small and it prices accordingly. Early reading needs a teacher who can hear which sound a child is substituting and has a sequence to fix it, and the pool of people who can do that is larger. What is genuinely scarce at primary level in the UAE is not maths or English. It is Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education taught in Standard Arabic, and experienced early years practitioners, and those three lines sit at the top of the primary band rather than the bottom.

Read the table across rather than down. The column that moves a family's budget most is not the rate but the format: a visiting tutor's travel is inside the hourly figure, so two short sessions a week means paying for two journeys. At primary, where frequency beats duration, that single structural fact is usually worth more than the headline difference between two providers' rates. Primary years tutoring rates in AED look similar across formats until you multiply by the number of sessions a seven-year-old actually needs.

sections.heading: What forty-five minutes should contain when the student is eight
paragraphs: A parent buying Diploma tuition can check the purchase against a past paper. A parent buying primary tuition has no such instrument, which is why so much primary tutoring money in this market is spent on supervised homework. Supervised homework is a childcare service with an educational label, and it is worth roughly what a babysitter costs rather than what a teacher costs. The way to avoid paying teacher rates for it is to know what should be inside the session before you buy one.

The structure below is what an effective primary session looks like, and every row has something a parent can verify afterwards without having watched. The pattern matters more than the exact minutes: a short warm-up that gets the child talking, one named skill retaught from the point it broke, guided practice with the tutor deliberately withdrawing help, then independent work, then a reflection the child says out loud. If a session has no independent stretch, the child has watched an adult be competent for forty-five minutes.

The last row is the one to insist on. A two-line written note on the same day, naming one thing that worked and one next step, is the cheapest accountability mechanism in tutoring and almost nobody in this market supplies it by default. Over a term those notes become a record you can take to the school's parent meeting, which is frequently more useful than the report that prompted you to hire somebody in the first place.

sections.heading: The seven things that move a PYP quote, and the question that tests each
paragraphs: Two providers can quote AED 80 and AED 240 for what looks like the same primary hour, and both can be quoting honestly. The difference lives in seven variables, and a parent who asks about all seven stops comparing numbers and starts comparing purchases. The table sets each one out with the question that exposes it, because every one of these is answerable in a sentence by somebody who is telling the truth and answerable only in adjectives by somebody who is not.

Two of the seven deserve a warning. Session length is sold as a benefit when it is usually a cost: sixty minutes for a six-year-old is forty minutes of teaching and twenty minutes of a tired child, charged at the same rate. And group size is quoted per child in a way that looks like a bargain until you ask the ages. A group of four spanning Years 2 to 5 is four different lessons delivered at once, and the fee split does not make that work.

The seventh variable, timing, is the one families underestimate. The 4:30pm to 6pm Gulf Standard Time window is the busiest hour in UAE tutoring because every school bus arrives inside it. A slot held for a whole term is worth paying slightly more for than a slot rebooked weekly, because the thing that actually breaks primary progress is not the rate. It is a month of missed and rescheduled sessions.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor and a live video session, costed for a seven-year-old
paragraphs: Parents searching for a primary tutor in the UAE are usually picturing somebody arriving after school, and that market is real: published rates for a visiting one-to-one tutor run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, and monthly packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits have been advertised in Dubai. It is worth understanding properly before choosing, because the comparison at primary level is different from the comparison at Diploma level, and it is different in ways that favour the screen.

IB Gram does not send anybody to a UAE address. Household visits are a service offered only in India, and that is stated the same way on the /uae/ page and across every other country page on this site. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. The case for it at primary is not cost. It is that a thirty-minute session twice a week is financially absurd for a visiting tutor and entirely normal online, that the pool of PYP-experienced primary teachers is small enough that a thirty-minute driving radius removes most of it, and that a parent can sit in the same room and watch.

That last point carries more weight at seven than at seventeen. A Diploma student can tell you what happened in a lesson. A Year 2 child cannot reliably report whether the tutor taught, tested or simply sat beside them while they copied. An online PYP tutor working on a shared screen in your living room is the most observable form of tutoring there is, and observability is what lets a parent judge value in a programme that issues no grades.

sections.heading: No exams and no grades: how to tell whether you are getting value
paragraphs: The PYP sets no external IB examination. Assessment is carried out by the school, it is largely formative, and it is reported through written comments, portfolios and student-led conferences rather than percentages. That is sound practice for a nine-year-old and genuinely difficult for a parent who is spending money and wants to know whether it is working. It is also the reason primary tuition in this market is so often sold on reassurance: there is no number for anybody to be held to.

The honest answer is that you have to build your own instrument, and the materials are already in your hands. Each document a PYP school gives you carries real information and leaves something specific out, and the gaps are consistent. A learner-profile report tells you how your child engages and says nothing about whether decoding is below age expectation. A portfolio afternoon shows you what the child is proud of and not which pieces were scaffolded by an adult. The right-hand column of the table is the question that closes each gap, and all five are reasonable things to ask a class teacher.

A sourced comparison makes the point sharper. A British-curriculum primary school in the UAE may enter children for Cambridge Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which Cambridge International offers in March, May and October, producing an external benchmark on paper. A PYP school has no equivalent. Neither approach is better pedagogy, but the PYP parent has to ask for information that the Checkpoint parent is handed, and that asking is free.

sections.heading: The PYP Exhibition: what you may pay a tutor to do, and what you may not
paragraphs: The Exhibition closes the Primary Years Programme. It is an extended, largely student-directed inquiry, usually collaborative, presented to the school community, and it is the first time most children carry a multi-week deadline. It is also the first point at which a UAE family is likely to be offered something they should refuse. There are operators in this market selling finished secondary coursework outright; one advertises completed Internal Assessments. The same logic reaches down to ten-year-olds, and it is worth naming plainly.

A tutor's role in an Exhibition is process. Helping a child turn a vague interest into a researchable question. Teaching them to plan backwards from the presentation date across the available weeks. Showing them how to take notes in their own words rather than copying a web page, how to check whether a source is any good, how to rehearse a presentation and how to write a reflection that says something. All of that is teaching, all of it transfers to secondary school, and none of it touches the product.

What a tutor must not do is produce any part of the work. Not drafting the written outcome, not building the display, not writing the reflection, not scripting the presentation. PYP Exhibition support that crosses that line teaches a child that adults will produce their work for them, which is a lesson that gets expensive at Diploma level where academic honesty rules make it a malpractice matter. We say this on every page because it is a real difference in this search results page, not a disclaimer.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in a primary timetable
paragraphs: Every family budgeting for IB Primary Years Programme tuition in the UAE should start with the mandatory subjects, because this is where the unexplained report comments usually come from. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are required in Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA's own guidelines required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. These lessons are not an optional extra on the side of the PYP. They are part of the week.

The organisational rules are specific and they explain a great deal. KHDA requires schools to run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects.

Two further details shape what tuition can honestly offer. Mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. And for these subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited. An Arabic as an additional language tutor therefore works inside the scheme the child's own school uses, at the school's pace, rather than importing a separate syllabus.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's primary school, and what that changes
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are regulated at emirate level, and which authority holds the file changes what you can ask for and who you can hire. In Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's private education is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge, while the federal Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That is the complete map, and ADEK is named by almost nobody else writing about tutoring in this country.

Two of those relationships have direct consequences for a primary tutoring plan. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so what a school may assess is itself an approved matter rather than a school preference. And in Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to children enrolled at their own school, with the private tuition work permit carrying a code of conduct to the same effect. That has been reported in the press rather than read here from the current policy document, so confirm the exact wording with ADEK, but the practical point stands: your child's own class teacher is not the person to hire.

None of this means a regulator vets your tutor. IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or the International Baccalaureate, and any tutoring service telling you otherwise is describing something it would have to be able to show you. What the regulators do give you is leverage: published mandatory-subject rules, published inspection outcomes and a named authority to ask.

sections.heading: The primary school year read as a spending calendar
paragraphs: Because there is no external examination, primary tuition money has no natural deadline to organise itself around, and that is precisely why so much of it is spent in the wrong weeks. Families tend to buy in a panic after a report and stop in the summer, which is almost exactly backwards. The windows below map what is happening in a UAE PYP classroom across the year against what an hour is worth in each one, and what to decline.

Three of the rows are worth reading twice. The January-to-February block is the longest uninterrupted stretch of teaching in the UAE school year and the period in which fluency measurably moves, so it is where a steady weekly slot earns the most. The shortened Ramadan school day calls for shorter sessions moved later rather than cancelled ones, because frequency is what is doing the work. And the long summer break is nine to ten weeks without instruction, which is the single largest predictable loss of reading accuracy and number fact recall in the calendar.

What to decline matters as much as what to buy. There is nothing to crash-revise for in the PYP, so an intensive block sold as exam preparation at primary level is selling you a product that has no object. Equally, an open-ended monthly retainer agreed before you have a diagnosis commits you to a year of something nobody has yet defined. Buy a short diagnostic block, get a named skill list, then commit.

sections.heading: Leaving the PYP, and the cost of closing the gap late
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake in primary tuition is not overpaying. It is waiting. A child who leaves the Primary Years Programme writing well about a central idea but unable to write to a criterion descriptor, or reasoning confidently but unable to recall a number fact, does not fail anything in Year 7. The cost appears two or three years later, as Middle Years Programme criterion marks that sit a band lower than the child's understanding, or as IGCSE method marks lost because the working was never shown.

Four destinations account for almost every UAE family leaving a PYP primary, and each demands something different on day one. MYP Year 1 brings subject-specialist teachers, eight subject groups and criterion-based marking across four criteria per subject. A British Year 7 heading for IGCSE brings syllabuses, set texts and timed written assessment. An American middle school brings letter grades, a grade point average and continuous quizzing. A CBSE or ICSE Year 6 brings a textbook-and-syllabus model with formal examinations twice a year.

The last row is the one nobody warns UAE families about. Moving between two PYP schools in different emirates looks like the easy transfer and often is not, because the Arabic stream placement may change and a child can arrive placed a year behind on a scheme they have never seen. If you are transferring, ask the receiving school which Arabic stream your child will sit in and which scheme of work it follows before term starts, not after the first report.

sections.heading: Where primary tuition money actually changes something
paragraphs: Four things at primary level respond reliably to one-to-one teaching, and a family that spends only on those four will outperform a family that spends twice as much on general support. The first is decoding and reading accuracy. A child who guesses from the first letter, or who reads accurately but at half the expected rate, is spending so much attention on the words that none is left for the meaning, and every unit of inquiry task in every subject group then reads as weak comprehension.

The second is number fact recall. A nine-year-old who still counts on to add single digits is not bad at maths; they are using working memory on arithmetic that the reasoning problem needs. This is the clearest case in all of primary education for short, frequent, timed practice, and it is why a PYP maths tutor working twice a week for twenty minutes achieves more than one long weekly session. The third is handwriting speed and stamina, which is a mechanical skill with its own practice sequence and is routinely mistaken for a lack of ideas.

The fourth is the academic register of English for a child learning the language of instruction alongside the content. A confident speaker in the playground can be two years behind in the written English a summative task requires, and that gap is invisible to everybody until a report describes the child as careless. Everything else, including most of what is sold as general homework support, is either a consequence of these four or is childcare with a teacher's invoice attached.

process.title: Tell us the year group and the one thing that is not working
process.description: Not the whole report. The single sentence that worries you most, plus the year group, the school's curriculum and which Arabic stream your child sits in. For primary enquiries that is usually enough to know whether the issue is reading, number fluency, written English or an Arabic placement, and which of those a tutor can actually move.

process.title: A free forty-five-minute trial lesson, with you in the room
process.description: One trial lesson per family, no card details taken and nothing to cancel. It is a working session rather than a sales call: the tutor checks reading accuracy or number recall, teaches something, and tells you what they found. You watch the whole thing on the shared screen and decide afterwards whether it was teaching.

process.title: A named skill list instead of a topic list
process.description: After the trial you get the diagnosis in plain words: which sounds are being substituted, which number bonds are not recalled, how many words a minute are read accurately, what the unaided writing sample actually shows. A skill list can be checked in six weeks. A topic list such as 'maths and English' cannot be.

process.title: A fixed Gulf Standard Time slot for the term
process.description: Primary progress is destroyed by rescheduling, so the slot is held for the term rather than rebooked weekly. Most families take two thirty-minute sessions in the 4:30pm to 6pm window, shortening them during Ramadan rather than cancelling. The quote comes at this point, once somebody knows the shape of the work.

process.title: A note after every session and a review at six weeks
process.description: Two written lines the same day, naming one thing that worked and one next step, which over a term becomes a record you can take to the school. At six weeks we re-check the same measures from the diagnosis against the baseline, and if nothing has moved we change the tutor, the shape or the recommendation.

whyPoints.title: Primary teachers, not Diploma specialists working downwards
whyPoints.description: Hearing which sound a six-year-old substitutes, and knowing the sequence that fixes it, is a different craft from teaching Chemistry at Higher Level. Our primary matches are made from people who have taught PYP year groups, including the ones who have planned units of inquiry rather than only delivered somebody else's.

whyPoints.title: Thirty and forty-five-minute sessions as the default
whyPoints.description: Sixty minutes is the industry default because it prices neatly, not because it suits a seven-year-old. Under age nine we recommend two shorter sessions a week over one long one, which costs the same total minutes and produces more because the child is fresh and gets a second attempt inside the same week.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, with the source and the date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page came from another provider's own published page or from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026, and is labelled as such. Three of the six highest-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: The Exhibition handled as coaching, not production
whyPoints.description: A tutor helps a child shape a research question, plan backwards from a deadline, take notes in their own words and rehearse a presentation. A tutor does not produce any part of the outcome. There are operators in this market selling finished coursework; a ten-year-old learning that adults supply their work is the expensive version of cheap help.

whyPoints.title: A tutor pool set by the timetable, not a driving radius
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video at a Gulf Standard Time slot, so the match is made from everybody free at five o'clock rather than everybody within half an hour of your community. In Al Ain, Fujairah and Ras Al Khaimah that is the difference between a specialist and whoever is nearest.

faqs.question: How much does an IB PYP tutor in the UAE cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates for primary one-to-one work run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the student-tutor end to around AED 250 for an experienced primary teacher online, with visiting tutors advertised at AED 180 to AED 500 because travel sits inside the figure. Those are other providers' numbers, read in October 2026 from their own pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. Primary rates sit below the AED 200 to AED 450 band quoted for IB Diploma specialists, mainly because the pool of capable primary teachers is larger. We quote after the free trial lesson, once somebody knows whether the right shape is thirty minutes twice a week or forty-five minutes once.

faqs.question: Is one-to-one tuition worth paying for when my child is only six?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and for a narrower set of reasons than agencies suggest. At six the things that reliably respond to one-to-one teaching are decoding, early number fact recall, handwriting formation and the academic English of a child learning the language of instruction. Those are measurable and they move in weeks. General homework supervision at six is childcare with a teacher's invoice attached. The honest test is whether anybody can name the skill they are working on. If the answer is a subject rather than a skill, buy a four-session diagnostic block first and make the decision afterwards with a diagnosis in hand.

faqs.question: There are no exams in the PYP, so what is a tutor preparing my child for?
faqs.answer: Nothing external, which changes what the hours are for. The Primary Years Programme sets no IB examination; assessment is done by the school and reported through comments, portfolios and student-led conferences. A tutor is therefore working on capabilities rather than papers: reading accuracy and fluency, recall of number facts, writing mechanics and speed, research and self-management for the Exhibition year, and the written academic English a summative task demands. The payoff arrives at the transition into the Middle Years Programme or a British Year 7, where those capabilities suddenly get marked. It also means any intensive block sold as primary exam preparation has no object.

faqs.question: What is the PYP Exhibition, and what may a tutor help with?
faqs.answer: The Exhibition is the extended, largely student-directed inquiry that closes the Primary Years Programme in the final year, usually collaborative and presented to the school community. A tutor may help a child turn an interest into a researchable question, plan backwards from the presentation date, take notes in their own words rather than copying, judge whether a source is any good, rehearse the presentation and write a reflection with something in it. A tutor may not produce any part of the work: not the written outcome, not the display, not the reflection, not the script. That boundary is the whole value of honest Exhibition support.

faqs.question: My daughter's report has no grades on it. How do I tell whether she is behind?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions the report does not answer. Where would you place her reading age in years and months? Can she recall number bonds and tables under time pressure, or does she still count on? May we see an unaided writing sample rather than a scaffolded one? And if the school runs standardised screening, may we see the actual band and the date of the test? Those four answers turn a learner-profile comment into something you can act on and measure again in six weeks. All four are reasonable requests at a parent meeting, and all four are free.

faqs.question: How long should a session be for a child in Grade 2?
faqs.answer: Thirty minutes, twice a week, for almost every Grade 2 or Year 3 child. Sixty minutes is the default on most provider sites because it prices neatly in hourly units, not because a seven-year-old can sustain it. Reading fluency, number fact recall and handwriting speed are built by frequency rather than duration, so the same total minutes split across two days produces more: the child is fresh both times, and anything that did not stick on Monday gets a second attempt on Thursday. Thirty-minute sessions are economically awkward for a visiting tutor and entirely normal over live video.

faqs.question: The school already teaches Arabic. Why would we pay for more of it?
faqs.answer: Usually because of stream placement rather than teaching quality. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with different curriculum expectations and a different language of instruction for each. A child placed in the first-language stream who speaks Arabic at home but reads it slowly, or a non-Arab child who arrived mid-year into an established scheme, can look weak for two years for reasons unrelated to ability. Ask which stream your child sits in before buying any Arabic hours.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share one primary session to halve the cost?
faqs.answer: It works when the ages are close and the skill is the same, and it fails more often than families expect. Two children within about eighteen months of each other, both working on the same thing, can share a forty-five minute session productively. A Year 2 and a Year 5 in one session is two lessons delivered alternately, and each child gets roughly half the teaching for rather more than half the fee. Published UAE group rates of AED 40 to AED 160 per child look efficient on paper. Ask the age spread question before the price question.

faqs.question: Will a seven-year-old actually concentrate on a live video lesson?
faqs.answer: For thirty minutes, with the right structure and a parent nearby, yes. The things that break it are length, timing and passivity. Keep sessions to thirty minutes under age nine, put them inside the 4:30pm to 6pm window rather than after 6:30pm, and insist that the child is reading, writing, speaking or working something out for most of the session rather than watching an adult explain. One advantage over a closed-door session at home is that you can see all of this happening on the shared screen and judge it for yourself rather than taking a summary on trust.

faqs.question: How many weeks of reading support does a child in Year 3 usually need?
faqs.answer: Plan on a term and insist on a six-week checkpoint. A reading difficulty that turns out to be a specific decoding gap, such as unreliable vowel teams or weak polysyllabic blending, often moves substantially inside six to ten weeks of two short sessions a week. A fluency problem where decoding is accurate but slow takes longer, because the mechanism is practice volume. What should not happen is an open-ended arrangement with no baseline. Get the reading age in years and months before you start, re-measure at six weeks, and change something if the number has not moved.

faqs.question: Should we wait until MYP or IGCSE before spending anything on tuition?
faqs.answer: Waiting is the expensive choice if the issue is fluency. A child who leaves the Primary Years Programme reasoning well but unable to recall number facts, or writing thoughtfully but slowly and without secure sentence boundaries, does not fail anything in Year 7. The cost surfaces two or three years later as Middle Years Programme criterion marks a band below the child's actual understanding, or IGCSE method marks lost because working was never shown. Those are the most expensive hours in the whole system to buy back. Four to six well-aimed primary sessions are cheaper than a term of remediation at fourteen.

faqs.question: Does the person teaching my six-year-old privately need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service, Private Tutor Licensing, quotes a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with caution.

faqs.question: What should we buy over the ten-week UAE summer break?
faqs.answer: Frequency, not volume. Nine or ten weeks without instruction is the single largest predictable loss of reading accuracy and number fact recall in the UAE calendar, and it is also the cheapest loss to prevent. Two twenty or thirty-minute sessions a week, aimed only at holding fluency, do more than a full weekly hour and cost less in total. Avoid anything sold as a summer catch-up programme built around a syllabus the child has not met yet. The point of summer hours at primary is maintenance, so that September starts where June finished rather than six weeks behind it.

faqs.question: Where does a primary session fit on a shortened Ramadan school day?
faqs.answer: Later and shorter. UAE schools run reduced hours during Ramadan, children finish earlier and stamina is noticeably lower, so the usual answer for a primary family is to cut a forty-five-minute session to twenty or twenty-five minutes and move it to a later slot rather than cancel the week. Keeping the rhythm matters more than the minutes at this age, because fluency work depends on frequency. Slots in the hour after Iftar are in heavy demand across the Emirates, so agree the Ramadan pattern with your tutor a few weeks beforehand rather than during the first week.

faqs.question: We are moving from a CBSE primary school into a PYP school. What should we budget for?
faqs.answer: Two things, and neither is maths content. The first is the shift from a textbook-and-syllabus model to transdisciplinary units of inquiry, where a child is asked to pose questions, research them and write about a concept rather than reproduce a chapter. Capable CBSE pupils often look lost for a term purely because nobody taught them that. The second is the Arabic stream, which the new school assigns and which can place a child a year behind a scheme they have never seen. Four to six sessions on each, booked before term starts, is the usual pattern.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson cover for a primary-age child?
faqs.answer: One forty-five-minute working session per family, with no card details taken and nothing to cancel afterwards. The tutor checks something concrete, such as reading accuracy on an unseen passage or number fact recall under mild time pressure, teaches one small thing, and then tells you what they found in plain language. You sit in the room and watch it on the shared screen. What you should get afterwards is a named skill list rather than a subject list, plus an honest view of session shape, and sometimes a recommendation that your child does not need tuition.

ib-pyp-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the hour, then decide
ib-pyp-tutor.closingBody: An IB PYP tutor in the UAE is a cheap intervention bought at the wrong time by most families and at the right time by few. The cost of a diagnostic block of four to six sessions is small next to a term of unfocused weekly hours, and far smaller than buying back fluency at fourteen. Tell us the year group, the Arabic stream and the one sentence in the report that worries you. Take the free forty-five-minute trial lesson, watch it on the screen, and ask for the skill list afterwards. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, and nobody is sent to a UAE address.
