ib-retake-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the subjects UAE families repeat most often: Mathematics, the three sciences, Economics and English A. Each profile names the level taught and the papers that person specialises in, because a retake candidate needs whoever knows Paper 3, not a generalist who knows the course.

intro.heading: What changes the day a retake becomes the plan
paragraphs: A family searching for an IB retake tutor in the UAE is almost never shopping. The statement of results arrived a day or two ago, one or two grades came in below the predicted ones, and a university reply is sitting in an inbox. The IB examines twice a year, in May and in November, so the first question is not which tutor to hire. It is which session to enter. That single answer sets the budget, the weekly hours and the shape of the next ten months, and it has to be given quickly.

Retake teaching is a different job from Diploma teaching. The course has already been taught once and the papers have already been sat, so nothing on the syllabus is new. What is missing is a diagnosis. A grade 4 in Chemistry can come from an internal mark that was never going to lift the total, from a data-analysis paper that collapsed under time pressure, or from two topics revised the week before the exam and never properly understood. Each of those costs a different number of hours and needs a different kind of session, and guessing between them wastes the term.

Three clocks run at the same time, and they are not synchronised. The board's entry deadline closes months before the paper is sat. The university's offer carries its own reply date, which nobody at the school controls. The Ministry of Education equivalency file cannot be completed until a final certificate exists. Families who lose a retake year usually lose it to the second and third clocks rather than the first, because the tuition started on time and the paperwork did not. Everything on this page is organised around those dates, counted backwards from the paper.

Pricing in this market is wide and poorly published. Rates read on UAE provider pages in October 2026 run from AED 45 an hour for a university-student tutor to AED 650 an hour at the premium end, and most of the pages ranking for retake searches publish no figure at all. The AED table further down this page quotes what each provider puts on its own site, with the month it was read. IB Gram's own position is simpler: a free trial lesson, then a quote for the plan your child actually needs, with the hours written down before anyone pays.

One honesty note about dates. The IB publishes its session windows, upload deadlines and results dates on ibo.org, and those pages block automated checking, so no IB date is printed anywhere on this page. Cambridge and Pearson dates are quoted below because they come from the boards' own published key-dates documents. For your child's session, the exact entry deadline and results date come from the IB coordinator at the school, or from ibo.org read on the day you need it. A retake plan built on a date nobody verified is the most expensive mistake available here.
bullets: Retakes are entered subject by subject, not as a whole Diploma, in most cases
The entry deadline, not the exam date, is the one that ends the decision
A specific paper diagnosis changes the hours needed by a factor of three
Enquiry upon results and a retake entry are separate decisions with separate windows
Equivalency and university replies run on calendars the school does not set
Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, in UAE evening slots

ib-retake-tutor.programmesIntro: Four IB routes bring families to a retake conversation, and they behave differently. A full Diploma candidate is managing failing conditions. A courses candidate is managing one certificate. A CP student is managing the Diploma course inside a wider qualification. An MYP student is managing the year before any of it matters.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The award depends on a points total and on a set of failing conditions covering low individual grades and the core components. A Diploma can be missed on points, on a single condition, or on both, and the repair plan is different in each case. The coordinator's statement of results names which one applies.
programmes.countryNote: Most UAE Diploma candidates sit in May with their cohort, and schools here vary in whether they register second-attempt candidates at all. Dubai's private sector had 227 schools in the 2024-25 KHDA figures, with International Baccalaureate programmes covering about 7% of pupils, so the pool of schools able to enter a repeat candidate is smaller than the overall school count suggests.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Courses
programmes.description: A student takes individual DP subjects and receives a certificate for each, without attempting the full Diploma award. For a family deciding what to do after a disappointing results day, the courses route is sometimes the practical answer: repeat the one subject a university actually asked for, rather than re-entering six and the core alongside them.
programmes.countryNote: UAE universities and the Ministry of Education assess what the certificate shows, not how many subjects sat behind it, so a courses entry can be enough to satisfy a specific subject condition. The equivalency rules for the IB route are not stated in the public clarifications we hold, which is why this page sends every family to moe.gov.ae and the attestation desk in their emirate before planning around a points figure.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service element and a language component. When a CP student's DP course grade lands below what a progression route needs, only that course is repeated. The career-related study and the reflective project are not re-sat because of a paper result.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in the UAE is thinner than DP provision, so a CP candidate repeating a course often needs a subject specialist who is not on the staff of their own school. Live online delivery is what makes that match possible from Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain as easily as from Jumeirah, and the lesson time is set in Gulf Standard Time either way.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP ends in on-screen examinations and ePortfolios for schools that run eAssessment. An MYP result does not get retaken in the way a Diploma subject does, but a weak MYP year is the single best predictor of a Diploma subject that will need repeating two years later, particularly in Mathematics and the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run the MYP into an IGCSE year rather than straight into the Diploma, which changes what a Year 11 student has actually been assessed on. Families who fix an MYP Mathematics gap in Year 10 rarely meet a retake conversation at all, and that is the cheapest version of this page's advice.

ib-retake-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects UAE families most often return to for a second attempt, with the component where the marks usually went. A retake plan that names the paper is worth three that name the subject, because the hours go where the marks are rather than across a syllabus the student has already covered once.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level the non-calculator Paper 1 and the calculator Paper 2 carry 30% each, Paper 3 carries 20% and the exploration 20%. Retake marks are usually sitting in Paper 1 algebra and in the extended-response Paper 3, where a student who can do every topic separately cannot hold a long problem together.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Both papers allow a calculator, which hides the problem until results day: students lose marks on interpretation and on written justification rather than on computation. At SL the two papers carry 40% each with the exploration at 20%. A repeat here is often four weeks of statistics and modelling, not a full re-teach.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The scientific investigation carries 20% of the grade and is frequently the component that caps a result before the exams begin. In the papers, the marks go on multi-step mechanics, on circuits, and on the extended questions that ask for a derivation. HL candidates repeating Physics usually need Paper 2 technique more than new content.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and the data-based questions are where repeat candidates lose most. The internal investigation again carries 20%, so a family should establish what that mark was before buying a single hour of paper practice. A low internal mark and strong papers is a different plan from the reverse.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology retakes are rarely about recall. They are about command terms: outline, explain, evaluate and distinguish each carry a different expectation, and a student who answers all four as describe loses marks across every paper. Pair that with the statistics and experimental-design questions, which reward practice rather than revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams drawn without labels, evaluation written as a conclusion rather than as argument, and the HL quantitative paper are the three repeat failure points. The internal commentaries are already banked by the time results arrive, so a second attempt has to decide whether new commentaries are submitted or the existing mark is carried.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case study released ahead of the exam is where a retake candidate gains fastest, because the content is known months in advance and most students under-prepare it. Marks also go on applying tools to the stimulus instead of describing them, which is a writing habit a tutor can change in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen guided analysis and Paper 2 is comparative. At HL the essay adds a fourth component. Retake candidates almost always need Paper 1: a repeatable method for reading an unseen text under time, rather than more texts. The individual oral mark is usually already fixed.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Paper 1 source work has its own mark scheme and rewards a drilled routine; Paper 2 rewards two well-chosen case studies rather than broad coverage; the HL Paper 3 regional option is where candidates run out of time. A second attempt in History is mostly timed writing with marked feedback, not re-reading.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies quoted without dates, ethics questions answered generically, and the research-methods paper at HL account for most of the lost marks. The internal experimental study is a report against published criteria, so a retake candidate needs to know whether that mark is being carried before planning anything else.

ib-retake-tutor.regionsTitle: Where retake candidates sit, emirate by emirate
ib-retake-tutor.regionsIntro: A retake entry is made through a school or an examination centre, and both the regulator and the centre options change with the emirate. Families searching for a retake tutor in Dubai and families searching for a retake tutor in Abu Dhabi are working inside two different regulatory systems, and the northern emirates sit inside a third.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. The widest choice of IB schools and examination centres in the country, and the shortest list of excuses for a school that will not discuss a second-attempt entry.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for school staff bar paid private tutoring of a teacher's own enrolled students, which matters when a family is offered evening help by the school.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under the Department of Education and Knowledge. Fewer IB Diploma centres than the capital, so a repeat candidate may be travelling to Abu Dhabi for papers while studying with a tutor online. Worth confirming the centre before the entry is made rather than after.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum and fee approval sitting with the emirate regulator means a school's willingness to enter a second-attempt candidate is a local question.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here fall under the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Diploma provision is limited, so retake candidates often work with a school in Dubai or Sharjah for the entry itself.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah, approves curricula and assessment methods. Distance from the main examination centres makes the exam-fortnight logistics part of the plan, not an afterthought.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education. The east coast is the part of the country every competitor page ignores, and it is where online delivery matters most: a Higher Level specialist is a scheduling question rather than a driving question.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market in the country, which means a repeat candidate here will almost certainly be taught by someone who is not within reach of the house, whatever the delivery model promises.

schoolClusters.note: Students we support sit the Diploma at schools across the emirate, and the practical differences between them show up in a retake conversation: whether the school registers second-attempt candidates, how early internal coursework deadlines fall, and whether the IB coordinator will keep supervising a candidate who has already left.

Capital-region Diploma candidates face a shorter list of centres and the ADEK ethics rules on staff tutoring, so families here more often need a tutor with no connection to the school. That is a straightforward match online and a difficult one by postcode.

ib-retake-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Named schools are ecosystem context for families reading this page; IB Gram claims no affiliation with, endorsement by or partnership with any school or group listed.
ib-retake-tutor.modesIntro: Four shapes of support cover almost every retake conversation. The difference between them is time, not quality: a seventeen-week block and a three-week repair job are answers to different questions, and quoting the wrong one wastes a family's money as surely as hiring the wrong tutor does.

modes.title: The seventeen-week retake block
modes.description: The standard shape for one or two subjects entered into the next available session. Two sessions a week per subject, a marked paper every fortnight, and a written plan dated backwards from the first paper. The first three weeks are diagnosis and syllabus triage rather than teaching, which is what stops the block from becoming a second full course.
bullets: Two live one-to-one sessions a week per subject, 60 or 90 minutes
One full past paper under exam conditions every second week
Marked feedback returned before the next session, not during it
A fortnightly note to the parent naming what moved and what did not

modes.title: Single-paper repair
modes.description: For the candidate whose grade sat one or two marks below a boundary on one component. Three to six sessions on that paper alone, with timed practice and a mark-scheme routine. This is the cheapest useful version of retake support and the one most providers will not quote, because it does not fill a term.
bullets: Scoped from the component grades on the statement of results
Timed questions in the session, not set as homework
Mark-scheme language drilled until the student uses it unprompted
Stops when the technique holds, not when the package runs out

modes.title: Coursework review clinic
modes.description: Where a repeated subject allows a new internal submission, the student plans it, researches it and writes it. The tutor questions the method, challenges the analysis and marks drafts against the published criteria, which is the whole of what an IB academic-honesty rule permits a tutor to do.
bullets: Criteria read letter by letter with the marks attached
Feedback written as questions the student answers themselves
Every draft stays in the student's own document and own words
A record of what was discussed, for the supervisor's authenticity statement

modes.title: Gap-year holding pattern
modes.description: A student waiting a full year for the next session has no school timetable holding the week together. One session a week per subject keeps the content alive at a fraction of the cost of an intensive block, then the hours rise in the final seventeen weeks when the entry is confirmed and the paper is dated.
bullets: One maintenance session a week per subject through the quiet months
Hours scale up on a date agreed in advance, not on a sales call
Work set for the weeks between, with deadlines that are actually checked
Lessons continue through travel, because delivery is online

sections.heading: The retake question is a calendar question first
paragraphs: Parents type IB resit tutor and IB retake tutor into Google in the same week every year, and the search is almost always made with a statement of results open in another tab. The useful answer is not a list of tutors. It is a sequence: read the result properly, decide whether to challenge a mark or repeat the component, pick the session, make the entry, then buy hours. Reversing that order is how families end up paying for twelve weeks of teaching towards a paper their child was never entered for.

The IB assesses twice a year. A candidate who sat in May can therefore aim at a session a few months later or at the same month a year on. Those two routes are not variations of one plan. The short route is an intensive block with no new content and a hard entry deadline. The long route is a year of maintenance, a university conversation about deferral, and a decision about whether the student is enrolled anywhere while it happens. The hours, the cost and the risks are different in each.

There is also a third route that gets forgotten: accept the grades and let a university condition be met another way. Not every disappointing result needs a repeat. A foundation year, a different course with a lower subject requirement, or a January start can be a better answer than seventeen weeks of revision, and an honest conversation about that is part of what the first call is for. A retake that nobody actually needed is still a retake that costs AED thousands and a year.
bullets: Read the component grades, not just the subject grades
Separate the challenge decision from the repeat decision
Confirm who makes the entry before agreeing any teaching plan
Ask what the university will accept before assuming a repeat is required

sections.heading: The ten days after results day, and what each one is for
paragraphs: The window between a results release and the point where options start closing is short, and most of it is spent waiting for other people. The decisions below do not run in parallel by accident: each one depends on the one above it, and the enquiry upon results decision has to be made before a retake entry commits the family to anything. A school that is closed for the summer break makes all of this slower, which is why the first call is usually to the IB coordinator rather than to a tutor.

The statement of results carries component-level information that a subject grade hides. A Chemistry 4 built from a strong Paper 2 and a weak internal mark is a different problem from a Chemistry 4 built from the reverse, and only one of them is fixable with paper practice. Families routinely buy tuition before anyone has read that breakdown. Thirty minutes with the coordinator saves more money than any discount a tutoring provider will offer.

An enquiry upon results is a request to the IB, made through the school, for a mark to be checked. It has a published window for each session, it carries a fee, and the outcome can go down as well as up. It is worth asking for when a component sits one or two marks under a boundary and the school agrees the mark looks wrong. It is not a substitute for a retake entry, and the retake entry deadline does not wait for the enquiry result.

sections.heading: What may be repeated, and what is carried forward
paragraphs: An IB Diploma retake is not usually a repeat of everything. The Diploma is assembled from six subject grades plus the core, and a second attempt at the IB Diploma is normally built by repeating the components that cost the award and leaving the rest as awarded. Which components may be left alone, and which have to be resubmitted because the syllabus or the prescribed titles have moved on, is a question for the coordinator at the point of entry. It is also the question that decides whether a family is buying six weeks of work or sixty.

The number of attempts available to a candidate is limited, and the limit is set in the IB's own assessment regulations rather than by the school. Any family planning a third attempt should read the current regulations with the coordinator before paying for teaching, because the answer is a rule and not a negotiation. The same document governs how carried-forward marks are handled and how long a candidate's registration remains live after the first attempt.

The table below is a planning aid, not a ruling. Treat each row as the question to put to the coordinator in the first conversation, with your child's session and subjects named. The reason to put it in writing is that internal marks are the part families forget: a student who spends a term on paper technique and then discovers that a carried-forward internal mark caps the subject at a 5 has lost the term to a single unasked question.

sections.heading: Seventeen weeks, counted backwards from the next paper
paragraphs: A single-subject repeat into the next session usually gives a UAE family about seventeen usable weeks once the summer break, the entry paperwork and the first fortnight of diagnosis are taken out. The plan below is written backwards from the first paper because that is the only fixed point in it. Everything else - how many sessions a week, when the first full past paper is sat, when the student stops learning content and starts practising under time - is derived from that date.

The shape matters more than the hour count. Weeks seventeen to fifteen are not teaching: they are reading the statement of results, mapping the syllabus against what the student can actually do unaided, and throwing out the two thirds of the course that was never the problem. Families find this uncomfortable, because paying for a session where nobody is taught anything feels wasteful. It is the opposite: it is what stops the remaining fourteen weeks from being a second complete course at twice the price.

The back end of the plan is equally deliberate. From week eight, every fortnight contains a full paper sat under exam timing, marked against the published scheme and returned before the next session. From week three the content work stops entirely and the sessions become technique: reading the question, allocating time across a paper, writing to the command term, and recognising the two or three question types that previously cost this particular student marks.

sections.heading: Why an entry deadline sits months before the paper
paragraphs: Every examination board closes entries long before it prints a paper, because papers, invigilation and centre allocation are planned around a candidate list. Cambridge International publishes the clearest worked example: for the March 2027 series the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, results reach centres through Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Entries close more than two months before the first paper.

Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE exams in a May/June and a November series, and the published pattern is the same: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live PDF on its own site is the version to work from rather than any figure restated on a tutoring page.

Cambridge adds one detail that catches UAE families specifically. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For an IB November session retake the equivalent information - window, upload deadlines, entry cut-off - comes from the IB coordinator or ibo.org, and this page deliberately prints no IB date rather than an unverified one.

sections.heading: Where the marks were actually lost
paragraphs: Across the subjects UAE families repeat most, the pattern of lost marks is narrower than parents expect. Very few repeat candidates have failed to learn the syllabus. Most have learned it in a form that works in a classroom and breaks in an exam hall: topic by topic rather than in combination, with unlimited time, and without the specific vocabulary a mark scheme is looking for. That is a different problem from ignorance, and it responds to a different kind of session.

Mathematics is the clearest case. A student who can integrate when told to integrate, and who cannot see that a question requires integration, will fail Paper 1 and pass every homework. Sciences split differently: the internal investigation is already banked, so the repeat hinges on the data and extended-response questions. In the essay subjects, the loss is almost always structural - a conclusion written where evaluation was asked for, or sources described rather than used.

The diagnosis has to be done on the student's own work, under timing, in the first fortnight. A tutor who begins teaching in week one has skipped it. The output of that fortnight is short: a list of two or three question types, named, with the marks each one cost in the session that was sat. Everything after that is practice against the list, and the list is what the parent should be shown before any block of hours is agreed. If nobody can produce one, nobody has looked properly.

sections.heading: What a retake costs across the UAE market
paragraphs: Published rates for IB retake tuition in this market are wide, and the figures below are what each provider puts on its own site, read in October 2026. They are market rates rather than IB Gram prices. A university-student tutor online advertises from AED 45 an hour; a qualified subject tutor online from AED 150 to AED 300; an in-home visit, travel included, from AED 180 to AED 500; a specialist in an exam year from AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards; and a premium named tutor at AED 650.

Three things legitimately move a retake quote. The first is the level: a Higher Level paper with an extended-response component needs someone who has taught it, and that person is not interchangeable with a general maths tutor. The second is the shape of the work: a single-paper repair of five sessions costs a fraction of a seventeen-week block, and a provider who only quotes blocks is selling the block rather than the diagnosis. The third is timing, because the same tutor has fewer free hours in the eight weeks before a session than in the six months before it.

Two things should not move it. One is urgency - a quote that rises because results day was yesterday is pricing panic, not expertise. The other is a claimed outcome. No tutor can promise a grade, and a page that offers to sell one is telling you something about itself. For context on what families are already paying into education here, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, so a tutoring budget this year is being set against a flat school fee rather than a rising one.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live online, with one session left
paragraphs: Families searching for retake help in the UAE often start by looking for someone who will come to the house, and the honest answer is that the market offers it, at a price, with a travel cost built in. IB Gram does not sell that in the Emirates. Home visits are a service we provide only in India; across the UAE every lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The comparison below is why we think that is the right model for a repeat candidate specifically, rather than a limitation we are dressing up.

A retake candidate needs a narrow specialist. Not a maths tutor, but someone who has taught Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and marked Paper 3 answers. Inside a twenty-minute drive of any given villa, the number of people who fit that description is close to zero in Dubai and actually zero in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain. Online IB retake lessons change the question from who lives nearby to who is free at 7pm Gulf Standard Time, and that is a far better pool to choose from when a single component has to move.

The practical details favour online too, in this situation. A retake block runs through a summer in which many UAE families travel, and a schedule that survives three weeks in London or Kochi is worth more than one that pauses. Marked work can be returned as annotated files rather than as a verbal comment at the door. Sessions can be recorded for the student's own revision. And the travel time that a visiting tutor charges for, roughly 30 to 60 minutes a session in city traffic, goes back into teaching instead.

sections.heading: Coursework on a second attempt, and the line a tutor holds
paragraphs: Where a repeated subject permits a new internal submission, the honesty question arrives immediately, and the UAE market does contain people who will answer it badly. One provider researched for this project advertises finished Internal Assessments for a fee. A family who buys one is buying an academic-malpractice investigation for their child, and the IB's own rules make the consequence an expulsion risk, not a telling-off. No part of IB Gram's service touches that.

What a tutor is allowed to do is substantial, and worth being precise about. A tutor may explain the criteria, read a draft and mark it against the published descriptors, ask why a method was chosen, point at an argument that does not follow, and refuse to accept a conclusion the data does not support. The student plans the piece, gathers the evidence and writes every word that is submitted. Feedback is given as questions the student answers in their own document, which also keeps the supervisor's authenticity statement truthful.

The second honesty question concerns material. Past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and this page links to them rather than reproducing or supplying them. A tutor who offers a private library of mark schemes is handing a family a copyright problem. The table below is a planning reference for the components a repeat candidate most often has to resubmit, and the length limits are the published ones to check against your child's current subject guide.

sections.heading: Universities, equivalency and the months in between
paragraphs: A retake decision is really two decisions, and the second one belongs to a university admissions office. Before a single hour is bought, someone should ask the institution directly whether it will hold the place, defer the start, accept a later certificate, or has already released the offer. Admissions teams answer that question quickly and in writing, and the answer frequently changes the plan: a deferred start removes the urgency entirely, while a released offer may turn a repeat into a reapplication with a different deadline.

For study inside the UAE, the Ministry of Education's equivalency process sits behind admission, and it is one of the least-covered topics in this market. The published clarification for the British track requires five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and it states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor publishes six as the subject count; the sourced figure is five.

For the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with at least 450 in SAT Mathematics for the mathematics requirement. It states no IB points threshold, so no IB equivalency figure appears on this page. Equivalency is a process the family completes with the ministry and the attestation desk in their emirate; IB Gram describes it and points to the official channel, and nothing about tutoring is required for it.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the summer gap and the weeks a retake plan quietly loses
paragraphs: A seventeen-week block drawn on paper assumes seventeen usable weeks, and the UAE calendar does not provide them. Ramadan shortens school days and moves the whole family's working hours; most students here study better after Iftar than at 5pm, and a tutor who cannot move a slot to 9pm loses a month of productive sessions. Eid removes a week on each side in practice. The National Day break lands in early December, which is exactly where a November-session candidate would otherwise be starting their next plan.

The summer is the bigger trap for a repeat candidate specifically, because the gap between a July results release and an autumn preparation block falls straight into it. Families travel for six weeks, the school is closed, and the coordinator who has to make the entry is unreachable. The practical answer is to do the paperwork before anyone flies and to keep one weekly online session running through the travel, which is possible precisely because nobody has to arrive anywhere.

The mandatory UAE subjects take real timetable space in any repeat year, and no competitor page mentions them. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit, advises at least 25 minutes for any such lesson, requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes for the two groups. A student repeating subjects while still enrolled is carrying that load alongside the retake plan.
bullets: Move sessions after Iftar through Ramadan rather than losing the month
Make the entry before the summer travel, not after it
Keep one weekly session running through August to hold the content
Count the mandatory-subject hours into the week before promising three sessions a subject

process.title: Send the statement of results, not a summary
process.description: The first thing we ask for is the component breakdown, the subjects and levels, the session sat and the deadline the family is working to. A screenshot is fine. Without it any plan is guesswork, and guesswork in a retake year is what turns a five-session repair into a term of teaching nobody needed.

process.title: One free trial lesson on the paper that went wrong
process.description: A sixty-minute live session with a subject specialist, spent on the component that cost the grade rather than on introductions. No card details are taken and nothing is owed if the family stops there. What comes out of it is a short written view of what is actually missing, which the parent gets whether they continue or not.

process.title: A dated plan counted back from the entry deadline
process.description: Hours a week, which papers get sat under timing and when, what is marked between sessions, and the date by which the entry has to be registered. The plan names your child's session and deadline as confirmed by the school, because our page will not print an IB date we have not seen verified.

process.title: Weekly one-to-one, with work marked between sessions
process.description: Lessons run over live video in Gulf Standard Time, usually in the evening. Work set between sessions comes back marked against the published criteria before the next lesson, not during it, so the session itself is spent on what the marking found rather than on reading it together.

process.title: A review at the halfway point, and a switch if the fit is wrong
process.description: Halfway through a block the parent gets a written note on what has moved, what has not, and whether the hours should go up, down or elsewhere. If the match is wrong, the tutor changes and the plan carries over. A retake timetable is too short to spend four weeks hoping a mismatch resolves itself.

whyPoints.title: The diagnosis comes before the hours
whyPoints.description: The first fortnight produces a named list of two or three question types that cost marks in the session already sat. Everything after that is practice against the list. Parents see the list before agreeing a block, which is the only honest way to say how many hours a repeat actually needs.

whyPoints.title: Matched by paper, not by subject
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level extended-response paper and a Standard Level calculator paper are different teaching jobs. We match on the component, so a student repeating Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 works with somebody who has taught and marked that paper rather than with a general mathematics tutor.

whyPoints.title: Online because the clock is the constraint
whyPoints.description: Across the UAE we deliver one-to-one over live video and we do not send tutors to addresses in the Emirates; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For a retake candidate that trade is favourable: the specialist pool is national rather than local, and the schedule survives the summer travel that every repeat plan runs into.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can check against published sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider that published it and dated to the month it was read. Every regulatory statement links to u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE or the examination board. Nothing is presented as our own statistic, because a number without a source is not a reason to trust anyone.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is written down, not implied
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria, mark drafts and challenge arguments. They do not produce assessed work, supply mark schemes or edit a submission into shape. This is stated here so a family can hold us to it, and so the contrast with providers selling finished coursework in this market is explicit rather than hinted at.

faqs.question: My daughter missed the Diploma by two points. Is repeating one subject enough?
faqs.answer: Often it is, but the statement of results decides it rather than the points gap. Two points can sit inside one subject, or they can be tangled up with a failing condition in the core that a subject repeat will not touch. Ask the coordinator which condition was not met and which component in that subject lost the marks. If a single paper is two or three marks under a boundary, a short block aimed at that paper is the cheapest route. If the gap is spread across three subjects, a one-subject entry will not recover the award.

faqs.question: How soon after results day does a retake entry have to be registered?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families expect, and the exact date comes from your child's school rather than from a page like this. Boards close entries months before they print papers: Cambridge, for example, set final entries for its March 2027 series on 27 November 2026, more than two months before the first exam on 3 February 2027. For an IB session, ask the coordinator for the entry cut-off in writing in the first week after results. Buying tuition before that date is confirmed is the most common sequencing error in a retake year.

faqs.question: Does a repeated grade replace the first one on the certificate?
faqs.answer: How attempts appear on IB documentation is set in the IB's own assessment regulations, and your coordinator holds the current version. Rather than taking a number from a tutoring site, ask them two things directly: what the certificate will show after a second attempt, and what universities you are applying to will see. Admissions offices differ in how they treat a later sitting, and some ask about it at interview. Getting both answers in writing before the entry is made costs an email and removes the only part of this process that families tend to discover too late.

faqs.question: How many times can an IB subject be repeated?
faqs.answer: The number of attempts available to a candidate is limited by the IB's assessment regulations, not by the school's willingness or by what a tutor will sell. Read the current regulations with the coordinator before planning a third sitting, because the answer is a rule rather than a negotiation, and it also governs how long a registration stays live after the first attempt. Any provider happy to quote for an unlimited series of attempts without asking which attempt this is has not read the document that decides whether the plan is even possible.

faqs.question: We are four months from the next session. Can two Higher Levels realistically be repeated?
faqs.answer: Two Higher Levels in roughly seventeen weeks is possible for a student whose problem is technique and unrealistic for one whose problem is content. The test is the first fortnight: if the diagnosis produces a short list of question types in each subject, two subjects fit at three hours a week each. If it finds whole topics never understood, one subject in this session and the second in the next one will produce a better outcome than a rushed pair. The honest version of that conversation happens before the block is sold, not in week nine.

faqs.question: Will a retake tutor work from the statement of results, or does my son need re-testing?
faqs.answer: Both, in that order. The statement of results gives the component grades, which narrows the search immediately and costs nothing. A diagnostic session then tests whether the student can produce that work unaided and under time, which the certificate cannot show. The output is a written list of the specific question types that lost marks. Expect to see that list before agreeing a block of hours; a provider who proposes a package before anyone has looked at a component breakdown is selling a timetable rather than a repair.

faqs.question: What does retake tuition cost per hour in the UAE, and who publishes those figures?
faqs.answer: Rates read on UAE provider sites in October 2026 run from AED 45 an hour for a university-student tutor online, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for a visiting tutor with travel included, AED 200 to 450 and upwards for an exam-year specialist, and AED 650 at the premium end. EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, Bestimate, TutorChase and BartyED publish those bands on their own pages. They are market figures, not IB Gram prices; ours are quoted after a free trial lesson, against the plan your child needs.

faqs.question: Who registers the entry if my son has already left his school?
faqs.answer: A school that still holds the registration is usually the simplest route, and many UAE schools will keep supervising a former candidate for one further session if asked early. Where that is refused, an examination centre entry is the alternative, and an IB private candidate entry has conditions attached that differ by component - coursework supervision in particular. Ask the coordinator first, in the week results arrive, and ask the centre second. Settle this before buying hours, because teaching towards a paper nobody has entered a student for is the one wasted cost in this process.

faqs.question: Does a retake change what the Ministry of Education needs for equivalency?
faqs.answer: The requirement attaches to the certificate, not to how many attempts produced it. For the British track, the published clarification asks for five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, and states that Arabic and Islamic education are not among the five. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so verify the IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation desk in your emirate before planning around any figure you read elsewhere.

faqs.question: Can the Extended Essay mark stay as it is while one subject is repeated?
faqs.answer: Usually yes - the Extended Essay is its own component and is normally carried forward unless a new essay is entered. The practical question is whether the carried mark still lets the award arithmetic work, because the core contributes points alongside Theory of Knowledge. Put it to the coordinator as a calculation rather than as a yes-or-no question: with this essay grade carried and this subject lifted by one grade, does the Diploma come out? If the answer is no, the plan needs a second component, and better to know in week one.

faqs.question: How do lessons fit around Ramadan when the preparation block runs through it?
faqs.answer: Sessions move rather than pause. Most students here work better after Iftar than in the late afternoon, so slots shift to roughly 9pm or later for the month and the weekly count usually stays the same. The weeks around Eid are better treated as holiday in the plan than as sessions nobody attends. Because every lesson is delivered over live video, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation with someone who was going to drive across the city at 5pm.

faqs.question: My son is on a gap year with no timetable. What should his week look like?
faqs.answer: One maintenance session a week per subject through the quiet months, with work set between sessions and actually checked, then a rise to two or three sessions in the final seventeen weeks once the entry is confirmed. The failure mode in a gap year is not intensity, it is drift: three months pass, the content fades, and the block that was meant to be revision becomes re-teaching at a higher cost. A fixed weekly slot and a dated plan is what prevents that, and it is cheaper than the alternative.

faqs.question: Is an examiner-led tutor worth two or three times the hourly rate for a repeat?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the question to ask is what specifically is being bought. Current examiner status cannot be assumed from a profile line, and examiner experience does not give anyone access to marking, boundaries or unreleased papers - anybody suggesting otherwise is describing something that does not exist. What a genuinely experienced marker brings is accurate judgement about where a script loses marks. At AED 500 or more an hour that is worth paying for on a component that is one or two marks short, and poor value for re-teaching a topic.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a resubmitted internal assessment without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria letter by letter, mark a draft against the published descriptors, ask why a method was chosen, and refuse to accept a conclusion the evidence does not support. The student plans the piece, gathers the data and writes every word that is submitted, in their own document. Anyone offering a finished piece for a fee is selling your child a malpractice investigation - one provider in this market advertises exactly that. The supervisor also signs an authenticity statement, which should be true.

faqs.question: Nobody is listed for Physics Higher Level in our evening slot. What happens then?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting someone who nearly fits. Where no UAE-hours specialist is free for a specific Higher Level component, the options we put to a family are a different time slot, a short wait for a named tutor's availability, or a specialist based in India teaching into the Gulf Standard Time evening, which is how most of our Higher Level matches already run. If none of those works for your child's deadline, that is worth hearing in the first week rather than discovering in week six.

faqs.question: Should we pay for a remark before paying for preparation?
faqs.answer: Where a component sits one or two marks under a boundary and the school agrees the mark looks inconsistent, an enquiry upon results is worth requesting - it runs through the school, carries a fee, and the mark can move down as well as up. It is not an alternative to an entry, because the entry deadline does not wait for the outcome. The practical sequence is to lodge the enquiry, make the entry anyway, and start the diagnosis. Withdrawing an entry is easier than discovering the window closed while you waited.

faqs.question: Is my child's own school teacher allowed to tutor the repeat privately?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi, no. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours need that permit, which is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Verify the current wording with ADEK before relying on it, and treat an offer of this kind with caution.

ib-retake-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the date, then the diagnosis, then the hours
ib-retake-tutor.closingBody: If your child's results came in below what a place depended on, the next three phone calls matter more than the next three tutoring quotes. Call the IB coordinator for the component breakdown and the entry deadline. Call the university and ask in writing what it will accept. Then send us the statement of results and take a free trial lesson on the paper that actually went wrong - no card details, nothing owed if you stop there. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, anywhere from Dubai Marina to Fujairah, and the plan you get back is dated backwards from the paper rather than priced forwards from a package.

intro.heading: Revision has a calendar, and most UAE families meet it late
paragraphs: IB revision classes in the UAE are structured, dated sessions that take a Diploma or MYP syllabus a student has already been taught and turn it into marks on a paper. They are not re-teaching, and they are not a second school day. A revision class works on one candidate's gaps, in syllabus order, under exam conditions, with someone else marking the result. Searches for this phrase spike twice a year in the Gulf: once in January when mock results land, and once in March when study leave appears on the school calendar and the maths stops being abstract.

The unit most families buy is wrong. Revision gets purchased as hours per week, open-ended, starting whenever a tutor is free. Revision is actually a sequence with dates attached: an audit of what is secure, a repair phase while school is still teaching, a retrieval phase after the mocks, and a rehearsal phase under timed conditions. Each phase has a window, and the windows do not move because a family started late. Buying twelve hours in the right window beats buying thirty in the wrong one, and no amount of spend turns March into November.

The UAE adds its own constraints to that calendar, and they are specific rather than cosmetic. Your child's school week already carries Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies as mandatory subjects alongside the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA sets out how that time is organised in Dubai. Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar and lands squarely in the Gulf revision term. Many households run two candidates on two boards at once, one sitting IB papers and one sitting Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE in an overlapping series. A revision plan that ignores any of these is a plan for a different country.

This page is built as a calendar. It names what is sold under the words IB revision classes and what each product can diagnose, sets out the four passes and when each belongs, audits where revision hours actually come from in a UAE school week, ranks revision activities by the evidence they leave, shows where a revision hour still pays and where the marks are already closed, works through the exam fortnight day by day, and publishes the AED the market charges with the source and the date beside every figure. Several of those numbers do not flatter us, and they are printed anyway.

Delivery is stated plainly before anything else. Lessons for UAE families run one to one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the school day. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. For revision specifically that is an advantage rather than a compromise: a candidate in Mirdif who needs Higher Level Paper 3 technique gets a specialist in that paper, not whoever can reach Mirdif by half past four, and the marking that makes revision worth anything happens between sessions instead of in the car.

What a tutor will not do is also fixed. Tutors teach, question, mark and coach. The words, the data and the decisions in any assessed component belong to the candidate, and nothing on this site is an offer to supply them. That boundary costs us the families who were shopping for something else, and it is the reason the rest of this page can be read as advice rather than as a pitch.

ib-revision-classes.programmesIntro: Revision means a different exercise in each IB programme, because each one assesses differently. The Diploma ends in external papers and closed internal components. The MYP ends in on-screen eAssessment or in school-moderated work. The Career-related Programme carries a Diploma course load beside a separate professional qualification. The Primary Years Programme has nothing to revise at all, which is worth saying out loud.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the extended essay and CAS. The written papers at the end of DP2 carry most of each subject grade, and the internally assessed component in each subject is closed long before study leave. Revision at Diploma level therefore splits cleanly: anything still open is coachable, anything submitted is a sunk mark that should stop consuming hours. The Higher Level third paper, which Standard Level candidates never sit, is the single most under-revised component in the programme.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the Diploma sits inside a two-year school calendar that breaks for a long Gulf summer, Eid holidays that shift annually and Ramadan, which usually lands in the DP2 revision term. Dubai's private sector taught 17 different curricula to 387,441 pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25 and the International Baccalaureate accounted for seven per cent of that enrolment, so a DP cohort in a UAE school is often small enough that one teacher covers both levels of a subject. That is where a specialist revision hour earns its place.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of interdisciplinary teaching assessed against four criteria per subject, each carrying its own achievement levels. MYP 5 candidates in many schools sit on-screen eAssessment, which rewards reading the task command precisely rather than reproducing content. Revision here is mostly technique and criterion literacy: a student who can recite the content and still scores in the middle band is almost always misreading what the criterion asks for. Personal Project marks are internally assessed and close at the school's own deadline.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools differ widely on whether MYP 5 leads to eAssessment, to a school-awarded certificate, or sideways into Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE for the final two years. That choice decides what a Year 11 revision plan looks like, and it is a question for your child's coordinator rather than for a tutor. Families moving from MYP into the Diploma in the same school usually find the gap is in mathematical fluency and in writing under time, not in subject knowledge.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, a language development strand and personal and professional skills. CP candidates sit the same external papers as Diploma candidates in their DP subjects, so the revision mechanics for those courses are identical. The reflective project is internally assessed and has a school deadline, which means it drops out of a revision plan the moment it is handed in.
programmes.countryNote: A small number of UAE schools run the CP, usually alongside a business, hospitality or engineering partner qualification. The practical effect on revision is a compressed timetable: the career-related study takes timetabled hours that a full Diploma candidate spends on a sixth subject, so the DP papers a CP candidate does sit have to be revised in fewer available weeks. Counting those weeks honestly at the start of DP2 is the whole exercise.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations and no revision in the sense this page uses the word. What parents searching for revision classes at this stage usually want is either a diagnosed gap closed before it compounds, or preparation for an entrance assessment at a selective secondary school. Both are real pieces of work and neither is revision. Calling them by their proper names stops families buying exam technique for a nine-year-old who needs number fluency.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools the PYP exhibition in the final primary year is a presentation and inquiry exercise, not an examination, and coaching it to a script defeats its purpose. The genuinely useful early intervention for a UAE primary family is usually Arabic, because the mandatory subject stream runs from the start of schooling and a gap there follows a child into secondary school with its own examined requirements attached.

ib-revision-classes.subjectsIntro: IB DP revision classes have subject-specific priorities, and the differences are concrete rather than a matter of style. Below is what the final three passes should look like in the subjects UAE families book most, with the component where marks most often leak. Confirm every assessment detail against the subject guide your child's cohort is actually following, because guides change between cohorts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Revision is proof technique, algebraic fluency and calculator discipline. Higher Level candidates lose marks in proof by induction, complex numbers and the harder calculus questions, almost always through setting out rather than through ignorance. The exploration is internally assessed and closes at the school deadline, so after that date every hour belongs to the papers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical tests, modelling and graphical calculator technology carry the paper. The commonest leak is reporting a statistical result without interpreting it in context, which costs the final mark on a long question repeatedly. Revision here is best done as whole questions rather than topic drills, because the paper rewards reading a context correctly before any mathematics starts.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Define-and-derive questions are recoverable in weeks; graph and uncertainty work takes longer. Revision should separate the recall load from the technique load, then attack uncertainties, significant figures and unit algebra as their own exercise. Higher Level candidates who skip the extension topics in revision are skipping the paper where unfamiliar material is deliberately placed.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics reward structured recall; data-based questions reward technique. The repeated pattern on marked scripts is a correct mechanism drawn without curly arrows placed properly, which scores nothing. Revision should include at least one session purely on drawing conventions, because the marks are allocated to them explicitly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume makes retrieval practice unavoidable; reading notes does not work in this subject at all. Command terms decide the mark here more than in any other science, as outline, explain and evaluate carry different structural demands on the same content. Diagram labelling and data interpretation are the two fastest places to recover marks late.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams first, then evaluation. A correctly drawn and fully labelled diagram carries marks on its own, and most candidates arrive at revision drawing from memory with axes unlabelled. Higher Level calculation work is a separate exercise and is usually under-practised. Real-world examples should be chosen and rehearsed before study leave rather than improvised in the hall.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application and the case study decide the grade. Revision is best spent rehearsing frameworks against unfamiliar scenarios rather than memorising definitions, since the paper gives the context and asks for judgement. Candidates lose the evaluation marks by describing both sides without reaching a supported conclusion, which is a structural fix rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis improves with timed practice on texts the student has never met, which is the one exercise most candidates avoid. Revision should build a reusable approach to an unseen text and a bank of comparative points across studied works. The Higher Level essay is internally assessed and closes at the school deadline, taking its weighting with it.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source skills and essay structure are both trainable in the final two passes; content breadth is not, which is why the coverage audit has to happen early. Revision essays should be planned in ten minutes and written in thirty-five to match paper timing. The Higher Level regional option paper rewards narrow, deep preparation over broad reading.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Named studies with dates, methods and findings are the currency, and a vague recollection of a study earns almost nothing. Revision should produce a study bank the candidate can reproduce from a blank page, then practise selecting from it under a question stem. Research methods and ethical considerations are the marks most often left on the table.

ib-revision-classes.regionsTitle: Revision term emirate by emirate, and the authority behind each one
ib-revision-classes.regionsIntro: Which authority answers for your child's school changes the published inspection evidence you can read, the fee framework the school works inside and sometimes the holiday pattern your revision plan has to fit. All seven emirates are covered below. Sessions are delivered online to all of them on Gulf Standard Time, so an address changes the calendar rather than the availability.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes inspection reports families can read before buying any tutoring. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. Mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit in every timetable here.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and is named by almost no competitor page in this market. Its professional-ethics rules for school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, so a revision tutor should be someone outside that relationship.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain schools fall under ADEK alongside the capital, though the school-run distances and the smaller Diploma cohorts change the practical picture. A subject offered to a handful of candidates may be taught by one teacher across both levels, which is the situation where a Higher Level revision specialist makes the clearest difference.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is curriculum and fee approval rather than inspection alone, so the published SPEA framework is worth reading before assuming a school's exam-term support matches a Dubai neighbour's.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a supervisory role across Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families here often commute to Sharjah or Dubai schools, which means a revision session has to clear a long evening return before it can start on Gulf Standard Time.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. The emirate returns effectively no mentions across the competitor pages researched for this market, which is a gap rather than a signal that no Diploma candidates live here.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools sit under the Ministry of Education's supervision. The east-coast location makes a centre-based revision class a genuine logistical problem rather than an inconvenience, and it is the clearest case in the country for a Higher Level subject specialist delivered over live video instead of a local availability search.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the Ministry of Education, Umm Al Quwain has the smallest private-school population of the seven emirates. A family looking for Diploma revision in a less common subject will not find a local match at any price, which is precisely the problem online one-to-one delivery was built to solve.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai carries the largest Diploma cohort in the country, spread across schools that run the programme alongside a British or American primary phase. Revision patterns differ by school: some run full mock weeks in January, others two separate sitting windows, and a few publish study-leave dates only in the spring term.

Capital-region Diploma cohorts are smaller per school than Dubai's, and subject combinations are correspondingly narrower. That raises the chance that a Higher Level option is taught by a single teacher, and lowers the chance of finding a second opinion on a marked script inside the building.

Diploma provision thins out north of Dubai, and curricula vary sharply between schools in the same emirate. Check the regulator's own school listing for what a school is currently licensed to teach before planning a revision year around an assumption about its programme.

ib-revision-classes.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named here as context for the UAE Diploma and International GCSE ecosystem; no affiliation, endorsement or relationship with any school or school group is implied, and curriculum details should be verified against the school and its regulator.
ib-revision-classes.modesIntro: Online IB revision classes are bought in four shapes, and they suit different points in the calendar. All four run one to one over live video, so an IB revision timetable can be built around the school day rather than around a tutor's route across the city. Gulf Standard Time revision sessions start at the hour you choose, with marking returned in between. The right shape depends on how many weeks are left and on whether the gap is content, technique or pacing.

modes.title: Weekly revision cycle through DP2
modes.description: One or two sessions a week from September, running the four passes in order against a dated plan. This is the cheapest version of revision per mark recovered, because it uses the whole year rather than the last six weeks, and it lets the repair pass happen while school is still teaching the content. It also survives Ramadan and travel better than a block, since a missed week is a week rather than a third of the purchase.

One timed component marked every two to three weeks

modes.title: A dated block before a session
modes.description: A fixed number of hours bought for a known date: a mock window, study leave, or a November re-sit. The block is quoted in hours and dates before anything is paid, and it ends with a written handover rather than drifting into a subscription. Blocks work when the content has been taught once and the problem is retrieval and pacing. They do not work as a substitute for teaching that never happened.

modes.title: Per-paper clinic
modes.description: A short run of sessions aimed at one component: Higher Level Paper 3, an unseen analysis paper, a data-based paper, or source-skills work. Clinics suit candidates whose overall grade is fine but who lose the same marks on the same component every sitting. Two to four hours on the structural fault usually moves more than ten hours of general revision, because the fault is structural rather than informational.

modes.title: Exam-fortnight standby
modes.description: Short, scheduled sessions inside the examination window itself, placed in the gaps between papers. The job is narrow: a timing plan, a structure drill, one section of the next paper, then stop. Standby sessions are deliberately short because the candidate's sleep is worth more than the hour, and they are scheduled around the actual timetable rather than at a fixed weekly slot.

No post-mortems on papers already sat

Scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, including early mornings

sections.heading: What the UAE market sells under the words IB revision classes
paragraphs: Five different products are advertised as IB revision classes in this market, and they diagnose different things. A school revision session re-teaches the syllabus at class pace. A tuition-centre group class works on errors common to a cohort. A holiday camp covers content in volume. One-to-one work isolates one candidate's lost marks. Unsupervised past-paper practice at home tests whether content can be retrieved at all. Only the last two produce evidence about your child specifically, and only one of them produces a second opinion on a script.

The distinction matters because families usually buy the cheapest product and then conclude that revision does not work. A group class of nine students cannot name why your child drops the final mark on a long Economics question, because that mark is lost in a way specific to how that candidate writes. Equally, one-to-one hours spent re-teaching content that a school revision session covers adequately are hours bought at four times the necessary rate. The products are complements, and the order in which they are used decides whether the spend was sensible.

Read the table below as a purchasing order rather than a ranking. A candidate three topics behind should be in the school sessions and working through past papers alone before any paid hour is bought, because paid hours are wasted on a gap the student has not yet mapped. A candidate whose content is secure and whose marks are stuck has the opposite problem: the group formats have nothing left to tell them, and the only remaining diagnostic is a marked script read by a specialist.

sections.heading: Four passes over one syllabus, and the window each one belongs in
paragraphs: A syllabus has to be crossed four times before a final paper, and each crossing does a different job. The first pass is an audit: the candidate marks every subtopic as secure, shaky or never properly taught, in the syllabus document's own order. This takes two or three hours per subject and it is the step almost everyone skips, which is why so many revision plans are built on a guess about where the gaps are. A gap list in syllabus order is the only honest input to everything that follows.

The second pass repairs. It runs while school is still teaching, which is the point: a topic re-learned in November has six months of incidental reinforcement ahead of it, and the same topic re-learned in April has none. The third pass is retrieval, and IB mock exam revision is where it starts, because mock scripts are the best diagnostic material a family will ever own for free. Retrieval means blank-page recall and question sets, not reading. The fourth pass is rehearsal: whole papers, timed, in paper order, marked by somebody who is not the candidate.

The hour counts in the table are per subject and assume the content was taught once, competently, the first time. They are deliberately unflattering. Four passes across three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects is a substantial commitment, which is exactly why the audit pass exists: it is what lets a family spend the repair and retrieval hours on four subtopics instead of across a whole syllabus. Families who start in March can still run passes three and four properly, and should be told plainly that pass two has gone.

sections.heading: The hour audit: where revision time actually comes from in a UAE school week
paragraphs: Every revision plan is a claim about hours that exist. Most plans are built by asking how many hours the work needs, which produces a number nobody can supply. The useful question runs the other way: how many hours are genuinely unclaimed in a UAE Diploma student's week, and what has to go to create more. The audit below is the one worth doing on paper with your child before any tutoring is booked, because it usually settles the argument about whether the plan is ambitious or fictional.

Two claims on the week are routinely left out. The mandatory UAE subject stream is the first: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA calculates the required instructional time in 40-minute lesson units, advising that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Those lessons are examined in their own right, so they are not spare capacity. The second omission is CAS and service, which is logged across eighteen months and which students habitually leave until the term they can least afford it.

The honest bottom line in most UAE households is six to ten hours a week genuinely available for revision in DP2, including weekends. That is the budget. A plan requiring twenty is not a stretch target, it is a plan that will fail in week three and take the family's confidence with it. Front-loading CAS into DP1, negotiating homework expectations with the school in the final term, and moving a weekly session to a Friday morning are the three levers that actually create time. Buying more hours is not one of them.

sections.heading: Revision that leaves evidence, and revision that leaves a feeling
paragraphs: The most common complaint in a diagnostic lesson is that a candidate revises for hours and the grade does not move. Almost always the hours were real and the activity was wrong. Re-reading notes and re-watching lessons produce recognition, which feels like knowledge and is not tested by any paper. Recall, structure and pacing are tested, and those three are trained only by exercises that produce something a third party can mark. The test of a revision activity is simple: at the end of it, is there an artefact somebody else can read?

That question sorts the list quickly. A blank-page topic dump produces a page whose holes are the week's syllabus. A set of topic questions with the answers hidden produces a marked set and an error pattern. Timed past paper practice produces a script. Re-reading a chapter produces nothing, and the four hours spent on it are gone with no residue to plan against. Candidates gravitate towards the activities that produce nothing precisely because those activities cannot fail, which is the whole problem with them.

Marking is the step families most often leave out, and it is the one that converts practice into revision. A candidate self-marking against a mark scheme reliably awards marks for intention rather than for what is written, because they can see what they meant. Somebody else reading the same script sees only the words on the page, which is exactly what an examiner sees. That is why one-to-one revision with marking returned between sessions does different work from the same number of unsupervised hours, and why an unmarked past paper is practice rather than revision.
